Choose Scenes → New scene → Import Universal VTT , starting inside the destination folder when appropriate. 2. Select the file and check the scene name, which must be 1–120 characters. 3. Choose Import scene and wait. Grid and lighting come from the file; this modal has no separate configuration for them. 4. Read the warnings after creation, then close the modal. 5. Inspect grid alignment, wall openings, door states and lighting before activating for players. Portals become doors. Baked-in lighting may cause imported lights to start disabled. Ambient color, shadows and unsupported light features are approximated; inspect warnings rather than assuming an exact match. Recover an uncertain import Validation errors create no partial scene. If the connection fails, keep the modal open with the same file/name and choose Import scene again: it reuses the operation identity. Changing fields or reopening starts another operation. If you already closed/refreshed, check Scenes before importing again to avoid a duplicate. Export the applied scene First generate/update a Builder scene if your latest changes are still in its project. Right-click the native scene, choose Export Universal VTT , then Prepare export , inspect warnings and Download Universal VTT . The prepared download is a snapshot of that moment; reopen and prepare again after scene changes. The background and supported visible images/surfaces are flattened into PNG. Walls, doors and enabled lights retain supported interchange data. Tokens, blueprints, variables, jobs, audio, cards, journals, particles, shaders and campaign state are not transferred. GM-only images are omitted, but secret-door geometry may remain; inspect before sharing. Limits Import accepts numeric format 0.2 or 0.3 ; export writes 0.2 . These interchange versions are separate from the app version. The JSON limit is 64 MiB; embedded compressed image limit is 48 MiB; raster area is at most 16,777,216 pixels or a smaller host limit. Geometry allows 5,000 native objects and 20,000 line-of-sight vertices. Import accepts embedded single-frame PNG/WebP rather than remote image URLs. Excessive geometry or missing export tiles fails the operation instead of producing a partial download. Keep the original project and a proper installation backup.

title: Backups, recovery and updates
summary: Protect the installation, distinguish portable exports from backups and apply releases deliberately.
text: Choose the right protection Option Purpose Important boundary --- --- --- Campaign export/import Transfer portable content May omit private history and adjust ownership Campaign snapshot Campaign recovery point Not the entire host or module installation state Full installation backup Recover data, private media and configuration together Requires a consistent database/file set Universal VTT export Exchange a map scene Omits most game and automation state Availability depends on permissions and host options. Before restoring campaign content, preserve the current state and read the consequences shown by the interface. In 0.3.2, selected campaign exports/copies include clocks, clues, mind maps, preparation, journal history and reusable PDF mappings. Typed references remap included targets while omitted ones stay inert; local page/chapter/topic IDs and authored text stay exact. Portable copies clear source member/editor grants rather than granting new access. Snapshots are for recovery within the same campaign. See upgrade and recovery (docs:upgrading) for the seven migrations added since 0.3.1, including the PDF mapping-template table. Make a full backup 1. Arrange a maintenance window and stop writes, including ASGI/Runner and maintenance processes. 2. Copy the configured SQLite database with associated journal/WAL files when present, private media and installed package files, optional compendiums and required configuration/trust keys. 3. Preserve .env privately and record the matching code version and lock file. Include recovery/updates state when preserving an installation for rollback. 4. Restore into a separate writable folder first, with paths pointing to the copy. 5. Verify login, a campaign, representative uploads and required modules before directing players there. The default database is data/gravewright.sqlite3 , not a root db.sqlite3 . A database without its matching media is incomplete. Never publish backups or secrets with site/application source. Apply an update The owner can open the library notification bell and choose View update , or go to Administration → Updates . Review installed/available versions and release notes, create a backup, then choose the install action when ready. Keep the Runner open while download, verification, dependency preparation, backup, migration and restart complete. Table connections are interrupted during the change; the page reloads after the expected version is confirmed. The bell is informational; it does not automatically authorize an installation. Installed release notes remain available offline. Direct ASGI deployments require their operator's update procedure rather than assuming the local Runner workflow applies. Manual replacement and recovery Stop the Runner, preserve .env , configured data/media, local extensions and recovery state, replace application files with the verified full release and rerun the platform installer. Updates to a reissued ZIP with the same version need manual installation because the updater compares versions. If recovery fails, keep transaction and backup directories and inspect diagnostics. Do not delete them or restore old code over a newer migrated database. Restore matching code, database and media together. Pending Blueprint Delay/Timer jobs are excluded from exports, snapshots and copies but included in a full database backup. A restored database may resume expired work at startup. When inspecting a recovery copy, the operator can disable its automation worker until they intentionally resume it.

title: Learn to build modules and systems
summary: Choose what you want to build and follow it from the first file to a working tabletop feature.
text: Choose the outcome you want to deliver Use the complete capability map (docs:tutorial-capability-map) to locate every method, operation, surface and Map Builder family. I want to build Tutorial What I can test --- --- --- My first module Create, install and update a module from scratch (docs:tutorial-first-module) Table button, authorized read and native modal A journal tool How to create a journal module (docs:tutorial-journal-module) Create a journal and append a section from module UI An action in an existing sheet How to create a module that acts on a sheet (docs:tutorial-sheet-module) Edit a name while preserving sheet data and token snapshots A module-created library How to create a compendium module (docs:tutorial-compendium-module) Create a pack, capture content, read an entry and import a copy Content shipped with my system How to include compendiums in a system (docs:tutorial-system-compendiums) Install one ZIP with a system, JSON files and three original packs Start with the first tutorial if you have never installed your own module. The table above supplies entry points. The full catalog below also covers actors, items, scenes, tokens, combat, cards, audio, chat/dice, quests, roll tables, files, persistence, translation, windows and server code. Every guide provides files, adaptation points, installation, activation and observable results. Use a development campaign and original content. Every project and its recipes - All extension capabilities and where to implement them (docs:tutorial-capability-map): An explicit method-by-method map to projects, local helpers, surfaces, server integrations and release limits. - How to create a complete original system package (docs:tutorial-complete-system): One installable ZIP with working actor/token sheets, item types, stored initiative and three original compendium packs. - How to create a journal module (docs:tutorial-journal-module): Build, install and run a normal module that creates private journals and appends saved GM session drafts. - Create a journal from a module, from scratch (docs:tutorial-create-journal): Use the public create operation from a table.interface form and open the resulting private document. - How to create a module that acts on a sheet (docs:tutorial-sheet-module): Start with an empty folder and ship a working rename action on existing actor and token sheets. - How to build and replace a complete system sheet (docs:tutorial-system-sheet): Use the working Example Expedition package, install it, create actors and verify linked and independent tokens. - How to create a compendium module (docs:tutorial-compendium-module): Build the complete package from an empty directory, install it and verify its original content. - How to include compendiums in a system (docs:tutorial-system-compendiums): Build the complete package from an empty directory, install it and verify its original content. - How to create a scene tools module (docs:tutorial-maps): Build a working module to inspect scene layers, edit metadata, manage folders, draw a native door and broadcast a test scene. - How to create a token tools module (docs:tutorial-tokens): Place, move, duplicate, configure and remove tokens; control native vision/visibility and timed conditions. - How to create a combat tools module (docs:tutorial-combat): Build a working encounter laboratory covering participants, initiative, order, flags, turns, rounds and cleanup. - How to build item and inventory tools (docs:tutorial-items): Create, organize, duplicate, share and edit original items with native revisions and permissions. - How to build deck and card tools (docs:tutorial-cards): Create reusable deck definitions, draw, reveal, move, transfer and recover cards with real ownership. - How to build scene audio and soundtrack tools (docs:tutorial-audio): Configure native tracks, playlists, spatial sources, scene voices and timed scores with the correct revisions. - How to build chat, dice and ready-check tools (docs:tutorial-chat-dice): Create a working module that sends messages, publishes rolls, moderates chat, searches documents and updates readiness. - How to create quest automation and quest-board actions (docs:tutorial-quests): Create and read a real quest, advance objectives, assign actors and manage every board relationship. - How to create, draw and reset weighted roll tables (docs:tutorial-roll-tables): Build an original journal roll table, edit a weight without losing data and publish native draws with or without replacement. - How to create, organize and share journal documents (docs:tutorial-journal-management): Build native rich diaries, preserve pages when editing, organize folder trees and control access and presentations. - Build an actor-directory module (docs:tutorial-actors): Create, organize, rename and authorize actors using system-owned types. - Persist module settings safely (docs:tutorial-storage): Implement personal, shared and browser-local JSON with revisions and cleanup. - Upload and use module and campaign files (docs:tutorial-assets): Use File/Blob, actor images, card assets, native file providers and downloads. - Translate a module and react to changes (docs:tutorial-localization-events): Read package files, format translated UI and subscribe without leaking listeners. - Maintain a module using the original host.call SDK (docs:tutorial-sdk-operations): Concrete actor/token DTOs, opaque revisions and the remaining multipart/local operations. - Build Customize forms and native module windows (docs:tutorial-customize-ui): A complete personal settings form with migration, CAS, translations, modal lifecycle and preferences mounting. - Create a trusted Django integration and server hooks (docs:tutorial-server-integration): Complete Python app with authenticated routes, native mutations and after-commit signals. - How to create and activate an installation language package (docs:tutorial-language-package): Package six original interface strings, install globally, choose a personal locale and verify English fallback. - How to version, sign and distribute a module (docs:tutorial-publish-module): Prepare immutable ZIP releases, verify Ed25519 catalog records and understand installation, activation and revocation. Before choosing a “module type” Journal, sheet and compendium describe what your module does. They are not values for a manifest kind field. A journal module is a regular package registering journal.sheet and calling journals. A sheet action registers actor.sheet and token.sheet. A library can be created as campaign content through the API. A system catalog declares system and content.compendiums in the same manifest. Decision Choice --- --- Add a button or panel mode: augment, keeping the existing UI Draw your system's own sheet mode: replace with system-owned types, as in the sample system (docs:example-package-system) Save journal/actor data The public document API with the revision you read Save a module preference Module storage, without overwriting the document Ship a catalog with a system Physical ZIP files and content.compendiums The complete development cycle 1. Define an observable action, such as “clicking the button creates a section.” Choose a resource supported by the 0.3.0 contract. 2. Create a folder containing manifest.json, a JavaScript entry, styles and a license. The manifest names files; it does not implement the action. 3. Implement start/register/stop. Use the mount's root and api, and register the surface where the tool should appear. 4. Build a ZIP with the manifest at its root. The installation owner installs it on a development host. 5. The GM activates the exact version for the table. A system also needs to be selected as the campaign system. 6. Open the window or directory receiving the mount. Execute the action and inspect persisted data rather than relying on a success message. 7. Test read access, conflicts, cancellation and player behavior. Installed versions are immutable: increase the package version before installing changed bytes. When to use the reference Tutorials teach the full flow. Use Examples by kind (docs:examples-index) to vary a contract and the module reference (docs:modules) for limits and signatures. The API guide (docs:api) covers methods. When an idea cannot be implemented on the requested release, explain that limitation before inventing an endpoint or requiring a host upgrade. How to use AI to start a module text I want to build observable action on Gravewright 0.3.0. Start from tutorial link and its ZIP. Before coding, identify the mounting surface, the API that saves the resource, and package installation/activation. Deliver the complete tree, every file, installation steps and tests with observable results. Preserve revisions, permissions, private sections and snapshots. Do not invent a manifest kind or an unavailable API.

title: Create, install and update your first module
summary: From an empty folder to a table button, with complete files, installation, activation and a second version.
text: What you will build A browser module named Example campaign summary. It adds a Campaign summary button to the table, reads actors the caller may open and displays their count in a native modal. The result is a ZIP installed through the UI. You do not need to modify VTT source, install an npm SDK or configure a Python server for this module. You need a Gravewright 0.3.0 development installation, installation-owner access to install code and a GM account in a test campaign. Use a text editor and Python in your terminal to write and package files. If your current installation contains valuable campaigns, prepare another development installation. Installation owner and campaign GM are different permissions. 1. Start with an empty folder Create campaign-summary in your development work area. Save these four files as UTF-8. Check extensions: main.mjs.txt is not main.mjs. You may also download the finished project (../../assets/examples/packages/browser/browser-source.zip), extract it and compare each file. text campaign-summary/ manifest.json main.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Do not put a database, .env, credentials or campaign files here. The ZIP needs only module files. The following source matches the download. 2. Declare the package in manifest.json json { "id": "example.campaign-summary", "name": "Example campaign summary", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "description": "Adds an authorized read-only summary in a native modal.", "author": "Gravewright documentation examples", "license": "GPL-3.0-only", "entry": "main.mjs" } id identifies the package across versions. name is displayed to the owner and GM. version identifies immutable bytes. entry is a path inside the ZIP. sdk describes the module contract rather than the VTT release. Do not add kind: journal or type: compendium: behavior comes from code and supported manifest blocks. 3. Write main.mjs javascript export default { start({styles}) { styles.use('styles.css'); }, register({register}) { register('table.interface', ({root, api, signal, onDispose}) = { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const panel=doc.createElement('section'); panel.className='example-panel'; const button=doc.createElement('button'); button.type='button'; button.textContent='Campaign summary'; const status=doc.createElement('p'); status.setAttribute('role','status'); panel.append(button,status); root.append(panel); let modal; button.addEventListener('click', async () = { button.disabled=true; try { const actors=await api.actors.list({}, {signal}); if(signal.aborted) return; if(modal) await modal.close(); if(signal.aborted) return; const content=doc.createElement('section'); content.setAttribute('role','dialog'); content.setAttribute('aria-modal','true'); content.setAttribute('aria-label','Campaign summary'); const text=doc.createElement('p'); text.textContent='Readable actors: '+actors.filter(actor= actor.canOpen).length; const close=doc.createElement('button'); close.type='button';close.textContent='Close'; content.append(text,close); modal=api.ui.openModal(content); close.addEventListener('click',()= void modal.close(),{signal}); status.textContent='Summary loaded.'; } catch(error) { if(!signal.aborted) status.textContent=error.code 'unavailable'; } finally { if(!signal.aborted) button.disabled=false; } },{signal}); onDispose(()= {panel.remove();}); }); }, stop() {} }; start loads styles once per activation. register declares an extension for table.interface. Its callback runs when the table offers that surface and receives an owned root, a mount-scoped api and a cancellation signal. Reading happens on click. actors.list returns the authorized collection; canOpen distinguishes readable documents from listing-only entries. api.ui.openModal uses the VTT modal infrastructure. The example does not create an HTML dialog element or call alert. The signal prevents a late read from opening a window after deactivation. onDispose removes the panel; signal-bound listeners are cancelled with the mount. 4. Write styles.css and copy the license css .gw-module-root .example-panel { padding: var(--space-4, 16px); font-size: 14px; } .gw-module-root .example-panel label { display: block; margin-bottom: var(--space-3, 12px); } .gw-module-root .example-panel button { margin-right: var(--space-2, 8px); } .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.campaign-summary" .example-panel { position: fixed; left: 16px; bottom: 112px; z-index: 20; max-width: min(360px, calc(100vw - 32px)); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-md); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); pointer-events: auto; } The data-module-id selector scopes table positioning to this package. Its panel appears above the table and below native windows while leaving controls available. Download the complete LICENSE.txt (../../assets/examples/packages/browser/LICENSE.txt) into the folder with that exact name. Preserve the notice when reusing this example. The sample uses GPL-3.0-only; choose the appropriate license for a different original module and keep its manifest and license file consistent. Do not distribute just a license label without its text. 5. Build and inspect the ZIP In PowerShell, starting in the folder containing campaign-summary: powershell Set-Location .\campaign-summary python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ..\campaign-summary-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ..\campaign-summary-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS: sh cd campaign-summary python3 -m json.tool manifest.json python3 -m zipfile -c ../campaign-summary-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python3 -m zipfile -l ../campaign-summary-1.0.0.zip json.tool must finish without errors. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root beside main.mjs. campaign-summary/manifest.json means you zipped the folder instead of its contents. Close the archive before installation. 6. Install as the installation owner 1. Enter Inside and open Modules. 2. Select Install module, then Install from ZIP. 3. Choose campaign-summary-1.0.0.zip in ZIP file and press Install. 4. Wait for Example campaign summary 1.0.0 to appear. Campaign activation is still required. Local upload is the development path for owner-reviewed code. Marketplace publication uses its separate signed-catalog workflow. Installing a ZIP does not enable it on every table. 7. Activate as GM and inspect the result 1. Open a test campaign as GM. Open the Gravewright menu, select Extensions, then Table modules. Find Example campaign summary 1.0.0 and click Activate. 2. Return to the table. Campaign summary appears near the lower-left corner. 3. Create an actor through the native directory, give the caller appropriate access and click the button. With one readable actor, the modal displays Readable actors: 1; the count depends on campaign data. 4. Close using Close or Escape. Reopen, then deactivate the module. Its button disappears while actors remain in the campaign. If the campaign has no system declaring actor types, first test a zero count or select an appropriate system in your development campaign. Do not invent an actor type just to load this module. 8. Make a change and install version 1.0.1 In main.mjs, change the button text from Campaign summary to Campaign notebook. In manifest.json, change version from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 while keeping id. Build another ZIP containing the same four files, named campaign-summary-1.0.1.zip, then install it. Activate 1.0.1 on the table and check its new text and action. Installing a newer version does not automatically change a table's selection. Do not modify installed package files or reinstall changed bytes as 1.0.0: the installer may reject that with conflict. There is no source-folder hot reload. The cycle is edit, increment version, package, install and activate. 9. Locate the failing stage Symptom Check --- --- ZIP rejected Root layout, valid JSON, existing entry, license and numeric version conflict during installation Same id/version already has different bytes; install 1.0.1 Installed but no button GM account, exact table activation and main.mjs import errors Button appears but read fails Caller access, network and the panel's error.code Player sees a different count Actor permissions; each account reads its authorized collection Old label remains Active version, open tabs and reload after selecting the new release Open browser developer tools and inspect Console and Network while reproducing the action. Never paste session cookies or tokens into an issue. The entry must be a valid ES module; removing export default prevents loading. 10. Choose your next implementation - Create a journal module (docs:tutorial-journal-module): two mounts, document creation and an action in an open journal. - Act on a sheet (docs:tutorial-sheet-module): edit generic data without losing existing fields. - Create a compendium module (docs:tutorial-compendium-module): create campaign content and capture snapshots. - Ship compendiums with a system (docs:tutorial-system-compendiums): JSON files and manifest in one ZIP. How to use AI to adapt this project text Start from the tutorial campaign-summary ZIP on Gravewright 0.3.0. Replace its summary with action . Explain whether table.interface remains appropriate or another mount is needed. Deliver complete main.mjs, manifest.json and CSS. Preserve the scoped API, signal, onDispose and native modal. Increment the package version and explain testing after installation/activation, including console diagnostics.

title: All extension capabilities and where to implement them
summary: An explicit method-by-method map to projects, local helpers, surfaces, server integrations and release limits.
text: How to use this map This index crosses public contracts from host 0.3.3, revision cc4fd08, with implementation projects. It covers 213 domain API methods , 17 original SDK operations , 13 surfaces and lifecycle helpers. Each method links to an executable tutorial or the canonical guide covering its contract, permissions and examples. Older projects retain their declared host version; APIs added in 0.3.2 use the current reference rather than being attributed retroactively to older projects. Begin with the outcome you want to build (docs:tutorial-index). Use this table to locate a specific capability. A recipe can combine create/configure/read/remove because they are parts of one feature. Actions execute on click and destructive operations are identified. Use a disposable installation/campaign. They may coalesce invalidations and perform initial/reconnect reads. They are not exactly-once automation triggers. Dispose each subscription. Map Builder and visual automation All four door/lever/torch/region owners, execution/data connections and 49 node.type values have complete graphs, JSON and editor steps (docs:examples-blueprints). The node catalog (docs:example-blueprint-nodes) explains targets, resources and effects. shaderControl requires host 0.3.3 and an existing shader; older recipes keep their stated minimum versions. Use native Test behavior/playtest before live application. These graphs are development documents, not a browser API for importing arbitrary JSON or a new manifest field. The scene tutorial (docs:tutorial-maps) implements public layer/object operations. Adding new kinds or editor ports requires a core contribution and tests; 0.3.3 does not promise a plugin API for arbitrary node-type registration. Server integrations and release boundaries The Django integration (docs:tutorial-server-integration) implements Context.from_request, public commands, authenticated/CSRF routes and after-commit hooks. Python facades api.actors/tokens/maps/journals/items/combat/cards/audio/compendiums/clocks/clues/mindmaps/resources/chat/dice/table/events have signatures in the reference (docs:api python-interface). Context retains IDs rather than cached authority, and each service checks access. Account/admin/package/campaign management are global application adapters rather than methods on a mount’s api; see adapter reference (docs:api account-campaign-owner-and-module-adapters) for operator tools. There is no maps.create domain method. The 0.3.2 API adds native file adapters, including audio.upload and maps.upload/importUniversalVtt; pass a real File through the documented file API. Older tutorials may prepare scenes and files through the native interface to retain their declared compatibility. Browser modules do not receive arbitrary SQL/Python execution, implicit GM powers, campaign switching through foreign UUIDs or hidden-data bypasses. system.combat supports declarative initiative. Existing Python providers are trusted server code, not permission to distribute a new RPG as a system plus separate Server Rules companion. Explain unsupported requirements while preserving the requested host version. Maintain coverage when the host changes This map uses a versioned frontend.json/registry.json snapshot in extension-contracts.json. For a host upgrade, compare actual source files/revisions, update projects and run their recipes against real services. Matching names alone does not prove payload, permission, visual or transaction behavior. Repeat mutation/snapshot tests in new fixtures.

title: How to create a complete original system package
summary: One installable ZIP with working actor/token sheets, item types, stored initiative and three original compendium packs.
text: What the single system ZIP provides Build Complete Example Expedition on Gravewright 0.3.0 . This is a functional original system package: complete character/NPC sheet replacements on actor.sheet and token.sheet, a saved stamina field, gear/spell item types, native initiative and three installed compendium packs. No separately installed module or server-rules companion is required. It is a small teaching system, not a complete implementation of a published RPG. The sheet code is reused from the working editable system package (docs:example-package-system), and the original JSON is derived from installed system compendiums (docs:tutorial-system-compendiums). This guide prints every functional file, so you can build from an empty folder. The package is GPL-3.0-only; the MIT notices for the derived original collection remain intact. 1. Create the directory and understand the contract Download the complete system source ZIP (../../assets/tutorials/complete-expedition/complete-expedition-source.zip) text complete-expedition/ manifest.json main.mjs styles.css compendiums/expedition.json LICENSE.txt MIT-COMPENDIUM.txt THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt README.md Create complete-expedition and its compendiums subdirectory. Save the exact files in section 5 as UTF-8. Copy LICENSE.txt (../../assets/tutorials/complete-expedition/LICENSE.txt) unchanged from the ZIP. Do not replace that GPL license with the separate MIT notice. No npm build, Python app or host source modification is required. The manifest ID example.complete-expedition is also the systemId of every catalog entry. character and npc must match system.actorTypes; gear and spell must match system.itemTypes. content.compendiums names the physical JSON file. The three permitted installed pack types are actor_pack, item_pack and spell_pack; the spell pack follows item import semantics, without adding spell rules to the core. 2. Package, install and create the campaign From the source folder, use an existing Python interpreter and explicitly list the package files. On POSIX replace python with python3 or the path to the host virtual environment. Keep the output ZIP outside the source folder. powershell Set-Location -LiteralPath ./complete-expedition python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m json.tool compendiums/expedition.json python -m zipfile -c ../complete-expedition-source.zip manifest.json main.mjs styles.css compendiums/expedition.json LICENSE.txt MIT-COMPENDIUM.txt THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt README.md python -m zipfile -l ../complete-expedition-source.zip 1. As installation owner, open Inside → Systems → Install system → Install from ZIP , review and select complete-expedition-source.zip, then click Install . Use Systems, because this manifest declares system. Local upload needs explicit trust but no remote catalog signature. 2. Create a new disposable campaign and choose Complete Example Expedition as its system. Enter the table as GM and verify the exact 1.0.0 version in Gravewright → Extensions → Table modules . Installing a system does not switch existing campaigns automatically. 3. In Actors, create one Character and one NPC, then open both sheets. You should see the real Example Expedition sheet form with Stamina, Save and Reload server value. Native window controls remain supplied by the host. 3. Import and edit the original content Open Compendiums . Under Complete Expedition Library , inspect Scouts , Equipment and Signals . As GM, read then import Harbor Scout, Signal Rope and Blue Glow. The entry bodies belong to this system; the API returns those installed collection documents, not an invented envelope with a required kind field. Import creates campaign copies only when requested. Reopening the campaign does not silently import duplicates. Open the imported Harbor Scout actor. Its stored data starts with stamina 8, role Watch keeper and combat.initiative 3. Change Stamina to 17, click Save, close and reopen. The value must remain 17; role and combat must still be present. The sheet copies the existing data and changes only stamina, sending both version and sheetVersion read from the same sheet. Test another session with a stale version; the form reloads on conflict and asks for a review rather than forcing the write. Create linked and independent tokens for the imported actor. A linked token saves actor data. An independent token uses its own tokenId snapshot and sheetVersion. Changing its stamina must leave the original actor unchanged. With a read-only player, editing and saving are disabled; verify a direct attempted write is also rejected by the server. The gear and spell are original item data, not implemented equipment or spell automation. This package reuses the host item interface and does not replace item.sheet with an incomplete custom editor. You may add a complete package-owned item editor later using the item surface example (docs:example-surface-item-sheet) after checking the target API. 4. Roll initiative with the actual stored modifier Open a scene, add Harbor Scout or its token to the native initiative tracker and use Roll initiative . The package provides formula 1d20+@combat.initiative , so this imported actor rolls 1d20+3 , a value from 4 through 23. The core resolves this numeric path from the actor or independent snapshot and evaluates the native dice expression. No system-specific calculation derives it from another attribute. A freshly created actor has no catalog data unless you import it. A missing combat.initiative path resolves to 0, so that actor rolls 1d20. Its form displays stamina 10 as an initial UI default until the user saves. The form does not expose initiative editing; to add that field, implement its input, validation and revision-preserving save inside this package. manualInput number describes numeric manual initiative when applicable; the configured formula selects the native roll input. There is no required external provider. 5. Complete package files manifest.json json { "id": "example.complete-expedition", "name": "Complete Example Expedition", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "description": "One original system with editable actor/token sheets, initiative and three installed content packs.", "author": "Gravewright documentation examples", "license": "GPL-3.0-only", "entry": "main.mjs", "system": { "actorTypes": { "id": "character", "label": "Character" }, { "id": "npc", "label": "NPC" } , "itemTypes": { "id": "gear", "label": "Gear" }, { "id": "spell", "label": "Spell" } , "combat": { "formula": "1d20+@combat.initiative", "manualInput": "number", "showRoll": true } }, "content": { "compendiums": "compendiums/expedition.json" } } main.mjs javascript export default { start({styles}) { styles.use('styles.css'); }, register({register}) { const sheet={ mode:'replace',types: 'character','npc' , async mount({root,context,api,signal,onDispose}) { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const form=doc.createElement('form');form.className='example-panel'; form.setAttribute('aria-label','Example Expedition sheet'); const title=doc.createElement('h2'); const label=doc.createElement('label');label.textContent='Stamina (0–100)'; const input=doc.createElement('input');input.type='number';input.min='0';input.max='100'; label.append(input); const saveButton=doc.createElement('button');saveButton.type='submit';saveButton.textContent='Save'; const reloadButton=doc.createElement('button');reloadButton.type='button';reloadButton.textContent='Reload server value'; input.disabled=true;saveButton.disabled=true;reloadButton.disabled=true; const status=doc.createElement('p');status.setAttribute('role','status'); form.append(title,label,saveButton,reloadButton,status);root.append(form); let current,dirty=false,pending; const token=context.tokenId ? {tokenId:context.tokenId} : {}; async function load() { input.disabled=true;saveButton.disabled=true;reloadButton.disabled=true; try { const sheet=await api.actors.sheet(context.actorId,token,{signal}); if(signal.aborted) return; current=sheet;title.textContent=sheet.name; input.value=String(sheet.data.stamina ?? 10); input.disabled=!sheet.canEdit;saveButton.disabled=!sheet.canEdit; dirty=false; } finally { if(!signal.aborted) reloadButton.disabled=false; } } function save() { if(pending) return pending; if(!dirty !current?.canEdit) return Promise.resolve(); const stamina=Number(input.value); if(input.value.trim()==='' !Number.isInteger(stamina) stamina<0 stamina 100) { status.textContent='Enter an integer from 0 to 100.'; return Promise.reject(new Error('Invalid stamina')); } const payload={actorId:context.actorId,name:current.name,version:current.version, sheetVersion:current.sheetVersion,data:{...current.data,stamina}, ...(current.tokenId ? {tokenId:current.tokenId} : {})}; const requestId=crypto.randomUUID(); input.disabled=true;saveButton.disabled=true;reloadButton.disabled=true; pending=(async()= { try { await api.actors.saveSheet(payload,{requestId,signal}); if(signal.aborted) return; await load();status.textContent='Saved.'; } catch(error) { if(!signal.aborted) { if(error.code==='conflict') { await load(); status.textContent='Conflict: server value loaded. Review it before editing again.'; } else status.textContent=error.code 'Save failed. Reload before retrying.'; } throw error; } finally { pending=undefined; if(!signal.aborted){input.disabled=!current?.canEdit;saveButton.disabled=!current?.canEdit;reloadButton.disabled=false;} } })(); return pending; } input.addEventListener('input',()= {dirty=true;},{signal}); form.addEventListener('submit',event= {event.preventDefault();void save().catch(()= {});},{signal}); reloadButton.addEventListener('click',()= { void load().then(()= {if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent='Server value loaded.';}) .catch(error= {if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent=error.code 'unavailable';}); },{signal}); root.closest('.gw-window')?.addEventListener('gravewright:sheet-flush',event= { if(pending dirty) event.detail.waitUntil(save()); },{signal}); onDispose(()= form.remove()); await load(); } }; register('actor.sheet',sheet); register('token.sheet',sheet); }, stop() {} }; styles.css css .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.complete-expedition" .example-panel { box-sizing: border-box; padding: var(--space-4); color: var(--text); background: var(--surface); font: 14px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; } .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.complete-expedition" .example-panel h2 { font-size: 18px; margin: var(--space-0) var(--space-0) var(--space-3); } .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.complete-expedition" .example-panel label { display: block; margin-bottom: var(--space-3); } .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.complete-expedition" .example-panel input { display: block; title: How to create a journal module
summary: Build, install and run a normal module that creates private journals and appends saved GM session drafts.
text: What you will build A normal browser module for Gravewright 0.3.0 with two working actions: create a private journal from the table, then append a session draft to an existing journal. The sheet action is Add session section . It writes a Session notes page under Sessions , containing original draft text with audience gm . It preserves the existing authored text. The package uses public api.journals.state , create and update . It imports no private host code and requires no Django app. Both surfaces use mode: augment , retaining the native editor. 1. Start with the files Use a disposable development installation of host0.3.0, an installation-owner account for installation and a GM account in a campaign. You need a text editor and the project's prepared Python environment. There are no npm dependencies or frontend build. Create a session-journal folder under data/ or another explicitly chosen development directory. Save the five files as UTF-8. text session-journal/ manifest.json main.js styles.css messages.json LICENSE.txt Download complete project (../../assets/tutorials/session-journal/session-journal-source.zip) - manifest.json (../../assets/tutorials/session-journal/manifest.json) - main.js (../../assets/tutorials/session-journal/main.js) - styles.css (../../assets/tutorials/session-journal/styles.css) - messages.json (../../assets/tutorials/session-journal/messages.json) - LICENSE.txt (../../assets/tutorials/session-journal/LICENSE.txt) 2. Understand the different types Concept This example Meaning --- --- --- Package type browser module Manifest has entry and no system/django/locales; there is no manifest kind: journal Surfaces table.interface and journal.sheet Where the module mounts Document type diary Native Journal; the other types are quest, quest_board and roll_table Page kind text New section contains text; image/pdf pages have different resource needs Page audience gm Draft page is omitted from player projections Do not change an existing document's type to fit this example. Quests and roll tables require their own data contracts. The tool explicitly refuses those types. 3. Package the project From the directory containing the five files, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json Compress-Archive -LiteralPath manifest.json,main.js,styles.css,messages.json,LICENSE.txt -DestinationPath ../session-journal-1.0.0.zip python -m zipfile -l ../session-journal-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS: sh python3 -m json.tool manifest.json python3 -m zipfile -c ../session-journal-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.js styles.css messages.json LICENSE.txt python3 -m zipfile -l ../session-journal-1.0.0.zip The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root beside main.js. This is an unsigned local source package. You can instead review and install the downloadable source ZIP. Do not add an extra outer directory. 4. Install as owner and activate as GM 1. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP . 2. Select session-journal-1.0.0.zip and click Install . Local installation is the owner's explicit trust decision. 3. Open the campaign as GM. Select the table's Gravewright button → Extensions , then Activate version 1.0.0 of Session notebook . Installation alone does not activate a campaign module. 4. Close Extensions. The bottom-left panel contains Journal title and Create session journal . 5. When changing the source later, increment to 1.0.1 , build/install a new ZIP and activate that version. Installed releases are immutable; do not edit their extracted files. Your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) explains each installation screen. 5. Create and open a journal from scratch 1. Keep the default title Session notebook and click Create session journal once. It sends {title, journal_type: "diary", folder_id: null} to create with a fresh operation UUID. 2. Wait for confirmation. Open Journals at the table and open Session notebook . The host creates an empty private journal at the directory root. 3. Native creation does not consume a module data field. The next sheet action writes the session draft. Do not invent a create parameter for initial content. If creation is not confirmed, inspect Journals before clicking again. Cancellation or a lost response cannot undo a write already committed by the server. 6. Act on an existing journal 1. In the opened journal, find the added Session notebook panel. The native editor remains available. 2. If you were editing, wait for the native Saved indicator first. The public module API does not supply a command to flush another editor's local draft. 3. Click Add session section . It reads a current server projection, preserves title, visibility, introduction, cover, pages and GM documents, then appends a page. 4. In the native index, open Sessions → Session notes . It reads: Draft: record the date, discoveries, decisions and loose ends from this session. 5. The page is GM-only. Edit it using the native editor. To share it, deliberately choose the native Make public option and suitable journal permissions. The module does not automatically publish or present content. 6. Close/reopen to verify persistence. A second click after the first operation finishes creates another independent page with a fresh ID. Overlapping clicks in one mount are blocked. 7. Understand writes and conflicts journals.update takes journal_id , title , visibility , the integer version read from the server and the complete data object. For diary, data contains content , cover , sections and gm . Do not use the entire projection as data: its field names differ, including content_doc and cover_image. Each page's can_edit is projection metadata and is removed before saving. This example writes only from a GM projection because a player's filtered projection is incomplete. The UI checks context.role, and each write separately verifies state.is_gm . The server still checks the authenticated member, campaign, permissions and revision. A player with journal editing rights continues to use the native editor. If another window saves between reading and writing, update returns conflict . The module rereads current state, blocks Add and requests Review latest journal . Review native content and resolve local drafts before confirming the review. It never automatically retries or silently replaces version. Each later approved click is a fresh logical operation with a new UUID. 8. Complete source start loads CSS and catalogs through the official translation API. register synchronously declares both surfaces. Every mount owns its state; every read/write receives signal. Closing or deactivating aborts the mount, removes its listeners and disposes its panel. Labels support en, pt-BR and es; original draft titles/text remain unchanged across locales. manifest.json json { "id": "example.session-notebook", "name": "Session notebook", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.js", "description": "Create private journals and append GM-only session drafts while preserving existing journal content.", "author": "Gravewright documentation examples", "license": "MIT" } main.js javascript // Original tutorial. MIT. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0, SDK 1.x. const error = key = Object.assign(new Error(key), { tutorialKey: key }); const alive = signal = !signal.aborted; function elements({ root, signal, onDispose, api }, kind) { const el = (tag, text) = { const node = root.ownerDocument.createElement(tag); if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text; return node; }; const t = (key, params) = api.i18n.t(key, params); const panel = el('section'); panel.className = 'gw-session-tools gw-session-tools--' + kind; const heading = el('h3', t('Session notebook')); const status = el('p'); status.setAttribute('role', 'status'); status.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite'); panel.append(heading); root.append(panel); onDispose(() = panel.remove()); const report = problem = { if (!alive(signal)) return; status.textContent = problem.tutorialKey ? t(problem.tutorialKey) : t('Request failed: {code}. Review the journal before trying again.', { code: problem.code 'unavailable' }); }; return { el, t, panel, status, report }; } async function journalSnapshot(api, signal, journalId) { const snapshot = await api.journals.state({}, { signal }); if (!alive(signal)) return null; // Only the server's GM projection contains all pages, hidden blocks and GM docs. if (snapshot.is_gm !== true) throw error('This tool requires a GM.'); const view = snapshot.journals.find(row = row.id === journalId); if (!view view.can_open === false) throw error('Journal is unavailable.'); if (view.type !== 'diary') throw error('This tool only edits Journal documents (diary).'); if (!view.can_edit) throw error('This journal is read-only.'); } return view; } function appendPayload(view) { if (view.sections.length = 64) throw error('This journal already has 64 pages.'); const last = Math.max(0, ...view.sections.map(page = Number(page.sortOrder) 0)); const sections = view.sections.map(({ can_edit, ...section }) = structuredClone(section)); return { journal_id: view.id, title: view.title, visibility: view.visibility, version: view.version, data: { content: structuredClone(view.content_doc), cover: structuredClone(view.cover_image), sections: ...sections, page , gm: structuredClone(view.diary.gm) } }; const label = el('label', t('Journal title')); const input = el('input'); input.type = 'text'; input.required = true; input.maxLength = 120; input.value = 'Session notebook'; const create = el('button', t('Create session journal')); create.type = 'submit'; label.append(input); form.append(label, create); panel.append(form, status); let busy = false; form.addEventListener('submit', async event = { event.preventDefault(); if (busy !alive(signal)) return; const title = input.value.trim(); if (!title title.length 120) { report(error('Enter a title from 1 to 120 characters.')); return; } busy = true; create.disabled = true; input.disabled = true; status.textContent = t('Creating journal...'); try { const snapshot = await api.journals.state({}, { signal }); if (!alive(signal)) return; if (snapshot.is_gm !== true) throw error('This tool requires a GM.'); const result = await api.journals.create({ title, journal_type: 'diary', folder_id: null }, { requestId: crypto.randomUUID(), signal }); if (!alive(signal)) return; status.textContent = t('Created "{title}". Open it in Journals, then add a session section.', { title }); status.dataset.journalId = result.journal_id; } catch (problem) { report(problem); } finally { if (alive(signal)) { busy = false; create.disabled = false; input.disabled = false; } } }, { signal }); } async function mountAppend(block) { const { context, api, signal } = block; if (context.role !== 'gm' !alive(signal)) return; const { el, t, panel, status, report } = elements(block, 'journal'); const add = el('button', t('Add session section')); const review = el('button', t('Review latest journal')); add.type = review.type = 'button'; add.disabled = review.disabled = true; const hint = el('p', t('Save pending native edits first. New session drafts are GM-only.')); panel.append(hint, add, review, status); let busy = false, ready = false, needsReview = false; const controls = () = { if (!alive(signal)) return; add.disabled = busy !ready needsReview; review.disabled = busy; }; async function refresh() { if (busy !alive(signal)) return; busy = true; ready = false; controls(); try { const view = await journalSnapshot(api, signal, context.journalId); if (!view !alive(signal)) return; ready = view.sections.length < 64; needsReview = false; status.textContent = t('Latest saved version: {version}. Pages: {count}.', { version: view.version, count: view.sections.length }); if (!ready) report(error('This journal already has 64 pages.')); } catch (problem) { report(problem); } finally { if (alive(signal)) { busy = false; controls(); } } } review.addEventListener('click', () = void refresh(), { signal }); add.addEventListener('click', async () = { if (busy !ready needsReview !alive(signal)) return; busy = true; controls(); status.textContent = t('Saving session section...'); try { const view = await journalSnapshot(api, signal, context.journalId); if (!view !alive(signal)) return; const payload = appendPayload(view); await api.journals.update(payload, { requestId: crypto.randomUUID(), signal }); if (!alive(signal)) return; ready = payload.data.sections.length < 64; status.textContent = t('Added GM-only "Session notes". Open it under Sessions in the native journal.'); } catch (problem) { if (!alive(signal)) return; needsReview = true; if (problem.code === 'conflict') { try { const latest = await journalSnapshot(api, signal, context.journalId); if (!latest !alive(signal)) return; ready = latest.sections.length < 64; status.textContent = t('Conflict: server version {version} loaded. Review native content, then choose Review latest journal. No automatic retry.', { version: latest.version }); } catch (refreshProblem) { ready = false; report(refreshProblem); } } else report(problem); } finally { if (alive(signal)) { busy = false; controls(); } } }, { signal }); await refresh(); } export default { async start({ api, assets, styles, signal }) { styles.use('styles.css'); const messages = await assets.json('messages.json'); if (!alive(signal)) return; api.i18n.register(messages); }, register({ register }) { register('table.interface', { mode: 'augment', mount: mountCreate }); register('journal.sheet', { mode: 'augment', mount: mountAppend }); }, stop() {} }; title: Create a journal from a module, from scratch
summary: Use the public create operation from a table.interface form and open the resulting private document.
text: Create a journal through a normal module Use the same Session notebook package without installing a second module. Start at the table with no journal open and create a persistent private document. Follow the complete journal module tutorial (docs:tutorial-journal-module) for the tree, source, ZIP, installation and activation. Run it 1. Download the complete package (../../assets/tutorials/session-journal/session-journal-source.zip), install through Modules as owner and Activate Session notebook1.0.0 under Gravewright → Extensions as GM. 2. Enter Lighthouse expedition in Journal title , then click Create session journal . 3. Wait for confirmation and open Journals . Lighthouse expedition appears at the root, empty and private. 4. Open it and choose Add session section to write the original first draft. Edit using the native editor and reopen the journal. The concrete public call This is the core of mountCreate, using api/context/signal supplied by the mount. The full package adds form validation, translations and duplicate-submit prevention. javascript const state = await api.journals.state({}, { signal }); if (signal.aborted) return; if (context.role !== "gm" state.is_gm !== true) throw new Error("GM required"); const result = await api.journals.create({ title: "Lighthouse expedition", journal_type: "diary", folder_id: null }, { requestId: crypto.randomUUID(), signal }); if (signal.aborted) return; // result.journal_id identifies the created document; result.version is its revision. Create does not add a package type named journal or accept initial data in this contract. To add content, read the full GM projection and call update as in the main tutorial. The creating account receives ownership access and the new document starts private. Verify Open a player account and verify the private journal is absent. Click once and confirm one document. Deactivate before the read completes and confirm create is never sent. If the create response is lost, inspect Journals before deciding to create another document. Never reuse the operation UUID for a different journal. How to use AI to change creation text Adapt mountCreate in example.session-notebook to request an original title and an existing folder in Gravewright0.3.0. Verify folder_id and actual server permissions. Preserve the GM check, signal and one UUID per logical operation. Do not add data or invented manifest fields. Deliver complete code and tests for missing folder, another campaign and double submission. Complete tutorial (docs:tutorial-journal-module) · All tutorials (docs:tutorial-index)

title: How to create a module that acts on a sheet
summary: Start with an empty folder and ship a working rename action on existing actor and token sheets.
text: The result you will build Add a Sheet name action form below the existing sheet. It reads the authorized document, enables editing only when canEdit is true, saves a new name and reloads the committed value. It registers both actor.sheet and token.sheet , so this is an action on real documents rather than a disconnected example label. Use a disposable campaign on Gravewright 0.3.0 , SDK 1.x , an owner account to install and a GM account to activate. Any system can use the actor rename. Independent tokens use the host presentation convention data.token.name ; if a system occupies token with a nonobject value, the example refuses that snapshot change. No rulebook content or RPG attribute is added. 1. Create the folder and all five files Download the complete source ZIP (../../assets/tutorials/example.sheet-name/example.sheet-name-source.zip) text example.sheet-name/ manifest.json main.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt README.md Create a folder named example.sheet-name . Save the listings below as UTF-8 files. The package needs no npm, bundler, Python app or server restart. You can also download each original file: manifest.json (../../assets/tutorials/example.sheet-name/manifest.json) · main.mjs (../../assets/tutorials/example.sheet-name/main.mjs) · styles.css (../../assets/tutorials/example.sheet-name/styles.css) · LICENSE.txt (../../assets/tutorials/example.sheet-name/LICENSE.txt) · README.md (../../assets/tutorials/example.sheet-name/README.md) manifest.json json { "id": "example.sheet-name", "name": "Sheet name action", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Rename an actor or its independent token from an existing sheet, preserving data and revisions.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript export async function mountSheetName({root,context,api,signal,onDispose}) { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const t=key= api.i18n.t(key); const el=(tag,text)= {const node=doc.createElement(tag);if(text)node.textContent=text;return node;}; const form=el('form');form.className='tutorial-sheet-name'; form.setAttribute('aria-label',t('Sheet name action')); const title=el('h3',t('Sheet name action')); const label=el('label',t('Sheet name')); const input=el('input');input.type='text';input.maxLength=120;input.required=true;label.append(input); const saveButton=el('button',t('Save name'));saveButton.type='submit'; const reloadButton=el('button',t('Reload server value'));reloadButton.type='button'; const status=el('p');status.setAttribute('role','status');status.setAttribute('aria-live','polite'); form.append(title,label,saveButton,reloadButton,status);root.append(form); input.disabled=!edit;saveButton.disabled=!edit !dirty; reloadButton.disabled=loading !!pending; } function report(error){if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent=error.code error.message 'unavailable';} function reject(message){const error=new Error(message);report(error);return Promise.reject(error);} async function load(){ const ticket=++generation;loading=true;ready=false;controls(); try { const sheet=await api.actors.sheet(context.actorId,token,{signal}); if(signal.aborted ticket!==generation)return; if(typeof sheet.name!=='string' !sheet.data typeof sheet.data!=='object' Array.isArray(sheet.data))throw new Error('invalid_data'); current=sheet;input.value=sheet.name;dirty=false;ready=true; status.textContent=t(sheet.canEdit?'Server value loaded.':'Read-only sheet.'); } finally {if(ticket===generation&&!signal.aborted){loading=false;controls();}} } function save(){ if(pending)return pending; if(!dirty)return Promise.resolve(); if(!ready !current?.canEdit)return reject('permission_denied'); const name=input.value.trim(); if(!name Array.from(name).length 120)return reject(t('Use a name with 1 to 120 characters.')); const data=structuredClone(current.data),snapshot=!!current.tokenId; if(snapshot){ if(current.tokenId!==context.tokenId)return reject('stale_context'); if(data.token!==undefined&&(!data.token typeof data.token!=='object' Array.isArray(data.token)))return reject(t('This system uses an incompatible token field.')); data.token={...(data.token {}),name}; } const payload={actorId:context.actorId,...token,name:snapshot?current.name:name, version:current.version,sheetVersion:current.sheetVersion,data}; const requestId=crypto.randomUUID(); pending=(async()= { try { await api.actors.saveSheet(payload,{requestId,signal}); if(signal.aborted)return; await load(); if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent=t(snapshot?'Saved independent token name.':'Saved actor name.'); } catch(error){ if(!signal.aborted){ if(error.code==='conflict'){ try {await load();if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent=t('Conflict: server value loaded. Review it and edit again.');} catch(refreshError){ready=false;report(refreshError);} } else {ready=false;report(error);} } throw error; } finally {pending=undefined;if(!signal.aborted)controls();} })(); controls();return pending; } input.addEventListener('input',()= {dirty=true;controls();},{signal}); form.addEventListener('submit',event= {event.preventDefault();void save().catch(()= {});},{signal}); reloadButton.addEventListener('click',()= {void load().catch(report);},{signal}); root.closest('.gw-window')?.addEventListener('gravewright:sheet-flush',event= { if(pending)event.detail.waitUntil(pending); else if(dirty)event.detail.waitUntil(Promise.reject(new Error(t('Save the name or reload the server value before closing.')))); },{signal}); controls();await load(); } export default { start({styles,api}){ styles.use('styles.css'); const en={}; const pt={ 'Sheet name action':'Ação no nome da ficha','Sheet name':'Nome da ficha', 'Save name':'Salvar nome','Reload server value':'Recarregar valor do servidor', 'Server value loaded.':'Valor do servidor carregado.','Read-only sheet.':'Ficha somente leitura.', 'Saved actor name.':'Nome do ator salvo.','Saved independent token name.':'Nome do token independente salvo.', 'Use a name with 1 to 120 characters.':'Use um nome com 1 a 120 caracteres.', 'This system uses an incompatible token field.':'Este sistema usa um campo token incompatível.', 'Conflict: server value loaded. api.i18n.register({en,'pt-BR':pt}); }, register({register}){ register('actor.sheet',{mode:'augment',mount:mountSheetName}); register('token.sheet',{mode:'augment',mount:mountSheetName}); }, stop(){} }; README.md text Sheet name action, target Gravewright 0.3.0 / SDK 1.x. ZIP the contents of this folder, with manifest.json directly at its root. An installation owner reviews and installs the ZIP under Modules, Install module, Install from ZIP. A GM activates example.sheet-name version 1.0.0 in the campaign. Open an actor or token sheet and find Sheet name action below the existing sheet. Save native sheet edits first. Click Reload server value, edit Sheet name, then Save name. Do not edit the native form and this panel simultaneously. Every save sends both revisions read by actors.sheet and preserves all other JSON data. Snapshot tokens use data.token.name; linked tokens rename their actor. An existing nonobject data.token is rejected rather than replaced. The server checks access. Closing waits for a pending save. An unsaved name blocks closing until Save name or Reload server value. Conflicts reload the server value and never retry a write. On an uncertain network failure, reload before editing again. Deactivation aborts pending client work but cannot undo a write the server already committed. See the bilingual tutorial-sheet-module guide for complete instructions and tests. 2. Build a ZIP with the manifest at its root From the directory containing example.sheet-name , run one of these commands. The output ZIP is a sibling of the source folder; it is never included inside itself. powershell Compress-Archive -LiteralPath './example.sheet-name/manifest.json','./example.sheet-name/main.mjs','./example.sheet-name/styles.css','./example.sheet-name/LICENSE.txt','./example.sheet-name/README.md' -DestinationPath './example.sheet-name-source.zip' sh (cd example.sheet-name && zip ../example.sheet-name-source.zip manifest.json main.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt README.md) 3. Install, activate and open an existing sheet 1. Sign in as the installation owner. Open Modules , Install module , Install from ZIP and choose the ZIP. Review the trusted source before uploading. This local route does not require a catalog signature. 2. Open the disposable campaign as GM. Open its Modules / Extensions list, activate Sheet name action 1.0.0 , and keep the system that already owns the campaign. Installing a package alone does not activate it. 3. Open Actors , create a character using that system or open an existing one, then open its sheet. Scroll below the original content to Sheet name action . 4. Save any pending edits through the original sheet first, then click Reload server value in this panel. Change Sheet name to Harbor Scout and click Save name . Expect Saved actor name. Close and reopen the sheet and confirm the name. 4. Understand exactly what gets written actors.sheet(actorId, {tokenId}, {signal}) supplies the data and both revisions. For an actor, or a linked token, saveSheet receives the new name , the exact version and sheetVersion , and a deep copy of all existing data . For an independent token, the server returns its own tokenId and snapshot sheetVersion ; the code changes only data.token.name , preserving all other snapshot fields and token hints. The actor is left untouched. The scoped API fixes campaign and scene identity; the server rechecks ownership. This public API does not expose another package’s unsaved editor buffer. Save the original sheet before reloading this panel and avoid editing both forms at once. A concurrently committed edit produces conflict ; the panel loads current state, discards its old name draft and requires a new explicit edit. It never substitutes a newer expected revision to force the failed write. 5. Verify tokens, permissions, conflicts and closing 1. Place a linked token and an independent token for the same actor. Rename the linked one: reopening the actor must show that name. Rename the independent one: only its own name must change. Compare existing sheet fields and token hints before and after. 2. Use a player with read-only access. The form displays Read-only sheet. and disables editing. A player with ownership can use the action; the server remains the permission boundary. 3. Open the same actor in two sessions. Save a name in one, then save the stale draft in the other. Expect the server value to reload and a conflict message, with no automatic overwrite. 4. Type without saving, then close. The window stays open and asks you to save or reload. Reload server value explicitly discards that draft. During a pending save, the native gravewright:sheet-flush lifecycle waits for its promise; a failed save keeps the window open. 5. Deactivate while a read is pending, reopen the sheet three times and switch scenes. No removed panel may reappear, no listener may survive disposal, and no duplicate form may accumulate. A server write already committed is not undone by browser cancellation. Augment, replace and release updates Use augment for an extra action on another system’s working sheet, as here. It gets a dedicated root after native content and does not hide the editor. Use replace only when you provide the whole sheet body, including loading, editing, saving, validation and navigation. A system can filter actor types with types ; generic add-ons should not assume a type. The campaign system’s sheet takes precedence by default; competing replacement candidates use the table’s explicit replacement preferences. See the complete replacement tutorial (docs:tutorial-system-sheet) and SDK selection rules (docs:modules available-surfaces). For a new package revision, change version to 1.0.1 , rebuild the ZIP, install it and select that exact version in the campaign. Do not edit extracted installed files or overwrite the same ID/version with different bytes. Read and verify existing data after the upgrade. How to use AI to add another sheet action text Use this complete example.sheet-name package on Gravewright 0.3.0. Add one concrete action to actor.sheet and token.sheet without replacing their editor. Read actors/services.py, domain-api.js and both context schemas first. Explain actor versus linked and independent token writes, preserve data and both loaded revisions, allocate a new request UUID per logical save, handle conflict without forcing a write, support read-only ownership, native sheet-flush and disposal. Do not invent access to another package’s unsaved buffer. Deliver all files, ZIP instructions and behavior tests, with limitations and actual validation results.
