title: How to build and replace a complete system sheet
summary: Use the working Example Expedition package, install it, create actors and verify linked and independent tokens.
text: Start with the complete system package The Example Expedition package (docs:example-package-system) contains a complete original character/NPC sheet with a validated stamina field, its manifest, styles and license. Download that package rather than copying only a register call. Follow its exact file listings and ZIP instructions. This tutorial targets Gravewright 0.3.0 and adds no RPG catalog. Install and create a campaign 1. As the installation owner, open Systems, Install system, Install from ZIP and choose the reviewed system-source.zip. Its manifest declares system.actorTypes, system.itemTypes and the browser entry. 2. As GM, create a disposable campaign and select Example Expedition as its system. Open the table and confirm the exact installed release is active. An unrelated add-on does not become a system by registering a sheet. 3. In Actors, create a character and an NPC. Open both. The package registers replace for actor.sheet and token.sheet, filtered to character and npc. The host provides the window title and controls; the package renders the complete body. Exercise the complete editing flow Enter stamina 17, save, close and reopen. Try empty, negative and greater-than-100 values; rejected drafts must not replace server data. Open a read-only player view. Create one linked and one independent token for the same character and change stamina separately. Linked sheets share actor data; the independent token uses its snapshot and its own sheetVersion. The package must preserve all other data and supply both revisions to saveSheet. Choose the correct replacement With no explicit competing preference, a matching campaign system sheet wins. A system may register disjoint types lists; omit types only when it implements every actor type. If two modules compete for the same surface, review the table replacement preference rather than assuming load order. Explicit token.sheet handles tokens; an actor.sheet replacement can be the system fallback for tokens when there is no matching token registration. Native UI is restored after a failed selected mount. Read the SDK rules (docs:modules). Keep a rename add-on such as Sheet name action (docs:tutorial-sheet-module) in augment mode. Two full replacements cannot display as one merged editor. Save the system sheet before using an add-on that sends its own complete sheet data. Validate an update Change the package version, rebuild and install the new ZIP, then explicitly activate the new release. Do not mutate installed bytes. Open old characters and both token modes, preserve stamina, test two-session conflicts and close while saving. A failure must keep the window open or restore the native surface, with an actionable diagnostic. Deactivation must abort reads and remove DOM/listeners. Keep this system’s assets, translations and automation in one package and use only host APIs available in 0.3.0. How to use AI for a complete replacement text Use the full Example Expedition source package on Gravewright 0.3.0. Add one original sheet field and its validation while preserving character/NPC types, actor and token reads, revisions, native sheet-flush, permissions and disposal. Explain every changed file. Do not ship a placeholder replacement, split system rules into a companion package, import private host internals or upgrade the host. Verify create, edit, save, close, reopen, linked/snapshot tokens and conflicting sessions. All tutorials (docs:tutorial-index) · Complete source package (docs:example-package-system)

title: How to create a compendium module
summary: Build the complete package from an empty directory, install it and verify its original content.
text: What you will build Start with an empty directory and finish with an installable module. It displays Harbor library on the table. The GM clicks Prepare my library to create a Harbor Library compendium containing a Beacon Watch journal entry, then reads the snapshot and imports a copy through the module's own interface. Use this route for an ordinary module working with campaign documents. Authorized API actions create the content, which persists in the campaign. An ordinary module cannot declare content.compendiums without system; learn that separate route in How to include compendiums in a system (docs:tutorial-system-compendiums). Use Gravewright 0.3.0 and a disposable campaign. You need the installation owner's account to install and the campaign GM role to prepare/import. No npm, database access, RPG catalog or rules module is required. All sample text is original. Package buttons are English. 1. Create the directory and understand the files Create a directory named campaign-library. Save every complete file from section 4 as UTF-8 with the exact names and paths, or extract the ZIP below. manifest.json identifies the package; main.mjs renders its panel; library.mjs owns the write sequence; maintenance.mjs contains optional maintenance functions; styles.css scopes the module styling; LICENSE.txt permits reuse of this example. text campaign-library/ manifest.json main.mjs library.mjs maintenance.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Download the complete ZIP (../../assets/tutorials/campaign-library/campaign-library-source.zip) - manifest.json (../../assets/tutorials/campaign-library/manifest.json) - main.mjs (../../assets/tutorials/campaign-library/main.mjs) - library.mjs (../../assets/tutorials/campaign-library/library.mjs) - maintenance.mjs (../../assets/tutorials/campaign-library/maintenance.mjs) - styles.css (../../assets/tutorials/campaign-library/styles.css) - LICENSE.txt (../../assets/tutorials/campaign-library/LICENSE.txt) 2. Package and install Use Python already available in your development environment. These commands start in the directory containing campaign-library. On POSIX use python3 if that is your interpreter name. They archive only the listed files with manifest.json at the root, excluding local state. POSIX sh cd campaign-library python -m zipfile -c ../campaign-library-source.zip "manifest.json" "main.mjs" "library.mjs" "maintenance.mjs" "styles.css" "LICENSE.txt" PowerShell powershell Set-Location -LiteralPath .\campaign-library python -m zipfile -c ..\campaign-library-source.zip "manifest.json" "main.mjs" "library.mjs" "maintenance.mjs" "styles.css" "LICENSE.txt" List the ZIP using python -m zipfile -l ../campaign-library-source.zip while still in the project directory. As owner open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP , choose it and click Install . This local upload requires no signature; catalog publication uses the documented signing workflow. Open your test campaign as GM. Use its Gravewright button → Extensions , find Harbor campaign library 1.0.0 and click Activate . Close the menu. Harbor library appears below the top bar. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) to locate these screens. 3. Prepare, read and import 1. Click Prepare my library . The controller checks isGM, saves four operation UUIDs in storage.user and creates the compendium. 2. It creates a native journal, uses the returned journal_id/version to save a page in gw-journal-doc-v1 format, then snapshots the journal with kind journal and resourceId. It does not send the journal body directly to compendiums.add. 3. Wait for Library ready . The selectors show Harbor Library and Beacon Watch. Click Read snapshot to see the kind journal envelope and the original blue-lantern page. 4. Click Import copy . The result identifies the created document. Open Journals and inspect the imported diary and its page. Import uses the mounted campaign; there is no payload field for a different campaign. 5. Click Prepare my library again, then deactivate/reactivate the module. The same GM resumes the stored workflow without creating another pack or entry. Refresh to verify. Clicking Import copy again after success is a new action and may create another copy. Preparation belongs to the user, module and campaign. A different GM has their own workflow and creates their own library if they click prepare. This keeps retry UUIDs with the account that performed the operations. The resulting compendium belongs to the campaign and survives deactivation. 4. Copy every complete file To change sample content edit journalData in library.mjs before preparing a new library. Every section has a stable ID, title, audience and rich document. To rename documents, change the create/update/add literals. Changing the module code does not rewrite existing snapshots: they are captured copies rather than live journal links. manifest.json json { "id": "example.harbor-library", "name": "Harbor campaign library", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Creates an original journal and reusable campaign snapshot through the public API.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {createLibrary} from "./library.mjs"; export default { start({styles}) { styles.use("styles.css"); }, register({register}) { register("table.interface", async ({root, api, storage, signal, onDispose}) = { const library = createLibrary({api, storage, signal}); const el = (tag, text) = { const node = root.ownerDocument.createElement(tag); if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text; return node; }; const panel = el("section"); panel.className = "harbor-library"; const prepare = el("button", "Prepare my library"); const refresh = el("button", "Refresh list"); const read = el("button", "Read snapshot"); const copy = el("button", "Import copy"); for (const button of prepare, refresh, read, copy ) button.type = "button"; const packLabel = el("label", "Compendium"); const packs = el("select"); packLabel.append(packs); const entryLabel = el("label", "Entry"); const entries = el("select"); entryLabel.append(entries); const output = el("pre"); output.setAttribute("role", "status"); panel.append(el("h3", "Harbor library"), prepare, refresh, packLabel, entryLabel, read, copy, output); root.append(panel); onDispose(() = panel.remove()); let state, busy = true, importAttempt; const controls = () = { prepare.disabled = busy !state?.isGM; refresh.disabled = busy; read.disabled = busy !entries.value; copy.disabled = busy !state?.isGM !entries.value; packs.disabled = busy; entries.disabled = busy; }; const options = (select, rows, selected) = { select.replaceChildren(); const empty = el("option", "Choose..."); empty.value = ""; select.append(empty); for (const row of rows) { const option = el("option", row.name); option.value = row.id; select.append(option); } select.value = rows.some(row = row.id === selected) ? selected : ""; }; const chooseEntries = selected = { options(entries, state?.packs.find(pack = pack.id === packs.value)?.entries ?? , selected); controls(); }; const load = async (packId = packs.value, entryId = entries.value) = { const next = await api.compendiums.state({}, {signal}); if (signal.aborted) return; state = next; options(packs, state.packs, packId); chooseEntries(entryId); }; const run = async task = { if (busy signal.aborted) return; busy = true; controls(); output.textContent = "Working..."; try { await task(); } catch (error) { if (!signal.aborted) output.textContent = "Error: " + (error.code ?? "unavailable") + ". Refresh and review before retrying."; } finally { if (!signal.aborted) {busy = false; controls();} } }; prepare.addEventListener("click", () = void run(async () = { const saved = await library.prepare(); await load(saved.packId, saved.entryId); if (!signal.aborted) output.textContent = "Library ready. const checkpoint = async changes = { record = await storage.user.set(key, {...record.value, ...changes}, {expectedRevision: record.revision}); }; // Save request identities before making writes; retries reuse exact inputs. if (!record.value.packId) { const created = await api.compendiums.create({name: "Harbor Library"}, {signal, requestId: record.value.requests.pack}); await checkpoint({entryId: added.id}); } return record.value; }, async read(packId, entryId) { return api.compendiums.read({packId, id: entryId}, {signal}); }, async importCopy(packId, entryId, requestId) { return api.compendiums.import({packId, id: entryId}, {signal, requestId}); }; export async function shareCampaignPack(api, packId, signal) { editable(packId); const pack = (await api.compendiums.state({}, {signal})).packs.find(row = row.id === packId); if (!pack) throw Object.assign(new Error("Pack not found"), {code: "not_found"}); return api.compendiums.setPermissions({packId, level: "read"}, options(signal)); } export async function readBatch(api, packId, entryIds, signal) { return api.compendiums.read({packId, ids: entryIds}, {signal}); Share and maintain the library The pack starts private. As GM integrate maintenance.mjs's shareCampaignPack into an explicit module action and pass the packId returned by prepare. It reads the current version before configure, sets shared true and leaves the pack unlocked. Check that native ownership grants do not further restrict the test account. As a player with reading permission click Refresh list, select the pack and Read snapshot. Prepare and Import are disabled; the server also rejects writes/importing. maintenance.mjs includes readBatch for 1–100 unique IDs (never combine id and ids), removeSnapshot and deleteCampaignPack. Use them only for your test library after verifying the IDs. Removing an entry uses the entry version; deleting a pack reads its version after other changes. Neither removes the source diary or already imported documents. Unlock a locked pack through configure before editing/deleting it. grantInstalledPackRead demonstrates setPermissions for native/installed packs identified by native:. For table-created packs use configure.shared or native ownership controls. The complete file above contains actual payloads for all these actions. 6. Verify repetition, failures and permissions Prepare twice with the same GM and count one pack and one entry. Edit the source diary through the interface, read the snapshot and confirm its captured text stays unchanged. Import, reopen and inspect the page. Grant a player reading permission, test reading and attempt a direct API import: the server must reject it. If a write response is lost, Prepare resumes with the same account's saved UUIDs and exact payloads. Every checkpoint uses expectedRevision; on conflict reload before retrying. If someone edited the diary before the body-save step, its old revision is rejected without silently replacing it: review the source and pending operation before changing code/state. Import copy retains its UUID for a pending attempt in the panel; if the context closes with an unknown outcome, inspect journals before requesting another import. Cancelling a context cannot undo a committed write. A network failure is an error rather than an empty list. Deleted IDs or revoked access produce not_found/permission_denied; do not erase workflow state or create replacements to conceal failures. Do not reset the workflow to update content. For changed package bytes use version 1.0.1, install and activate it; existing documents and workflow data remain saved. How to use AI to adapt this library Adapt tutorial-compendium-module into a library of original notices. Inspect frontend.json, journals/services.py and compendiums/services.py for release 0.3.0. Preserve journal_id/version, rich documents, snapshots by resourceId, retry UUIDs and expectedRevision. Provide every file, click and GM/player checks. Do not add content to an ordinary module manifest or update snapshots automatically. Include batch reading and versioned maintenance without deleting campaign content. title: How to include compendiums in a system
summary: Build the complete package from an empty directory, install it and verify its original content.
text: What you will build Create one system package named Beacon Expedition Library , containing actor/item descriptors and a physical compendium file. Once installed and selected for a campaign, Compendiums will show Scouts, Equipment and Signals. The GM imports Harbor Scout, Signal Rope and Blue Glow. Use this route for original content shipped with a system. Unlike the campaign library module (docs:tutorial-compendium-module), no JavaScript click creates the collection: installation validates its declared JSON and the host exposes it only with the campaign's active exact system version. Installed catalogs are read only; imports create campaign documents that evolve independently. Use Gravewright 0.3.0, a disposable installation and the owner account for installation. The GM selects the campaign system and imports documents. This package is complete as a type/content provider; its entry registers no sheets or rules. For an editable custom sheet extend this same package using the sheet example (docs:example-package-system). 1. Start with an empty directory Create system-library and its compendiums subdirectory. Save every file from section 4. manifest.json registers system and content; main.mjs implements start/register/stop without running actions; compendiums/beacon.json contains the actual content; LICENSE.txt travels with the package. There is no separately installed Modules companion. text system-library/ manifest.json main.mjs compendiums/beacon.json LICENSE.txt Download the complete ZIP (../../assets/tutorials/system-library/system-library-source.zip) - manifest.json (../../assets/tutorials/system-library/manifest.json) - main.mjs (../../assets/tutorials/system-library/main.mjs) - compendiums/beacon.json (../../assets/tutorials/system-library/compendiums/beacon.json) - LICENSE.txt (../../assets/tutorials/system-library/LICENSE.txt) 2. Understand the binding before packaging The system ID is example.beacon-library. It appears in the manifest and every entry's systemId. actor_pack uses character from system.actorTypes. item_pack uses gear and spell_pack uses spell, both declared in system.itemTypes. The core routes spell_pack to items; it does not implement spell rules. content.compendiums points exactly to compendiums/beacon.json. The file has a collection name and packs array; each pack has id, label, type and entries. Each entry has id, name, type, systemId and data. Do not add campaigns: the host associates the collection with the active campaign. Do not put journal_pack, scene_pack, card_pack or deck_pack in this package; installation accepts only actor_pack, item_pack and spell_pack. 3. Package, install and select Start in the directory containing system-library and use one command below. Both include the nested JSON at its correct path with manifest.json at the root. Use python3 on POSIX where appropriate. POSIX sh cd system-library python -m zipfile -c ../system-library-source.zip "manifest.json" "main.mjs" "compendiums/beacon.json" "LICENSE.txt" PowerShell powershell Set-Location -LiteralPath .\system-library python -m zipfile -c ..\system-library-source.zip "manifest.json" "main.mjs" "compendiums/beacon.json" "LICENSE.txt" List the archive with python -m zipfile -l ../system-library-source.zip to check manifest.json and compendiums/beacon.json. As owner open Inside → Systems → Install system → Install from ZIP , select it and click Install . Open a test campaign using Beacon Expedition Library as its system. Verify the exact active 1.0.0 release in its Extensions; installing a version does not automatically switch existing campaigns. Open Compendiums and find Beacon Expedition Library / Scouts , / Equipment and / Signals . Read Harbor Scout: type is character and stamina is 8. Import through the native pack control. Repeat for Signal Rope (gear, length 12) and Blue Glow (spell, color blue). Imported actors/items appear in the campaign's directories. 4. Copy every complete file To add original content edit JSON entries while preserving stable IDs. Add document types to the manifest before using them in entries. data belongs to the system: stamina, length, color and duration are example fields rather than host-interpreted rules. The no-op entry creates no campaign documents on activation and no duplicate catalogs on reload. manifest.json json { "id": "example.beacon-library", "name": "Beacon Expedition Library", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Original actor and item types with three installed read-only compendium packs.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT", "system": { "actorTypes": { "id": "character", "label": "Character" } , "itemTypes": { "id": "gear", "label": "Gear" }, { "id": "spell", "label": "Spell" } }, "content": { "compendiums": "compendiums/beacon.json" } } main.mjs javascript export default { start() {}, register() {}, stop() {}, }; compendiums/beacon.json json { "name": "Beacon Expedition Library", "packs": { "id": "scouts", "label": "Scouts", "type": "actor_pack", "entries": { "id": "harbor-scout", "name": "Harbor Scout", "type": "character", "systemId": "example.beacon-library", "data": { "stamina": 8, "role": "Watch keeper" } } }, { "id": "equipment", "label": "Equipment", "type": "item_pack", "entries": { "id": "signal-rope", "name": "Signal Rope", "type": "gear", "systemId": "example.beacon-library", "data": { "length": 12, "description": "An original training rope with blue knots." } } }, { "id": "signals", "label": "Signals", "type": "spell_pack", "entries": { "id": "blue-glow", "name": "Blue Glow", "type": "spell", "systemId": "example.beacon-library", "data": { "color": "blue", "duration": 1, "description": "An original fictional signal, with no host automation." } } } } LICENSE.txt text MIT License Copyright (c) 2026 Gravewright contributors Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions: The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software. THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE. 5. Read through the API and grant reading In a module mounted in the same campaign discover authorized IDs with api.compendiums.state. Packs have host-generated native: IDs; do not construct IDs from filenames. This complete function reads a Scouts entry and returns IDs usable by a GM for granting reading: javascript export async function inspectScout(api, signal) { const state = await api.compendiums.state({}, {signal}); const pack = state.packs.find(row = row.name === "Beacon Expedition Library / Scouts"); if (!pack) throw new Error("Activate the system version and check read grants"); const entry = pack.entries.find(row = row.id === "harbor-scout"); if (!entry) throw new Error("Scout entry unavailable"); const body = await api.compendiums.read({packId: pack.id, id: entry.id}, {signal}); return {packId: pack.id, entryId: entry.id, body}; } export async function shareScouts(api, packId, signal) { return api.compendiums.setPermissions({packId, level: "read"}, {signal, requestId: crypto.randomUUID()}); } state returns metadata; read returns the collection's original document without requiring the kind envelope of a table-created entry. For a batch in the same pack use read({packId, ids: ... }) with 1–100 unique IDs. As GM use native permission controls or shareScouts with the discovered packId. A reader may view but cannot import. Inspect full bodies before sharing: a compendium read grant authorizes its content. 6. Verify and publish an immutable update Check all three packs and import every entry. Reopen: the same packs remain and no document imported itself. Test a campaign using a different system; these collections must not appear as that system's content. Revoke a player's read access and check that fresh reads fail; UI controls are not the authorization boundary. For an update preserve the package ID, file paths and pack/entry IDs; change version to 1.0.1 and edit the original JSON. Build another ZIP, install and explicitly select 1.0.1 for the campaign. Do not edit the installed extracted directory: the host verifies approved bytes and rejects different content under the same version. Stable IDs preserve references/grants. Already imported documents remain copies and are not rewritten. A new import uses the new content. Unregistered types, mismatched systemId, missing files, invalid JSON, duplicate IDs or forbidden pack types prevent installation. A collection allows up to 8 MiB, 64 packs and 20,000 entries; an entry up to 256 KiB and depth 24. A manifest allows up to 16 collection paths. Missing/changed approved bytes, revoked packages or inactive versions make collections unavailable. Do not bypass this with assets helpers: declared collections use the authorized API. How to use AI to add a catalog to your system Start from tutorial-system-compendiums on Gravewright 0.3.0. Replace only original data with authorized types/fields . Provide the complete manifest, entry, physical collection and license. Check every systemId/type, validate with the installer/validate_collection and show Systems installation with exact-version activation. Test all three packs, players with/without reading, imports and a 1.0.1 update preserving existing copies. Keep one system package and the requested host. All tutorials (docs:tutorial-index) · API (docs:api)

title: How to create a scene tools module
summary: Build a working module to inspect scene layers, edit metadata, manage folders, draw a native door and broadcast a test scene.
text: The project you will build Create Scene workshop, a browser module with a native workbench modal. Follow a concrete sequence: inspect an existing disposable scene, rename it, organize its folder, create/edit/operate a door and deliberately broadcast it. Delete the test data only after the token and combat tutorials. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named maps-workshop. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/maps-workshop/maps-workshop-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text maps-workshop/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt In a disposable campaign, create an empty scene at least8×8 cells using the native Scenes → New scene → Map Builder flow, then Generate scene . Start with no valuable scene content. The public browser domain API has no maps.create method for a new raster/Builder project. Use Map Builder (docs:map-builder) for authored projects; native source generation remains separate from the commands below. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../maps-workshop-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../maps-workshop-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Scene workshop. Close that menu and click Scene workshop. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Inspect scenes, folders and native layers Run with the Scene ID blank first. Copy the test scene ID, enter it and run again to inspect walls, images, lights, fog, lighting and their returned versions. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const directory=await api.maps.state({},read); const layers=v.mapId.trim()?await api.maps.layers({mapId:v.mapId.trim()},read):null; return {directory,layers}; } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.maps.state({},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: Authorized scene/folder IDs, activeMapId and navigatingMapId; selected native layer state when supplied. How to verify: Compare the GM scene directory with a player account. Player state must omit private scenes, regions and private graph data. Rename the test scene and set grid visibility Use a disposable scene. Name and gridVisible are supplied settings; other scene settings remain unchanged. Do not send the entire projected scene as settings. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const before=await api.maps.get(v.mapId,{},read); await api.maps.update({mapId:before.id,version:before.version,settings:{name:v.name,gridVisible:v.gridVisible}},write()); return await api.maps.get(before.id,{},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.maps.state({},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The same scene ID with the chosen name, grid visibility and a new integer version. How to verify: Open native scene settings and verify name/grid while checking that imageScale, gridSize and measurement units remain as before. Create a scene folder Enter an original folder label. Copy created.folderId for the next two recipes. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const created=await api.maps.createFolder({label:v.label,color:' b49a5a',parentId:null},write()); return {created,folders:(await api.maps.state({},read)).folders}; } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.maps.state({},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: A folder UUID and the updated scene folder list. How to verify: Find Workshop scenes in the native Scenes directory. Rename or reparent a scene folder Use the folder created above. Blank Parent puts it at the root. The server rejects cycles, foreign folders and nesting deeper than its supported limit. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.maps.updateFolder({folderId:v.folderId,label:v.label,color:' b49a5a',parentId:v.parentId.trim() null},write()); return (await api.maps.state({},read)).folders; } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.maps.state({},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The retained folder ID with its new label/parent. How to verify: Expand the scene tree and verify nesting. Try the same folder as its own parent and confirm rejection. Move the scene into the tutorial folder Paste the test scene and folder IDs. This command uses groupId; it is not the journal folder_id contract. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.maps.get(v.mapId,{},read); await api.maps.move({mapId:v.mapId,groupId:v.folderId.trim() null},write()); return await api.maps.get(v.mapId,{},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.maps.state({},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The scene groupId references the chosen folder, or null at the root. How to verify: Locate the same scene under Workshop rooms. The scene ID and native objects are unchanged. Draw a native test door through updateObjects Use a scene at least 8 cells wide. Coordinates are scene pixels, not the cell coordinates used by token.move. The endpoints must differ. This creates a plain native door with no blueprint or image dependency. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.maps.get(v.mapId,{},read); const result=await api.maps.updateObjects({mapId:v.mapId,area:'walls',action:'create',data:{x1:v.x1,y1:v.y1,x2:v.x2,y2:v.y2,kind:'door',door_state:'closed'}},write()); return {created:result.wall,layers:await api.maps.layers({mapId:v.mapId},read)}; } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.maps.state({},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: A wall entry with kind door, an ID and version. Copy its ID. How to verify: Open Walls in the native scene and find the horizontal door. Inspect its projected endpoints. Adjust a door endpoint with its object version Use the door created above. Only x2 changes; the native validator retains its other fields. Permissions, failures and final test Every write is an explicit Run action. Reads use recipient projections; writes keep native permissions and fresh operation UUIDs. Scene update, object update, token move/configuration and combat use their real revision fields. Some native selection commands have no expected revision parameter in this release; the examples do not invent one. On conflict the recipe rereads current state and stops. Review it, then intentionally run a new operation. Multiple API calls are separate transactions: a completed earlier call is not rolled back if a later read fails. Deactivation aborts scoped work; it cannot undo a server commit. Test GM/player scene filtering, one stale scene revision, one stale door revision, denied folder cycles and deactivation during a read. Activation explicitly broadcasts to players. Map Builder boundary: this package does not author Blueprint JSON or call private Builder routes. Use the real Smart Object editor, Simulate and Test behavior to create automation, then Generate/Update scene. Four Blueprint kinds (docs:examples-blueprints), 48 complete node examples (docs:example-blueprint-nodes) and execution/data connections (docs:example-blueprint-connections) provide complete graph recipes. title: How to create a token tools module
summary: Place, move, duplicate, configure and remove tokens; control native vision/visibility and timed conditions.
text: The project you will build Build Token workshop as one browser module. Place two disposable tokens in the scene from the previous tutorial, then test movement, snapshot duplication, rotation/elevation, vision, hidden state and an original condition. Keep the tokens for the combat tutorial before removal. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named tokens-workshop. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/tokens-workshop/tokens-workshop-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text tokens-workshop/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Complete Scene workshop (docs:tutorial-maps) and keep its scene ID. Create a disposable actor with the selected system through the native Actors directory, or follow the actor tutorial. Copy actual IDs from Inspect. The module calls public api.tokens methods. Its gridX/gridY are cell-space placement coordinates; native wall geometry uses scene pixels. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../tokens-workshop-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../tokens-workshop-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Token workshop. Close that menu and click Token workshop. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Inspect available actors and scene tokens Paste the test Scene ID from the maps tutorial. Copy a readable actor ID for Place, then a token ID for later actions. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { return {actors:await api.actors.list({},read),tokens:await api.tokens.list({mapId:v.mapId},read)}; } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: Authorized actor metadata and token IDs, versions, positions, vision and visible conditions. How to verify: Compare GM and player: hidden tokens and GM-only conditions are filtered before delivery. Place an actor token in the test scene Create an original disposable actor using the native/system sheet first. Coordinates use cell-space gridX/gridY for token placement, not scene pixels. The host validates bounds and token size. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.actors.get(v.actorId,{},read); const created=await api.tokens.place({mapId:v.mapId,actorId:v.actorId,gridX:v.x,gridY:v.y},write()); return {createdIds:created.createdIds,tokens:created.tokens}; } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: A created token ID and current token projection. The host decides linked/snapshot mode. How to verify: Find the token at grid2,2. A first token may be linked; another placement of the same actor may turn existing links into independent snapshots through the native service. Move a controlled unlocked token Enter the token ID and a nearby destination. path: requests the direct segment; intermediate waypoints must use the same grid coordinates. Player movement still checks walls and ownership. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const token=await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); if(!token.canControl token.locked) throw new Error('Choose a controlled unlocked token'); return await api.tokens.move({mapId:v.mapId,id:token.id,expectedVersion:token.version,gridX:v.x,gridY:v.y,path: },write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The same token at its accepted grid position with an incremented version. How to verify: Test as its controlling player: an unlocked open path succeeds, a wall-blocked path fails and leaves the position unchanged. An old expectedVersion conflicts. Duplicate one tutorial token Use the token placed above. The native service creates an independent snapshot and chooses its bounded offset. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); const result=await api.tokens.duplicate({mapId:v.mapId,tokenIds: v.id },write()); return {createdIds:result.createdIds,tokens:result.tokens}; } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: A different token ID, usually offset by one cell, with linkMode snapshot. How to verify: Inspect both IDs and open their sheets. Copy the duplicate ID for cleanup or combat. Configure rotation, elevation and disposition Configure a single disposable token. Keep locked false for the movement recipe. Elevation can affect region eligibility. A player may rotate a controlled token only with the rotation-only values variant; this multi-field recipe is GM-only. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const token=await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); await api.tokens.configure({mapId:v.mapId,tokenIds: token.id ,expectedVersion:token.version,values:{rotation:v.rotation,elevation:v.elevation,disposition:v.disposition,locked:v.locked}},write()); return await api.tokens.get(token.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: Requested native rotation, elevation, disposition and locked state, retaining actor/sheet data. How to verify: Inspect the native token configuration and confirm locked prevents a later move until explicitly cleared. Enable and configure token vision Use the placed token; range is a nonnegative cell distance. To observe line-of-sight, configure dynamic lighting in the native scene and use the token controlling player. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); await api.tokens.setVision({mapId:v.mapId,tokenIds: v.id ,enabled:v.enabled,range:v.range},write()); return await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: visionEnabled and visionRange match the form. How to verify: Toggle enabled false/true and verify player visibility using the native lighting setup. A GM omniscient view alone does not prove player vision. Hide and show the tutorial token Run with Hidden selected, inspect the player account, then clear it and run again. This changes token visibility, not the actor permission map. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); await api.tokens.setHidden({mapId:v.mapId,tokenIds: v.id ,hidden:v.hidden},write()); return await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: GM retains the token; players receive it only when not hidden and otherwise authorized. How to verify: Compare Inspect outputs in two accounts. Hidden presence still follows server presence-filter rules. Add an original timed token condition Use an original label. This is a generic marker, not a bundled rule. Copy condition_id from the result for Remove condition. Duration advances through real forward combat events when the token participates. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); if(! 'everyone','gm' .includes(v.visibility)) throw new Error('Use everyone or gm'); if(!Number.isInteger(v.rounds) v.rounds<1) throw new Error('Use a positive integer duration'); if(v.visibility==='gm'&&context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required for hidden conditions'); await api.tokens.addCondition({mapId:v.mapId,tokenIds: v.id ,label:v.label,description:'Original tutorial marker with no RPG rules.',kind:'positive',visibility:v.visibility,duration:{type:'rounds',value:v.rounds,expires:'end'}},write()); return await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: A new condition with unique condition_id and an explicit rounds/end duration. How to verify: As player, add only to a controlled token with visibility everyone. A private GM condition must be absent from player state. Remove the chosen token condition Paste the exact condition_id, not its display label. Remove only the marker created in this tutorial. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const token=await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); if(!token.conditions.some(item= item.condition_id===v.conditionId)) throw new Error('Choose a visible condition from this token'); await api.tokens.removeCondition({mapId:v.mapId,tokenIds: v.id ,conditionId:v.conditionId},write()); return await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The selected condition disappears while other conditions remain. How to verify: Inspect before/after. A player cannot discover/remove a GM-only condition by guessing its ID. Remove the disposable token Use only the tutorial token/duplicate. Run after combat cleanup. Removing a token does not delete its actor. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(!v.confirm) throw new Error('Confirm the disposable token'); await api.tokens.get(v.id,{mapId:v.mapId},read); await api.tokens.remove({mapId:v.mapId,tokenIds: v.id },write()); return await api.tokens.list({mapId:v.mapId},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.tokens.state({mapId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The selected token is absent; its actor remains in Actors. How to verify: Check the scene and actor directory, and confirm other token IDs remain. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Permissions, failures and final test Every write is an explicit Run action. Reads use recipient projections; writes keep native permissions and fresh operation UUIDs. Scene update, object update, token move/configuration and combat use their real revision fields. Some native selection commands have no expected revision parameter in this release; the examples do not invent one. On conflict the recipe rereads current state and stops. Review it, then intentionally run a new operation. Multiple API calls are separate transactions: a completed earlier call is not rolled back if a later read fails. Deactivation aborts scoped work; it cannot undo a server commit. Use GM and controlling/noncontrolling player accounts. Condition advancement belongs to real combat events, not a local UI timer. Inspect after reconnect instead of replaying mutation events as side effects. title: How to create a combat tools module
summary: Build a working encounter laboratory covering participants, initiative, order, flags, turns, rounds and cleanup.
text: The project you will build Create Combat workshop and operate the native encounter of one disposable scene. Add the two tokens, enter or roll initiative, start, select/reorder participants, advance turns/rounds, then stop and remove participants. The selected RPG system remains responsible for its rules and provider. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named combat-workshop. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/combat-workshop/combat-workshop-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text combat-workshop/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Keep the scene and two tokens from Token workshop (docs:tutorial-tokens). Run Inspect to copy exact scene/combatant identities. Use tokenId for placed tokens or actorId for actor-only participants. This module supplies no RPG system, catalog or Server Rules companion. Its explicit test formula is an encounter setting on the disposable campaign. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../combat-workshop-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../combat-workshop-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Combat workshop. Close that menu and click Combat workshop. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Inspect this scene encounter Paste the disposable scene ID. It need not contain an encounter yet. Copy combatant IDs from the projected list after adding participants. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { return await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: Encounter version, active/round/turn, configuration and authorized combatants. How to verify: Compare with the native Combat tracker. A player must not receive hidden entries or unauthorized resources. Add a placed token or an actor to combat Use tokenId with the two token IDs from the token tutorial, one run per token. Or use actorId for an actor without a scene token. Each Run action is one operation. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(! 'tokenId','actorId' .includes(v.identityType)) throw new Error('Use tokenId or actorId'); const identity={ v.identityType :v.id}; const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); return await api.combat.add({sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,...identity},write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: A combatant is added without duplicating an existing identity; encounter version advances. How to verify: Add two distinct combatants and verify both in the native tracker. Tokens from another scene must be refused. Set an explicit encounter initiative formula On the disposable encounter only, set the generic dice expression1d20. The selected system owns its default formula/provider; this explicit native encounter override does not implement new RPG rules. Clear the input to use manual mode. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); return await api.combat.configure({sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,formula:v.formula.trim()},write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: config.formula reflects the chosen expression; system-dependent config.input reports how initiative is entered. How to verify: Open Combat settings and inspect the formula. Invalid formulas are rejected without a partial config write. Set one combatant initiative value Use a participating identity. The recipe follows the current config: text input stays text; numeric/rolled input becomes a finite number. Do not hardcode a system attribute. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(! 'tokenId','actorId' .includes(v.identityType)) throw new Error('Use tokenId or actorId'); const identity={ v.identityType :v.id}; const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); const value=before.config?.input==='text'?v.value:Number(v.value); if(typeof value==='number'&&!Number.isFinite(value)) throw new Error('Enter a finite initiative number'); return await api.combat.setInitiative({sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,...identity,value},write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The selected initiative changes; numeric initiative follows the native ordering policy. How to verify: Set values12 and8 for two participants and inspect order. Text-mode systems may retain manual order. Roll initiative for a chosen scope Configure an explicit valid formula first. Missing rolls only unset entries; all rerolls all; npcs uses native player-ownership rules; one uses the supplied participating identity. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(! 'all','missing','npcs','one' .includes(v.scope)) throw new Error('Choose an initiative scope'); const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); if(!before.config?.formula) throw new Error('Configure an initiative formula first'); const identity={}; if(v.scope==='one'){ if(!v.id ! 'tokenId','actorId' .includes(v.identityType)) throw new Error('Supply the selected combatant identity'); identity v.identityType =v.id; } return await api.combat.rollInitiative({sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,scope:v.scope,...identity},write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: Only the selected scope receives server-side rolls; the native tracker orders results. How to verify: Set one manual value, run missing and confirm that value remains. Do not claim a specific random roll result. Move a participant up or down Use a combatant and run up, then down. Manual reordering preserves the active combatant identity rather than silently granting the turn to another entry. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(! 'tokenId','actorId' .includes(v.identityType)) throw new Error('Use tokenId or actorId'); const identity={ v.identityType :v.id}; const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); const payload={sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,...identity}; if(v.direction==='up') return await api.combat.moveUp(payload,write()); if(v.direction==='down') return await api.combat.moveDown(payload,write()); throw new Error('Choose up or down'); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The selected participant changes position while the active identity is preserved. How to verify: Start combat, note the current ID and reorder a different entry. The same participant should remain current. Set hidden and defeated flags deliberately The two checkboxes set exact booleans; they do not invert an unknown state. Defeated entries are skipped by forward next-turn processing. Clear both to restore the tutorial participant. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(! 'tokenId','actorId' .includes(v.identityType)) throw new Error('Use tokenId or actorId'); const identity={ v.identityType :v.id}; const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); return await api.combat.toggle({sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,...identity,hidden:v.hidden,defeated:v.defeated},write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The selected entry has the chosen flags. A hidden combat entry is absent for players. How to verify: Compare player/GM tracker, then clear defeated before testing a full turn cycle. Start or stop the disposable encounter Add at least two participants. Start creates an encounter identity and begins round1/turn0. Stop resets the active cursor/history but retains participants. Use only this tutorial encounter. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); const payload={sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version}; if(v.action==='start') return await api.combat.start(payload,write()); if(v.action==='stop') return await api.combat.stop(payload,write()); throw new Error('Choose start or stop'); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: start: active true, round1. stop: active false, round0. How to verify: Inspect encounterId and the native tracker after each intentional action. Select a specific current participant Start the encounter first, then use a participating identity. This selects its position without pretending that skipped turns ran normal forward effects. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(! 'tokenId','actorId' .includes(v.identityType)) throw new Error('Use tokenId or actorId'); const identity={ v.identityType :v.id}; const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); return await api.combat.setTurn({sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,...identity},write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The chosen participant is current in the tracker. How to verify: Compare current_name and the is_current flag against the selected ID. Advance or return one turn Start first. Next advances valid native turn clocks and skips defeated entries. An authorized player may end their own current turn; previous is GM-only and requires history. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); if(!before.active) throw new Error('Start combat first'); const payload={sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version}; if(v.direction==='next') return await api.combat.nextTurn(payload,write()); if(v.direction==='previous'){ if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required for previous turn'); return await api.combat.previousTurn(payload,write()); } throw new Error('Choose next or previous'); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: Current identity changes according to native order; previous returns the stored cursor when available. How to verify: Try next as the current controlling player and a different player. Only the former is allowed. Going back does not resurrect expired conditions or undo periodic effects. Advance or return one round Use next to move forward a round, then previous to inspect the native cursor behavior. Forward rounds can advance condition/effect clocks. Previous is navigation, not an undo of persisted effects. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); if(!before.active) throw new Error('Start combat first'); const payload={sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version}; if(v.direction==='next') return await api.combat.nextRound(payload,write()); if(v.direction==='previous') return await api.combat.previousRound(payload,write()); throw new Error('Choose next or previous'); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: Round changes within native bounds; the turn resets to the first entry. How to verify: Inspect round/turn and a timed condition from the token tutorial. Do not expect previous to restore consumed duration. Remove only a tutorial combat participant Stop the disposable encounter and remove its participants one at a time. This removes tracker membership, not the token or actor. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v) = { if(context.role!=='gm') throw new Error('GM required'); const read={signal}; const write=()= { if(signal?.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Mount closed'),{code:'cancelled'}); return {signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}; }; try { if(! 'tokenId','actorId' .includes(v.identityType)) throw new Error('Use tokenId or actorId'); const identity={ v.identityType :v.id}; if(!v.confirm) throw new Error('Confirm the tutorial participant'); const before=await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); return await api.combat.remove({sceneId:v.mapId,version:before.version,...identity},write()); } catch(problem) { if(problem.code==='conflict'&&!signal?.aborted) await api.combat.state({sceneId:v.mapId},read); throw problem; } } Expected result: The chosen identity leaves combat; native current/history handling remains consistent. How to verify: Confirm the token is still present, then clean it through the separate token removal recipe if desired. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Each business function remains responsible for revisions, permissions and transaction sequencing. manifest.json json { "id": "tutorial.combat-workshop", "name": "Combat workshop", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Build a working encounter laboratory covering participants, initiative, order, flags, turns, rounds and cleanup.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {recipes} from './recipes.mjs'; export default { start({styles}) { styles.use('styles.css'); }, register({register}) { register("table.interface", ({root,api,host,assets,storage,context,events,viewport,signal,onDispose}) = { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const button=doc.createElement('button'); button.type='button';button.className='tutorial-launcher'; button.textContent="Combat workshop"; root.append(button); for(const type of 'pointerdown','mousedown' )button.addEventListener(type,event= event.stopPropagation(),{signal}); let modal,pending=false; button.addEventListener('click',event= { event.stopPropagation(); if(modal?.isConnected) { modal.focus();return; } const panel=doc.createElement('section'); panel.className="tutorial-workbench-combat-workshop"; panel.setAttribute('role','dialog');panel.setAttribute('aria-modal','true'); panel.setAttribute('aria-label',button.textContent);panel.tabIndex=-1; const title=doc.createElement('h2');title.textContent=button.textContent;panel.append(title); const choose=doc.createElement('select');choose.setAttribute('aria-label','Action'); for(const recipe of recipes) { const option=doc.createElement('option');option.value=recipe.id;option.textContent=recipe.label;choose.append(option); } const form=doc.createElement('form'),fields=doc.createElement('div'); const description=doc.createElement('p'); const run=doc.createElement('button');run.type='submit';run.textContent='Run action'; const close=doc.createElement('button');close.type='button';close.textContent='Close'; const output=doc.createElement('pre');output.setAttribute('role','status');output.setAttribute('aria-live','polite'); form.append(description,fields,run,close,output);panel.append(choose,form); function renderFields(){ const recipe=recipes.find(item= item.id===choose.value);fields.replaceChildren(); description.textContent=recipe.description; for(const field of recipe.fields ) { const label=doc.createElement('label');label.textContent=field.label; const input=doc.createElement('input');input.name=field.name;input.type=field.type 'text'; if(field.type==='number')input.step=String(field.step??'any'); if(field.type==='checkbox')input.checked=!!field.value; else if(field.type!=='file')input.value=String(field.value??''); input.required=!!field.required; if(field.accept)input.accept=field.accept; label.append(input);fields.append(label); } output.textContent=''; } choose.addEventListener('change',renderFields,{signal});renderFields(); form.addEventListener('submit',async event= { event.preventDefault();if(pending)return; const recipe=recipes.find(item= item.id===choose.value),values={}; for(const input of fields.querySelectorAll('input')) { values input.name =input.type==='file'?input.files 0 :input.type==='checkbox'?input.checked:input.type==='number'?Number(input.value):input.value; } pending=true;choose.disabled=true;run.disabled=true;close.disabled=true; for(const input of fields.querySelectorAll('input'))input.disabled=true; output.textContent='Running…'; try { const value=await recipe.run({api,host,assets,storage,context,events,viewport,signal,onDispose},values); if(!signal.aborted)output.textContent=typeof value==='string'?value:JSON.stringify(value??null,null,2); } catch(error) { if(!signal.aborted)output.textContent=String(error.code error.message 'unavailable'); } finally { pending=false; if(!signal.aborted){choose.disabled=false;run.disabled=false;close.disabled=false;for(const input of fields.querySelectorAll('input'))input.disabled=false;} } },{signal}); close.addEventListener('click',()= void modal.close(),{signal}); modal=api.ui.openModal(panel,{canClose:()= !pending signal.aborted}); },{signal}); onDispose(()= {button.remove();if(modal)void modal.close();}); }); }, stop() {} }; recipes.mjs javascript export const recipes= { id:"inspect", label:"Inspect this scene encounter", description:"Paste the disposable scene ID. Permissions, failures and final test Every write is an explicit Run action. Reads use recipient projections; writes keep native permissions and fresh operation UUIDs. Scene update, object update, token move/configuration and combat use their real revision fields. Some native selection commands have no expected revision parameter in this release; the examples do not invent one. On conflict the recipe rereads current state and stops. Review it, then intentionally run a new operation. Multiple API calls are separate transactions: a completed earlier call is not rolled back if a later read fails.
