title: How to build item and inventory tools
summary: Create, organize, duplicate, share and edit original items with native revisions and permissions.
text: The project you will build Build an Expedition item tools module. First discover this campaign's registered types, create a Survey kit and a spare, then organize and grant access. The core has no generic actor inventory/equip transaction: these recipes manage campaign item documents; a system must own inventory rules and relationships. Every available item mutation is demonstrated below. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named items. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/items/items-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text items/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use a disposable campaign with an installed system declaring an item type, such as gear in the compendium-system tutorial. Create/duplicate/permissions/folder/deletion require GM; an item owner may update permitted data. The workbench uses concrete UUID inputs copied from its authorized outputs. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../items-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../items-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Expedition item tools. Close that menu and click Expedition item tools. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Inspect real item types and folders Choose this first and Run action. Copy a registered type ID from types; the creation recipe defaults to gear, supplied by the tutorial systems. javascript async ({api,signal}) = { return {...await api.items.state({}, {signal}),readableItems:await api.items.list({}, {signal})}; } Expected result: The authorized items, folder tree, registered types and isGM flag. A listing-only row has no readable body. How to verify: Compare the same state as GM and a read-only player; no hidden item data may appear. Create and duplicate an expedition kit Enter a real registered item type, then Run action once. Copy folderId, itemId and duplicateId from the result for the next recipes. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const state = await api.items.state({}, {signal}); if (!state.types.some(type = type.id === values.type)) throw new Error("Choose an item type registered by this campaign system"); const folder = await api.items.createFolder({name:"Expedition supplies",color:" 6498cc",parentId:null}, {signal}); const created = await api.items.create({name:"Survey kit",type:values.type,folderId:folder.id,data:{quantity:1,description:"An original compass and a blank notebook."},permissions:{default:"none"}}, {signal}); const duplicate = await api.items.duplicate({id:created.id,version:created.item.version,name:"Spare survey kit"}, {signal}); return {folderId:folder.id,itemId:created.id,duplicateId:duplicate.id}; } Expected result: A folder and two separate items containing original system-owned JSON. Each explicit run creates another set. How to verify: Open Items. Edit one kit and verify the duplicate remains independent. Edit and move the kit Use itemId, set a name/quantity and paste the created folderId, or leave the destination blank to move to root. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const current = await api.items.get(values.id, {}, {signal}); return api.items.update({id:current.id,version:current.version,name:values.name,folderId:values.folderId null,data:{...current.data,quantity:values.quantity}}, {signal}); } Expected result: The item changes atomically using its current version; unrelated data keys remain. Quantity is an example system field, not a core inventory rule. How to verify: Verify the folder and quantity, then attempt a stale direct payload from a second session: the server must report conflict. Grant reading or editing deliberately As GM enter the kit UUID. Use read for the default grant or a real member UUID for a specific override; owner grants editing. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const current = await api.items.get(values.id, {}, {signal}); const permissions = {...current.permissions, values.userId "default" :values.level}; return api.items.setPermissions({id:current.id,version:current.version,permissions}, {signal}); } Expected result: Versioned permission changes. limited permits listing rather than opening; none removes the selected grant. How to verify: Test read, limited and none in a player session. A reader cannot update data; a hidden button is not the security boundary. Rename or reparent the folder Paste folderId. A blank parent keeps this folder at root; another campaign folder UUID reparents it. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { return api.items.updateFolder({id:values.id,name:values.name,parentId:values.parentId null,color:" 6498cc"}, {signal}); } Expected result: The folder is renamed/moved; the server rejects parent cycles and foreign-campaign IDs. Folder commands have no version field in this contract. How to verify: Refresh Items, inspect the tree and try setting the folder as its own parent. Delete the spare kit Use only duplicateId from this demonstration. This action deletes that item and requires GM. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const current = await api.items.get(values.id, {}, {signal}); return api.items.delete({id:current.id,version:current.version}, {signal}); } Expected result: The spare disappears; the original kit remains. How to verify: Refresh the directory and confirm the original UUID still opens. Remove the demonstration folder Move items you want to retain to root with the update recipe before removing your test folder. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { return api.items.deleteFolder({id:values.id}, {signal}); } Expected result: The selected folder is removed through the native service. How to verify: Refresh Items and inspect remaining items/folders instead of assuming client-side state stayed current. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Each business function remains responsible for revisions, permissions and transaction sequencing. manifest.json json { "id": "tutorial.items", "name": "Expedition item tools", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Create, organize, duplicate, share and edit original items with native revisions and permissions.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {recipes} from './recipes.mjs'; export default { start({styles}) { styles.use('styles.css'); }, register({register}) { register("table.interface", ({root,api,host,assets,storage,context,events,viewport,signal,onDispose}) = { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const button=doc.createElement('button'); button.type='button';button.className='tutorial-launcher'; button.textContent="Expedition item tools"; root.append(button); for(const type of 'pointerdown','mousedown' )button.addEventListener(type,event= event.stopPropagation(),{signal}); let modal,pending=false; button.addEventListener('click',event= { event.stopPropagation(); if(modal?.isConnected) { modal.focus();return; } const panel=doc.createElement('section'); panel.className="tutorial-workbench-items"; panel.setAttribute('role','dialog');panel.setAttribute('aria-modal','true'); panel.setAttribute('aria-label',button.textContent);panel.tabIndex=-1; const title=doc.createElement('h2');title.textContent=button.textContent;panel.append(title); const choose=doc.createElement('select');choose.setAttribute('aria-label','Action'); for(const recipe of recipes) { const option=doc.createElement('option');option.value=recipe.id;option.textContent=recipe.label;choose.append(option); } const form=doc.createElement('form'),fields=doc.createElement('div'); const description=doc.createElement('p'); const run=doc.createElement('button');run.type='submit';run.textContent='Run action'; title: How to build deck and card tools
summary: Create reusable deck definitions, draw, reveal, move, transfer and recover cards with real ownership.
text: The project you will build Build Harbor card tools with original signaling cards. Choose a text-only deck or define a reusable two-card deck with optional uploaded front/back images. Draw to your hand, place/reveal/move a card, take it back, give it to another member, discard/return and finally shuffle/reset/delete the test instance. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named cards. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/cards/cards-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text cards/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use a disposable campaign, GM account and one player account. A scene is needed for table placement; Inspect returns authorized scene IDs. GM creates definitions/instances and manages decks. A player with a deck read grant can draw to their own hand and control their own cards; knowing a UUID does not grant control. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../cards-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../cards-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Harbor card tools. Close that menu and click Harbor card tools. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Find decks, your hand and scene cards Run without a scene first. Copy a scene UUID from scenes, run again with it, and keep the IDs/versions from hand or cards. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const maps = await api.maps.state({}, {signal}); const cards = await api.cards.state(values.sceneId ? {sceneId:values.sceneId} : {}, {signal}); return {scenes:maps.maps.map(row= ({id:row.id,name:row.name})),...cards}; } Expected result: Authorized decks, this account's hand and cards on the chosen scene. Private faces remain filtered. How to verify: Compare recipient and nonrecipient accounts. A deck count does not reveal concealed front images. Create a text-only deck Run once as GM. This route creates an instance directly, without image assets or a reusable definition. Copy id as your deck UUID. javascript async ({api,signal}) = { return api.cards.create({name:"Harbor signals",cards: "Blue lantern","Return to harbor","Hold position" }, {signal}); } Expected result: A three-card deck instance. Another explicit run creates another deck. How to verify: Inspect draw_count 3 in the state recipe and find the native deck list. Define and instantiate a deck with optional artwork Choose original PNG/JPEG/WebP images or leave both files empty. The host uploads real File objects, defines two cards and creates an instance. Keep deckDefinitionId to instantiate another copy with the same public method. javascript async ({api,host,signal},values) = { const front = values.front ? await host.call("card.asset.upload", {purpose:"card_front",file:values.front}, {signal}) : null; const back = values.back ? await host.call("card.asset.upload", {purpose:"card_back",file:values.back}, {signal}) : null; const definition = await api.cards.define({name:"Reusable harbor signals",default_back_asset_id:back?.assetId ?? null,cards: {name:"Blue lantern",front_asset_id:front?.assetId ?? null}, {name:"Hold position",front_asset_id:front?.assetId ?? null}, }, {signal}); const instance = await api.cards.instantiate({deck_definition_id:definition.deck.id}, {signal}); return {deckDefinitionId:definition.deck.id,deckId:instance.id}; } Expected result: Reusable definition plus a separate two-card instance. Images belong to the campaign/uploader and are referenced by assetId. How to verify: Draw a card and compare private hand versus revealed scene presentation. Image limits are 10 MiB and 16 megapixels; the native server converts valid images to WebP. Find a recipient for a transfer Use this if the host has the ready-check/lobby feature enabled. Copy a real member userId for Draw recipient or Give. If disabled, obtain the authorized member UUID from your controlled test fixture; do not guess IDs. javascript async ({api,signal}) = { const lobby = await api.table.lobby({signal}); return lobby.members.map(row= ({userId:row.user_id,name:row.name,role:row.role})); } Expected result: Current campaign member IDs and names, without account credentials. How to verify: Give to an actual participant. A UUID from another campaign must fail. Draw cards into a real destination Use a deck instance UUID, count 1 and destination hand for the first run. scene/table need a scene UUID. chat deliberately publishes a card event and discards the drawn cards; use it only when that is the intended action. Only GM can choose another recipient. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { return api.cards.draw({deck_instance_id:values.deckId,count:values.count,destination:values.destination, ...(values.sceneId ? {sceneId:values.sceneId} : {}),...(values.recipient ? {recipient:values.recipient} : {}), face_state:"face_up",x:140,y:140}, {signal}); } Expected result: The selected count leaves the draw pile and enters the requested destination. A direct hand draw remains private to its owner. How to verify: Inspect draw_count and hand/cards as the recipient; insufficient cards fail instead of returning a partial draw. Play, move, reveal and transfer a controlled card After Draw to your hand, paste its card UUID and a scene UUID. Run place, then move, flip and take one at a time. Give needs a real recipient; switch to that account to continue. Discard sends to discard; return sends back to draw. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const state = await api.cards.state(values.sceneId ? {sceneId:values.sceneId} : {}, {signal}); const card = ...state.hand,...state.cards .find(row= row.id===values.id); if (!card?.canControl) throw Object.assign(new Error("Card is not controllable in this view"),{code:"permission_denied"}); const payload = {id:card.id,version:card.version}; switch (values.action) { case "place": return api.cards.place({...payload,sceneId:values.sceneId,x:values.x,y:values.y,reveal:true,scale:1,z_index:0}, {signal}); case "move": return api.cards.move({...payload,x:values.x,y:values.y,rotation:45,scale:1,z_index:1}, {signal}); case "flip": return api.cards.flip(payload, {signal}); case "take": return api.cards.take(payload, {signal}); case "give": return api.cards.give({...payload,recipient:values.recipient}, {signal}); case "discard": return api.cards.discard(payload, {signal}); case "return": return api.cards.return(payload, {signal}); default: throw new Error("Choose a documented card action"); } } Expected result: Each click reads the current card version and applies exactly one action. Move requires a scene card; ownership and face visibility remain server-enforced. How to verify: Follow hand → scene → hand → another participant, then discard/return a controlled card. Read fresh state after every action. Another player cannot control your hand. Shuffle, gather or delete the test deck As GM use the instance UUID. shuffle randomizes the draw pile; reset gathers all cards, clears owners/scenes/faces and shuffles; deleteDeck removes the instance. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const deck = (await api.cards.state({}, {signal})).decks.find(row= row.id===values.deckId); if (!deck) throw new Error("Deck unavailable"); const payload={deck_instance_id:deck.id,version:deck.version}; switch(values.action) { case "shuffle": return api.cards.shuffle(payload, {signal}); case "reset": return api.cards.reset(payload, {signal}); case "deleteDeck": return api.cards.deleteDeck(payload, {signal}); default: throw new Error("Choose shuffle, reset or deleteDeck"); } } Expected result: A version-checked deck operation. Definitions and reusable image assets have their own lifetime. How to verify: Draw/discard, then reset and confirm all cards return to draw. Delete only your disposable deck and verify it disappears. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Each business function remains responsible for revisions, permissions and transaction sequencing. manifest.json json { "id": "tutorial.cards", "name": "Harbor card tools", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Create reusable deck definitions, draw, reveal, move, transfer and recover cards with real ownership.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {recipes} from './recipes.mjs'; reset gathers all cards, clears owners/scenes/faces and shuffles; deleteDeck removes the instance.", fields: { "name": "deckId", "label": "Deck instance UUID", "value": "", "type": "text", "required": true }, { "name": "action", "label": "Action: shuffle, reset or deleteDeck", "value": "shuffle", "type": "text", "required": true } , run:async ({api,signal},values) = { const deck = (await api.cards.state({}, {signal})).decks.find(row= row.id===values.deckId); if (!deck) throw new Error("Deck unavailable"); const payload={deck_instance_id:deck.id,version:deck.version}; switch(values.action) { case "shuffle": return api.cards.shuffle(payload, {signal}); case "reset": return api.cards.reset(payload, {signal}); Permissions, failures and final test Follow the recipes in order and inspect fresh state after each click. Use the definition route and verify its instance has two cards; use direct create for three text-only cards. Compare the two accounts before and after Give. Test hidden fronts, face-down scene cards, wrong ownership, stale card/deck versions and insufficient draws. A card operation checks the card version; shuffle/reset/delete checks the deck version; draw is a native serialized draw action. Each repeated successful Draw removes another card, and Import-like creation actions are not a refresh. After an unknown write result inspect state before running again. title: How to build scene audio and soundtrack tools
summary: Configure native tracks, playlists, spatial sources, scene voices and timed scores with the correct revisions.
text: The project you will build Build Harbor audio tools. Prepare two original tracks through the real Library, then configure a harbor ambience, operate one scene voice, compose arrival music, navigate its score and position a spatial beacon. These are separate layers of audio state, with different revisions and listener projections. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named audio. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/audio/audio-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text audio/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use a disposable campaign, a scene and two short original WAV/Ogg/FLAC/MP3 files. As GM open the native table Library and use Ambient audio or Sound effect to upload them; this browser domain API has no uploadTrack method, so the package starts from existing tracks. Inspect returns UUIDs. Click Enable audio on each client and check local volume. All audio mutations require GM; players receive only their authorized listening projection. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../audio-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../audio-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Harbor audio tools. Close that menu and click Harbor audio tools. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Inspect tracks, scene transport and score revisions Prepare original audio through the native Library. Run without a scene to discover scene UUIDs, then run again with the chosen one. A GM may specify an existing token UUID to preview its spatial listening position. Copy track, playlist and source IDs from this result. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const maps = await api.maps.state({}, {signal}); const audio = await api.audio.state({...(values.sceneId ? {sceneId:values.sceneId} : {}),...(values.previewTokenId ? {previewTokenId:values.previewTokenId} : {})}, {signal}); return {scenes:maps.maps.map(row= ({id:row.id,name:row.name})),...audio}; } Expected result: scenes, tracks, playlists, spatialSounds, playback, score, version and serverTime. Ambient commands use top-level version; score commands use score.version. How to verify: Players only receive related tracks. GM spatial effectiveGain is zero without an eligible preview listener; that is not a missing sound source. Configure a real track Paste a native-uploaded track UUID. Set music/ambience/effect, gain 0–1 and loop. effect always disables looping on the server. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const track=(await api.audio.state({}, {signal})).tracks.find(row= row.id===values.trackId); if (!track) throw new Error("Upload an original track through the native Library first"); return api.audio.updateTrack({id:track.id,version:track.version,name:"Harbor atmosphere",kind:values.kind,volume:values.volume,loop:values.loop}, {signal}); } Expected result: The track metadata changes with its current version; no upload API or external audio URL is invented. How to verify: Inspect the library again and play it with the next recipe. Changing defaults is different from changing an existing scene voice. Control one scene voice Run play, pause, seek, play, setVolume and stop as separate explicit actions. Click Enable audio on this device before expecting sound. Seek must stay within the actual track duration. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const state=await api.audio.state({sceneId:values.sceneId}, {signal}); const payload={sceneId:values.sceneId,trackId:values.trackId,version:state.version}; switch(values.action) { case "play": return api.audio.play({...payload,volume:values.volume,loop:true}, {signal}); case "pause": return api.audio.pause(payload, {signal}); case "stop": return api.audio.stop(payload, {signal}); case "seek": return api.audio.seek({...payload,position:values.position}, {signal}); case "setVolume": return api.audio.setVolume({...payload,volume:values.volume}, {signal}); default: throw new Error("Choose a documented scene transport action"); } } Expected result: The scene voice uses authoritative server-clock position and a fresh transport version. Local device mute/volume remains independent. How to verify: Compare two clients on the scene. A paused voice retains position; stop returns it to zero. A stale version must conflict. Compose an arrival playlist or simultaneous preset Paste two native track UUIDs and choose playlist for sequential music or preset for simultaneous looping layers. Duration must be 1–86400 seconds. Run once and copy the returned id. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { return api.audio.createPlaylist({name:"Harbor arrival",kind:values.kind,mode:"sequential",fade:2,tracks: {soundId:values.trackId,duration:values.duration,gain:0.5}, {soundId:values.secondTrackId,duration:values.duration,gain:0.35}, }, {signal}); } Expected result: A composition definition with two explicit soundId/duration/gain entries and a two-second transition fade. It does not start playback. How to verify: Inspect playlists; then start it with the score recipe. Each repeated create is a separate definition. Revise a composition without discarding its tracks Use the created composition id. This edits the definition, retaining its track list and kind while changing name, mode and fade. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const current=(await api.audio.state({}, {signal})).playlists.find(row= row.id===values.id); if (!current) throw new Error("Composition unavailable"); return api.audio.updatePlaylist({id:current.id,version:current.version,name:"Harbor arrival revised",kind:current.kind,mode:"shuffle",fade:1,tracks:current.tracks}, {signal}); } Expected result: A versioned definition update. Already running score snapshots do not rewrite themselves. How to verify: Inspect the definition, then explicitly start it again to use the revised definition. Start the composition as a score Choose the scene and the composition UUID. The kind comes from the actual definition; it is not guessed from its name. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const state=await api.audio.state({sceneId:values.sceneId}, {signal}); const definition=state.playlists.find(row= row.id===values.id); if (!definition) throw new Error("Composition unavailable"); return api.audio.startScore({sceneId:values.sceneId,id:definition.id,kind:definition.kind,repeat:true,expectedVersion:state.score.version}, {signal}); } Expected result: A playing score with its own revision and timed playbacks. Starting another composition can crossfade from the current one. How to verify: Inspect score.state/playbacks on two clients. Use expectedVersion from score, not the ambient transport version. Pause, resume, navigate and stop the score Start a playlist first. Run pause, resume, next, previous, then stop one at a time. next/previous apply to playlist, not a simultaneous preset. A stopped composition needs Start rather than Resume. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const state=await api.audio.state({sceneId:values.sceneId}, {signal}); const payload={sceneId:values.sceneId,expectedVersion:state.score.version}; switch(values.action) { case "pause": return api.audio.pauseScore(payload, {signal}); case "resume": return api.audio.resumeScore(payload, {signal}); case "next": return api.audio.nextScore(payload, {signal}); case "previous": return api.audio.previousScore(payload, {signal}); case "stop": return api.audio.stopScore(payload, {signal}); default: throw new Error("Choose a documented score action"); } } Expected result: Each action preserves the server timeline and checks the score revision. How to verify: Inspect position/state after each action; a missing score or wrong kind fails clearly. Place an audible harbor beacon Enter scene, track and logical scene-pixel center. Radius is in the scene's configured distance units. The eligible token/listener determines received gain. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { return api.audio.createSpatialSound({sceneId:values.sceneId,trackId:values.trackId,x:values.x,y:values.y,radius:values.radius,gain:0.7,falloff:"smooth",loop:true,enabled:true,occlusion:true}, {signal}); } Expected result: A native spatial sound source, with smooth falloff and wall occlusion. This is separate from an ambient voice or composition. How to verify: Use a player-controlled token near/far; as GM set previewTokenId in Inspect. Confirm effectiveGain changes and hidden data remains filtered. Adjust the source range or disable it Use the created source UUID in its own scene. This preserves the source track/location while changing radius, enabled and falloff. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const state=await api.audio.state({sceneId:values.sceneId}, {signal}); const source=state.spatialSounds.find(row= row.id===values.id); if (!source) throw new Error("Source unavailable in this scene"); return api.audio.updateSpatialSound({sceneId:values.sceneId,id:source.id,version:source.version,radius:values.radius,enabled:values.enabled,falloff:"linear"}, {signal}); } Expected result: Versioned native source edit, without restarting the entire campaign audio library. How to verify: Inspect source fields and effectiveGain. With enabled false the effective gain is zero. Remove the test spatial source Use only the source created for this tutorial. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const source=(await api.audio.state({sceneId:values.sceneId}, {signal})).spatialSounds.find(row= row.id===values.id); if (!source) throw new Error("Source unavailable"); return api.audio.deleteSpatialSound({sceneId:values.sceneId,id:source.id,version:source.version}, {signal}); } Expected result: The source disappears; its reusable track remains in the library. How to verify: Refresh spatialSounds and confirm that track metadata is still available to GM. Remove the test composition Stop its score first, then delete only the demonstration definition. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const current=(await api.audio.state({}, {signal})).playlists.find(row= row.id===values.id); if (!current) throw new Error("Composition unavailable"); return api.audio.deletePlaylist({id:current.id,version:current.version}, {signal}); } Expected result: The composition definition is removed with its version. Track files remain reusable. How to verify: Refresh playlists and confirm the native track library remains intact. Delete only the disposable uploaded audio Use an original track uploaded for this tutorial after finishing playback/source/composition tests. This deletes its file and detaches native references. javascript async ({api,signal},values) = { const track=(await api.audio.state({}, {signal})).tracks.find(row= row.id===values.trackId); if (!track) throw new Error("Track unavailable"); return api.audio.deleteTrack({id:track.id,version:track.version}, {signal}); } Expected result: Versioned track removal with native reference cleanup. How to verify: Refresh tracks, playlists and scene sources. This action is not a volume control or merely hiding an asset. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Each business function remains responsible for revisions, permissions and transaction sequencing. manifest.json json { "id": "tutorial.audio", "name": "Harbor audio tools", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Configure native tracks, playlists, spatial sources, scene voices and timed scores with the correct revisions.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {recipes} from './recipes.mjs'; export default { start({styles}) { styles.use('styles.css'); }, register({register}) { register("table.interface", ({root,api,host,assets,storage,context,events,viewport,signal,onDispose}) = { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const button=doc.createElement('button'); button.type='button';button.className='tutorial-launcher'; button.textContent="Harbor audio tools"; root.append(button); for(const type of 'pointerdown','mousedown' )button.addEventListener(type,event= event.stopPropagation(),{signal}); let modal,pending=false; button.addEventListener('click',event= { event.stopPropagation(); if(modal?.isConnected) { modal.focus();return; } const panel=doc.createElement('section'); panel.className="tutorial-workbench-audio"; panel.setAttribute('role','dialog');panel.setAttribute('aria-modal','true'); panel.setAttribute('aria-label',button.textContent);panel.tabIndex=-1; const title=doc.createElement('h2');title.textContent=button.textContent;panel.append(title); const choose=doc.createElement('select');choose.setAttribute('aria-label','Action'); for(const recipe of recipes) { const option=doc.createElement('option');option.value=recipe.id;option.textContent=recipe.label;choose.append(option); } const form=doc.createElement('form'),fields=doc.createElement('div'); const description=doc.createElement('p'); const run=doc.createElement('button');run.type='submit';run.textContent='Run action'; for(const field of recipe.fields ) { const label=doc.createElement('label');label.textContent=field.label; const input=doc.createElement('input');input.name=field.name;input.type=field.type 'text'; if(field.type==='number')input.step=String(field.step??'any'); if(field.type==='checkbox')input.checked=!!field.value; else if(field.type!=='file')input.value=String(field.value??''); input.required=!!field.required; if(field.accept)input.accept=field.accept; label.append(input);fields.append(label); } output.textContent=''; } choose.addEventListener('change',renderFields,{signal});renderFields(); form.addEventListener('submit',async event= { event.preventDefault();if(pending)return; const recipe=recipes.find(item= item.id===choose.value),values={}; if(!signal.aborted)output.textContent=typeof value==='string'?value:JSON.stringify(value??null,null,2); } catch(error) { if(!signal.aborted)output.textContent=String(error.code error.message 'unavailable'); } finally { pending=false; if(!signal.aborted){choose.disabled=false;run.disabled=false;close.disabled=false;for(const input of fields.querySelectorAll('input'))input.disabled=false;} } },{signal}); close.addEventListener('click',()= void modal.close(),{signal}); modal=api.ui.openModal(panel,{canClose:()= !pending signal.aborted}); },{signal}); onDispose(()= {button.remove();if(modal)void modal.close();}); }); }, stop() {} }; recipes.mjs javascript export const recipes= { id:"inspect", label:"Inspect tracks, scene transport and score revisions", description:"Prepare original audio through the native Library. title: How to build chat, dice and ready-check tools
summary: Create a working module that sends messages, publishes rolls, moderates chat, searches documents and updates readiness.
text: The project you will build Build a native-modal workbench with twelve independent actions. Begin with Read history, send a public message, test whisper/GM/emote delivery, roll public and secret dice, then inspect and update the lobby. Moderation is intentionally explicit and restricted to a disposable campaign. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named chat-dice. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/chat-dice/chat-dice-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text chat-dice/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use a disposable campaign with two members and one original actor. Enable native ready checks and command search through the installation settings if you want those recipes; their APIs report permission_denied when the feature is disabled. Copy a player display name from the table and document UUIDs from native lists. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../chat-dice-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../chat-dice-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Chat, dice and lobby. Close that menu and click Chat, dice and lobby. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Read visible chat history Leave Scene UUID empty to use the broadcast scene, or enter an authorized scene UUID. The returned array is the visible recent history, not every message ever sent. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= api.chat.history(v.sceneId.trim()?{sceneId:v.sceneId.trim()}:{},{signal}) Expected result: Message IDs, authors, text and visibility for this account. How to verify: Compare sender, whisper recipient and an unrelated player. Hidden messages must be absent. Send one public message Enter original text. This recipe rejects a leading slash so the public action cannot accidentally become a command. Optional scene selection uses sceneId. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const text=v.text.trim();if(text.startsWith('/'))throw new Error('Use a dedicated command recipe.');return api.chat.send({text,...(v.sceneId.trim()?{sceneId:v.sceneId.trim()}:{})},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});} Expected result: One visible chat message and its server ID. How to verify: Check native chat as two table members. Run again only if you intend a second message. Send a recipient-bound whisper Enter the exact display name of a member in this campaign, including spaces. Native /w parsing resolves members, not a client-supplied audience list. Identical display names can resolve multiple matching members. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= api.chat.send({text:'/w '+v.recipient.trim()+' '+v.text.trim()},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}) Expected result: The server returns a whisper visible to sender and matching recipients. How to verify: Read history as recipient and nonrecipient; only the former receives the content. Use unique test names. Send a message to the GMs The /gm native command addresses campaign GMs plus the sender. It is a chat command, not a visibility field on chat.send. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= api.chat.send({text:'/gm '+v.text.trim()},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}) Expected result: A recipient-filtered message in GM and sender chat. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Publish an emote Enter an action. The native /me command marks the message as an emote and retains normal public delivery. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= api.chat.send({text:'/me '+v.text.trim()},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()}) Expected result: A chat message with metadata.emote true. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Roll and publish public or GM-only dice Enter an expression supported by the native parser, label and repeat count. GM-only result chooses visibility gm. This action persists and publishes a roll; it is not a local calculator. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {if(!Number.isInteger(v.repeat) v.repeat<1 v.repeat 12)throw new Error('Repeat must be 1 to 12.');return api.dice.roll(v.expression,{label:v.label,repeat:v.repeat,visibility:v.secret?'gm':'public'},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});} Expected result: One durable submission containing the requested roll(s), with the selected audience. How to verify: Compare public and GM-only rolls in two accounts. Reject repeat 0 or 13. A retry of the same logical submission must reuse its original UUID rather than roll again. Moderate one message As GM, copy the numeric ID from history. This removes that message content and attachments while preserving retry identity. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');if(!/^\d+$/.test(v.messageId))throw new Error('Use the numeric chat ID from history.');return api.chat.remove(v.messageId,{signal});} Expected result: A removed count; subsequent history omits that message. How to verify: Moderate only a synthetic message created for this tutorial. A player must be rejected by the server. Clear the disposable campaign chat Use only a disposable campaign. Type CLEAR CHAT. This GM moderation operation is campaign-wide, including scenes, rather than just the history currently displayed. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');if(v.confirmation!=='CLEAR CHAT')throw new Error('Type CLEAR CHAT to clear the whole campaign chat.');return api.chat.clear({signal});} Expected result: All undeleted messages in this campaign are removed. How to verify: Read history in another scene and confirm it is also cleared. Submission receipts remain. Inspect the ready check and selectable actors The installation must have its native ready check enabled. Read members, summary and the actors this account may select. javascript async ({api,signal})= api.table.lobby({signal}) Expected result: members, actors and summary.ready/total. How to verify: Compare a read-only actor with an actor owned by this player; only controllable actors are selectable. Update this member’s ready state Set the checkbox, a selectable actor UUID from the lobby result, and assets_state. Leave actor UUID blank to clear the selection. The API chooses the current member; no user ID can impersonate someone else. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {if(! 'unknown','loading','ready','error' .includes(v.assets))throw new Error('Choose a native assets_state.');if(v.actorId.trim()){const lobby=await api.table.lobby({signal});if(!lobby.actors.some(actor= actor.id===v.actorId.trim()))throw new Error('Actor is not selectable.');}return api.table.updateLobby({is_ready:v.ready,assets_state:v.assets,selected_actor_id:v.actorId.trim() null},{signal});} Expected result: The returned lobby has this member’s new selection and readiness. How to verify: Use two accounts: only the current member’s row changes. Unknown actor or assets state must fail. Search all seven document kinds Use at least two characters. Blank kind searches all; accepted filters are actor, item, journal, quest, quest_board, scene and compendium. A result is a search projection with title, kind, snippet and actions, not a full document. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const kind=v.kind.trim();if(! '','actor','item','journal','quest','quest_board','scene','compendium' .includes(kind))throw new Error('Unknown search kind.');return api.table.search(v.query,{...(kind?{kind}:{}),signal});} Expected result: An array of up to 20 authorized matches. How to verify: Search the same private title as GM and player; it must be absent for the player. Test quest separately from journal. Revalidate a recent document Use one previously read result ID. Recent references use type journal for quests and quest boards, while search kind distinguishes those categories. Up to 12 unique references can be supplied in an array. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {if(! 'actor','item','journal','scene','compendium' .includes(v.type))throw new Error('Invalid reference type.');return api.table.search('',{recent: {id:v.id,type:v.type} ,signal});} Expected result: Only references still readable by the current member are returned. How to verify: Remove the player’s read permission, then repeat the same recent reference. It must disappear. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Each business function remains responsible for revisions, permissions and transaction sequencing. manifest.json json { "id": "tutorial.chat-dice", "name": "Chat, dice and lobby", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Create a working module that sends messages, publishes rolls, moderates chat, searches documents and updates readiness.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {recipes} from './recipes.mjs'; export default { start({styles}) { styles.use('styles.css'); }, register({register}) { register("table.interface", ({root,api,host,assets,storage,context,events,viewport,signal,onDispose}) = { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const button=doc.createElement('button'); button.type='button';button.className='tutorial-launcher'; button.textContent="Chat, dice and lobby"; root.append(button); for(const type of 'pointerdown','mousedown' )button.addEventListener(type,event= event.stopPropagation(),{signal}); let modal,pending=false; button.addEventListener('click',event= { event.stopPropagation(); if(modal?.isConnected) { modal.focus();return; } const panel=doc.createElement('section'); panel.className="tutorial-workbench-chat-dice"; panel.setAttribute('role','dialog');panel.setAttribute('aria-modal','true'); panel.setAttribute('aria-label',button.textContent);panel.tabIndex=-1; const title=doc.createElement('h2');title.textContent=button.textContent;panel.append(title); const choose=doc.createElement('select');choose.setAttribute('aria-label','Action'); for(const recipe of recipes) { const option=doc.createElement('option');option.value=recipe.id;option.textContent=recipe.label;choose.append(option); } finally { pending=false; if(!signal.aborted){choose.disabled=false;run.disabled=false;close.disabled=false;for(const input of fields.querySelectorAll('input'))input.disabled=false;} } },{signal}); close.addEventListener('click',()= void modal.close(),{signal}); modal=api.ui.openModal(panel,{canClose:()= !pending signal.aborted}); },{signal}); onDispose(()= {button.remove();if(modal)void modal.close();}); }); }, stop() {} }; recipes.mjs javascript export const recipes= { id:"history", label:"Read visible chat history", description:"Leave Scene UUID empty to use the broadcast scene, or enter an authorized scene UUID. Mutation submissions use a fresh UUID, except lobby/moderation whose native service signatures do not use receipts. To retry the same chat or dice submission in your own integration, retain its UUID and identical payload; clicking Run again is a new logical action. Use two accounts for private audiences and revoked document access. On conflict, read and review state before a new command. The server filters membership, scenes, messages and resource access; disabled buttons are not authorization. How to use AI to extend this project text Extend this complete chat-dice project on Gravewright 0.3.0 with one feature . Read modules/frontend.py, chat/services.py, dice/services.py and table/services.py. Keep native chat command parsing, real lobby snake_case payloads, audience filtering, request UUIDs, permissions and cancellation. Show all files and validate with two users, private messages, stale access and disabled installation features. All tutorials (docs:tutorial-index) · API (docs:api)

title: How to create quest automation and quest-board actions
summary: Create and read a real quest, advance objectives, assign actors and manage every board relationship.
text: The project you will build Build a module for an original harbor quest and job board. Run Create quest, copy its ID, read objective IDs, mark completion and assign a character. Create a board, link the quest, create another through the board, pin and reorder both, then unlink without deleting content. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named quests. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/quests/quests-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text quests/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use a disposable campaign as GM. Obtain a readable actor UUID from Actors. For sharing, use the access and presentation recipes in journal management (docs:tutorial-journal-management); board visibility and player-visible quest statuses both matter. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../quests-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../quests-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Quest and board tools. Close that menu and click Quest and board tools. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Create a complete original quest As GM, enter a title, summary and objective. Create allocates an empty quest; the next independent command fills its complete original data. If setup fails, the error includes the created ID so you can repair that document. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required for the complete seed.');const created=await api.journals.create({title:v.title,journal_type:'quest'},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});try{const data={status:'available',public:{summary:v.summary},gm:{},objectives: {id:'beacon_platform',text:v.objective,completed:false,optional:false,visibleToPlayers:true,sortOrder:10} ,rewards: ,tags: 'tutorial' ,assignees: };await api.journals.update({journal_id:created.journal_id,version:created.version,title:v.title,visibility:'private',data},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(created.journal_id,{}, {signal});}catch(error){throw new Error('Quest '+created.journal_id+' was created; setup failed: '+(error.code error.message)+'. Inspect it before creating another.');}} Expected result: A private available quest with one visible objective and its UUID/version. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Read quest fields and objective IDs Paste the created journal_id. Copy quest.objectives .id for the completion action; the GM projection also includes gm notes and secrets that players never receive. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(row.type!=='quest')throw new Error('Choose a quest.');return row;} Expected result: The authorized quest projection, not a raw ORM document. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Advance a quest status with its revision Choose one of the six status values. This reads the current version once, performs one command and reads the result. A conflict is reported rather than retried. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(row.type!=='quest' ! 'draft','available','active','completed','failed','archived' .includes(v.status))throw new Error('Choose a quest and valid status.');await api.journals.setStatus({journal_id:row.id,version:row.version,status:v.status},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(row.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: The same quest with the requested status and a newer version. How to verify: Move an available quest to draft and compare its visibility through a player’s board. Complete or reopen an objective Use the ID from the read recipe, not the objective label. Completed is a boolean. The server prevents players from choosing hidden objective IDs. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(row.type!=='quest')throw new Error('Choose a quest.');await api.journals.setObjective({journal_id:row.id,version:row.version,objective_id:v.objectiveId,completed:v.completed},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(row.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: Only the chosen objective completion flag changes. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Assign a readable character without dropping existing assignments Use an actor UUID from the Actors directory or actor API. The recipe keeps visible assignees and adds one unique ID; the server preserves assignments hidden from non-GM editors. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {await api.actors.get(v.actorId,{}, {signal});const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(row.type!=='quest')throw new Error('Choose a quest.');await api.journals.assignCharacters({journal_id:row.id,version:row.version,assignees: ...new Set( ...(row.quest.assignees ),v.actorId ) },{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(row.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: quest.assignees includes the chosen character, within the 32-character limit. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Create an empty quest board Create a quest_board document. Its data is empty; links to quests are separate server-owned board entries. Copy its ID for the next actions. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const created=await api.journals.create({title:v.title,journal_type:'quest_board'},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(created.journal_id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: An empty board with board_entries and a document UUID. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Create and link a quest through the board Paste the board UUID. The native board-create command creates an available quest in the board folder and links it in one server operation. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const board=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(board.type!=='quest_board')throw new Error('Choose a quest board.');const result=await api.journals.createBoardQuest({journal_id:board.id,title:v.title},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return {result,board:await api.journals.get(board.id,{}, {signal})};} Expected result: created_quest_id plus the updated board entries. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Link an existing quest Use the board UUID and an existing readable quest UUID. This adds a board relationship; it does not copy quest content. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {await api.journals.addQuest({journal_id:v.id,quest_id:v.questId},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: The quest appears once in board_entries. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Pin or unpin a board card Use a quest already linked to the chosen board. Pinned is boolean; pinned entries are displayed before ordinary entries. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {await api.journals.pinQuest({journal_id:v.id,quest_id:v.questId,pinned:v.pinned},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: The chosen entry changes pinned, preserving quest data. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Reverse the complete board order As GM, read every entry and submit every quest ID exactly once in reversed sort_order. A player’s filtered list is not a complete order. The native command validates the set and rejects concurrent membership changes. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('Use GM to read the complete board order.');const board=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(board.type!=='quest_board')throw new Error('Choose a quest board.');const ids= ...board.board_entries .sort((a,b)= a.sort_order-b.sort_order).map(entry= entry.quest_id).reverse();await api.journals.reorderQuests({journal_id:board.id,ordered_quest_ids:ids},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(board.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: All sort_order positions change; pinned grouping still has display priority. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Unlink a card while preserving its quest Choose the board and quest relationship to remove. This is not journal deletion. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {await api.journals.removeQuest({journal_id:v.id,quest_id:v.questId},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return {board:await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal}),quest:await api.journals.get(v.questId,{}, {signal})};} Expected result: The board no longer links it, while the original quest remains readable. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. 4. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. Permissions, failures and final test Creation plus setup uses separate commands, so a setup failure names the created UUID instead of pretending nothing happened. Repair that object before clicking Create again. Status/objective/assignment edits send the exact read version and never retry conflicts automatically. Board ordering requires every linked quest ID exactly once, including drafts visible to GM. The server enforces ownership and hides private quest fields. Verify as a player after changing draft/available status and explicit grants. How to use AI to extend this project text Extend the quests tutorial on Gravewright 0.3.0 with workflow . title: How to create, draw and reset weighted roll tables
summary: Build an original journal roll table, edit a weight without losing data and publish native draws with or without replacement.
text: The project you will build Create a two-entry harbor-weather table, inspect its real schema, change a weight, draw until it is exhausted and reset it. This uses journal_type roll_table rather than a compendium pack or a system-specific random table. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named roll-tables. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/roll-tables/roll-tables-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text roll-tables/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use a disposable campaign as GM and a second player account for audience checks. Keep all entry results original. Use an authorized scene UUID only if the draw should target that scene; otherwise the native broadcast context is used. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../roll-tables-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../roll-tables-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Roll table tools. Close that menu and click Roll table tools. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Create a weighted original roll table As GM, create journal_type roll_table and configure its two complete entries. Weights 3 and 1 give different probabilities. Without replacement, drawn entries stop being eligible until reset. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');const created=await api.journals.create({title:v.title,journal_type:'roll_table'},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});try{await api.journals.update({journal_id:created.journal_id,version:created.version,title:v.title,visibility:'private',data:{withReplacement:v.replacement,resultVisibility:v.secret?'gm':'public',entries: {id:'clear',name:'Clear sky',weight:3,result:'The beacon is visible across the bay.',active:true,drawn:false,sortOrder:10},{id:'fog',name:'Fog',weight:1,result:'The boats wait for the fog to lift.',active:true,drawn:false,sortOrder:20} }},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(created.journal_id,{}, {signal});}catch(error){throw new Error('Roll table '+created.journal_id+' exists; configuration failed: '+(error.code error.message)+'. Repair this table before creating another.');}} Expected result: A table with totalWeight 4, independent entry IDs and the chosen result audience. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Read weights, results and draw flags Use the table UUID. The projected roll_table contains entries and totalWeight; GM-only result text is removed for other members. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(row.type!=='roll_table')throw new Error('Choose a roll_table journal.');return row;} Expected result: Authorized entries with weight, active, drawn and sortOrder. How to verify: Give a player read access and compare a secret table. The player must receive empty result text and cannot roll it. Change one weight while preserving every other entry As GM, use the exact entry ID. Copy the complete projected table and alter one weight; totalWeight is derived and omitted from the submitted data. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required to preserve complete results.');if(!Number.isInteger(v.weight) v.weight<1 v.weight 1000000)throw new Error('Invalid weight.');const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(row.type!=='roll_table')throw new Error('Choose a roll_table.');const data=structuredClone(row.roll_table);if(!data.entries.some(entry= entry.id===v.entryId))throw new Error('Entry not found.');data.entries=data.entries.map(entry= entry.id===v.entryId?{...entry,weight:v.weight}:entry);delete data.totalWeight;await api.journals.update({journal_id:row.id,version:row.version,title:row.title,visibility:row.visibility,data},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(row.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: The chosen weight changes and a fresh totalWeight is computed. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Draw and publish one table result Run as GM. The native command uses a secure weighted draw, persists drawn when needed and publishes a chat result. Its payload uses mapId for an explicit scene. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');return api.journals.roll({journal_id:v.id,...(v.sceneId.trim()?{mapId:v.sceneId.trim()}:{})},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});} Expected result: The chosen entry and message_id; native chat shows its authorized result. How to verify: Without replacement, roll twice and verify distinct entries, then a third roll must fail until reset. Do not rerun after a lost response using a new UUID if the same draw is being retried. Reset drawn flags without changing results Use the exhausted table UUID. Reset changes drawn to false for every entry; it does not clear native chat or replace table text. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');await api.journals.reset({journal_id:v.id},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: The active entries are eligible again and totalWeight is restored. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. 4. Permissions, failures and final test Only GMs can roll or reset. A read-access player may inspect authorized metadata but receives no hidden result text for resultVisibility gm. With replacement false, two active entries allow two draws, then no entry remains. Reset restores eligibility without rerolling or clearing chat. How to use AI to extend this project text Extend roll-tables on Gravewright 0.3.0 with behavior . Read normalize_roll_table_data, journals.types.apply and the public browser mapping. title: How to create, organize and share journal documents
summary: Build native rich diaries, preserve pages when editing, organize folder trees and control access and presentations.
text: The project you will build Begin with the native directory read. Create an original diary, rename it without replacing its pages, move it through a folder tree, grant one player read access and present a public page. The final recipes delete only explicitly confirmed tutorial resources. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named journal-management. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/journal-management/journal-management-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text journal-management/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use a disposable campaign as GM for complete projections and destructive actions. Copy user UUIDs from members, folder UUIDs from folders and document UUIDs from journals. A diary page ID comes from sections .id, not a scene or actor ID. Targeted presentation requires the corresponding native installation feature. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../journal-management-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../journal-management-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Journal management tools. Close that menu and click Journal management tools. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Read documents, folders and campaign member IDs Run first as GM to obtain journals .id, folders .id and members .id. The last field is a user UUID for setAccess and presentation, not an actor UUID. Player projections omit the GM member directory and private content. javascript async ({api,signal})= api.journals.state({}, {signal}) Expected result: The authorized directory with native types, permissions and feature flags. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Create a real block-document diary Create a diary, then fill content using the supported gw-journal-doc-v1 envelope. Plain HTML or a Markdown string is not that rich-document format. Copy the returned ID. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const created=await api.journals.create({title:v.title,journal_type:'diary'},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});try{const doc=text= ({format:'gw-journal-doc-v1',version:1,doc:{type:'doc',content: {type:'paragraph',content: {type:'text',text} } }});await api.journals.update({journal_id:created.journal_id,version:created.version,title:v.title,data:{content:doc(v.body),cover:{},sections: ,gm:{}}},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(created.journal_id,{}, {signal});}catch(error){throw new Error('Diary '+created.journal_id+' exists; setup failed: '+(error.code error.message)+'. Inspect it before creating another.');}} Expected result: A private diary whose native editor displays the original paragraph. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Rename a diary without erasing its pages or GM notes As GM, reconstruct the write shape from the read projection: content_doc becomes content, cover_image becomes cover, and diary.gm becomes gm. Preserve sections and the exact read version. This example deliberately targets diary, not quest/table shapes. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('Use GM to preserve the full diary projection.');const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(row.type!=='diary')throw new Error('Choose a diary.');const data={content:row.content_doc,cover:row.cover_image,sections:row.sections,gm:row.diary.gm};await api.journals.update({journal_id:row.id,version:row.version,title:v.title,visibility:row.visibility,data},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(row.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: Only the title changes; all authorized page and GM data remains. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Move a document into a folder or the root As GM, use a folder UUID from the directory. Blank target selects the root. This changes organization rather than visibility or content. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {await api.journals.move({journal_id:v.id,target_folder_id:v.folderId.trim() null},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: The document folder_id becomes the target UUID or null. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Grant or revoke one member’s journal access Use members .id from the GM directory. none denies access, limited allows listing, read opens authorized content, and owner permits editing under server rules. This persists a grant, unlike a temporary presentation. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');if(! 'none','limited','read','owner' .includes(v.level))throw new Error('Invalid access level.');await api.journals.setAccess({journal_id:v.id,target_user_id:v.userId,access_level:v.level},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});} Expected result: A native per-user access grant for that journal. How to verify: Check the targeted player’s list and editor. GM-only blocks must remain hidden even after read access. Present a player-filtered document or public page Leave user UUID blank to present to everyone, or target one campaign user when targeted handouts are enabled. Optional page ID must refer to a public diary page. ownership unchanged avoids a permanent access change. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');const payload={journal_id:v.id,ownership:'unchanged',...(v.userId.trim()?{targets: v.userId.trim() }:{}),...(v.pageId.trim()?{page_id:v.pageId.trim()}:{})};return api.journals.present(payload,{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});} Expected result: A native presentation is delivered to recipients with short-lived read access and player-filtered content. How to verify: Confirm receipt in the targeted account and no delivery to another. Try a GM-only page and expect rejection. Create a folder with a validated color Enter a name and optionally an existing parent UUID. The native color is a six-digit hexadecimal string. Copy result.folder_id. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const result=await api.journals.createFolder({name:v.name,color:' c09a5a',parent_id:v.parentId.trim() null},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return {result,directory:await api.journals.state({}, {signal})};} Expected result: One new folder, attached to the selected parent. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Rename and recolor a folder Use the folder ID created above. This API requires both name and color, so send them explicitly. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {await api.journals.updateFolder({folder_id:v.folderId,name:v.name,color:v.color},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.state({}, {signal});} Expected result: The same folder ID with its new name and color. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Move a folder without creating cycles Choose an existing folder and new parent. A blank parent moves to root. The server rejects moving a folder into itself or a descendant. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {await api.journals.moveFolder({folder_id:v.folderId,target_parent_id:v.parentId.trim() null},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.state({}, {signal});} Expected result: The folder has a new parent_id while its children stay attached. How to verify: Create a child and attempt to move its parent into it; the operation must fail without changing the tree. Delete a folder while retaining its contents Use only the synthetic folder and type its exact name. Native deletion reparents its child folders and documents to its former parent. It does not recursively delete journals. javascript async ({api,signal},v)= {const state=await api.journals.state({}, {signal});const folder=state.folders.find(folder= folder.id===v.folderId);if(!folder)throw new Error('Folder not found.');if(v.confirmation!==folder.name)throw new Error('Type the exact folder name.');await api.journals.deleteFolder({folder_id:folder.id},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.state({}, {signal});} Expected result: The folder disappears, while its documents remain in the parent or root. How to verify: Open the native directory or document and compare its server state. Compare GM and player views; only authorized content may appear. Delete one disposable document and refresh the list As GM, type the exact title of the tutorial document. This deletes that journal and related native references; it is different from removing a board link. javascript async ({api,context,signal},v)= {if(context.role!=='gm')throw new Error('GM required.');const row=await api.journals.get(v.id,{}, {signal});if(v.confirmation!==row.title)throw new Error('Type the exact document title.');await api.journals.delete({journal_id:row.id},{signal,requestId:crypto.randomUUID()});return api.journals.list({}, {signal});} Expected result: The returned list omits the deleted UUID.
