Permissions, failures and final test Folder operations are not recursive document deletion: deleting a folder reparents its documents and children. Deleting a document is separate and requires exact-title confirmation here. update requires exact version and the correct per-type data envelope; the diary recipe reconstructs its GM projection while keeping pages, cover and private notes. title: Build an actor-directory module
summary: Create, organize, rename and authorize actors using system-owned types.
text: The project you will build Build a GM actor organizer. Start by inspecting actual types, create one disposable actor and folder, move/rename them and grant one player read access. The sheet tutorial covers full sheet data and independent tokens. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named actor-workshop. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/actor-workshop/actor-workshop-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text actor-workshop/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../actor-workshop-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../actor-workshop-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Build an actor-directory module. Close that menu and click Build an actor-directory module. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Inspect actor types, documents and folders Run this first. The actorType comes from the selected system; copy an existing actor ID for later steps. javascript async ({api,signal}) = { const state=await api.actors.state({}, {signal}); return {actorTypes:state.actorTypes,actors:state.actors,folders:state.folders,players:state.players,isGM:state.is_gm}; } Expected result: A projected directory, registered type IDs and player IDs. Sheet bodies are read separately. How to verify: Compare with Actors as GM and as player. Listing-only entries have canOpen:false. Create an actor using the selected system Enter a fictional name; create only a disposable actor. This uses the first real registered type, not an assumed RPG type. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { const state=await api.actors.state({}, {signal}); if(!state.is_gm) throw new Error('GM required'); const type=state.actorTypes 0 ?.id; if(!type) throw new Error('Select a system declaring actor types first'); const created=await api.actors.create({name:v.name,type,data:{}},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); return api.actors.get(created.id,{}, {signal}); } Expected result: The created actor metadata including its ID. How to verify: Open Actors, find Workshop scout and open its native/system sheet. Rename an actor with an explicit revision Paste the ID created above and a new name. Only metadata changes; use saveSheet when editing system data. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { const before=await api.actors.get(v.id,{}, {signal}); await api.actors.update(v.id,{name:v.name,version:before.version},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); return api.actors.get(v.id,{}, {signal}); } Expected result: The same ID, new name and a new version. How to verify: Refresh the directory. An old version must return conflict, never a silent forced update. Create and identify an actor folder Choose an original folder name. The service does not promise an ID in every command result, so find the newly added folder in state. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { const before=await api.actors.state({}, {signal}); if(!before.is_gm) throw new Error('GM required'); await api.actors.createFolder({name:v.name,color:' b49a5a'},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); const after=await api.actors.state({}, {signal}); return after.folders.filter(folder= !before.folders.some(old= old.id===folder.id)); } Expected result: A newly created folder and its real UUID. How to verify: Find the same folder in Actors; copy its ID. Rename a folder and move an actor into it Use the disposable folder and actor IDs. parentId:null moves the folder to the root. Nesting is bounded by the service. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { await api.actors.updateFolder({id:v.folderId,name:v.name,parentId:null,color:' b49a5a'},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); const actor=await api.actors.get(v.actorId,{}, {signal}); await api.actors.update(actor.id,{folderId:v.folderId,version:actor.version},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); return api.actors.state({}, {signal}); } Expected result: Actor folderId now matches the folder. How to verify: Expand the folder in Actors and find the actor inside. Grant one player read access Copy a real player ID from Inspect, not an actor ID. Merge the existing permission map to preserve other grants. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { const actor=await api.actors.get(v.actorId,{}, {signal}); if(!actor.permissions) throw new Error('GM projection required'); await api.actors.setPermissions({id:actor.id,version:actor.version,permissions:{...actor.permissions, v.userId :'read'}},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); return api.actors.get(actor.id,{}, {signal}); } Expected result: The GM sees the retained permission map with the new read grant. How to verify: Open a second player session: reading succeeds, saving the sheet remains denied. Remove only the disposable actor folder Confirm a folder you created in this tutorial. recursive:false preserves actors; never use recursive:true as an unrelated cleanup shortcut. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { if(!v.confirm) throw new Error('Select the disposable folder confirmation'); await api.actors.deleteFolder({id:v.folderId,recursive:false},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); return api.actors.state({}, {signal}); } Expected result: The folder disappears; its actors survive with native folder-removal behavior. How to verify: Check that your disposable actor remains in Actors. Delete the disposable actor Use only the actor created above. Deleting an actor can also remove its tokens through native domain services. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { if(!v.confirm) throw new Error('Select the disposable actor confirmation'); await api.actors.delete({id:v.id},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); return api.actors.list({}, {signal}); } Expected result: The actor no longer appears in the authorized list. How to verify: Refresh Actors and the test scene. No user data outside this test should be selected. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Each business function remains responsible for revisions, permissions and transaction sequencing. manifest.json json { "id": "tutorial.actor-workshop", "name": "Build an actor-directory module", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Create, organize, rename and authorize actors using system-owned types.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {recipes} from './recipes.mjs'; title: Persist module settings safely
summary: Implement personal, shared and browser-local JSON with revisions and cleanup.
text: The project you will build Create a settings lab. Its actions show the complete lifecycle of one key in each storage scope, including reads, writes, listing and removal. Use these primitives inside preferences or customize to build your actual settings form. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named module-settings. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/module-settings/module-settings-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text module-settings/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../module-settings-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../module-settings-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Persist module settings safely. Close that menu and click Persist module settings safely. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Read personal settings and list their keys Run before saving. A missing key returns null; this is different from an unavailable storage service. javascript async ({storage}) = { return {current:await storage.user.get('workshop.preferences'),keys:await storage.user.list('workshop.')}; } Expected result: null on first use and a key/revision list. How to verify: Repeat as another account or in another campaign; server-backed user storage is separated. Save a versioned personal setting with CAS Choose a label. Read supplies the expected revision; a concurrent edit causes conflict. Do not replace that revision and retry automatically. javascript async ({storage},v) = { const current=await storage.user.get('workshop.preferences'); if(current && current.value?.schema!==1) throw new Error('Unsupported settings schema; migrate explicitly'); return storage.user.set('workshop.preferences',{schema:1,label:v.label},{expectedRevision:current?.revision??null}); } Expected result: Stored value and new opaque revision, retained across deactivation. How to verify: Read again, deactivate/reactivate and compare. Simulate two reads before two writes; the second stale write must fail. Delete only this tutorial preference Delete uses the latest revision of one exact key. No other module or campaign preference is removed. javascript async ({storage}) = { const current=await storage.user.get('workshop.preferences'); if(current) await storage.user.delete('workshop.preferences',{expectedRevision:current.revision}); return storage.user.get('workshop.preferences'); } Expected result: null. How to verify: Read and list again; the tutorial key is absent. Share one GM-authored setting with the table GM writes; players take the read-only branch. This is shared module JSON, not permission to change unrelated documents. javascript async ({api,storage,signal},v) = { if(!(await api.actors.state({}, {signal})).is_gm) return {readOnly:true,current:await storage.table.get('workshop.shared')}; const current=await storage.table.get('workshop.shared'); const saved=await storage.table.set('workshop.shared',{schema:1,label:v.label},{expectedRevision:current?.revision??null}); return {saved,keys:await storage.table.list('workshop.')}; } Expected result: GM receives the saved revision; player receives that same shared value. How to verify: Use two accounts in the same campaign. Direct player storage.table.set must be rejected server-side. Remove the shared tutorial key Run as GM after testing the shared value. javascript async ({storage}) = { const current=await storage.table.get('workshop.shared'); if(current)await storage.table.delete('workshop.shared',{expectedRevision:current.revision}); return storage.table.get('workshop.shared'); } Expected result: null; a player cannot delete this key. How to verify: Read as a player after GM deletion. Use browser-local settings and clear them Only UI choices belong here. This namespace is module+browser origin, shared across accounts and tables in that browser. javascript async ({storage},v) = { await storage.local.set('workshop.local',{schema:1,density:v.density}); const value=await storage.local.get('workshop.local'); await storage.local.delete('workshop.local'); return {observed:value,afterDelete:await storage.local.get('workshop.local')}; } Expected result: observed contains the choice and afterDelete is null. Local storage has no CAS revision. How to verify: Do not store private notes, permissions or account secrets in this namespace. 4. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. title: Upload and use module and campaign files
summary: Use File/Blob, actor images, card assets, native file providers and downloads.
text: The project you will build Create a file-handling module, not a URL-writing shortcut. Its forms pass real File objects to the public multipart SDK. Each recipe explains which native library owns the resulting ID. Package assets are covered by the next localization/events tutorial. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named asset-workshop. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/asset-workshop/asset-workshop-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text asset-workshop/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../asset-workshop-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../asset-workshop-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Upload and use module and campaign files. Close that menu and click Upload and use module and campaign files. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe List reusable campaign assets Use a test campaign with a native-supported asset, such as an original PDF in the PDF system. This operation lists unattached actor-template assets, not every map/audio file. javascript async ({host,signal}) = host.call('asset.list',{}, {signal}) Expected result: items with id, name, contentType and createdAt. How to verify: Compare the native asset/template library; an empty array is valid. Upload a real provider-supported file Choose your own small valid PDF on a PDF campaign. asset.upload selects a registered content provider and its validator; it is not an arbitrary binary file store. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { if(!(v.file instanceof File)) throw new Error('Choose a file'); return host.call('asset.upload',{file:v.file},{signal}); } Expected result: An asset DTO with its new ID; unsupported content fails invalid_data. How to verify: List again and compare its name. Test a text file and verify rejection. Read a downloadable file as a Blob Paste an asset ID from List. The result contains a Blob; it is not a URL string. A UI may create an object URL for download and must revoke it afterward. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { const result=await host.call('asset.download',{id:v.id},{signal}); return {name:result.name,contentType:result.contentType,size:result.size,blobBytes:result.blob.size}; } Expected result: Metadata and equal size/blobBytes without dumping file contents into the page. How to verify: Compare size with the original. Another campaign’s ID must not be readable. Upload portrait or token artwork Use portrait, then token, with an editable disposable actor. Multipart requires a real File. Limits and conversion are enforced by the host. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { if(! 'portrait','token' .includes(v.kind))throw new Error('kind must be portrait or token'); if(!(v.file instanceof File))throw new Error('Choose an image'); return host.call('actor.image.upload',{id:v.id,kind:v.kind,file:v.file},{signal}); } Expected result: The saved image URL. actor.version changes; re-read before subsequent writes. How to verify: Reopen the actor and inspect both images. Read-only player and invalid image must fail. Upload front/back artwork for a deck As GM, choose an original image and purpose. Paste the returned assetId into the card-definition tutorial, not an external URL. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { if(! 'card_front','card_back' .includes(v.purpose))throw new Error('Choose card_front or card_back'); return host.call('card.asset.upload',{purpose:v.purpose,file:v.file},{signal}); } Expected result: assetId for the native card asset library. How to verify: Define a deck with front_asset_id/back_asset_id using this ID and inspect it in Cards. Delete only a reusable tutorial asset Select only the unattached reusable asset you uploaded. Native deletion checks provider support and updates references. This does not delete arbitrary media paths. javascript async ({api,signal},v) = { if(!v.confirm)throw new Error('Confirm the disposable asset'); await api.actors.deleteAsset({id:v.id},{requestId:crypto.randomUUID(),signal}); return {deleted:v.id}; } Expected result: The asset is removed through the native actor domain. How to verify: List it again; it must be absent. Actor-owned artwork IDs are not accepted here. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. title: Maintain a module using the original host.call SDK
summary: Concrete actor/token DTOs, opaque revisions and the remaining multipart/local operations.
text: The project you will build Build an original-SDK module with real buttons for actor and token operations. Use a development campaign, an active scene and an original external system. These interfaces coexist with the domain API; their signatures and revision formats are different. Target host: Gravewright 0.3.0 . Actions run only when you click Run action, using the signed-in account. The demonstration panel is English. Each recipe specifies inputs and an observable result. 1. Create the files Create a folder named sdk-compat. Save the complete files below as UTF-8, or download the project (../../assets/tutorials/sdk-compat/sdk-compat-source.zip). manifest.json belongs at the root. No npm dependencies or JavaScript build is required. text sdk-compat/ manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt The remaining original operations are implemented in file handling (docs:tutorial-assets) (asset.list/upload/download, actor.image.upload, card.asset.upload) and localization (docs:tutorial-localization-events) (locale.apply). Together these guides cover every operation in registry.json. Use the modern domain API for new modules unless you specifically need the multipart SDK. 2. Package, install and activate From the project folder, run in PowerShell: powershell python -m json.tool manifest.json python -m zipfile -c ../sdk-compat-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs recipes.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt python -m zipfile -l ../sdk-compat-1.0.0.zip On Linux/macOS, replace python with python3 in the same commands. The archive listing must show manifest.json at its root. As installation owner, open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP, select the ZIP and click Install. As GM, open the campaign, select its Gravewright button → Extensions and Activate version 1.0.0 of Original SDK workshop. Close that menu and click Original SDK workshop. See your first module (docs:tutorial-first-module) for screen-by-screen instructions. The package stays inactive until selected for the table. Test one demonstration extension at a time because their launchers share a position. For changed bytes, increment version to 1.0.1, build another ZIP, install and activate that version; do not edit installed files. 3. Run each recipe Read every authorized actor page This is the original SDK DTO list, not api.actors.list. It paginates and includes opaque revision strings. javascript async ({host,signal}) = { const items= ;let cursor=null; do { const page=await host.call('actor.list',{limit:50,cursor},{signal}); items.push(...page.items);cursor=page.nextCursor; } while(cursor&&!signal.aborted); return items; } Expected result: All readable actors in this campaign, reauthorized on each page. How to verify: Compare IDs with the directory; use a player to check filtering. Read one actor DTO and its data revision Paste a readable actor UUID. Actor metadata and sheet data have different revision domains. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = ({ actor:await host.call('actor.read',{id:v.id},{signal}), sheet:await host.call('actor.data.read',{id:v.id},{signal}) }) Expected result: actor.revision and sheet.revision, each retained with its own response. How to verify: Do not decode or interchange revision tokens. Create a disposable actor through host.call The domain API discovers the selected system type. The legacy create schema accepts name/type, not an arbitrary actor data payload. javascript async ({api,host,signal},v) = { const type=(await api.actors.state({}, {signal})).actorTypes 0 ?.id; if(!type)throw new Error('Choose a system with an actor type'); return host.call('actor.create',{name:v.name,type},{signal}); } Expected result: The created actor DTO and its opaque revision. How to verify: Find the same ID in Actors; retain it for the next recipes. Rename with the legacy metadata revision Use the disposable actor. changes contains only supported metadata changes. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { const before=await host.call('actor.read',{id:v.id},{signal}); return host.call('actor.update',{id:v.id,expectedRevision:before.revision,changes:{name:v.name}},{signal}); } Expected result: Same actor with the new name and a new metadata revision. How to verify: A stale expectedRevision must yield conflict; reload instead of forcing it. Preserve a complete actor JSON while changing one owned field Use an external example system that accepts opaque original JSON, such as Example Expedition. workshop is owned by this example; do not overwrite fields belonging to another package. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { const before=await host.call('actor.data.read',{id:v.id},{signal}); const data={...before.data,workshop:{note:v.note}}; return host.call('actor.data.update',{id:v.id,expectedRevision:before.revision,data},{signal}); } Expected result: Updated data with all other top-level fields preserved. How to verify: Read again and compare unrelated keys. A system-specific validator may reject unsupported fields. Read token center coordinates and its own sheet data Activate an existing scene and use a token from that scene. This package mounts scene.controls so the legacy scene scope is present. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = ({ token:await host.call('token.read',{id:v.id},{signal}), sheet:await host.call('token.data.read',{id:v.id},{signal}) }) Expected result: position is a center point in scene pixels, not gridX/gridY. Sheet data resolves linked or independent storage. How to verify: Compare one linked and one snapshot token; never substitute actor data for the snapshot. Move a token using its own opaque revision Use a token you control and an in-bounds target center. The server converts scene pixels into its grid geometry. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { const token=await host.call('token.read',{id:v.id},{signal}); return host.call('token.move',{id:v.id,expectedRevision:token.revision,position:{x:v.x,y:v.y}},{signal}); } Expected result: Updated token position; movement validation and permissions still apply. How to verify: Try another campaign token and a stale revision. Both must fail without moving it. Update the token’s resolved data without replacing unrelated fields For a linked token this edits actor data; for an independent token it edits its snapshot. Use only the original opaque-JSON example system. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { const before=await host.call('token.data.read',{id:v.id},{signal}); return host.call('token.data.update',{id:v.id,expectedRevision:before.revision,data:{...before.data,workshop:{note:v.note}}},{signal}); } Expected result: A new data revision in the correct document domain. How to verify: Read source actor and both tokens; snapshot changes must not change its source actor. Delete the disposable legacy actor Remove only an unused actor created by this tutorial, with no scene tokens. New integrations should prefer the domain API, whose native deletion includes token/automation cleanup. javascript async ({host,signal},v) = { if(!v.confirm)throw new Error('Confirm the disposable actor'); const actor=await host.call('actor.read',{id:v.id},{signal}); return host.call('actor.delete',{id:v.id,expectedRevision:actor.revision},{signal}); } Expected result: null from the original delete contract. How to verify: Read again and expect not_found. Do not use this path as a replacement for native lifecycle cleanup. 4. Understand and adapt the complete files main.mjs renders the launcher and form. recipes.mjs owns behavior: change the chosen recipe’s run function while keeping its signature. The form passes real number, boolean and File values, blocks overlapping requests and renders using textContent. It does not evaluate user-provided code. api, host, assets and storage belong to the mount; signal cancels work on deactivation. The modal stays open during pending work and is released when the mount aborts. Each business function remains responsible for revisions, permissions and transaction sequencing. manifest.json json { "id": "tutorial.sdk-compat", "name": "Original SDK workshop", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "Concrete actor/token DTOs, opaque revisions and the remaining multipart/local operations.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {recipes} from './recipes.mjs'; export default { start({styles}) { styles.use('styles.css'); }, register({register}) { register("scene.controls", ({root,api,host,assets,storage,context,events,viewport,signal,onDispose}) = { const doc=root.ownerDocument; const button=doc.createElement('button'); button.type='button';button.className='tutorial-launcher'; button.textContent="Original SDK workshop"; root.append(button); for(const type of 'pointerdown','mousedown' )button.addEventListener(type,event= event.stopPropagation(),{signal}); let modal,pending=false; button.addEventListener('click',event= { event.stopPropagation(); if(modal?.isConnected) { modal.focus();return; } const panel=doc.createElement('section'); panel.className="tutorial-workbench-sdk-compat"; panel.setAttribute('role','dialog');panel.setAttribute('aria-modal','true'); panel.setAttribute('aria-label',button.textContent);panel.tabIndex=-1; const title=doc.createElement('h2');title.textContent=button.textContent;panel.append(title); const choose=doc.createElement('select');choose.setAttribute('aria-label','Action'); for(const recipe of recipes) { const option=doc.createElement('option');option.value=recipe.id;option.textContent=recipe.label;choose.append(option); } const form=doc.createElement('form'),fields=doc.createElement('div'); const description=doc.createElement('p'); const run=doc.createElement('button');run.type='submit';run.textContent='Run action'; const close=doc.createElement('button');close.type='button';close.textContent='Close'; const output=doc.createElement('pre');output.setAttribute('role','status');output.setAttribute('aria-live','polite'); for(const field of recipe.fields ) { const label=doc.createElement('label');label.textContent=field.label; const input=doc.createElement('input');input.name=field.name;input.type=field.type 'text'; if(field.type==='number')input.step=String(field.step??'any'); if(field.type==='checkbox')input.checked=!!field.value; else if(field.type!=='file')input.value=String(field.value??''); input.required=!!field.required; if(field.accept)input.accept=field.accept; label.append(input);fields.append(label); } output.textContent=''; } choose.addEventListener('change',renderFields,{signal});renderFields(); form.addEventListener('submit',async event= { event.preventDefault();if(pending)return; const recipe=recipes.find(item= item.id===choose.value),values={}; for(const input of fields.querySelectorAll('input')) { values input.name =input.type==='file'?input.files 0 :input.type==='checkbox'?input.checked:input.type==='number'?Number(input.value):input.value; if(!signal.aborted)output.textContent=typeof value==='string'?value:JSON.stringify(value??null,null,2); } catch(error) { if(!signal.aborted)output.textContent=String(error.code error.message 'unavailable'); title: Build Customize forms and native module windows
summary: A complete personal settings form with migration, CAS, translations, modal lifecycle and preferences mounting.
text: What to build A module with a personal table note, a preferences-surface panel and a real Customize form in the extension list. It uses storage.user, so each account in each campaign owns its note. It explicitly migrates a legacy string into schema:1 and refuses unknown formats. 1. Create the project and inspect its JavaScript files Create personal-note. Download the complete ZIP (../../assets/tutorials/personal-note/personal-note-source.zip) or save the complete files below. main.mjs owns mounting, translation and modal UI; settings.mjs owns reading, migration and writes. Game data is unaffected. 2. Package and install From the project folder run: powershell python -m zipfile -c ../personal-note-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs settings.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt Use python3 on Linux/macOS. As owner, install via Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP. As GM, open the campaign and select Gravewright → Extensions → Activate for Personal note workshop 1.0.0. Test one floating tutorial panel at a time. 3. Open Customize and save a preference 1. In Gravewright → Extensions, click Customize beside Personal note workshop. The runtime displays this because the module exports customize(context). 2. Note text loads your current preference. Enter “Prepare session materials” and click Save preference. 3. Wait for Saved. Close and click Refresh on the note panel. Your new text appears. 4. Leave/reopen the campaign; the value persists. Sign in as a player and choose another note: accounts do not overwrite each other. 5. Open the table menu’s Preferences section. Its preferences mount displays the same value with a refresh action, without modifying host-internal preferences. 4. Understand the modal and closing api.ui.openModal receives an accessibly named section and owns focus, background state and Escape. During writes, buttons are disabled and canClose guards Escape. gravewright:sheet-flush also joins the pending write. Deactivation aborts the mount and releases the modal. Preview table for 2 seconds calls suspend, exposes the table and later resumes. onDispose cancels the timer. For an actual map picker, replace only the interval with a selection mechanism supported by the target contract; do not invent a selection API. 5. Evolve data without losing preferences settings.mjs accepts a missing key, a legacy string and a schema:1 object. Migration occurs in memory; server data changes only on Save preference. The spread preserves additional fields in the accepted shape. Unknown schemas disable editing instead of deleting data. get supplies the CAS revision used by set. Open forms in two tabs. Save in the first, then save in the second. The second receives conflict, reloads the current preference and asks for review, without an automatic forced retry. Unsaved field edits stay local and are discarded when closed. 6. Complete source to adapt manifest.json json { "id": "example.personal-note", "name": "Personal note workshop", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.mjs", "description": "A real Customize form, personal settings migration and translated live panel.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT" } main.mjs javascript import {load,save} from './settings.mjs'; export default { start({styles,i18n}){ styles.use('styles.css'); i18n.register({en:{title:'Personal note',refresh:'Refresh'},'pt-BR':{title:'Nota pessoal',refresh:'Atualizar'},es:{title:'Nota personal',refresh:'Actualizar'}}); }, register({register}){ register('table.interface',ctx= this.mount(ctx,true)); register('preferences',ctx= this.mount(ctx,false)); }, async mount({root,api,storage,signal,onDispose},floating){ const doc=root.ownerDocument,panel=doc.createElement('aside'); panel.className='personal-note'+(floating?' personal-note--floating':''); const title=doc.createElement('strong'),text=doc.createElement('p'),refresh=doc.createElement('button'); title.textContent=api.i18n.t('title');refresh.type='button';refresh.textContent=api.i18n.t('refresh'); panel.append(title,text,refresh);root.append(panel); let generation=0; async function read(){ const ticket=++generation;refresh.disabled=true; try {const current=await load(storage);if(!signal.aborted&&ticket===generation)text.textContent=current.value.label;} catch(error){if(!signal.aborted&&ticket===generation)text.textContent=error.code error.message;} finally{if(!signal.aborted&&ticket===generation)refresh.disabled=false;} } refresh.addEventListener('click',()= void read(),{signal}); onDispose(()= {generation++;panel.remove();});await read(); }, async customize({api,storage,signal,onDispose}){ const panel=document.createElement('section');panel.className='personal-note-settings'; panel.setAttribute('role','dialog');panel.setAttribute('aria-modal','true');panel.setAttribute('aria-label','Personal note settings'); const heading=document.createElement('h2');heading.textContent='Personal note settings'; const form=document.createElement('form'),label=document.createElement('label');label.textContent='Note text'; const input=document.createElement('input');input.maxLength=120;label.append(input); const submit=document.createElement('button');submit.type='submit';submit.textContent='Save preference'; const preview=document.createElement('button');preview.type='button';preview.textContent='Preview table for 2 seconds'; const close=document.createElement('button');close.type='button';close.textContent='Close'; const status=document.createElement('p');status.setAttribute('role','status'); form.append(label,submit,preview,close,status);panel.append(heading,form); let current,pending,timer; function enabled(value){input.disabled=!value;submit.disabled=!value;preview.disabled=!value;close.disabled=!value;} enabled(false); const modal=api.ui.openModal(panel,{canClose:()= !pending}); async function refresh(){current=await load(storage);if(!signal.aborted)input.value=current.value.label;} panel.addEventListener('gravewright:sheet-flush',event= {if(pending)event.detail.waitUntil(pending);},{signal}); form.addEventListener('submit',event= { event.preventDefault();if(pending !current)return;enabled(false); pending=(async()= { try{await save(storage,current,input.value);await refresh();if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent='Saved. Close and refresh the note panel.';} catch(error){ if(!signal.aborted){ if(error.code==='conflict'){await refresh();status.textContent='Conflict: current server preference loaded. Review before saving again.';} else status.textContent=error.code error.message; } throw error; }finally{pending=undefined;if(!signal.aborted)enabled(true);} })();void pending.catch(()= {}); },{signal}); preview.addEventListener('click',()= { modal.suspend();clearTimeout(timer); timer=setTimeout(()= {if(!signal.aborted)modal.resume();},2000); },{signal}); close.addEventListener('click',()= void modal.close(),{signal}); onDispose(()= {clearTimeout(timer);void modal.close();}); try{await refresh();if(!signal.aborted)enabled(true);} catch(error){if(!signal.aborted){status.textContent=error.code error.message;close.disabled=false;}} }, stop(){} }; settings.mjs javascript export const key='panel-preferences'; export function migrate(value){ if(value===null value===undefined)return {schema:1,label:'My campaign note'}; if(typeof value==='string')return {schema:1,label:value}; if(value?.schema===1 && typeof value.label==='string')return {...value}; throw new Error('Unsupported preference schema. Export/migrate before saving.'); } export async function load(storage){ const current=await storage.user.get(key); return {value:migrate(current?.value),revision:current?.revision??null}; } export async function save(storage,current,label){ if(typeof label!=='string' !label.trim() label.length 120)throw new Error('Enter 1–120 characters'); return storage.user.set(key,{...current.value,schema:1,label:label.trim()},{expectedRevision:current.revision}); } styles.css css .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.personal-note" .personal-note { padding: var(--space-4); font-size: 14px; } .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.personal-note" .personal-note--floating { position: fixed; left: 16px; bottom: 112px; z-index: 10; max-width: min(340px, calc(100vw - 32px)); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-md); pointer-events: auto; } .personal-note-settings { width: min(520px, calc(100vw - 48px)); padding: var(--space-5); font-size: 14px; } .personal-note-settings label { display: block; margin-bottom: var(--space-4); } .personal-note-settings input { width: 100%; display: block; } .personal-note-settings button { margin-right: var(--space-3); margin-bottom: var(--space-3); } LICENSE.txt text MIT License Copyright (c) 2026 Gravewright contributors Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions: The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software. THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE. Practical tests Test a legacy/unknown schema, two tabs, another player/campaign, interrupted network and deactivation during reads/writes. textContent renders HTML-like input as text. Original en/pt-BR/es catalogs follow the explicit account language and disappear with the activation lifetime. How to use AI for customization text Adapt Personal note workshop for specific preference on Gravewright 0.3.0. Preserve customize, preferences mounting, CAS and schema migration. Use a native modal and localized labels without changing host internals. Deliver complete files and test two tabs, player access, closing and version updates.

title: Create a trusted Django integration and server hooks
summary: Complete Python app with authenticated routes, native mutations and after-commit signals.
text: What this package does Build a generic trusted server integration with authorized actor reads, native-command renaming and after-commit event observation. Python code is owner-activated for the installation, separately from campaign browser modules. It is not a separately installed RPG rules companion. A new system remains one package using the requested host contracts. 1. Choose browser or server correctly Use browser code when an action fits the public domain API. Use Django only for an explicitly trusted integration requiring server routes/services. A Django manifest cannot contain entry, system or locales. Browser modules cannot ask the host to import Python or execute SQL. This example creates no models, migrations, extra dependencies or startup writes. 2. Create server-workshop with these files manifest.json json { "id": "example.server-workshop", "name": "Server integration workshop", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "description": "Authenticated campaign reads, native actor commands and bounded process-local event counters.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT", "django": { "apps": "example_workshop.apps.ExampleWorkshopConfig" } } example_workshop/__init__.py python example_workshop/apps.py python from django.apps import AppConfig class ExampleWorkshopConfig(AppConfig): name = "example_workshop" label = "example_workshop" gravewright_urlconf = "example_workshop.urls" def ready(self): from api.events import resource_changed from .hooks import observe resource_changed.connect(observe, dispatch_uid="example.server-workshop.observe", weak=False) example_workshop/hooks.py python from collections import Counter from threading import Lock counts = Counter() lock = Lock() def observe(sender, change, kwargs): Only fixed resource names are retained, never campaign/user/document IDs. if change.resource not in {"actors", "tokens", "maps", "journals", "items", "combat", "cards", "audio", "compendiums"}: return with lock: counts change.resource += 1 def snapshot(): with lock: return dict(counts) example_workshop/urls.py python from django.urls import path from . import views urlpatterns = path("api/tutorials/campaign/<uuid:campaign_id /actors/", views.read_actors), path("api/tutorials/campaign/<uuid:campaign_id /rename/", views.rename_actor), path("api/tutorials/event-counts/", views.event_counts), example_workshop/views.py python import json from uuid import UUID, uuid4 from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required from django.http import JsonResponse from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_POST from api import Context, actors from api.errors import AuthError, JournalError, MapError from .hooks import snapshot def failure(error): code = getattr(error, "code", "invalid_data") code = {"not_a_member": "permission_denied", "forbidden": "permission_denied", "invalid_input": "invalid_data"}.get(code, code) status = {"permission_denied": 403, "not_found": 404, "conflict": 409}.get(code, getattr(error, "status", 400)) return JsonResponse({"error": code}, status=status) @login_required @require_GET def read_actors(request, campaign_id): try: context = Context.from_request(request, campaign_id) value = actors.state(context.campaign_id, context.user_id) return JsonResponse({"actors": value "actors" , "actorTypes": value "actorTypes" }) except (AuthError, JournalError, MapError) as error: return failure(error) @login_required @require_POST def rename_actor(request, campaign_id): Normal Django CSRF middleware remains active; never mark this csrf_exempt. if len(request.body) 8192: return JsonResponse({"error": "invalid_data"}, status=400) try: body = json.loads(request.body) if not isinstance(body, dict) or set(body) != {"id", "version", "name"}: raise ValueError("Invalid payload") identifier = str(UUID(body "id" )) if not str(body "version" ).isdigit(): raise ValueError("Invalid version") if not isinstance(body "name" , str) or not 2 <= len(body "name" .strip()) <= 120: raise ValueError("Invalid name") context = Context.from_request(request, campaign_id) result = actors.command(context.campaign_id, context.user_id, "actor.update", { "id": identifier, "version": body "version" , "name": body "name" .strip(), }, uuid4()) return JsonResponse({"result": result}) except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, AttributeError): return JsonResponse({"error": "invalid_data"}, status=400) except (AuthError, JournalError, MapError) as error: return failure(error) @login_required @require_GET def event_counts(request): if request.user.role != "owner": return JsonResponse({"error": "permission_denied"}, status=403) return JsonResponse({"processLocal": True, "resources": snapshot()}) LICENSE.txt text MIT License Copyright (c) 2026 Gravewright contributors Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions: The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software. THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE. 3. Package and activate on a development host Download the complete ZIP (../../assets/tutorials/server-workshop/server-workshop-source.zip) or save the files and archive manifest.json, LICENSE.txt and example_workshop together. From the project root: powershell python -m zipfile -c ../server-workshop-1.0.0.zip manifest.json LICENSE.txt example_workshop Use python3 on Linux/macOS. As owner, install through Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP. Choose installation activation rather than the table’s Activate action. The Runner stages selection and restarts through managed supervision; await completion and reload. managed_start_required on a directly launched server means activation must use the Runner. Do not bypass it through a browser module import. 4. Test authenticated reads and writes Open /api/tutorials/campaign/YOUR_UUID/actors/ in an authenticated tab with your disposable campaign UUID. The native service filters the list for that caller. As campaign GM, use a disposable actor and execute in that host’s Console: javascript // Run on your own development host in an authenticated browser tab. const campaignId = "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_TEST_CAMPAIGN_UUID"; const state = await fetch('/api/tutorials/campaign/'+campaignId+'/actors/').then(r= r.json()); const actor = state.actors.find(row= row.canOpen); const csrf = await fetch('/__gravewright/csrf').then(r= r.json()); const response = await fetch('/api/tutorials/campaign/'+campaignId+'/rename/', { method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json', csrf.header :csrf.token}, body:JSON.stringify({id:actor.id,version:actor.version,name:'Original workshop navigator'}), }); console.log(response.status,await response.json()); A successful response is 200. Inspect the persisted name in Actors. An old version yields conflict; reread before deciding another change. Passing a GM UUID does not grant GM access: Context.from_request uses authenticated identity and membership. Middleware rejects POST without valid CSRF. 5. Observe events without exposing data AppConfig.ready connects observe once. The receiver only counts nine fixed resource names without storing user/campaign/document IDs or querying the database. As owner, open /api/tutorials/event-counts/. A completed public command may increment its counter. Counts are process-local and reset on restart; they are neither durable audit history nor multi-worker totals. Chat/dice writes do not all emit this signal. An after-commit receiver failure does not undo a committed transaction. Do not perform irreversible external work expecting rollback. Durable integrations require their own transactional queue in a trusted app; the browser SDK does not supply it. 6. Use the remaining Python facades Authenticate Context, invoke the public facade and let its service enforce permissions/revisions. Signatures differ; consult the Python API table (docs:api python-interface): actors/tokens/maps/journals; items/combat/cards/audio/compendiums; resources as a generic dispatcher; chat/dice/table for messages, rolls and search; events for signals. Private imports and direct ORM writes do not replace native commands. Family recipes in the implementation index (docs:tutorial-index) supply concrete action payloads. Server command(campaign_id,user_id,action,data,request_id) uses native action names declared in frontend.json, with state for reads. For example journals.update uses action update, while combat.nextTurn uses next. Do not pass JavaScript method names as native actions without checking the registry. 7. Test before distribution Check owner, GM, player, nonmember, anonymous session, missing CSRF, malformed body, stale revision and another campaign’s actor. GET routes must not write or import operator apps. Inspect the ZIP and publish a new version for changed bytes. Owner deactivation also uses the Runner and restart; do not remove active package files forcibly. How to use AI for server integration text Start from Server integration workshop for generic integration on Gravewright 0.3.0. Use Context.from_request and public api facades; preserve authentication, CSRF, permissions and revisions. No ready/import queries. Document after-commit signals, process-local limits and Runner activation. Do not introduce a system companion or require a newer host. Deliver complete files and cross-account/campaign tests.

title: How to create and activate an installation language package
summary: Package six original interface strings, install globally, choose a personal locale and verify English fallback.
text: What this package actually changes Create a declarative, installation-wide language package for Gravewright 0.3.0 . This original demonstration translates exactly six interface keys into Portuguese and Spanish. It is deliberately partial, so most host text remains English. It does not translate authored character names, chat, journals, PDFs or exact legal notices. It is not a complete release of the official Translator. Use a disposable installation. Activating this language package selects it globally and disables the previously enabled global package; do not replace an operator’s active translation just to test six strings. Individual accounts still choose their own interface language. 1. Start with the complete existing sources Download language-source.zip (../../assets/examples/packages/language/language-source.zip) text language/ manifest.json main.mjs locales/pt-BR.json locales/es.json LICENSE.txt README.md Create a folder named language and save the exact files below as UTF-8. Preserve the existing GPL license (../../assets/examples/packages/language/LICENSE.txt) and README (../../assets/examples/packages/language/README.md) from the source ZIP. There are no npm dependencies or Python files in this browser package. manifest.json json { "id": "example.language-demo", "name": "Example language demo", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "description": "Partial original interface catalogs for Portuguese and Spanish.", "author": "Gravewright documentation examples", "license": "GPL-3.0-only", "entry": "main.mjs", "locales": { "pt-BR": { "name": "Português (Brasil)", "path": "locales/pt-BR.json" }, "es": { "name": "Español", "path": "locales/es.json" } } } main.mjs javascript export default { start() {}, register() {}, stop() {} }; locales/pt-BR.json json { "Actors": "Personagens", "Items": "Itens", "Settings": "Configurações", "Close": "Fechar", "Save": "Salvar", "Search": "Buscar" } locales/es.json json { "Actors": "Personajes", "Items": "Objetos", "Settings": "Ajustes", "Close": "Cerrar", "Save": "Guardar", "Search": "Buscar" } locales is metadata, not a kind field. The no-op start/register/stop entry satisfies the released browser manifest contract and mounts no table surface. A manifest cannot combine system with locales, cannot override en and cannot put a Django app in this language package. 2. Validate JSON and build the ZIP From the language folder, use the already managed Python in the host. In PowerShell, replace the path to python.exe with that of your disposable host. On POSIX use its .venv/bin/python. No package installation is needed. powershell & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' -m json.tool manifest.json & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' -m json.tool locales/pt-BR.json & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' -m json.tool locales/es.json & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' -m zipfile -c ../language-demo-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.mjs locales LICENSE.txt README.md & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' -m zipfile -l ../language-demo-1.0.0.zip The listing must place manifest.json directly at the ZIP root. json.tool checks JSON syntax; native installation also validates catalogs: nonempty objects, at most 15,000 entries, nonblank strings up to 12,000 characters and exactly preserved {placeholder} names/counts. A missing translation falls back to its original English key. 3. Install and activate the global languages 1. Sign in as installation owner. Open Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP , choose the reviewed ZIP and click Install . Local upload is an explicit trust decision; it does not require a signed remote catalog. 2. In the installed Modules library, find Example language demo . Use its power icon with accessible label/tooltip Activate languages . In Portuguese the label is Ativar idiomas . The page reloads after activation. 3. Do not look for the package under a campaign’s Extensions. Language packages are installation-wide and deliberately absent from that table list. Installing, globally activating and choosing a personal language are three different steps. 4. Choose a language for your account On the 0.3.0 table, click the Gravewright button, open Preferences and find Interface language . Choose Português (Brasil) or Español and wait for the page to reload. This control saves UserPreference.locale for the authenticated account; it is not a campaign setting. The general account/security form does not contain this selector in this release. Repeat as another account and select English there. Check supported labels where the host uses those exact keys: Save becomes Salvar or Guardar, Close becomes Fechar or Cerrar, and Search becomes Buscar. Most text remains English because only six keys are included. A package-local i18n catalog and an authored name are separate content; do not promise that this six-key package translates every extension. 5. Verify fallback, updates and disabling As owner, use Deactivate languages / Desativar idiomas , then reload existing pages. An unavailable personal locale resolves to English on the next request; authored campaign text is unchanged. Re-enable and verify each account’s explicit choice. To expand the catalog, add exact current host keys with preserved placeholders to both files, change version to 1.0.1, build and install that new ZIP, then activate that exact release globally. Do not edit extracted installed files or overwrite the original ID/version. How to use AI to extend the catalog text Extend this exact language-demo package for Gravewright 0.3.0 with specified host strings . Inspect localization.py, the host templates and the existing language package before proposing keys. Preserve source strings, placeholders, GPL notices, en fallback and the separate per-account language choice. Keep one global locales package with no system/Django block. Deliver both complete JSON files, versioned manifest, ZIP commands and tests for owner activation, two accounts, missing keys and disabling. SDK (docs:modules) · Publish a module (docs:tutorial-publish-module) · All tutorials (docs:tutorial-index)

title: How to version, sign and distribute a module
summary: Prepare immutable ZIP releases, verify Ed25519 catalog records and understand installation, activation and revocation.
text:
From a working local package to an immutable release This guide prepares a publisher’s own distribution for Gravewright 0.3.0 . It does not publish anything on your behalf. Start with a complete working first module (docs:tutorial-first-module), sheet action (docs:tutorial-sheet-module) or language package (docs:tutorial-language-package), and test it on a disposable host. Keep original or authorized code/assets and their licenses together. Exclude .env, databases, campaign media, installed packages, logs, private keys and operator files. 1. Prepare a new version and validate the final ZIP For changed bytes, increment the package manifest version, for example 1.0.0 to 1.0.1. Keep the ID stable, entry path correct and sdk.requires/tested honest for the target host. A release ID/version cannot be replaced with different bytes. Save previous archives and catalog records before publishing an update. Existing users remain on their explicitly selected campaign version until it is changed. Build the ZIP with manifest.json directly at its root. List the archive and test CRC before signing. The native installer enforces compressed/expanded quotas, file count/type rules, manifest schema, SDK compatibility, entry presence, traversal, duplicate paths and executable-content checks. The signer below adds basic offline checks; it is not a substitute for native installation and activation tests. powershell & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' -m zipfile -l ./example.sheet-name-1.0.1.zip & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' -m zipfile -t ./example.sheet-name-1.0.1.zip 2. Keep installation and activation distinct Local testing: owner uses Inside → Modules → Install module → Install from ZIP . A system uses Systems → Install system . Installation validates and stores a release. A GM then opens the table’s Gravewright → Extensions → Table modules and selects Activate for the exact browser-module version. A campaign system is selected as the system. A language uses the global Activate languages control; a Django app requires owner activation of trusted server code and a managed restart. Do not treat any of these as the same operation. 3. Choose the signed catalog type Manifest type Activation --- --- --- entry, without system/django module Campaign; locales are global system system Campaign system django, without entry/system/locales django Owner, server restart type participates in the signature and must match the ZIP manifest. A language package is catalog type module with locales metadata, not a fourth catalog type. Publish complete RPG systems as one installable system package using the requested host APIs; do not create a separately installed rules companion to work around missing host support. 4. Download the complete offline signer sign_catalog.py (../../assets/tutorials/distribution/sign_catalog.py) Save this original MIT helper outside the module source folder. Run it with the host’s already prepared virtual environment; cryptography is an existing host dependency. It imports no private host API, creates no production key and never overwrites an output record. Use the path of a publisher-managed Ed25519 private PEM that you already control. Keep that private key outside the ZIP, site, catalog and repository. For an encrypted PEM, --password-env names an environment variable containing its password; the helper does not print it. python """Offline catalog signer for Gravewright 0.3.0. License: MIT. Uses cryptography already installed in the host virtual environment. It imports no host internals, executes no archive code, generates no production key and overwrites no output. Native installation remains the authoritative ZIP check. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import base64 import hashlib import hmac import io import json import os from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath import re import stat import sys from urllib.parse import urlsplit import zipfile from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519PublicKey def canonical(record): Exact wire representation used by packages.canonical in the target host. return json.dumps( {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k != "signature"}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False, ).encode("ascii") def archive_info(path): path = Path(path) if path.stat().st_size 64 1024 1024: raise ValueError("Archive exceeds 64 MiB: " + str(path)) data = path.read_bytes() with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive: entries = archive.infolist() if len(entries) 4096 or sum(item.file_size for item in entries) 256 1024 1024: raise ValueError("Archive quota exceeded") seen = set() for item in entries: name = item.filename.rstrip("/") if item.is_dir() else item.filename parts = name.split("/") mode = item.external_attr 16 if (not name or PurePosixPath(name).is_absolute() or any(part in ("", ".", "..") for part in parts) or any(char in name for char in ("\", "\x00", ":", "%", "?", " ")) or stat.S_ISLNK(mode) or stat.S_IFMT(mode) not in (0, stat.S_IFREG, stat.S_IFDIR) or item.flag_bits & 1 or name.casefold() in seen): raise ValueError("Unsupported archive path or entry: " + name) seen.add(name.casefold()) info = archive.getinfo("manifest.json") if info.file_size 1024 1024: raise ValueError("Manifest exceeds 1 MiB") manifest = json.loads(archive.read(info)) if not isinstance(manifest, dict) or not isinstance(manifest.get("sdk"), dict): raise ValueError("Manifest and sdk must be objects") bad_crc = archive.testzip() if bad_crc: raise ValueError("Archive CRC failure: " + bad_crc) if "entry" in manifest and manifest "entry" not in archive.namelist(): raise ValueError("Manifest entry is missing from the ZIP") if not re.fullmatch(r" a-z a-z0-9 (?: .- a-z0-9 +)+", manifest.get("id", "")): raise ValueError("Invalid manifest ID") if not re.fullmatch(r"(0 1-9 \d )\.(0 1-9 \d )\.(0 1-9 \d )", manifest.get("version", "")): raise ValueError("Invalid manifest version") if not isinstance(manifest.get("sdk", {}).get("requires"), str): raise ValueError("Missing sdk.requires") if "system" in manifest and "locales" in manifest: raise ValueError("A system cannot also declare locales") if "django" in manifest and any(key in manifest for key in ("entry", "system", "locales")): raise ValueError("A Django package cannot also declare entry, system or locales") kind = "django" if "django" in manifest else "system" if "system" in manifest else "module" return data, manifest, kind def valid_download(value): parsed = urlsplit(value) if parsed.scheme != "https" or not parsed.hostname or parsed.username or parsed.password or parsed.fragment: raise ValueError("Use an HTTPS download URL without credentials or a fragment") parsed.port def record_shape(record): required = {"id", "version", "sdk", "download", "sha256", "keyId", "signature"} allowed = required {"status", "name", "description", "type", "tags"} if not isinstance(record, dict) or not required <= set(record) or not set(record) <= allowed: raise ValueError("Invalid catalog record fields") if any(not isinstance(value, str) or not value.isascii() for key, value in record.items() if key != "tags"): raise ValueError("Record scalar fields must be ASCII strings") tags = record.get("tags", ) if (not isinstance(tags, list) or len(tags) 24 or any(not isinstance(tag, str) or not tag.strip() or tag != tag.strip() or len(tag) 64 or any(ord(char) < 32 for char in tag) for tag in tags) or len({tag.casefold() for tag in tags}) != len(tags)): raise ValueError("Invalid tags") if record.get("type", "module") not in ("module", "system", "django"): raise ValueError("Invalid package type") if record.get("status", "active") not in ("active", "revoked"): raise ValueError("Invalid release status") if not re.fullmatch(r" a-f0-9 {64}", record "sha256" ): raise ValueError("Invalid SHA-256") valid_download(record "download" ) def sign(args): data, manifest, kind = archive_info(args.archive) record = {"id":manifest "id" , "version":manifest "version" , "sdk":manifest "sdk" "requires" , "type":kind, "download":args.download, "sha256":hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), "keyId":args.key_id, "status":args.status, "signature":""} if args.tag: record "tags" = args.tag record_shape(record) password = None if args.password_env: if args.password_env not in os.environ: raise ValueError("The requested password environment variable is not set") password = os.environ args.password_env .encode("utf-8") private = serialization.load_pem_private_key(Path(args.private_key).read_bytes(), password=password) if not isinstance(private, Ed25519PrivateKey): raise ValueError("The private PEM must contain an Ed25519 key") record "signature" = base64.b64encode(private.sign(canonical(record))).decode("ascii") Exclusive creation protects an existing reviewed record from replacement. with Path(args.output).open("x", encoding="utf-8", newline="
") as stream: json.dump(record, stream, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2) stream.write("
") print("Signed " + record "id" + "@" + record "version" + " - " + args.output) def verify(args): record = json.loads(Path(args.record).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) record_shape(record) data, manifest, kind = archive_info(args.archive) if (record "id" != manifest "id" or record "version" != manifest "version" or record "sdk" != manifest "sdk" "requires" or record.get("type", "module") != kind or not hmac.compare_digest(record "sha256" , hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest())): raise ValueError("The final ZIP does not match the signed identity, SDK, type or digest") keys = json.loads(Path(args.keys).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) raw = base64.b64decode(keys record "keyId" , validate=True) Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(raw).verify(base64.b64decode(record "signature" , validate=True), canonical(record)) print("Verified " + record "id" + "@" + record "version" + " (" + record.get("status", "active") + ")") def self_test(_args): Public, deterministic test material. Never use these bytes as a publisher key. private = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(bytes(range(32))) record = {"id":"example.synthetic", "version":"1.0.0", "sdk":" =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "type":"module", "download":"https://publisher.example/synthetic.zip", "sha256":"0" 64, "keyId":"synthetic-test", "status":"active"} record "signature" = base64.b64encode(private.sign(canonical(record))).decode("ascii") record_shape(record) signature = base64.b64decode(record "signature" ) private.public_key().verify(signature, canonical(record)) record "status" = "revoked" try: private.public_key().verify(signature, canonical(record)) except InvalidSignature: pass else: raise AssertionError("Changing signed status must invalidate the signature") assert canonical({"z":"a", "signature":"ignored", "a":"b"}) == b'{"a":"b","z":"a"}' print("Synthetic Ed25519 and canonicalization tests passed") def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True) signing = sub.add_parser("sign", help="Write one signed record, not a complete catalog") signing.add_argument("--archive", required=True) signing.add_argument("--download", required=True) signing.add_argument("--key-id", required=True) signing.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default= , help="Optional signed catalog tag, repeat for multiple tags") signing.add_argument("--private-key", required=True) signing.add_argument("--password-env", help="Name of an optional PEM-password environment variable") signing.add_argument("--status", choices=("active", "revoked"), default="active") signing.add_argument("--output", required=True) signing.set_defaults(run=sign) verifying = sub.add_parser("verify") verifying.add_argument("--archive", required=True) verifying.add_argument("--record", required=True) verifying.add_argument("--keys", required=True) verifying.set_defaults(run=verify) sub.add_parser("self-test").set_defaults(run=self_test) args = parser.parse_args() try: args.run(args) except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, zipfile.BadZipFile, InvalidSignature) as error: parser.exit(2, "Error: " + (str(error) or type(error).__name__) + "
") if __name__ == "__main__": main() 5. Sign the final bytes and verify them The self-test uses public deterministic synthetic material in memory, never a real publishing key. Run it first. Then replace all example paths, URL and key ID with the publisher’s own values. On POSIX use the existing host .venv/bin/python path in place of python.exe. No dependency install, global Python registration or permanent PATH change is required. powershell & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' ./sign_catalog.py self-test & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' ./sign_catalog.py sign --archive ./example.sheet-name-1.0.1.zip --download https://publisher.example/releases/example.sheet-name-1.0.1.zip --key-id publisher-2026 --private-key 'E:/Publisher private material/publisher-ed25519.pem' --output ./release-record-1.0.1.json & 'E:/Your disposable host/.venv/Scripts/python.exe' ./sign_catalog.py verify --archive ./example.sheet-name-1.0.1.zip --record ./release-record-1.0.1.json --keys ./publisher-public-keys.json publisher-public-keys.json maps key IDs to base64-encoded raw 32-byte Ed25519 public keys. It contains no private key. Export the matching public key through your publisher key-management process. A renamed keyId with the same signature does not verify, because keyId is signed too. The SHA-256 covers the final ZIP bytes, including archive metadata. The signature covers every catalog field except signature, using the exact packages.canonical format: sorted keys, compact comma/colon separators, ensure_ascii true and allow_nan false. Scalar record values are ASCII strings; supported tags are the explicit exception and remain covered by canonicalization. Use --tag Exploration --tag Original when signing if you want catalog categories; there may be at most 24 unique nonblank tags of up to 64 characters. Recompressing, altering a URL, adding a type/status/tag or changing any signed field requires re-signing. Do not sign a directory and later rebuild its ZIP. 6. Assemble and host the catalog The helper writes one record object. The Marketplace feed is an array. To create a new one-release draft catalog without overwriting an existing feed, save and run this small script beside the reviewed record. For an established multi-package catalog, merge the new record into the publisher’s existing reviewed feed, preserve unrelated records and coordinate concurrent publishers. python import json from pathlib import Path record = json.loads(Path("release-record-1.0.1.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) with Path("catalog-draft.json").open("x", encoding="utf-8") as output: json.dump( record , output, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2) output.write("
") Host the immutable ZIP at its signed HTTPS download URL and the reviewed array at an HTTPS catalog URL. Publish the matching public key separately through a trusted channel; do not treat a key obtained only from an untrusted catalog as trust. Confirm a fresh download has the exact signed digest before making the catalog discoverable. Keep backup artifacts and do not replace an already distributed ID/version. This guide supplies no hosting credentials and performs no upload. 7. Configure a disposable consumer and diagnose failures On a disposable consumer only, explicitly configure GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_URL with the catalog HTTPS URL and GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_KEYS_FILE with its trusted public-key JSON. The key file defaults and relative paths remain inside that installation when you choose installation-relative paths. Restart after changing environment configuration. Do not edit a real operator .env just to run this tutorial. The owner can read GET /api/marketplace/status without contacting the remote publisher. Diagnostic What to inspect --- --- marketplace_catalog_missing / invalid Catalog URL, HTTPS, credentials and fragment marketplace_keys_missing / unreadable / invalid / empty Trusted public-key path, JSON and raw key length permission_denied Unknown key ID, signature, revocation or authorization invalid_data Manifest/catalog shape, digest, type, paths and quotas unavailable SDK compatibility, HTTPS transport and publisher availability conflict Refresh activation state and review its new revision Open the appropriate Modules or Systems installation modal to fetch that catalog. Selecting a release installs its verified archive; activate it separately. Configuration failure must not disable signature checks. Test one altered ZIP, one changed signed field, a missing public key and a mismatching type on the disposable consumer, and verify that each is rejected. 8. Revoke or roll back without promising data rollback To revoke, sign a new record for the same existing ID/version with status revoked, keeping its immutable archive identity. Use the helper sign command with --status revoked and a new output filename; changing status without re-signing invalidates the old signature. Replace that version’s catalog record with the signed revoked record while preserving other releases. When consumers fetch that catalog, the host marks installed releases revoked, disables global activation, removes affected table modules, clears replacement preferences and changes table revisions. This is catalog-fetch-driven, not an immediate push to offline users. Selecting an older installed release changes code selection only. Module storage and campaign documents do not revert automatically; deactivating a Django app does not generally undo its migrations. Version and migrate your own storage explicitly and keep compatible code/data recovery backups. Re-enable only a reviewed compatible version. How to use AI to prepare a release text Prepare a reviewable distribution for this exact working package on Gravewright 0.3.0. Inspect the manifest and packages.py before choosing catalog type or SDK range. Preserve private data and earlier work. Provide a new version, exact file tree, final ZIP checksum, canonicalization-compatible Ed25519 signing steps using an existing private key outside the repo, public-key trust setup, HTTPS catalog draft and native disposable-host validation. Do not generate or publish a real key, upload artifacts or mutate an operator environment without authorization. Explain installation versus activation, signed revocation, immutable releases and storage/data rollback limits. SDK (docs:modules) · All tutorials (docs:tutorial-index)

text: Goal and prerequisites Create a campaign using Example Expedition. The package declares character and npc actors, an empty gear item type, and replaces the actor sheet with an editable stamina field. It provides no published game rules or catalogs. Target host: 0.3.0 , SDK 1.0.0 . Sample interface strings are English. Preserve the requested version when adapting.
