{tokenId:context.tokenId} : {}; async function load() { input.disabled=true;saveButton.disabled=true;reloadButton.disabled=true; try { const sheet=await api.actors.sheet(context.actorId,token,{signal}); if(signal.aborted) return; current=sheet;title.textContent=sheet.name; input.value=String(sheet.data.stamina ?? 10); input.disabled=!sheet.canEdit;saveButton.disabled=!sheet.canEdit; dirty=false; } finally { if(!signal.aborted) reloadButton.disabled=false; } } function save() { if(pending) return pending; if(!dirty !current?.canEdit) return Promise.resolve(); const stamina=Number(input.value); if(input.value.trim()==='' !Number.isInteger(stamina) stamina<0 stamina 100) { status.textContent='Enter an integer from 0 to 100.'; return Promise.reject(new Error('Invalid stamina')); } const payload={actorId:context.actorId,name:current.name,version:current.version, sheetVersion:current.sheetVersion,data:{...current.data,stamina}, ...(current.tokenId ? {tokenId:current.tokenId} : {})}; const requestId=crypto.randomUUID(); input.disabled=true;saveButton.disabled=true;reloadButton.disabled=true; pending=(async()= { try { await api.actors.saveSheet(payload,{requestId,signal}); if(signal.aborted) return; await load();status.textContent='Saved.'; } catch(error) { if(!signal.aborted) { if(error.code==='conflict') { await load(); status.textContent='Conflict: server value loaded. Review it before editing again.'; } else status.textContent=error.code 'Save failed. Reload before retrying.'; } throw error; } finally { pending=undefined; if(!signal.aborted){input.disabled=!current?.canEdit;saveButton.disabled=!current?.canEdit;reloadButton.disabled=false;} } })(); return pending; } input.addEventListener('input',()= {dirty=true;},{signal}); form.addEventListener('submit',event= {event.preventDefault();void save().catch(()= {});},{signal}); reloadButton.addEventListener('click',()= { void load().then(()= {if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent='Server value loaded.';}) .catch(error= {if(!signal.aborted)status.textContent=error.code 'unavailable';}); },{signal}); root.closest('.gw-window')?.addEventListener('gravewright:sheet-flush',event= { if(pending dirty) event.detail.waitUntil(save()); },{signal}); onDispose(()= form.remove()); await load(); } }; register('actor.sheet',sheet); register('token.sheet',sheet); }, stop() {} }; styles.css css .gw-module-root .example-panel { padding: var(--space-4, 16px); font-size: 14px; } .gw-module-root .example-panel label { display: block; margin-bottom: var(--space-3, 12px); } .gw-module-root .example-panel button { margin-right: var(--space-2, 8px); } .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.campaign-summary" .example-panel { position: fixed; left: 16px; bottom: 112px; z-index: 20; max-width: min(360px, calc(100vw - 32px)); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-md); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); pointer-events: auto; } How to run 1. Review and install the source ZIP through Systems → Install from ZIP on a disposable host; select Example Expedition for a new campaign. 2. Create a Character or NPC, open its sheet, change Stamina and press Save. Close and reopen the window. 3. Assign a player read access and then edit access to the actor. Compare disabled/enabled controls and the server response. 4. Open the same actor in two sessions. Save one, then save the stale one. Review the refreshed server value before editing again. Expected result and lifecycle The saved value survives reopening. The payload keeps version and sheetVersion from the same read. Linked tokens use the actor; independent tokens use the returned tokenId snapshot. Pending saves participate in gravewright:sheet-flush. Errors and limits A conflict reloads the authoritative sheet and asks the user to review it. Validation rejects blank/noninteger/out-of-range stamina in the sample UI; external system JSON remains subject to host JSON limits and permissions. Add authoritative rule validation only through contracts actually supported by the target host. How to validate - Create/edit/save/reopen both actor types. - Verify read-only access cannot write, including a direct attempted call. - Test linked and independent tokens separately. - Close during a slow save and during an invalid edit; failed flush must keep the window open. How to use AI with this example text Extend Example Expedition with original fields . Keep one installable system package, the declared actor/item types and sheet-flush/version behavior. Preserve unrelated data fields. Do not add a Server Rules companion or require a newer host. State unsupported backend requirements explicitly.

summary: A trusted server app with a valid manifest, AppConfig, URL and permission-checked read view.
text: Goal and prerequisites Expose GET /examples/status/ for the authenticated installation owner. It returns the public Python API version and no campaign content. This is an independent generic server integration, not a companion for an RPG system. Target host: 0.3.0 , SDK 1.0.0 . Sample interface strings are English. Preserve the requested version when adapting. Complete files Download source package ZIP (../../assets/examples/packages/django/django-source.zip) These are complete unsigned sources. No private signing key is included. - manifest.json (../../assets/examples/packages/django/manifest.json) - example_status/__init__.py (../../assets/examples/packages/django/example_status/__init__.py) - example_status/apps.py (../../assets/examples/packages/django/example_status/apps.py) - example_status/urls.py (../../assets/examples/packages/django/example_status/urls.py) - example_status/views.py (../../assets/examples/packages/django/example_status/views.py) - LICENSE.txt (../../assets/examples/packages/django/LICENSE.txt) - README.md (../../assets/examples/packages/django/README.md) Complete manifest json { "id": "example.server-status", "name": "Example server status", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "description": "Trusted owner-only read endpoint with no models or background tasks.", "author": "Gravewright documentation examples", "license": "GPL-3.0-only", "django": { "apps": "example_status.apps.ExampleStatusConfig" } } Example code example_status/__init__.py python example_status/apps.py python from django.apps import AppConfig class ExampleStatusConfig(AppConfig): name = "example_status" label = "example_status" gravewright_urlconf = "example_status.urls" example_status/urls.py python from django.urls import path from .views import status urlpatterns = path("examples/status/", status, name="example_status") example_status/views.py python from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required from django.http import JsonResponse from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET from api import API_VERSION @login_required @require_GET def status(request): if request.user.role != "owner": return JsonResponse({"error": "permission_denied"}, status=403) return JsonResponse({"ok": True, "apiVersion": API_VERSION}) How to run 1. Review all Python sources. In an isolated host, install the source ZIP through Modules → Install from ZIP. For Marketplace publication, the signed catalog record must carry type: django. 2. Installation validates/extracts only. Activate the trusted app explicitly using the managed Runner or main.py and the documented uv-backed supervisor. 3. After restart, open /examples/status/ as owner, participant and an anonymous browser. Deactivate and restart to remove the route. Expected result and lifecycle Owner GET returns 200 with ok and apiVersion. An authenticated participant receives 403. An anonymous request follows the normal login redirect. An authenticated non-GET receives 405. No models, migrations or background tasks are added. Errors and limits Missing AppConfig package, duplicate app labels or invalid manifest/pins fail installation/activation. Django manifests cannot include entry, system or locales. Python execution requires owner activation; do not paste server code into a browser manifest. How to validate - Use Django RequestFactory or an isolated Client to check owner/participant/anonymous/method behavior. - Confirm the route appears only after activation and no database content changes during reads. - Review supervisor checks/recovery; deactivation does not generally undo app migrations, although this example defines none. How to use AI with this example text Adapt example_status into a read-only owner administration endpoint for generic task . Keep authentication, require_GET, explicit owner authorization, a distinct AppConfig label and no startup side effects. If campaign data is needed, call the supported Python API with a real authorized Context. Do not bypass permissions with ORM writes.

Download the complete package Download source ZIP (../../assets/examples/surfaces/table-interface/table-interface-source.zip) · manifest.json (../../assets/examples/surfaces/table-interface/manifest.json) · main.mjs (../../assets/examples/surfaces/table-interface/main.mjs) · styles.css (../../assets/examples/surfaces/table-interface/styles.css) · LICENSE.txt (../../assets/examples/surfaces/table-interface/LICENSE.txt) Save all four files in the same folder. ZIP the folder contents , with manifest.json directly at the archive root. Do not include a wrapper folder, local state or private keys. Local upload is the owner’s trust decision; for catalog distribution, use the signing workflow in the module reference (docs:modules). text table-interface/ manifest.json main.mjs styles.css LICENSE.txt manifest.json json { "id": "example.surface-table-interface", "name": "Authorized document search", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "description": "Search table documents from a workspace panel and render their names, kinds and snippets as text.", "author": "Gravewright documentation", "license": "MIT", "entry": "main.mjs" } main.mjs javascript // Original documentation example. License: MIT. Target: Gravewright 0.3.0, SDK 1.x. export default { start({ api, styles }) { styles.use("styles.css"); api.i18n.register({ "en": { "Search": "Search", "Search documents": "Search documents", "No results": "No results", "Refresh": "Refresh", "Loading…": "Loading…", "Error: {code}": "Error: {code}", "Authorized document search": "Authorized document search" }, "pt-BR": { "Search": "Buscar", "Search documents": "Buscar documentos", "No results": "Nenhum resultado", "Refresh": "Atualizar", "Loading…": "Carregando…", "Error: {code}": "Erro: {code}", "Authorized document search": "Busca de documentos autorizados" } }); }, register({ register }) { register("table.interface", { mode: "augment", mount: this.mount }); }, async mount({ root, context, api, storage, viewport, events, signal, onDispose }) { const el = (tag, text) = { const node = root.ownerDocument.createElement(tag); if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text; return node; }; const t = (key, params) = api.i18n.t(key, params); const panel = el("section"); panel.className = "gw-example"; const heading = el("h3", t("Authorized document search")); const output = el("pre"); output.setAttribute("role", "status"); panel.append(heading, output); root.append(panel); onDispose(() = panel.remove()); const report = error = { if (!signal.aborted) output.textContent = t("Error: {code}", { code: error.code ?? "unavailable" }); }; const form = el("form"); const label = el("label", t("Search documents")); const input = el("input"); input.type = "search"; input.maxLength = 200; const submit = el("button", t("Search")); submit.type = "submit"; label.append(input); form.append(label, submit); panel.append(form); let ticket = 0; form.addEventListener("submit", async event = { event.preventDefault(); const current = ++ticket; try { const value = await api.table.search(input.value.trim(), { signal }); if (signal.aborted current !== ticket) return; output.textContent = value.map(result = result.title + " (" + result.kind + ") · " + (result.snippet ?? "")).join("\n") t("No results"); } catch (error) { if (current === ticket) report(error); } }, { signal }); }, stop() { // Mount and module lifetimes already dispose styles, catalogs and subscriptions. } }; outline-offset: 2px; } data-module-id="example.surface-table-interface" .gw-example--compact { padding: var(--space-1); } data-module-id="example.surface-table-interface" .gw-example-center { position: absolute; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); pointer-events: none; color: var(--text); background: var(--surface); padding: var(--space-1); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); font: 14px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; } data-module-id="example.surface-table-interface" .gw-example { position: fixed; top: 64px; left: var(--space-4); width: 360px; max-width: min(360px, calc(100vw - 32px)); max-height: 40vh; overflow: auto; margin: var(--space-0); z-index: 20; } Expected result and cleanup Search table documents from a workspace panel and render their names, kinds and snippets as text. The native interface remains usable. Closing a sheet, switching scenes, leaving the table or deactivating the module aborts the mount. Listeners use signal ; events and owned elements are released through onDispose . Async reads check cancellation and discard old responses before rendering. Errors are displayed through error.code , including network failures. The search panel floats below the top bar, constrained to the viewport width and 40% of its height, with its own scrolling. Its z-index: 20 is above table controls and below windows and modals. Every selector in this package uses data-module-id , preserving host and other module styles. Validate on a disposable table 1. Search the same term as GM and as player; hidden documents must not appear. Submit quickly twice and check that the latest search wins. 2. Open/close three times, then deactivate while a read or modal is pending. Check that no old panel or error appears after disposal. 3. Test empty state, long document names, keyboard navigation and a narrow viewport. Compare GM and player accounts. 4. Check the browser console. These source examples have runtime contract tests; installation and visual behavior still require validation on the target host. How to use AI for this surface text Adapt the table.interface example for concrete goal on Gravewright 0.3.0. Read registry.json, this surface’s context schema, frontend.json and the native services used. Keep start/register/stop, mount-scoped api, signal, onDispose and native modals. Provide the complete manifest and files. Do not use app.shell/inside.content in packages. Do not invent payload fields, core RPG rules, permissions or APIs. Test player/GM, empty data, abort, repeated mounting and this example’s behavior. Explain limitations and which checks actually ran. title: Search: all 7 kinds and the empty filter
summary: Eight concrete browser functions, quest versus journal categories, authorized recents and validation.
text: Use the api supplied to a mounted module block. These are complete JavaScript functions; import one into main.js and call it inside mount({ api, signal }) . See the minimal package (modules.html minimal-browser-package) for installation and lifecycle. As GM, create synthetic documents with the names below in a disposable campaign. Grant a player read access when testing visibility. Command search must be enabled on the host. Every query has at least two characters. An empty filter searches all categories; omitting kind has the same effect. kind describes the result category. Quests and boards remain journal documents: their result type is journal , while kind is quest or quest_board . The journal filter returns other journals, excluding quests and quest boards. kind: "" : All document kinds Prerequisite: create at least two Beacon documents in different categories. javascript export async function findAll(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon", { kind: "", signal, }); } Expected result: Up to 20 readable documents of any category matching Beacon , sorted by title. Validate: run findAll(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. kind: "actor" : Actors Prerequisite: create Beacon Scout in the actor category. javascript export async function findActors(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon Scout", { kind: "actor", signal, }); } Expected result: Readable documents with kind: "actor" matching Beacon Scout . Validate: run findActors(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. kind: "item" : Items Prerequisite: create Beacon Rope in the item category. javascript export async function findItems(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon Rope", { kind: "item", signal, }); } Expected result: Readable documents with kind: "item" matching Beacon Rope . Validate: run findItems(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. kind: "journal" : Journals Prerequisite: create Beacon Notes in the journal category. javascript export async function findJournals(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon Notes", { kind: "journal", signal, }); } Expected result: Readable documents with kind: "journal" matching Beacon Notes . Validate: run findJournals(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. kind: "quest" : Quests Prerequisite: create Beacon Rescue in the quest category. javascript export async function findQuests(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon Rescue", { kind: "quest", signal, }); } Expected result: Readable documents with kind: "quest" matching Beacon Rescue . Validate: run findQuests(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. kind: "quest_board" : Quest boards Prerequisite: create Beacon Jobs in the quest_board category. javascript export async function findQuestBoards(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon Jobs", { kind: "quest_board", signal, }); } Expected result: Readable documents with kind: "quest_board" matching Beacon Jobs . Validate: run findQuestBoards(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. kind: "scene" : Scenes Prerequisite: create Beacon Harbor in the scene category. javascript export async function findScenes(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon Harbor", { kind: "scene", signal, }); } Expected result: Readable documents with kind: "scene" matching Beacon Harbor . Validate: run findScenes(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. kind: "compendium" : Compendiums Prerequisite: create Beacon Collection in the compendium category. javascript export async function findCompendiums(api, signal) { return api.table.search("Beacon Collection", { kind: "compendium", signal, }); } Expected result: Readable documents with kind: "compendium" matching Beacon Collection . Validate: run findCompendiums(api, signal) as GM and player; revoke access to one document and repeat. No matches returns an empty array, not an error. Recent results and errors For recents, use an empty query and up to 12 references previously returned by search. Use type: "journal" for a quest/board; quest is not a valid recent.type . Every call revalidates campaign and read access. javascript export async function recentDocuments(api, previousResults, signal) { const recent = previousResults.slice(0, 12).map(({ id, type }) = ({ id, type })); return api.table.search("", { recent, signal }); } A query shorter than two characters without recent returns . More than 200 characters, unknown filters and invalid references are rejected. Disabled search or revoked membership prevents the call; the adapter exposes codes such as permission_denied and invalid_data . cancelled / stale_context indicate cancellation or a disposed block. Do not cache permissions from search results. How to use AI to build a typed search text On the target release, inspect table/services.py and domain-api.js. Adapt the quest_board example into a readable-board picker. Render titles with textContent, use the block signal and handle empty results, revoked permissions and cancellation. Do not invent api.quests or expose private notes. Include a GM/player check using Beacon fixtures.

title: Actor images: portrait and token
summary: Two complete File-picker mount functions using the actual multipart host.call operation.
text: Both examples use host.call("actor.image.upload", payload) , a block SDK operation. File transmission is not an api.actors.update operation. The result is {url} ; the server validates campaign, actor editing and image content. Prepare the minimal package (modules.html minimal-browser-package), a synthetic actor and an original PNG/JPEG/WebP. Register each function on actor.sheet : register("actor.sheet", mountPortraitUpload) or register("actor.sheet", mountTokenUpload) . The context must provide actorId and canEdit ; the user must be GM or have actor editing permission. The control is disabled unless canEdit is true; the server remains the authority. Copy one complete function into main.js . Do not pass the JSON Schema file descriptor as file : browser code passes the real File from the picker. The bridge creates multipart data and metadata. Do not encode images as base64. kind: "portrait" : Upload a portrait Use: change the actor portrait displayed by its sheet. javascript export function mountPortraitUpload({ root, context, host, signal }) { const doc = root.ownerDocument; const label = doc.createElement("label"); label.textContent = "Upload a portrait"; const input = doc.createElement("input"); input.type = "file"; input.accept = "image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp"; const status = doc.createElement("output"); status.setAttribute("aria-live", "polite"); const preview = doc.createElement("img"); preview.alt = "Uploaded image"; preview.width = 128; preview.height = 128; preview.hidden = true; label.append(input); root.append(label, status, preview); input.disabled = context.canEdit !== true; input.addEventListener("change", async () = { const file = input.files?. 0 ; if (!file signal.aborted) return; input.disabled = true; status.textContent = "Uploading…"; try { const result = await host.call("actor.image.upload", { id: context.actorId, kind: "portrait", file, }, { signal }); if (signal.aborted) return; preview.src = result.url; preview.hidden = false; status.textContent = "Image saved."; } catch (error) { if (!signal.aborted) status.textContent = "Failed: " + error.code; } finally { if (!signal.aborted) input.disabled = context.canEdit !== true; } }, { signal }); } Expected result: the preview uses the returned authorized URL and the actor retains its new portrait image after reopening. Validate: upload a small image, reopen the sheet and check the image. Repeat as an authorized player and a read-only user. Close during upload and verify that the disposed UI receives no updates. kind: "token" : Upload token artwork Use: change the actor token artwork; this does not set position, scale or linking of existing placed tokens. javascript export function mountTokenUpload({ root, context, host, signal }) { const doc = root.ownerDocument; const label = doc.createElement("label"); label.textContent = "Upload token artwork"; const input = doc.createElement("input"); input.type = "file"; input.accept = "image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp"; const status = doc.createElement("output"); status.setAttribute("aria-live", "polite"); const preview = doc.createElement("img"); preview.alt = "Uploaded image"; preview.width = 128; preview.height = 128; preview.hidden = true; label.append(input); root.append(label, status, preview); input.disabled = context.canEdit !== true; input.addEventListener("change", async () = { const file = input.files?. 0 ; if (!file signal.aborted) return; input.disabled = true; status.textContent = "Uploading…"; try { const result = await host.call("actor.image.upload", { id: context.actorId, kind: "token", file, }, { signal }); if (signal.aborted) return; preview.src = result.url; preview.hidden = false; status.textContent = "Image saved."; } catch (error) { if (!signal.aborted) status.textContent = "Failed: " + error.code; } finally { if (!signal.aborted) input.disabled = context.canEdit !== true; } }, { signal }); } Expected result: the preview uses the returned authorized URL and the actor retains its new token image after reopening. Validate: upload a small image, reopen the sheet and check the image. Repeat as an authorized player and a read-only user. Close during upload and verify that the disposed UI receives no updates. Limits, errors and lifecycle The server accepts PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 10,000,000 bytes and 25,000,000 pixels. It normalizes orientation and saves PNG. The accept attribute only guides the picker; it does not replace validation. An inaccessible actor may produce not_found or permission_denied ; invalid images produce invalid_data ; transport failures may produce unavailable . Disposal cancels the context: skip DOM updates after signal.aborted . A server-committed upload remains saved even when the UI closes. The listener uses {signal} and is removed on disposal. Read api.actors.get(context.actorId) again before a later edit that depends on the actor version. How to use AI to build an image picker text Inspect the actor.image.upload schemas and browser-bridge.js on the target release. Adapt mountTokenUpload to display accessible progress using host.call's onProgress option. Preserve multipart File data, native permissions, signal, cleanup and textContent. Do not invent an endpoint or write a user URL directly into the actor. Include invalid-image, close-during-upload and read-only-player checks.

title: Compendium entries: all five kinds
summary: Capture actor, item, journal, scene and deck resources with authorized reads and GM imports.
text: api.compendiums.add captures a resource that already exists in the campaign. kind selects its resource category; resourceId is its real UUID. The server stores a snapshot with dependencies in a portable bundle. It does not accept arbitrary sheet JSON instead of resourceId . Run these examples in a module mounted in a disposable campaign using its api and signal . You must be GM, have the source documents in the same campaign and choose an unlocked table-created compendium. Native and installed-system compendiums are read only. Create the destination once and keep created.id as packId : javascript export async function createExamplePack(api, signal) { const created = await api.compendiums.create({ name: "Beacon Collection" }, { requestId: crypto.randomUUID(), signal, }); return created.id; } kind: "actor" : Actor snapshot Use the UUID of a Beacon Scout actor created with the example system character type. The snapshot preserves actor type and data. javascript export async function storeActor(api, packId, resourceId, signal, requestId = crypto.randomUUID()) { const added = await api.compendiums.add({ packId, kind: "actor", resourceId, name: "Beacon Scout", }, { requestId, signal }); return api.compendiums.read({ packId, id: added.id }, { signal }); } Expected result: storeActor(api, packId, resourceId, signal) returns an entry with kind: "actor" , id , name , data and version . The source remains in the campaign. Validate: inspect the compendium entry; import a copy in a compatible test campaign and open the created document. kind: "item" : Item snapshot Use the UUID of a Beacon Rope item with the gear type registered by the campaign system. The snapshot preserves item type and data. javascript export async function storeItem(api, packId, resourceId, signal, requestId = crypto.randomUUID()) { const added = await api.compendiums.add({ packId, kind: "item", resourceId, name: "Beacon Rope", }, { requestId, signal }); return api.compendiums.read({ packId, id: added.id }, { signal }); } Expected result: storeItem(api, packId, resourceId, signal) returns an entry with kind: "item" , id , name , data and version . The source remains in the campaign. Validate: inspect the compendium entry; import a copy in a compatible test campaign and open the created document. kind: "journal" : Journal snapshot Use the UUID of the Beacon Notes journal. The same kind accepts native journal document types; a quest still uses kind journal when stored in a compendium. javascript export async function storeJournal(api, packId, resourceId, signal, requestId = crypto.randomUUID()) { const added = await api.compendiums.add({ packId, kind: "journal", resourceId, name: "Beacon Notes", }, { requestId, signal }); return api.compendiums.read({ packId, id: added.id }, { signal }); } Expected result: storeJournal(api, packId, resourceId, signal) returns an entry with kind: "journal" , id , name , data and version . The source remains in the campaign. Validate: inspect the compendium entry; import a copy in a compatible test campaign and open the created document. kind: "scene" : Scene snapshot Use the UUID of the campaign scene Beacon Harbor . The read body may show only its name; the portable bundle retains the exported resource and dependencies. javascript export async function storeScene(api, packId, resourceId, signal, requestId = crypto.randomUUID()) { const added = await api.compendiums.add({ packId, kind: "scene", resourceId, name: "Beacon Harbor", }, { requestId, signal }); return api.compendiums.read({ packId, id: added.id }, { signal }); } Expected result: storeScene(api, packId, resourceId, signal) returns an entry with kind: "scene" , id , name , data and version . The source remains in the campaign. Validate: inspect the compendium entry; import a copy in a compatible test campaign and open the created document. kind: "deck" : Deck snapshot Use the UUID of the existing Beacon Signals deck from api.cards.state().decks. Do not use a deck_definition_id: add expects a deck instance. javascript export async function storeDeck(api, packId, resourceId, signal, requestId = crypto.randomUUID()) { const added = await api.compendiums.add({ packId, kind: "deck", resourceId, name: "Beacon Signals", }, { requestId, signal }); return api.compendiums.read({ packId, id: added.id }, { signal }); } Expected result: storeDeck(api, packId, resourceId, signal) returns an entry with kind: "deck" , id , name , data and version . The source remains in the campaign. Validate: inspect the compendium entry; import a copy in a compatible test campaign and open the deck to check its cards. Reading and importing are different actions state lists metadata without bodies or portable bundles. read returns authorized data without creating documents. import creates a copy and requires GM. Use the entry id returned by an example above: javascript export async function importExampleEntry(api, packId, entryId, signal) { return api.compendiums.import({ packId, id: entryId }, { requestId: crypto.randomUUID(), signal, }); } The import destination is the mounted block's campaign; this call has no field for choosing a different campaign. To test another campaign, use a block mounted there and its own resource and compendium IDs. Each logical action needs its own UUID; retain it and pass the function's fifth argument only when retrying that same add after transport failure. If add committed but read failed, inspect state/read before adding again: these calls are separate transactions. Errors and validation Writes require GM. Resources from another campaign and inaccessible packs are unavailable; locked packs reject editing; an unknown kind rejects add. A mismatched system rejects import. Do not treat a failed read as empty content or force versions. For configure/remove/delete, read the pack/entry version and use the operation's documented version field. Validate every kind with a real source, then try the same add as a player, with a locked pack and with another campaign's UUID. Confirm that the original is unchanged and the imported copy retains its resources. A player with a valid read grant may read; importing remains a GM action. How to use AI to build a snapshot library text Inspect frontend.json and compendiums/services.py on the target release. Extend storeScene with a readable scene selector and an unlocked GM compendium selector. Use a real resourceId, a new requestId per action and read the result. Handle errors, empty state and retry without duplicate captures. Do not send arbitrary scene JSON to add or replace the bundle with a name.

title: Compendium packs: 3 installed and 7 local types
summary: Complete original JSON for every pack type, exact manifest restrictions and downloadable fixtures.
text: A pack uses type , called a “pack kind” in documentation. It differs from entry.kind returned by the directory and from entry.type , the system's document type. Do not put kind at the root of manifest.json. There are two origins with different limits: collections supplied by an installed system package and local catalogs prepared by the operator. All Beacon data below is original and synthetic. Pack type Directory kind Installed system Local catalog --- --- --- --- actor_pack actor Yes Yes item_pack item Yes Yes spell_pack item Yes Yes journal_pack journal No Yes scene_pack scene No Yes card_pack deck No Yes deck_pack deck No Yes Installed-system preparation Use a target release supporting content.compendiums , available since VTT 0.2.1. The system must be installed, active at the campaign's exact pinned version and not revoked. Start from the minimal package (modules.html minimal-browser-package) and use this manifest. It explicitly registers character, gear and spell; these names belong to the example system. json { "id": "example.beacon", "name": "Beacon Example System", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.js", "description": "Original example document types and compendium data.", "author": "Example author", "license": "MIT", "system": { "actorTypes": { "id": "character", "label": "Character" } , "itemTypes": { "id": "gear", "label": "Gear" }, { "id": "spell", "label": "Spell" } }, "content": { "compendiums": "compendiums/beacon.json" } } Place the collection at compendiums/beacon.json inside the same package. Download the three-pack collection (../../assets/examples/compendiums/system-collection.json). The minimal main.js below only demonstrates types and data; add sheets through the SDK surfaces. Include the chosen license, customize author/name and follow Systems and modules (modules.html) for ZIP installation or signing. Do not modify release files after installation. javascript export default { start() {}, register() {}, stop() {}, }; Installed system: actor_pack Imports Beacon Scout as a character actor with stamina 6. This is a complete single-pack collection; use it alone or combine packs in the downloadable collection packs array. json { "name": "Beacon Examples", "packs": { "id": "beacon-actors", "label": "Beacon Actors", "type": "actor_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-scout", "name": "Beacon Scout", "type": "character", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "stamina": 6 } } } } Validate: locate beacon-scout in the system pack and import as GM. The directory shows kind: "actor" ; the imported document has type: "character" . Installed system: item_pack Imports Beacon Rope as a gear item with length 10. This is a complete single-pack collection; use it alone or combine packs in the downloadable collection packs array. json { "name": "Beacon Examples", "packs": { "id": "beacon-items", "label": "Beacon Items", "type": "item_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-rope", "name": "Beacon Rope", "type": "gear", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "length": 10 } } } } Validate: locate beacon-rope in the system pack and import as GM. The directory shows kind: "item" ; the imported document has type: "gear" . Installed system: spell_pack Imports Beacon Glow as a spell item with color blue. spell_pack is an item compatibility alias; it does not add spell rules to the core. This is a complete single-pack collection; use it alone or combine packs in the downloadable collection packs array. json { "name": "Beacon Examples", "packs": { "id": "beacon-spells", "label": "Beacon Spells", "type": "spell_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-glow", "name": "Beacon Glow", "type": "spell", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "color": "blue" } } } } Validate: locate beacon-glow in the system pack and import as GM. The directory shows kind: "item" ; the imported document has type: "spell" . Validate the contract before installation Each collection is limited to 8 MiB, 64 packs and 20,000 entries; each entry is limited to 256 KiB and JSON nesting to 24 levels. A manifest accepts up to 16 collection paths. IDs must be unique within their pack/collection, up to 120 characters, use ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens, and start with a letter or digit. Names/labels are limited to 120 characters. Entry document types must be registered by the manifest and systemId must be example.beacon for this example. Installed-system collections have NO campaigns list. The host binds access to the campaign's approved version. A player needs a valid read grant; importing requires GM. Declared collections are not served through assets.json: discover IDs with api.compendiums.state and read through the authorized API. To run the real validator in a development checkout, save the JSONs as manifest.json and compendiums/beacon.json in a disposable folder. Run this in python manage.py shell with that folder as the working directory, or adjust the two paths: python import json from pathlib import Path from gravewright.compendiums.content import validate_collection manifest = json.loads(Path("manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) collection = json.loads(Path("compendiums/beacon.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) validate_collection( collection, manifest "id" , {row "id" for row in manifest "system" "actorTypes" }, {row "id" for row in manifest "system" "itemTypes" }, ) print("Collection accepted") Local catalogs: operator preparation This is a host-operator file integration, not a browser module write capability. In a development checkout use the directory configured by settings.GRAVEWRIGHT_CONTENT_ROOT; do not assume a global directory or edit .env for an experiment. Configuration (configuration.html) and the Runner determine the effective root. A local catalog uses a subdirectory with index.json and a campaigns array containing real campaign UUIDs authorized by the operator. The UUID below is synthetic: replace it with your disposable campaign using example.beacon. These catalogs are read only in the tabletop. journal_pack/scene_pack/card_pack/deck_pack belong to this origin and are rejected in an installed package's content.compendiums. Download the complete local index.json (../../assets/examples/compendiums/local/index.json) and original beacon.webp artwork (../../assets/examples/compendiums/local/artwork/beacon.webp). Preserve local/index.json and local/artwork/beacon.webp. Each block below is one complete pack for the index packs array. The minimal collection wrapper is: json { "name": "Beacon Local Examples", "systemId": "example.beacon", "campaigns": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" , "packs": } Local catalog: actor_pack json { "id": "beacon-actors", "label": "Beacon Actors", "type": "actor_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-scout", "name": "Beacon Scout", "type": "character", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "stamina": 6 } } } Expected result and validation: Creates a character actor. The type must exist in the campaign system; this example uses stamina 6. Refresh compendiums, read the entry by ID and import as GM; inspect the created resource in the disposable campaign. Local catalog: item_pack json { "id": "beacon-items", "label": "Beacon Items", "type": "item_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-rope", "name": "Beacon Rope", "type": "gear", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "length": 10 } } } Expected result and validation: Creates a gear item with length 10. Do not use an item type from a different system. Refresh compendiums, read the entry by ID and import as GM; inspect the created resource in the disposable campaign. Local catalog: spell_pack json { "id": "beacon-spells", "label": "Beacon Spells", "type": "spell_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-glow", "name": "Beacon Glow", "type": "spell", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "color": "blue" } } } Expected result and validation: Creates a spell item. The directory kind remains item rather than a native spell entity. Refresh compendiums, read the entry by ID and import as GM; inspect the created resource in the disposable campaign. Local catalog: journal_pack json { "id": "beacon-journals", "label": "Beacon Journals", "type": "journal_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-notes", "name": "Beacon Notes", "type": "diary", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": {} } } Expected result and validation: Creates an empty diary journal named Beacon Notes. Add original content through the interface after import. Refresh compendiums, read the entry by ID and import as GM; inspect the created resource in the disposable campaign. Local catalog: scene_pack json { "id": "beacon-scenes", "label": "Beacon Scenes", "type": "scene_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-harbor", "name": "Beacon Harbor", "type": "scene", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "width": 1400, "height": 980 } } } Expected result and validation: Creates the Beacon Harbor scene at 1400 × 980 pixels. This minimal entry has no background image, walls or objects. Refresh compendiums, read the entry by ID and import as GM; inspect the created resource in the disposable campaign. Local catalog: card_pack json { "id": "beacon-cards", "label": "Beacon Cards", "type": "card_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-card-deck", "name": "Beacon Signals", "type": "deck", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "cards": { "name": "Beacon Signal", "artwork": "artwork/beacon.webp", "quantity": 1 } } } } Expected result and validation: Creates a deck instance with one Beacon Signal card. WebP artwork must exist relative to the index directory. Refresh compendiums, read the entry by ID and import as GM; inspect the created resource in the disposable campaign. Local catalog: deck_pack json { "id": "beacon-decks", "label": "Beacon Decks", "type": "deck_pack", "entries": { "id": "beacon-deck", "name": "Beacon Watch", "type": "deck", "systemId": "example.beacon", "data": { "cards": { "name": "Beacon Watch", "artwork": "artwork/beacon.webp", "quantity": 2 } } } } Expected result and validation: Creates a deck instance with two Beacon Watch cards. quantity expands copies. card_pack and deck_pack use the same importer. Refresh compendiums, read the entry by ID and import as GM; inspect the created resource in the disposable campaign. Install only the local example catalog With both downloads saved under a local folder and the test campaign created, run this in the disposable installation's python manage.py shell. Set sample to the download folder and campaign_id to the real UUID. It reads the configured root and creates a new beacon-examples directory; it fails if that directory already exists, preserving existing installations and content. python import json import shutil from pathlib import Path from uuid import UUID from django.conf import settings sample = Path("downloaded-examples/local").resolve() campaign_id = str(UUID("00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001")) collection = json.loads((sample / "index.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) artwork = sample / "artwork" / "beacon.webp" if not artwork.is_file(): raise FileNotFoundError(artwork) collection "campaigns" = campaign_id root = Path(settings.GRAVEWRIGHT_CONTENT_ROOT).resolve() destination = root / "beacon-examples" destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False) (destination / "artwork").mkdir() shutil.copy2(artwork, destination / "artwork" / "beacon.webp") (destination / "index.json").write_text( json.dumps(collection, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8" ) print(destination) Errors and final checks An installed-system collection with unregistered document types, a wrong systemId, duplicate IDs or one of the four local-only pack types fails validation before installation. In the tabletop, an inactive/revoked version or changed approved bytes makes content unavailable. Do not repair integrity failures by editing installed files: prepare a new version. For local catalogs, missing campaigns or a wrong UUID hides the catalog. Cards/decks require 1–500 cards, integer quantity between 1 and 500, at most 500 expanded cards and valid WebP files up to 10 MiB inside the catalog directory; external paths and missing files fail. Check the directory tree and every import result. Packs start GM-visible; grant reading through the permission flow and confirm that a player may read but cannot import. How to use AI to create original-content packs text Inspect content.py, catalog.py and the target release manifest. Build an installed system with one actor_pack, one item_pack and one spell_pack using only declared document types, the correct systemId and original content. Provide complete JSONs, validate with validate_collection and demonstrate state/read/import. Explain why journal_pack, scene_pack, card_pack and deck_pack cannot enter that ZIP; if I request a local catalog, use the effective setting and explicit campaigns without replacing existing files.

title: Blueprint examples for every object kind
summary: Choose a complete recipe for door, lever, torch or region, then inspect execution/data connections and all 49 node types.
text: Choose an object kind A Smart Object document has four accepted blueprint.kind values. A node’s type and a connection’s kind are separate contracts. This guide covers each with complete JSON, editor steps, expected results, validation and a task-specific AI prompt. blueprint.kind Native states Starting events Complete example --- --- --- --- door closed, open, locked interact, destroy Door toggle with preserved lock (docs:example-blueprint-door) lever off, on interact, presence:enter, presence:exit, destroy Visible switch and Empty Object (docs:example-blueprint-lever) torch off, on interact, presence:enter, presence:exit, destroy Turn and set flame (docs:example-blueprint-torch) region empty, occupied presence:enter, presence:exit, destroy First-entry/last-exit pressure plate (docs:example-blueprint-region) Every kind can also receive a valid named signal:<name graph. A region has no direct interact event. An Empty Object is a lever without an image , private to the GM. A composed torch owns a linked native light; there is no Blueprint kind named light . Understand the three vocabularies Field Values Example --- --- --- blueprint.kind door, lever, torch, region The torch owns off/on mechanism states edge.kind execution, data Flow and typed values (docs:example-blueprint-connections) node.type 49 validated node types One complete graph per node type (docs:example-blueprint-nodes) The editor may label an event onInteract , onAreaEnter or onAreaExited . Stored graph/event IDs are interact , presence:enter and presence:exit . Use the serialized IDs shown in the examples. Do not recreate retired change or state-specific event graphs. ! Real Smart Object editor showing a door graph, a light, a message and a state action (../../assets/wiki/blueprints-030.webp) Existing Gravewright 0.3.0 screenshot, English interface. It shows the editor’s controls; the downloadable recipes below define their own graphs. Get the examples These JSON files describe the stored Blueprint v2 subdocument . They are development fixtures, not an installable module, a complete Builder project or a campaign archive. Recreate the nodes in the editor, or use the fixtures in isolated contributor tests. This guide does not assume a JSON import button in the Smart Object editor. Download the complete example bundle (../../assets/examples/blueprints/examples.zip) or the validator (../../assets/examples/blueprints/check-examples.py). Every example uses original synthetic data. The host's internal Python evaluator is for source development; browser modules must use the public SDK. Run the fixture in a development installation Extract the example bundle to data/blueprint-examples inside a disposable checkout of the documented host. From the checkout root, run: sh uv run --locked python data/blueprint-examples/check-examples.py --host . The checker configures an in-memory database, blocks database queries and calls the real clean_blueprint and evaluate_graph functions. It validates all four object kinds, both connection kinds and all 49 node types, including requestRoll and setQuestStatus. It checks both roll visibilities, all six quest statuses and continuing execution without drawing dice or changing journals. This verifies document shape and predicted actions. Test behavior is still needed to check real targets, authorization and the complete server chain. Safe starting assumptions - An event only starts a connected execution path. It does not automatically toggle, change artwork or set a flame. - Conditions and properties read the state at the beginning of the event. Use explicit actions for changes. - Region occupancy comes from authoritative token commands and eligible presence filters. - Simulate predicts one graph locally. Test behavior checks the server chain with rollback. Generation/update and player activation are separate operations. - Source definitions and graph links remain GM-only. A player sees the authorized resulting presentation. How to use AI to choose a kind text I am targeting Gravewright 0.3.3, source cc4fd08. Read blueprints.py and the Map Builder guide. My behavior is: describe the trigger, visible object, state changes, targets and audience . Choose among door/lever/torch/region and explain why. Start from the matching complete recipe. Preserve actual state and event IDs, execution/data ports and player permissions. Return complete JSON plus editor instructions and meaningful GM/player tests. title: Blueprint kind door: open, close and preserve a lock
summary: A complete v2 door graph that opens a closed door, closes an open door and leaves a locked door unchanged.
text: Goal Create a toggle for a native door while keeping lock handling explicit. The graph starts at interact, checks the current state and requests exactly one supported state action. It has no image, light or audio dependencies. These JSON files describe the stored Blueprint v2 subdocument . They are development fixtures, not an installable module, a complete Builder project or a campaign archive. Recreate the nodes in the editor, or use the fixtures in isolated contributor tests. This guide does not assume a JSON import button in the Smart Object editor. Download the complete example bundle (../../assets/examples/blueprints/examples.zip) or the validator (../../assets/examples/blueprints/check-examples.py). Every example uses original synthetic data. The host's internal Python evaluator is for source development; browser modules must use the public SDK. Build it in the editor 1. Draw a Door in Map Builder, name it Example Gate and choose Closed as its initial state. 2. Double-click the door to open Smart object. Select On interaction. Connect it to Check state: Opened. 3. Connect True to Change state: Closed. Connect False to a second Check state: Closed. 4. Connect the second condition’s True to Change state: Opened. Leave its False branch disconnected; a Locked door reaches that branch and has no authored state action. 5. Keep Default appearance by state on Native appearance. Closing shows the native door image; opening uses the native open presentation. Complete JSON Download door-toggle.json (../../assets/examples/blueprints/door-toggle.json) json { "version": 2, "kind": "door", "states": { "closed": { "appearance": "inherit" }, "open": { "appearance": "inherit" }, "locked": { "appearance": "inherit" } }, "graphs": { "interact": { "nodes": { "id": "start", "type": "event", "x": 40, "y": 80, "event": "interact" }, { "id": "isOpen", "type": "condition", "x": 300, "y": 80, "state": "open" }, { "id": "close", "type": "state", "x": 560, "y": 40, "targetState": "closed" }, { "id": "isClosed", "type": "condition", "x": 560, "y": 220, "state": "closed" }, { "id": "open", "type": "state", "x": 820, "y": 220, "targetState": "open" } , "edges": { "from": "start", "to": "isOpen", "output": "next", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "isOpen", "to": "close", "output": "true", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "isOpen", "to": "isClosed", "output": "false", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "isClosed", "to": "open", "output": "true", "kind": "execution" } } } } Expected result Initial state Predicted actions Expected live state --- --- --- closed state → open open open state → closed closed locked none locked Run the fixture in a development installation Extract the example bundle to data/blueprint-examples inside a disposable checkout of the documented host. From the checkout root, run: sh uv run --locked python data/blueprint-examples/check-examples.py --host . The checker configures an in-memory database, blocks database queries and calls the real clean_blueprint and evaluate_graph functions. It validates all four object kinds, both connection kinds and all 49 node types, including requestRoll and setQuestStatus. It checks both roll visibilities, all six quest statuses and continuing execution without drawing dice or changing journals. This verifies document shape and predicted actions. Test behavior is still needed to check real targets, authorization and the complete server chain. To inspect this recipe in the development Django shell after extracting the files: sh uv run --locked python manage.py shell --no-imports python import json from pathlib import Path from gravewright.maps.blueprints import clean_blueprint, evaluate_graph raw = json.loads(Path("data/blueprint-examples/door-toggle.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) blueprint = clean_blueprint(raw, asset_ids=set(), light_ids=set(), track_ids=set()) result = evaluate_graph(blueprint, "interact", "closed") print(result "trace" ) print(result "actions" ) assert action "targetState" for action in result "actions" == "open" Test as GM and player Run Simulate to inspect one local event. Then use Test behavior to rehearse through the server; its changes are rolled back. Generate or update the scene as GM, then test a synthetic scene with a GM and an authorized player. Verify that a streamer cannot write. After editing the project again, use Update scene before expecting different live behavior. As GM, run the three rows above and inspect Automation. As player, test an ordinary closed door and then a locked one: this example does not grant lock/unlock actions. Disable player interaction and verify direct player clicks are refused; the GM remains able to test. Hidden geometry and unrelated objects must not be disclosed to the player. Common failures - “It opened once but never closed”: both branches need their own Change state action; an event does not toggle automatically. - “The locked branch did nothing”: that is the intended result. Do not add players: true simply to suppress a permission error. - “The state changed but a custom image stayed”: a previous Change sprite override is separate live state. Use an explicit Change sprite action when a custom sprite must also change. How to use AI to adapt this example text Using Gravewright 0.3.3 source cc4fd08, extend the supplied door-toggle.json with an original message after a successful opening. Preserve locked → no state action. Inspect blueprints.py for node fields, execution ports and the audience contract. Return the complete v2 document, editor steps and closed/open/locked GM-player checks. Do not add private browser calls, an import button or implicit state-change events. title: Blueprint kind lever: a two-state switch and an Empty Object
summary: A complete off/on toggle, with the same kind reused by an image-free private controller.
text: Goal Make an ordinary switch alternate off → on → off. The JSON retains the existing artwork in both states; state actions alone do not choose different sprites. An Empty Object uses this same lever kind, not a fifth kind named empty. These JSON files describe the stored Blueprint v2 subdocument . They are development fixtures, not an installable module, a complete Builder project or a campaign archive. Recreate the nodes in the editor, or use the fixtures in isolated contributor tests. This guide does not assume a JSON import button in the Smart Object editor. Download the complete example bundle (../../assets/examples/blueprints/examples.zip) or the validator (../../assets/examples/blueprints/check-examples.py). Every example uses original synthetic data. The host's internal Python evaluator is for source development; browser modules must use the public SDK. Build it in the editor 1. Place an Object image, select it and choose Panels → Selection → Behavior → Lever. Set Initial state to Deactivated. 2. Open Edit behavior. Connect On interaction → Check state: Deactivated. 3. Connect True → Change state: Activated and False → Change state: Deactivated. 4. For an image-free controller instead, place Library → Objects → Empty Object. Use the same graph; retain inherit appearances and do not attach image actions to Self. 5. To show different artwork on a visible lever, choose a valid Object image for each state appearance, or append explicit Change sprite actions. That requires real campaign asset IDs beyond this self-contained fixture. Complete JSON Download lever-toggle.json (../../assets/examples/blueprints/lever-toggle.json) json { "version": 2, "kind": "lever", "states": { "off": { "appearance": "inherit" }, "on": { "appearance": "inherit" } }, "graphs": { "interact": { "nodes": { "id": "start", "type": "event", "x": 40, "y": 80, "event": "interact" }, { "id": "isOff", "type": "condition", "x": 300, "y": 80, "state": "off" }, { "id": "activate", "type": "state", "x": 560, "y": 40, "targetState": "on" }, { "id": "deactivate", "type": "state", "x": 560, "y": 220, "targetState": "off" } , "edges": { "from": "start", "to": "isOff", "output": "next", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "isOff", "to": "activate", "output": "true", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "isOff", "to": "deactivate", "output": "false", "kind": "execution" } } } } Expected result Initial state Branch Predicted action --- --- --- off true state → on on false state → off Each evaluation reads the starting state. A state action does not emit another interact event. Run the fixture in a development installation Extract the example bundle to data/blueprint-examples inside a disposable checkout of the documented host. From the checkout root, run: sh uv run --locked python data/blueprint-examples/check-examples.py --host . The checker configures an in-memory database, blocks database queries and calls the real clean_blueprint and evaluate_graph functions. It validates all four object kinds, both connection kinds and all 49 node types, including requestRoll and setQuestStatus. It checks both roll visibilities, all six quest statuses and continuing execution without drawing dice or changing journals. This verifies document shape and predicted actions. Test behavior is still needed to check real targets, authorization and the complete server chain. To inspect this recipe in the development Django shell after extracting the files: sh uv run --locked python manage.py shell --no-imports python import json from pathlib import Path from gravewright.maps.blueprints import clean_blueprint, evaluate_graph raw = json.loads(Path("data/blueprint-examples/lever-toggle.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) blueprint = clean_blueprint(raw, asset_ids=set(), light_ids=set(), track_ids=set()) result = evaluate_graph(blueprint, "interact", "off") print(result "trace" ) print(result "actions" ) assert result "actions" 0 "targetState" == "on" Test as GM and player Run Simulate to inspect one local event. Then use Test behavior to rehearse through the server; its changes are rolled back. Generate or update the scene as GM, then test a synthetic scene with a GM and an authorized player. Verify that a streamer cannot write. After editing the project again, use Update scene before expecting different live behavior. Test a visible lever on the Game layer as GM and authorized player. A single click selects; double-click runs the configured interaction. Then test the Empty Object as GM: it stays private on the GM layer, and players receive no marker or direct click target. Players can still trigger an Empty Object’s authored presence graphs through eligible token movement; this fixture only defines interact. Common failures - “The image did not change”: inherit deliberately keeps the native image. Add state appearances or sprite actions to the visible variant. - “The Empty Object is absent for players”: that is its privacy contract; it is a GM controller, not a public invisible button. - “The lever still toggles after deleting a node”: distinguish no blueprint/native behavior from an authored interaction path. Keep a connected complete graph when testing this example. Keep off/on states and explicit state actions. Explain the visible lever versus Empty Object permissions. Return complete JSON, correctly typed count comparison, editor steps and two-token tests. title: Blueprint kind torch: turn the mechanism and set the flame
summary: A composed torch example with independent state and flame actions in both toggle branches.
text: Goal Turn a normal torch 90 degrees and light its flame; on the next interaction return it and extinguish the flame. Mechanism and flame are separate properties. This recipe intentionally changes both with two actions in each branch. These JSON files describe the stored Blueprint v2 subdocument . They are development fixtures, not an installable module, a complete Builder project or a campaign archive. Recreate the nodes in the editor, or use the fixtures in isolated contributor tests. This guide does not assume a JSON import button in the Smart Object editor. Download the complete example bundle (../../assets/examples/blueprints/examples.zip) or the validator (../../assets/examples/blueprints/check-examples.py). Every example uses original synthetic data. The host's internal Python evaluator is for source development; browser modules must use the public SDK. Build it in the editor 1. Place an Object image and select Panels → Selection → Behavior → Torch. The Builder creates the linked native light. Use Torch components to configure optional particles or a shader. 2. Set Mechanism to Normal and Flame lit to false. Leave state appearances on Native appearance. 3. Open Edit behavior. Connect On interaction → Check state: Normal. 4. Connect True → Change state: Turned → Set flame: enabled. Connect False → Change state: Normal → Set flame: disabled. 5. Inspect the linked light’s own enabled setting. Set flame restores only components configured as enabled; it does not overwrite their brightness, radius or other native settings. Complete JSON Download torch-turn-flame.json (../../assets/examples/blueprints/torch-turn-flame.json) json { "version": 2, "kind": "torch", "states": { "off": { "appearance": "inherit" }, "on": { "appearance": "inherit" } }, "graphs": { "interact": { "nodes": { "id": "start", "type": "event", "x": 40, "y": 80, "event": "interact" }, { "id": "isNormal", "type": "condition", "x": 300, "y": 80, "state": "off" }, { "id": "turn", "type": "state", "x": 560, "y": 40, "targetState": "on" }, { "id": "lightFlame", "type": "flame", "x": 820, "y": 40, "enabled": true }, { "id": "return", "type": "state", "x": 560, "y": 220, "targetState": "off" }, { "id": "extinguish", "type": "flame", "x": 820, "y": 220, "enabled": false } , "edges": { "from": "start", "to": "isNormal", "output": "next", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "isNormal", "to": "turn", "output": "true", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "turn", "to": "lightFlame", "output": "next", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "isNormal", "to": "return", "output": "false", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "return", "to": "extinguish", "output": "next", "kind": "execution" } } } } Expected result Starting mechanism Action order Expected outcome --- --- --- off (Normal) state on, flame true Turned; enabled components emit on (Turned) state off, flame false Normal; components stop emitting Turning adds 90 degrees to the authored orientation. Off/on encode the mechanism, not the flame. Run the fixture in a development installation Extract the example bundle to data/blueprint-examples inside a disposable checkout of the documented host. From the checkout root, run: sh uv run --locked python data/blueprint-examples/check-examples.py --host . The checker configures an in-memory database, blocks database queries and calls the real clean_blueprint and evaluate_graph functions. It validates all four object kinds, both connection kinds and all 49 node types, including requestRoll and setQuestStatus. It checks both roll visibilities, all six quest statuses and continuing execution without drawing dice or changing journals. This verifies document shape and predicted actions. Test behavior is still needed to check real targets, authorization and the complete server chain. To inspect this recipe in the development Django shell after extracting the files: sh uv run --locked python manage.py shell --no-imports python import json from pathlib import Path from gravewright.maps.blueprints import clean_blueprint, evaluate_graph raw = json.loads(Path("data/blueprint-examples/torch-turn-flame.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) blueprint = clean_blueprint(raw, asset_ids=set(), light_ids=set(), track_ids=set()) result = evaluate_graph(blueprint, "interact", "off") print(result "trace" ) print(result "actions" ) assert (a "type" , a.get("targetState", a.get("enabled"))) for a in result "actions" == ("state", "on"), ("flame", True) Test as GM and player Run Simulate to inspect one local event. Then use Test behavior to rehearse through the server; its changes are rolled back. Generate or update the scene as GM, then test a synthetic scene with a GM and an authorized player. Verify that a streamer cannot write. After editing the project again, use Update scene before expecting different live behavior. As GM, verify the image, linked light and optional effects move together when the mechanism turns. Verify the light stops on the second interaction. As authorized player, double-click the public torch on Game and confirm the same visible result without exposing graph or component ownership data. Test an independently disabled component: lighting the flame must not re-enable that component’s own configuration. Common failures - “Changing state did not light the flame”: state and flame are independent; connect the flame action. - “Set flame did nothing on a door”: Self must be a torch, or Target must point to a composed torch. A light is a resource, not blueprint kind light. - “Light is still absent when flame is true”: inspect component enablement, hidden state appearance and dynamic lighting. Simulate only reports actions; inspect the live native light through Test behavior and playtest. Keep torch off/on separate from flame. Inspect reference output door → state input target, and preserve player lock rules. title: Blueprint kind region: a pressure plate with first/last occupancy
summary: Complete enter/exit graphs that open a referenced door on first arrival and close it on last departure.
text: Goal Open a door while at least one eligible token occupies a region. Enter and exit events occur for each eligible crossing, so compare the trusted event context count to1 on arrival and0 on departure. Do not use a state-change action to control region occupancy. These JSON files describe the stored Blueprint v2 subdocument . They are development fixtures, not an installable module, a complete Builder project or a campaign archive. Recreate the nodes in the editor, or use the fixtures in isolated contributor tests. This guide does not assume a JSON import button in the Smart Object editor. Download the complete example bundle (../../assets/examples/blueprints/examples.zip) or the validator (../../assets/examples/blueprints/check-examples.py). Every example uses original synthetic data. The host's internal Python evaluator is for source development; browser modules must use the public SDK. Build it in the editor 1. Create a native door and a Region rectangle in Map Builder. Name both, enable the region and keep it on the desired project layer. 2. For the built-in equivalent, choose the region’s Controlled door and Apply pressure plate. This replaces its behavior; use it only when intentionally replacing the existing graph. 3. For the manual example, open Edit behavior. On area enter: add Event context → Occupancy count, Compare value with number/eq/1 and Check state. Connect the Boolean result to the condition’s Test, overriding its fallback state check. 4. Connect On area enter to that condition; its True goes to Change state: Opened. Add Element reference for the chosen door and connect its Target output to the state action’s Target. 5. On area exit, build the same chain with number/eq/0 and Change state: Closed. Bind the same door. The fixture UUID 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 is synthetic; select an actual owned door in the editor. 6. Keep Empty and Occupied appearances on inherit. Region artwork and occupancy are not controlled by Change sprite or Change state. Complete JSON Download region-pressure-plate.json (../../assets/examples/blueprints/region-pressure-plate.json) json { "version": 2, "kind": "region", "states": { "empty": { "appearance": "inherit" }, the final row. Conditions read an event snapshot, not live values changed by preceding actions. Run the fixture in a development installation Extract the example bundle to data/blueprint-examples inside a disposable checkout of the documented host. From the checkout root, run: sh uv run --locked python data/blueprint-examples/check-examples.py --host . The checker configures an in-memory database, blocks database queries and calls the real clean_blueprint and evaluate_graph functions. It validates all four object kinds, both connection kinds and all 49 node types, including requestRoll and setQuestStatus. It checks both roll visibilities, all six quest statuses and continuing execution without drawing dice or changing journals. This verifies document shape and predicted actions. Test behavior is still needed to check real targets, authorization and the complete server chain. To inspect this recipe in the development Django shell after extracting the files: sh uv run --locked python manage.py shell --no-imports python import json from pathlib import Path from gravewright.maps.blueprints import clean_blueprint, evaluate_graph raw = json.loads(Path("data/blueprint-examples/region-pressure-plate.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) blueprint = clean_blueprint(raw, asset_ids=set(), light_ids=set(), track_ids=set()) result = evaluate_graph(blueprint, "presence:enter", "occupied", event_context={"count": 1, "presence": "enter"}) print(result "trace" ) print(result "actions" ) assert result "actions" 0 "targetState" == "open" assert result "actions" 0 "target" == "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111" Test as GM and player Run Simulate to inspect one local event. Then use Test behavior to rehearse through the server; its changes are rolled back. Generate or update the scene as GM, then test a synthetic scene with a GM and an authorized player. Verify that a streamer cannot write. After editing the project again, use Update scene before expecting different live behavior. As GM, move token A in, move B in, move A out and move B out. Verify the four rows and Automation’s actual trigger. Repeat with player-controlled tokens and an unlocked door. With a locked target door, the player’s normal lock restrictions still apply; the source region does not grant extra rights. Enabling/editing the region quietly recomputes occupancy and must not synthesize arrival actions. Common failures - “Removing one of two tokens closed the door”: compare count to0 on exit; an exit event alone does not mean empty. - “The region never becomes occupied”: check enabled state, token center, elevation and presence filters; blocked or preview-only movement does not commit a crossing. - “The UUID validates but nothing opens”: syntactically valid is not an owned live target. Bind the real door; inspect missing/unsupported targets in Automation. - “I tried state: occupied”: region state is derived. A state node only accepts writable door/lever states and cannot set a region. How to use AI to adapt this example text Review region-pressure-plate.json against Gravewright 0.3.3. Add an original message only on first entry while preserving last-exit close. Use eventContext count and numeric compareValue; preserve empty/occupied as derived region states. Explain source IDs versus generated native IDs and bind the door through the editor. Return complete JSON and tests with two tokens, elevation filters, a missing target and a player moving toward a locked door. Do not invent an interact port for region.
