title: Connection kinds: execution and data, a complete graph
summary: Trace a lever graph that reads a state through typed data edges and runs actions through ordered execution edges.
text: Goal Activate a lever only when its starting state is off, then show an original message to the triggering participant. The false branch deactivates it. This single document demonstrates both accepted edge.kind values. These JSON files describe the stored Blueprint v2 subdocument . They are development fixtures, not an installable module, a complete Builder project or a campaign archive. Recreate the nodes in the editor, or use the fixtures in isolated contributor tests. This guide does not assume a JSON import button in the Smart Object editor. Download the complete example bundle (../../assets/examples/blueprints/examples.zip) or the validator (../../assets/examples/blueprints/check-examples.py). Every example uses original synthetic data. The host's internal Python evaluator is for source development; browser modules must use the public SDK. Recreate the two connection kinds 1. Create a Lever as in the lever example (docs:example-blueprint-lever). Open On interaction. 2. Add Get property: Current state → Compare state: Deactivated → Check state: Test. These are the data links. Get property and Compare state are pure value nodes. 3. Connect On interaction → Check state. True → Change state: Activated → Show message, with text “The mechanism is active.” and audience Trigger. False → Change state: Deactivated. These are execution links. 4. Simulate once from off, then once from on. The first reads values and runs state/message; the second runs only the state action. edge.kind Required keys in addition to kind Concrete edge --- --- --- execution from, to, output start.next → branch data from, to, output, input compare.result → branch.test json { "kind": "execution", "from": "start", "to": "branch", "output": "next" } json { "kind": "data", "from": "compare", "to": "branch", "output": "result", "input": "test" } Complete JSON Download execution-data.json (../../assets/examples/blueprints/execution-data.json) json { "version": 2, "kind": "lever", "states": { "off": { "appearance": "inherit" }, "on": { "appearance": "inherit" } }, "graphs": { "interact": { "nodes": { "id": "start", "type": "event", "x": 40, "y": 80, "event": "interact" }, { "id": "read", "type": "property", "x": 300, "y": 300, "property": "state" }, { "id": "compare", "type": "compare", "x": 560, "y": 300, "state": "off" }, { "id": "branch", "type": "condition", "x": 560, "y": 80, "state": "off" }, { "id": "on", "type": "state", "x": 820, "y": 40, "targetState": "on" }, { "id": "message", "type": "showMessage", "x": 1080, "y": 40, "audience": { "scope": "trigger" }, "text": "The mechanism is active." }, { "id": "off", "type": "state", "x": 820, "y": 220, "targetState": "off" } , "edges": { "from": "start", "to": "branch", "output": "next", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "branch", "to": "on", "output": "true", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "on", "to": "message", "output": "next", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "branch", "to": "off", "output": "false", "kind": "execution" }, { "from": "read", "to": "compare", "output": "value", "kind": "data", "input": "value" }, { "from": "compare", "to": "branch", "output": "result", "kind": "data", "input": "test" } } } } Expected result From off, the exact trace is start → branch → read → compare → on → message . A pure value is evaluated when the executing condition needs it, so the trace lists branch before the values it reads. The actions are state:on and showMessage. From on, the trace ends with off and the only action is state:off. Run the fixture in a development installation Extract the example bundle to data/blueprint-examples inside a disposable checkout of the documented host. From the checkout root, run: sh uv run --locked python data/blueprint-examples/check-examples.py --host . The checker configures an in-memory database, blocks database queries and calls the real clean_blueprint and evaluate_graph functions. It validates all four object kinds, both connection kinds and all 49 node types, including requestRoll and setQuestStatus. It checks both roll visibilities, all six quest statuses and continuing execution without drawing dice or changing journals. This verifies document shape and predicted actions. Test behavior is still needed to check real targets, authorization and the complete server chain. python import json from pathlib import Path from gravewright.maps.blueprints import clean_blueprint, evaluate_graph raw = json.loads(Path("data/blueprint-examples/execution-data.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) blueprint = clean_blueprint(raw, asset_ids=set(), light_ids=set(), track_ids=set()) result = evaluate_graph(blueprint, "interact", "off") print(result "trace" ) print(result "actions" ) assert result "trace" == "start", "branch", "read", "compare", "on", "message" assert a "type" for a in result "actions" == "state", "showMessage" Ordering and rejected connections - Execution fan-out follows authored edge order depth-first. A sequence uses then1, then2, then3, then4 in that order. A shared descendant executes once per event. - Pure value nodes have no execution ports. An execution link to read, or from read.next, fails validation. - A data input has one source. Two sources for branch.test fail validation; one value output may feed compatible inputs. - State, boolean, number, text, element and resource references are typed. Compare state emits result:boolean; connect it to Test, not a state-valued input. - The saved Element reference output is still named door and has type element. This is compatible with non-door element references; do not rename the serialized port. - All connections, including disconnected draft branches, must be acyclic. Use named signals/timers through their supported runtime instead of a cable loop. Test as GM and player Run Simulate to inspect one local event. Then use Test behavior to rehearse through the server; its changes are rolled back. Generate or update the scene as GM, then test a synthetic scene with a GM and an authorized player. Verify that a streamer cannot write. After editing the project again, use Update scene before expecting different live behavior. On the first player interaction, the message audience is trigger. A second player must not receive a private trigger message merely because they share the scene. Check Automation as GM: values, Boolean decision and action order must match the simulation. A paused scene must execute no blueprint actions. Common failures A visible node without an execution path does not run. A data cable does not start an action. A correct simulation does not prove that a live target exists or that a player can modify it. When comparing the state after an earlier action in this event, remember that the property reads the starting snapshot. How to use AI to add a typed input text Extend execution-data.json for Gravewright 0.3.3 by adding a second Boolean requirement from getVariable(scope=element, name=ready, valueType=boolean, default=true). Combine it with the existing compare result through all inputs a/b. Inspect data_inputs/data_outputs and the real field validators. Keep pure nodes off execution cables, preserve one source per input and show the complete JSON plus off/on and ready true/false traces. Do not claim data edges execute actions. title: All 49 Blueprint node types, with complete examples

Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/reference.json) reveal action Reveal a secret door; use a compatible door target. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/reveal.json) barrier action Let movement pass through a door without changing its other barrier channels. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/barrier.json) soundControl action Stop a selected track; choose volume for an explicit volume adjustment. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/soundControl.json) flame action Light a composed torch’s configured enabled components; preserve its mechanism. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/all.json) any value Accept either of two closed comparisons; at least two inputs are required. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/any.json) getVariable value Read Boolean element variable ready, default true → condition → open. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/getVariable.json) setVariable action Store Boolean ready=true in the element scope. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/setVariable.json) compareValue value Compare a Boolean value to false; an unconnected Boolean Value defaults to false. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/emitEvent.json) delay execution Wait 3 seconds before open; the evaluator exposes a continuation, the server schedules it. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/delay.json) timer action Start a 3-second one-shot timer whose expiry emits signal:ready. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/timer.json) switch branch Match text open to case1 → open; unmatched values use default. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/switch.json) random branch Choose between two equally weighted branches; local deterministic evaluator defaults to branch1. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/random.json) elementGroup value Send two ordered door UUIDs to a state target; the runtime resolves each member. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/elementGroup.json) lightReference value Bind a native light through light → light.target. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/lightReference.json) soundReference value Bind a sound through sound → sound.target. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/soundReference.json) eventContext value Read trusted occupancy count → numeric comparison1 → condition → open. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/showMessage.json) showHandout action Present an existing authorized journal to trigger; use a real campaign journal ID. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/showHandout.json) requestRoll action Ask the trigger to roll 1d20+2 with a public result. The recipient chooses Roll; the graph continues without a result branch. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/requestRoll.json) setQuestStatus action Request active status for an existing campaign quest through a GM-authored action; this grants no general journal editing permission. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/setQuestStatus.json) cameraFocus action Focus trigger’s camera at 25%, 40% scene coordinates. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/cameraFocus.json) teleport action Move the verified trigger token to a compatible same-scene destination; requires token context. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/teleport.json) counter branch Pass on the second event, preserving memory between runs. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/counter.json) once branch Pass once, then choose false on subsequent events with the same node memory. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/once.json) cooldown branch Pass immediately, then block for 10 seconds using the server clock. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/cooldown.json) clockControl action Advance one segment of the selected campaign/scene clock. The server requires active GM authority; this grants no general clock editing access. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/clockControl.json) clueControl action Advance the selected clue one step; permitted content is revealed only after completion, without exposing GM notes. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/clueControl.json) openMindMap action Open an authorized mind map for the trigger, optionally focusing a topic. Original map and linked-resource permissions remain in force. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/openMindMap.json) mindMapNode action Complete one existing mind-map topic through a GM-authored action, without granting general graph editing permission. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/mindMapNode.json) shaderControl action Set the selected shader opacity to 0.35. Requires host 0.3.3; bind a real same-map shader, or connect a Number variable to Value. Complete graph (../../assets/examples/blueprints/nodes/shaderControl.json) Use and verify the examples In the editor, create a compatible owner and the nodes from the downloaded graph; bind resources through real selectors. File IDs are synthetic. Validation checks shape and evaluation predicts actions; neither resolves permissions, resource existence or target compatibility. The setRegion graph belongs to a region; setAppearance uses an explicit dynamic surface reference. Bind actual targets before live use. A predicted action is not proof of server application. Run the fixture in a development installation Extract the example bundle to data/blueprint-examples inside a disposable checkout of the documented host. From the checkout root, run: sh uv run --locked python data/blueprint-examples/check-examples.py --host . It validates all four object kinds, both connection kinds and all 49 node types, including requestRoll and setQuestStatus. It checks both roll visibilities, all six quest statuses and continuing execution without drawing dice or changing journals. This verifies document shape and predicted actions.
