Builder updates also verify their generated scene against an authoritative mounted scene. Rehearsals retain native rollback semantics. Rendering and tiling run outside an enclosing transport transaction; each owning service retains its own commit and cleanup boundary. Generation, scene updates, UVTT export and rehearsals default to no client deadline. options.timeoutMs can set an explicit deadline; null disables it. Builder collections use the existing map invalidations. Clocks and clues have the collection events described below. Progress clocks The clocks domain serves the same persistent records in the table and campaign manager. state({sceneId}) returns campaign clocks plus clocks in that authorized scene, filtered by current membership. The native page adapter uses the existing GET resource-state route so read-only stream sessions can view public clocks. Create accepts {name, description?, segments?, value?, color?, visibility?, playersCanEdit?, pinned?, scopeSceneId?} . Defaults are 4 segments, value 0, c9a44c , gm , false, false and campaign scope. Segments are integers 2–24; progress is 0–segments; there are at most 128 clocks per campaign. Update accepts those configuration fields plus the existing id and version . advance({id, version, delta}) accepts an integer delta from -24 to 24 and clamps progress to its valid range. Reset and delete accept {id, version} . Only GMs configure, reset or delete; players advance only public clocks with playersCanEdit: true . Streamers remain read-only. Returned clocks expose canEdit , canConfigure and their saved scope as sceneId . description is optional authored text, defaults to "" , and must be a string of at most 4,000 characters. Only GM configuration writes can change it. Omitted updates preserve it; readers receive it only when the clock is visible to them. The field is additive and introduces no new browser method or SDK version. scopeSceneId: null persists campaign scope; a scene UUID persists scene scope. The request's sceneId / mapId is the viewing context and never relocates a clock. A scene-bound handle rejects a different non-null scopeSceneId . Existing-clock writes require the saved version; conflicts require reviewing fresh state. The clocks.changed event uses the resource-state envelope below. See the clock guide (clocks.md) for visibility, pinning and synchronization. Clue discoveries The clues domain shares persistent discoveries between the table and campaign manager. state({sceneId}) returns campaign clues and clues in that authorized scene. Players and streamers receive only clues with visibility: "players" and value === segments ; undiscovered clues have no public record, title, content, ID or placeholder. gmNotes is absent from every public projection, including completed clues. All direct mutations require current GM authority. Create accepts {name, content?, gmNotes?, segments?, value?, color?, visibility?, pinned?, scopeSceneId?} . Defaults are empty content and notes, 4 steps, value 0, c9a44c , players , false and campaign scope. Names have at most 120 characters; content and GM notes each have at most 4000. Steps are integers 1–24; value is 0–segments. A single step supports immediate discovery. Each campaign can hold at most 128 clues, independently of clocks. Update accepts those fields plus {id, version} . advance({id, version, delta}) accepts integer -24–24 and clamps progress. reset({id, version}) clears progress and preserves visibility; hide({id, version}) selects GM visibility and preserves progress; reveal({id, version}) completes discovery and selects player visibility. Delete accepts {id, version} . Revisions and retry UUIDs follow native receipts; a former GM cannot replay a private receipt after losing authority. scopeSceneId controls saved scope; sceneId / mapId supplies viewing context, as for clocks. Native reads use the streamer-compatible GET resource route. clues.changed subscriptions reread projected state using the resource envelope below. The MapBuilder clueControl node delegates only its authored effect and does not grant players direct clue writes. Rehearsals roll back its changes and notifications. See clues (clues.md) for usage and node actions. Collaborative mind maps and typed resource links The mindmaps domain reads shared campaign graphs through each member's current permissions. It has no implicit current-scene default: state({}) lists every accessible map; state({sceneId}) selects campaign maps plus maps in that scene. An explicitly scene-bound module retains its authoritative scene context. Method Payload and result --- --- state / read {sceneId?} / {id, sceneId?} ; the collection envelope / one projected map resources {query?, kinds?, limit?, sceneId?} ; {kinds: {id,label} , resources: ... , truncated} resolve {reference} ; one live authorized display row or null for missing/denied targets create {name, visibility?, editorIds?, scopeSceneId?, document?} ; GM-only, defaults to private campaign scope update {id, version, name?, document?, visibility?, editorIds?, scopeSceneId?} node {id, version, nodeId, patch} ; update a topic's supplied fields delete {id, version} ; GM-only visibility is gm or players . editorIds contains current campaign player UUIDs; selected editors can read/edit even a private map. All GMs can edit, and public visibility grants other participants reading only. Players can change name , document and topic fields; configuring scope/access remains GM-only. Streamers cannot write. Writes return {id, version, mindmap} (delete returns {id} ), use a dedicated retry receipt and require the saved version for existing maps. Conflicts require reviewing current state, without replacing the draft's expected version silently. mindmaps.changed uses the resource-state envelope. A document is {nodes, edges} . Topics have UUID id , optional parentId , label , notes , hex color , x , y , collapsed , completed , and links . Parent links form an acyclic forest. Additional edges are {id, from, to, label?} between existing topics. Topic patches accept these topic fields except id . Limits are 64 maps per campaign, 500 topics/1,000 edges per map, 16 links per topic/2,048 overall, and 1 MiB per document. Labels have 240 characters, notes 8,000, and coordinates are bounded to ±100,000. Canonical resource references are exactly {kind, id, pageId?} . The resource registry (../../gravewright/table/resource_links.py) defines 37 types, including native numeric IDs, installed compendium entries ( packId/entryId ), journal pages ( id: journalId plus pageId ) and drawings ( sceneId/drawingId ). Discover kind IDs through resources , rather than inferring them from labels. Search accepts up to 120 characters; limit defaults to 80 and is bounded to 1–200. Labels come from current native projections. Authored labels stay literal; optional labelKey / descriptionKey identify generated text for Translator. Missing and denied links are both projected as {unavailable:true, key} without hidden kind/ID/name/URL. Return that opaque placeholder unchanged when editing other content, or omit it to remove the link. It cannot authorize a new hidden reference. Reopening resolves permissions again; naming a target or sharing a map does not grant target access. See Mind maps (mindmaps.md) for resource types, collaboration, MapBuilder nodes and typed archive remapping. Journal resource links api.journals.resources({query?, kinds?, limit?, sceneId?}, options) searches the same typed campaign catalog used by mind maps. api.journals.resolve({reference}, options) returns {resource: row null} after checking current target access. Both are read methods, available to authorized players and streamers. Unbound reads do not inherit the table's broadcast scene; an explicitly mounted scene remains authoritative. Rich text retains gw-journal-doc-v1 , version 1. A reference is an inline atom: json {"type":"gwResourceLink","attrs":{"reference":{"kind":"journal-page","id":"<journalUUID ","pageId":"page_main"}}} Stored references contain only kind , id and optional pageId . Recipient projections add current display metadata and an opaque key ; an inaccessible target becomes {unavailable:true,key} without its identity or title. Return that placeholder unchanged to preserve it during an authorized edit. It is bound to the source journal and cannot create a new private connection. A journal accepts up to 512 reference atoms; normal document size and depth limits also apply. Saving uses the existing journal version and operation UUID. Native reads use GET /api/containers/{campaign}/journals/resources with query parameters query , kinds (JSON array), limit and optional sceneId , and GET /api/containers/{campaign}/journals/resolve?reference=<JSON . Responses are private and not cached. Python packages use api.journals.resources(campaign_id, user_id, , query='', kinds=None, limit=80, scene_id=None) and api.journals.resolve(campaign_id, user_id, reference) . Resource lookup never changes table presence or navigation. See Journals and references (journals.md) for editing, access and portable copies. Diary chapters and pages Diary updates use the existing journal command, expected version and operation UUID. The data payload can include independent chapters, including empty ones: json { "chapters": {"id":"chapter_main", "name":"Chapter one", "parentId":null, "sortOrder":10}, {"id":"chapter_child", "name":"A subchapter", "parentId":"chapter_main", "sortOrder":10} , "sections": {"id":"page_main", "title":"A page", "kind":"text", "chapterId":"chapter_child"}, {"id":"page_loose", "title":"An ungrouped page", "kind":"text", "chapterId":null} } Each page belongs to zero or one chapter. Each chapter has zero or one parent and can contain zero to many pages and subchapters. IDs are local to the journal; copying a campaign preserves them and does not treat them as resource UUIDs. Chapter IDs are unique, 1–40 ASCII letters/digits/underscores/hyphens; names are 1–80 characters. The server allows up to 128 chapters, eight hierarchy levels and the existing 64 pages. Missing parents, cycles and dangling page assignments are rejected before saving. Chapter sorting uses sortOrder within each parent. Authorized diary projections expose chapters alongside sections . Private pages remain filtered, together with chapter branches containing only unreadable pages. Ancestors of readable pages and genuinely empty branches remain visible. Page-scoped presentations contain only their page's chapter path. Updates preserve server-owned hidden pages and the chapter structure those pages require. Legacy sections .category names receive stable chapter IDs on normalization; category remains a compatibility name mirror. An explicit chapterId: null removes a page's assignment. Older updates omitting chapters retain existing chapters, including empty ones. History and campaign archives retain the tree. System-owned operations and the PDF System The host routes api.system.call(name, data, options) only to the current campaign system's registered provider. Changing an operation name or a payload cannot select another system. Trusted server packages register callbacks from AppConfig.ready() with api.systems.register_api(system_id, operations) , where each entry declares {effect: "read" "write", handler, description?} . Registration does not query the database. Handlers receive (campaign_id, user_id, payload, request_id, scene_id) and own resource validation, transactions, revisions, retry receipts and notifications. The host rechecks membership, bounds JSON, prevents mounted-scene retargeting and makes every streamer write fail before invoking the handler.
