public exports (../../api/pdf_system.py) and call signatures (../../gravewright/pdf_system/public.py) api.systems capabilities(campaign_id, user_id) , call(campaign_id, user_id, operation, payload, request_id=None, , scene_id=None) , register_api(system_id, operations) ; provider contract (../../gravewright/campaigns/system_api.py) api.library state(campaign_id, user_id) , command(campaign_id, user_id, action, payload, request_id) ; native library service (../../gravewright/maps/library_services.py) api.ownership state(campaign_id, user_id, kind, resource_id) , command(campaign_id, user_id, kind, resource_id, payload, request_id) ; GM document, folder and page service (../../gravewright/table/permission_services.py) api.journals state(campaign_id, user_id) , command(campaign_id, user_id, action, data, request_id) , resources(campaign_id, user_id, search) , resolve(campaign_id, user_id, reference) api.clocks state(campaign_id, user_id, scene_id=None) , command(campaign_id, user_id, action, data, request_id) ; actions create , update , advance , reset , delete api.clues state(campaign_id, user_id, scene_id=None) , command(campaign_id, user_id, action, data, request_id) ; actions create , update , advance , reset , reveal , hide , delete api.mindmaps state(campaign_id, user_id, scene_id=None) , read(campaign_id, user_id, mindmap_id, scene_id=None) , resources(campaign_id, user_id, , query='', kinds=None, limit=80, scene_id=None) , resolve(campaign_id, user_id, reference) , command(campaign_id, user_id, action, data, request_id) ; actions create , update , node , delete api.items , api.combat , api.cards , api.audio , api.compendiums state(campaign_id, user_id, scene_id=None) , command(campaign_id, user_id, action, data, request_id) api.combat.register_provider Trusted system callback registration from AppConfig.ready() ; see system combat providers (modules.md system-combat-providers) api.resources state(campaign_id, user_id, name, scene_id=None, preview_token_id=None) , command(campaign_id, user_id, name, action, data, request_id) api.chat history(campaign_id, user_id, map_id=None) , send(campaign_id, user_id, text, request_id, map_id=None) , remove(campaign_id, user_id, message_id=None) api.dice evaluate(expression, repeat=1, , random_source=None) , roll(campaign_id, user_id, expression, request_id, , repeat=1, label="", visibility="public", map_id=None) api.table search(campaign_id, user_id, query) , lobby(campaign_id, user_id) , update_lobby(campaign_id, user_id, payload) api.events Change , resource_changed api.errors AuthError , JournalError , MapError , RollError Use positional arguments as illustrated where facade parameter names vary. resources selects the native items , combat , cards , audio , compendiums , clocks , clues , or mindmaps domain by name. dice.evaluate computes locally; dice.roll stores/publishes a table roll. Python exceptions preserve their original service types/codes rather than the browser's seven-code normalization. Transactions and server hooks Public command wrappers retain native transactions, permission checks, version checks, deduplication receipts where implemented, and notifications after commit. An enclosing transaction rollback produces neither the committed write nor its queued notifications. Direct ORM writes bypass this command behavior and should not be used as an equivalent mutation API. Connect trusted server hooks to the Django signal: python from api.events import resource_changed def observe_change(sender, change, kwargs): sender is the resource name; change contains identifiers, not a snapshot. print(change.resource, change.action, change.request_id) resource_changed.connect( observe_change, dispatch_uid="example.observe-change", weak=False, ) Register receivers once in your explicitly installed app's AppConfig.ready() . Change contains campaign_id , user_id , resource , action , and request_id . The signal is sent after commit through send_robust ; receiver failures are logged and do not roll back committed commands. It runs inside the serving process and is not a durable queue or a replayable audit log. Keep handlers short; do not forward identifiers or subsequently loaded private data to unfiltered browser audiences. The native chat and dice publishing paths have their own audience-aware notifications and are not a promise that every write emits resource_changed . Transport and maintenance The host browser domain endpoint is POST /api/tables/<table_id /api ; installed modules use POST /api/tables/<table_id /modules/<module_id /api . Both receive {domain, method, payload, requestId?} and return {value} . Module calls also carry mountId , moduleSetRevision , and optional sceneId ; the bridge acquires a lease before calling. Binary domain methods use the respective /files suffix, with JSON metadata in multipart metadata and the file in file ; download calls return bytes. The older schema API uses the same module prefix with /call and a {name, payload, ...context} envelope. These URLs describe the implementation for maintainers; module code should use its provided APIs. After changing the domain method registry, run: sh uv run --locked python scripts/generate_frontend_api.py uv run --locked python manage.py test gravewright.table.tests.test_frontend_api gravewright.table.tests.test_public_api gravewright.modules node --test tests/modules/ .test.mjs frontend-contract.js is generated from frontend.json ; update the source registry first. Keep native frontend calls, module-scoped calls, and public Python calls consistent in authorization, payload semantics and post-commit behavior. For new original SDK operations, update the schemas, registry, supported operation constants, dispatcher, and tests together; the repository has no general-purpose generator for all of those files. Module translations (Translator) Modules receive context.i18n and context.api.i18n . Register catalogs in the activation's start(context) , then translate through the API supplied to a surface: javascript export default { start({ i18n }) { i18n.register({ en: { 'sheet.title': 'Character sheet', 'sheet.greeting': 'Welcome, {name}' }, 'pt-BR': { 'sheet.title': 'Ficha de personagem', 'sheet.greeting': 'Boas-vindas, {name}' }, es: { 'sheet.title': 'Ficha de personaje', 'sheet.greeting': 'Bienvenido, {name}' }, }); }, register({ register }) { register('actor.directory', async ({ root, api }) = { root.setAttribute('translate', 'no'); root.textContent = api.i18n.t('sheet.greeting', { name: 'Arin' }); }); }, }; Catalogs can also be loaded with await context.assets.json('locales/messages.json') . locale follows the user's interface language. Lookup falls back from the exact locale to its base language, then English, then the source key. t(key, params) substitutes named or numbered placeholders as plain text. Use textContent for rendering. has(key) checks coverage; number(value, options) uses Intl.NumberFormat ; onChange(handler) returns an unsubscribe function for locale events and registration/removal of catalogs in that namespace. Changing the interface language currently reloads the page, preserving the table URL. Catalogs are isolated by module ID and shared across that module's contexts on the page. register returns a disposer and also removes its catalog when its owning context is disposed. Partial translations require an English fallback for each key and matching placeholders. Register during activation so surface mounts can reuse the catalog. No HTTP permission or external translation service is needed. Without Translator/language packs, the interface uses English. The native gravewright.i18n adapter resolves host catalogs; installed modules use their supplied context.

title: Systems and modules
summary: Installable packages, system declarations, browser lifecycle, signing and SDK contracts.
text: Documentation index (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/modules.md) · API reference (api.md) Gravewright installs signed ZIP packages containing browser JavaScript or trusted Django apps, assets, and a JSON manifest. A server owner installs releases; a campaign GM chooses browser modules and interface replacements for a table. Django apps are activated separately for the whole server. Third-party module licensing is described in the licensing policy (../../LICENSING.md). The manifest records the module author's chosen license; installation does not change it. Host compatibility VTT 0.2.1 is the first public release with the system.combat provider contract, installed content.compendiums , native api.ui.openModal , and the asynchronous sheet-save closing lifecycle documented below. These are additive host features; the SDK contract version remains 1.0.0 . An SDK version range alone does not distinguish VTT 0.2.0 from 0.2.1: packages using these features must document VTT 0.2.1 as their minimum and check optional browser APIs before calling them. VTT 0.2.0 already introduced private context.i18n catalogs; 0.2.1 also resolves translated document-type labels in native directories. Game rules, choices, sheet layouts, automation and game translation catalogs belong together in one installable system package. Do not require a separately installed Server Rules companion under Modules. The core validates descriptors, authorization and storage without interpreting a game's rules. The version references above describe historical minimum hosts; see the 0.3.2 release notes (../releases/0.3.2.md) for the current upgrade details and API reference (api.md) for the current browser and Python markers. Trust and installation boundaries Browser modules execute as ES modules in the application's main browser page. There is no iframe sandbox, Shadow DOM, or capability-based JavaScript isolation. Modules can interact with the page and browser environment. A signature authenticates the configured publisher and archive bytes; it does not prove that code is safe. Configure signing keys for publishers whose code you are prepared to run in users' sessions. The supported host interfaces enforce the authenticated user's campaign membership, native resource permissions, module activation revision, and mount lease. Those checks remain on the server. Modules receive no Python execution, SQL interface, or server-side service loader through this mechanism. Integrations installed separately as Django/Python code are trusted server code; see the Python API (api.md python-interface). Implementation entry points: File Responsibility --- --- packages.py (../../gravewright/modules/packages.py) Signatures, archive validation, immutable installation, activation revisions, JSON storage models.py (../../gravewright/modules/models.py) Installed releases, table activation, stored values, mount leases views.py (../../gravewright/modules/views.py) Owner/GM routes, downloads, leases, assets, schema-checked calls frontend.py (../../gravewright/modules/frontend.py) Shared browser domain API and authenticated dispatch module-runtime.js (../../gravewright/modules/static/gravewright_modules/module-runtime.js) Import, start/register/stop, mounting, replacement, disposal browser-bridge.js (../../gravewright/modules/static/gravewright_modules/browser-bridge.js) Package assets, storage, leased operations and domain API workspace.js (../../gravewright/modules/static/gravewright_modules/workspace.js) Attach extension surfaces to the live table and reconcile activation Minimal browser package Create this directory outside the source tree, or in an ignored development directory: text example.actor-counter/ ├── manifest.json ├── main.js ├── styles.css └── LICENSE.txt manifest.json : json { "id": "example.actor-counter", "name": "Actor counter", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": { "requires": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "tested": "1.0.0" }, "entry": "main.js", "description": "Shows the number of actors visible to the current user.", "author": "Your name", "license": "GPL-3.0-only" } Choose your actual license and include its text in LICENSE.txt . An extension's license need not match this illustrative value; see the licensing policy. The manifest schema rejects unknown keys and requires every field shown. IDs must contain at least one dot or hyphen, begin with a lowercase letter, and use lowercase letters/digits in their components. Versions use three numeric components, without prerelease/build suffixes. SDK ranges support whitespace-separated comparisons such as =1.0.0 <2.0.0 ; ^ , ~ , wildcards, and are not supported. The package loader currently checks SDK 1.0.0 ; the separate domain API reports 1.2.0 . The domain contract's api.capabilities() describes explicit methods without granting permissions. Trusted system packages register their own operations with api.systems.register_api(system_id, operations) from AppConfig.ready() ; browser modules discover the current campaign provider through api.system.state() and call it through api.system.call(operation, data, options) . Binary uploads accept File / Blob ; downloads return {blob, name, contentType, size} . These methods retain CSRF, native authorization, activation leases and the owning context's lifetime; disposal cancels pending work. See the API reference (api.md) for payloads, revisions and timeout options. main.js : javascript export default { start({ styles }) { styles.use("styles.css"); }, register({ register }) { register("actor.directory", async ({ root, api, signal }) = { const label = root.ownerDocument.createElement("p"); label.className = "example-actor-counter"; root.append(label); const render = actors = { if (!signal.aborted) label.textContent = Visible actors: ${actors.length} ; }; render(await api.actors.list()); api.events.on("actors.changed", snapshot = render(snapshot.actors)); }); }, stop() { // The host disposes styles, roots, subscriptions, and scoped API handles. } }; styles.css : css .gw-module-root data-module-id="example.actor-counter" .example-actor-counter { margin: 0.5rem; font-weight: 600; } Create the ZIP with files at its root, not under an extra package directory: sh cd example.actor-counter python -m zipfile -c ../actor-counter-1.0.0.zip manifest.json main.js styles.css LICENSE.txt This produces a package ready for signing. For a disposable local test, the installation owner may review and install a ZIP through Install from ZIP. Catalog publication uses signed records. There is no file-watching module development server. The module tests (../../gravewright/modules/tests.py) and browser integration fixture (../../tests/e2e/frontend_api.py) show isolated signing/install fixtures for development. Declaring an installed system A package can also provide a campaign system by adding system to its manifest: json "system": { "actorTypes": { "id": "character", "label": "Character" }, { "id": "npc", "label": "Non-player character" } , "itemTypes": { "id": "gear", "label": "Gear" } } Optionally declare initiative for the native combat manager: json "combat": { "formula": "1d20 + @combat.initiative", "manualInput": "number" } This object belongs inside system . The formula accepts up to 120 characters using the native dice grammar. @field.path references read finite numeric values from the actor sheet or independent token snapshot; missing fields are zero, while nonnumeric values are rejected. The system sheet must persist its calculated modifiers. Combat uses the table's selected installed release. showRoll optionally hides native initiative roll controls when false . manualInput accepts number or text and applies if scene configuration disables the formula. A manifest cannot supply executable JavaScript or Python. For live system rules, see system combat providers ( system-combat-providers). The system ID and title come from the package's id and name . Each package declares one system; it cannot replace an identity registered by a bundled provider. Declare at least one actor type; item types are optional. Type IDs must be unique within each list, start with a lowercase letter, and contain only lowercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens (80 characters maximum). Each list supports up to 64 entries with labels of 1–120 characters. Type descriptors optionally accept labelKey (a translation key up to 120 characters) and icon (an icon name up to 80 characters). Actor and item directories resolve labelKey in the package's own catalog registered with context.i18n.register , falling back to label . Available item icons include Backpack , Sword , ShieldCheck , Scroll , Sparkle and User ; unavailable names use the default icon. For example, {"id":"component","label":"Component", "labelKey":"types.component","icon":"Backpack"} . The host keeps no game-type label or icon mappings. i18n.onChange consumers also update when their namespace catalog is registered or disposed. After a signed installation, the system appears in Systems, /api/rulesets , and the campaign form. The catalog uses the newest compatible, non-revoked installed version per package, ordered by numeric version. Ordinary modules without system remain available under Installed modules. Existing campaigns can retain an unavailable system when editing their details, but it cannot be selected for a new campaign. Saving a campaign with an installed system selects its document types and activates its browser package. The existing exact release is retained when already active; switching systems removes the previous system package while preserving unrelated modules and replacement preferences. Tables use the document types of that exact activated release, or the latest installed version if none is activated. Actor data keeps the existing native document structure; module-specific data uses the supported module storage and document APIs. Installing a new version does not automatically change a table's activated release. System combat providers The core never selects a named game-rule profile. A trusted server extension registers callbacks for its own system ID from AppConfig.ready() : python from api.combat import register_provider register_provider('publisher.starship', prepare_initiative=prepare_initiative, advance_effects=advance_effects) prepare_initiative(formula, data, , conditions=()) receives isolated copies and returns (formula, data) . The native dice parser evaluates the returned formula and validates numeric results; it does not know the system's modifiers. advance_effects(data, event) mutates a bounded sheet copy and returns True when it needs persistence. The system owns field names, equipment activation, resource rules, conditions and effect clocks. Without a provider, sheet effects are left untouched. Registration for another system never affects the selected system; duplicate conflicting registrations fail startup. The event contains phase ( start / end ), roundBoundary , isCurrent , periodic , actorType , event-source tokenId / actorId / conditions , and ownerTokenId / ownerActorId for the supplied document. Linked tokens share one actor document; independent tokens receive their own snapshot. documentKey is an opaque tuple identifying that document; clockKeys is a set shared across one command's phases for system-owned clock deduplication. Skipped turns have periodic=False ; backward navigation never dispatches these callbacks. The host retains membership, ownership, encounter boundaries, transactions, JSON limits, revisions, retry receipts and publication. A callback failure rolls back the command. Callbacks must avoid external side effects: the transaction cannot undo them. These are trusted Python extensions enabled by the host owner through the existing Django package mechanism, never imports requested by a browser manifest. Each new RPG system must use one installable system package and the automation APIs supported by the requested host release. This release does not allow a browser system manifest to also declare a Django app. Document unsupported server-side requirements as limitations; do not create a separately installed companion or require a host upgrade to solve a system-package task. The Python provider contract remains a reference for trusted server integrations. Add "requiresProvider": true inside system.combat when its rules require that backend: combat actions fail clearly if it is missing, instead of silently using incomplete rules. No game-specific fallback is built into the VTT. Signed catalog and activation The marketplace uses the publisher catalog configured by the host owner; there is no built-in public feed. Installed modules load from /api/module-packages independently of the remote catalog and its configuration. Refreshing the marketplace discards previous remote results before loading the current catalog, and re-reads installed packages after signed revocations or installation. The owner-only GET /api/marketplace/status checks local configuration without contacting the publisher or writing package files. It returns HTTP 200 with catalogConfigured , trustedKeysConfigured , ready , sdk , and errors (an array of {field, code} , where field is catalog or keys ). The booleans indicate valid local configuration, not publisher availability. ready is true only when the HTTPS URL is valid and the trust store contains at least one valid key. Configuration failures return HTTP 503 from catalog and installation requests with { "error": "<code " } : Code Owner action --- --- marketplace_catalog_missing Set the publisher's HTTPS JSON catalog URL. marketplace_catalog_invalid Correct the URL; credentials, invalid ports and fragments are rejected. marketplace_keys_missing Set the trusted public keys file path. marketplace_keys_unreadable Check that the file exists and the server can read it. marketplace_keys_invalid Correct its JSON object, key IDs or base64 Ed25519 public keys. marketplace_keys_empty Add at least one trusted publisher key. Restart the host after changing environment settings; edits to the configured keys file are read on the next request. Publisher/network failure remains unavailable (503), invalid catalog/package data is invalid_data (400), and untrusted or invalid signatures remain permission_denied (403). Failed trust configuration never disables signature verification. Set GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_URL to an HTTPS JSON catalog, and GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_KEYS_FILE to a JSON file containing { "key-id": "base64-encoded-32-byte-Ed25519-public-key" } . Keep private signing keys outside distributed packages and public catalogs. The catalog is an array of records: json { "id": "example.actor-counter", "version": "1.0.0", "sdk": " =1.0.0 <2.0.0", "download": "https://your-publisher.example/actor-counter-1.0.0.zip", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters ", "keyId": "publisher-key", "signature": "<base64 Ed25519 signature " } Replace the placeholders with real values. The signature covers every field except signature , including optional status , serialized with sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escaping, and no NaN. All record values must be ASCII strings. An equivalent signer in initialized Django code is: python import base64 import hashlib from gravewright.modules.packages import canonical archive: the final ZIP bytes; private_key: publisher's Ed25519PrivateKey. record: the record above without its signature field. record "sha256" = hashlib.sha256(archive).hexdigest() record "signature" = base64.b64encode(private_key.sign(canonical(record))).decode("ascii") Publish the archive and catalog over HTTPS, configure the public key, then use the owner's Marketplace screen to install the release. A GM activates it under the table's Settings → Extensions. The HTTP installation route takes only id and version , looks up the configured catalog, and verifies the selected archive. It does not accept an arbitrary archive URL from the request. As a fully local alternative, the owner can use Install from ZIP in the same modal. This flow does not contact the marketplace or require a catalog or publisher keys: the local upload is the owner's explicit trust decision. The ZIP still undergoes the same manifest, compatibility, path, file-type, quota, and executable-content validation. In Systems it must declare system ; in Modules it must not. Because module JavaScript runs on the application origin, install only trusted files. Installation checks the archive digest, manifest identity and SDK range, entry-file presence, filenames, entry types, and extracted bytes. Limits are 64 MiB compressed, 256 MiB expanded, 4,096 entries, and 64 active modules per table. Paths cannot traverse directories or contain backslashes, percent escapes, URL punctuation, or NUL. Symlinks, encrypted entries, case-insensitive duplicate paths, disallowed extensions, and recognized native executable headers are rejected. Supported file extensions are listed in ModulePackages.install ; license texts should use .txt or .md because extensionless files are not accepted. By default, installed archives live under MEDIA_ROOT/modules/archives/ ; extracted packages live under MEDIA_ROOT/modules/packages/<id /<version /<digest / . Set, for example, GRAVEWRIGHT_MODULES_ROOT=/srv/gravewright/modules in .env to choose another folder; relative paths start at the source root and changing it requires a host restart. The database stores manifests and the trusted origin of each installation. A release ID/version cannot be replaced with different bytes. Activation and authenticated asset access recheck stored content; do not edit extracted files to develop an update. Publish a new version instead. Activation uses {modules, replacements, expectedRevision} . modules maps IDs to exact versions, replacements maps surface names to module IDs, and expectedRevision must equal the last read moduleSetRevision ( "0" initially). A stale revision produces conflict . Successful changes issue a fresh revision and notify table clients. Clients also poll and reconcile on reconnect, so activation does not depend solely on socket delivery. A signed catalog record with status: "revoked" revokes an installed release when that catalog is fetched, removes it from affected tables, clears its replacement preferences, and changes their revisions. This is catalog-fetch-driven revocation, not an always-connected publisher push. Rolling back to another installed version changes code selection; stored module data is not reverted. Lifecycle and mounting Every entry exports one default object with start , register , and stop functions. The runtime rejects the obsolete execute member. 1. The runtime invalidates old handles before reconciling a new activation revision. 2. It imports each selected package, calls and awaits start(moduleContext) , then calls register(registrationContext) once. 3. register must be synchronous. It declares mount callbacks; an async mount callback is allowed. Duplicate registrations for a domain produce conflict ; unknown domains and registrations after register returns produce invalid_data . 4. Each matching visible surface receives a separate mount root, frozen context, abort signal, API, assets/styles/storage, and onDispose callback registry. Scene surfaces also receive scene identifiers; scene.overlay has viewport coordinate conversion helpers. 5. Detaching a surface, leaving a table, changing scene/replacement/module revision, or revoking access invalidates the corresponding lifetimes. Cleanup aborts the signal first, runs registered cleanup callbacks in reverse order, and bounds each async cleanup to five seconds. stop runs after module disposal, including when start fails after the module was registered internally for cleanup. The module-level start context supplies api , assets , styles , storage , signal , and onDispose ; it has no surface root or scene identity. Mount blocks additionally supply root , context , host , events , and optionally viewport . Registration receives register and an API whose ui.register forwards to that same synchronous registration phase. Use the provided register when declaring module surfaces. Do not retain a mount's API for a later mount. Disposal rejects pending/scoped work with stale_context . Add listeners with { signal } , and register timer, observer, or external-resource cleanup through onDispose . Client cancellation cannot undo a write already committed by the server. An error in module start/registration tears down the activation and restores native UI; an individual mount failure is reported and a failed selected replacement restores its native surface. Available surfaces The registry and context schemas (../../gravewright/modules/contracts/registry.json) define the accepted names and context shapes: Surface Purpose / additional context --- --- actor.directory Actor list actor.sheet Actor sheet; actorId token.sheet Token sheet; actor/token and scene context item.directory Item list item.sheet Item sheet; itemId journal.sheet Journal document; journalId scene.directory Map/scene list scene.controls Controls for the current scene scene.overlay Overlay clipped to the current scene viewport chat.log Chat area combat.tracker Combat for the current scene preferences Table preferences table.interface Table workspace augment is the default and keeps native content. replace hides native content while the selected module mounts. One replacement candidate is selected automatically; competing candidates need an explicit table preference. Additional augmentations still mount. CSS is shared with the page, so namespace selectors. Scene overlay roots do not intercept input by default; opt in only for your interactive elements. Coordinates are logical scene pixels, origin at top left, positive x right and y down. Token coordinates refer to the center. viewport.sceneToViewport({x,y}) and viewport.viewportToScene({x,y}) convert to/from CSS viewport pixels independently of device pixel ratio. Use the mounted scene identity rather than a globally selected map. The global gravewright.ui also exposes app.shell and inside.content ; these are host-page surfaces, not accepted domains in the signed module runtime. See frontend architecture (frontend.md). Assets, persistence, and events Use assets.url(path) , assets.text(path) , assets.json(path) , or assets.bytes(path) with package-relative paths. styles.use(path) attaches a stylesheet and returns a disposer; it is also removed automatically on context disposal. These helpers do not provide arbitrary network access as part of the supported SDK. Store Scope Write policy --- --- --- storage.local Browser origin + module ID; not separated by table/user Browser-local JSON, 256 KiB per value storage.user Module + table + authenticated user That user's persistent JSON storage.table Module + table Members read; GM writes Persistent values have a 256 KiB limit and each persistent namespace a 4 MiB limit. Keys are at most 240 characters. get returns {value, revision} or null ; list(prefix) returns key/revision pairs. To create a value use expectedRevision: null ; update/delete with the exact revision returned by get or set : javascript const previous = await storage.user.get("panel-settings"); const saved = await storage.user.set("panel-settings", { collapsed: true }, { expectedRevision: previous?.revision ?? null }); await storage.user.delete("panel-settings", { expectedRevision: saved.revision }); On conflict , read again and decide how to merge. Do not repeatedly overwrite another client's update. These values outlive deactivation and code upgrades; version and migrate your own JSON data explicitly. Local browser storage is unsuitable for private user data on a shared browser because its module namespace is shared across accounts. Prefer api.events.on("actors.changed", handler) and the other domain events for current authorized snapshots. The older mount-level events.on exposes actor.created , actor.updated , actor.deleted , and scene.viewport.changed . In the current workspace bridge the actor events are inferred from successive visible actor lists: initial/repeated snapshots and changes of visibility can appear as creates, updates, or deletes. They are refresh hints, not a mutation audit. Re-read after reconnect and do not use these notifications as exactly-once side effects. Unsubscribe explicitly using the returned disposer or let mount disposal unsubscribe. Verification From the repository root: sh uv run --locked python manage.py test gravewright.modules gravewright.table.tests.test_frontend_api gravewright.table.tests.test_public_api node --test tests/modules/ .test.mjs uv run --locked python tests/e2e/frontend_api.py uv run --locked python tests/e2e/table_modules.py Browser tests require the development dependencies and installed Playwright browser; see testing (testing.md). Exercise activation/deactivation, a failed mount, scene changes, membership loss, reconnect, stale storage revisions, and the GM/player views of any new operation. Existing schema files and tests are concrete contract references; this checkout does not include a TypeScript SDK package or an automated major-version compatibility release checker. Installation-wide language packages A manifest may declare locales , mapping locale IDs to { "name": "Português (Brasil)", "path": "locales/pt-BR.json" } . Catalog files are nonempty JSON objects mapping original UI strings to translations, preserving {name} -style placeholders. English is built into the host and cannot be overridden; a package cannot combine system and locales . Language packages cannot contain Python. Language packages appear in Installed modules. An owner uses POST /api/module-packages/activation with { "id": "gravewright.translator", "version": "<installed-version ", "enabled": true } to activate one installation-wide language package. Replace the placeholder with the exact installed package version, which is independent of the VTT release. Activation verifies the installed signed archive. Campaign module configuration rejects language packages and the table extension list omits them. After activation, each authenticated user can choose a language in internal account Settings. The choice is stored in UserPreference.locale ; a signed cookie supports the anonymous login screen. A different signed-in account does not inherit the previous account's cookie preference. Disabling/revoking the package restores English on the next page load and removes the selector. Reload existing pages after changing global activation. The host translates application dictionaries and literal template text. Reactive template labels are translated before Datastar processes them to avoid conflicting DOM observers. Browser-created controls use the static catalog; user-authored names, chat and editable content are excluded. This does not translate PDFs, rule content or arbitrary third-party interfaces. The Translator Django app is maintained at <https://github.com/Gravewright/translator . Its build command creates the portable signed release input; the Django authoring app is not needed after marketplace installation. See that package's documentation for its build and validation workflow. The host owns the locale activation contract and runtime translation hooks documented here; package versions and VTT versions follow separate release histories. After changing native labels, run python scripts/audit_translations.py --catalogs data/translator-source/gravewright_translator/catalogs against an explicit Translator source checkout. The audit checks catalog parity, placeholders and literal t(...) , adapter .t(...) , gwText , modalText , text and label calls. It does not inventory every dynamic expression or template, so also check the rendered interface. The visibility panel translates its icon title, mode hints, status, accessibility labels and detached-window title through the same host adapter, including locale changes while open. Reviewed host corrections also supply its new labels to already installed Translator packages without modifying their signed archives. Package library and installation browser Inside now has separate Systems and Modules libraries, with a tile/list view preference, search and pagination. Install system or Install module opens the configured catalog in a dialog filtered to that category. The native PDF system remains visible without remote configuration. Installed libraries never require a catalog fetch; catalog diagnostics appear when opening the installation browser. The old section=marketplace link resolves to Modules for compatibility. New signed catalog records should include "type": "system" , "type": "module" , or "type": "django" . Django records require an explicit type and a django manifest block. This field participates in the signature and must match the ZIP manifest ( system means the manifest declares system ). Invalid values and mismatches are rejected. Legacy records without a type remain valid and default to modules when not yet installed; installed manifests determine their actual category. Publishers of system packages must include the signed type for correct discovery before installation. Catalog records may also declare tags : up to 24 unique, trimmed, nonempty Unicode strings of at most 64 characters. They participate in the canonical signature and form creator-defined categories in the installation modal. Categories are scoped to the selected package type. Missing tags remain valid and packages still appear under All packages. Tag labels follow the interface language selected through Translator. The host translates their presentation and recognizes aliases for Portuguese tags already in the official catalog, such as Tradução and Dados . Package IDs, original tag values, signed records and category filters retain their original identities. Search accepts both original and translated tags. Unknown tags without a translation remain as provided by the publisher. This host integration works with Translator 0.1.2 and requires no change to its signed package or the Marketplace catalog. The installation modal receives NDJSON progress from POST /api/marketplace/install when Accept: application/x-ndjson is sent. Events have stage values catalog , download (actual received bytes and nullable total ), verify , complete (manifest), or error (code). Completion is emitted only after archive verification, extraction and database installation. Without a known Content-Length, download progress is indeterminate with a byte count. The ordinary JSON endpoint remains compatible. Disconnecting a browser does not roll back an installation already running; refresh the installed library to check its result. Optional per-user customization An active browser module may export customize(context) alongside its required lifecycle methods. The table extension list displays Customize immediately before Deactivate (or on its own for players). The callback receives the same module-scoped assets, storage and lifetime as start ; no new permissions are granted. Use storage.user for personal choices, and close dialogs and dispose resources on onDispose . The host only supplies the button; the module owns its UI, assets and validation. Modules without this optional callback are unchanged. Explicitly installed Django apps The marketplace also accepts signed catalog records with "type": "django" . These appear in Modules with a Django · Server badge. A local Django ZIP can be installed through Install from ZIP in the same library. Installation only validates and extracts the archive; use its activation button to execute the trusted server code and restart the host. This requires the managed Runner or main.py , plus uv . There is no manual .env change for marketplace apps. Use the normal manifest identity, SDK, description, author and license fields, omit entry , system and locales , and add: json "django": { "apps": "my_extension.apps.MyExtensionConfig" , "requirements": "some-library==1.2.3" } The ZIP must contain my_extension/__init__.py and the app's Python sources, migrations, templates and static assets. requirements is optional and accepts exact name==version pins from the configured Python package index, without URLs, local paths, extras or installer flags. Dependency resolution cannot replace the core versions locked by Gravewright. Apps must use distinct import names and Django labels. An AppConfig may define gravewright_urlconf ; each app is responsible for authentication, CSRF and resource permissions on its routes. Activation prepares a separate Python environment, checks Django, backs up the database and files, applies migrations, collects static files and restarts. Failures restore the previous environment, package selection and data. Only one server operation may run at a time. Enabled selections live in MEDIA_ROOT/modules/server-apps.json (or the configured modules directory), survive core updates, and have their dependency pins reapplied during updates. Deactivation restarts the host without the app; it does not reverse migrations or delete the app's data. Revoked releases cannot be newly activated; an already running app must be deactivated by the owner. Python sources are not served by the browser-package asset endpoint or offered as table-level modules. The following remains an alternative for operator-managed source checkouts: A host operator may install a trusted Python app in the server's environment and set GRAVEWRIGHT_SERVER_APPS to its import path (comma-separated for multiple apps). An AppConfig may expose gravewright_urlconf to append its URL patterns. These apps run as trusted server code and must enforce authentication, CSRF and native domain permissions. This setting is never populated from browser package manifests. Environment rebuilds require reinstalling these separately managed Python dependencies. An invalid app import prevents startup rather than silently disabling its server functionality. Native item rows expose application/x-gravewright-item drag data containing {id, tableId} . Resolve the ID through the authenticated item API before copying it into a sheet; do not treat data supplied by a drag payload as authoritative. Actor and token sheet replacements own the complete window body . The host provides only the movable title bar, detach/minimize/close controls, permissions and document identity. PDF, Token and Notes tabs belong exclusively to the bundled PDF system module; other systems never load its controller, templates or styles. The bundled module registers its descriptor, sheet provider and data validator through its AppConfig. Legacy PDF campaigns keep their existing ID and stored data, with no conversion required. Signed system packages can register different sheets for declared actor types: js register("actor.sheet", { mode: "replace", types: "hero" , mount({ root, context, api, signal }) { // Render the entire sheet, including any navigation your system needs. // context includes actorId, actorType, systemId and canEdit. // Use api.actors.sheet(...) and api.actors.saveSheet(...) for document data. } }); Omitting types applies the registration to all actor types. Disjoint type lists allow multiple registrations on the same surface. An explicit table replacement wins; otherwise the campaign's system sheet takes precedence over competing add-ons. A token uses the system's actor sheet with tokenId and sceneId in its context unless that package registers a matching token.sheet replacement. Actor and snapshot-token data for external systems retain their own JSON shape; the host enforces size, JSON safety, ownership and revision checks without injecting PDF fields. Optional token and bars presentation hints still work; missing hints use neutral scene defaults without changing stored sheet data. Before closing, the window emits gravewright:sheet-flush ; a mounted extension can call event.detail.waitUntil(promise) synchronously to await pending writes. A rejection keeps the window open and displays the error. Bind listeners on root.closest('.gw-window') using the mount abort signal. Custom sheets own flush/refresh behavior when switching their internal tabs. The PDF provider continues emitting gravewright:sheet-flush and gravewright:sheet-refresh when switching its own tabs. Item sheet replacements retain the native title bar and also emit gravewright:sheet-flush before closing. Bind the listener on root.closest('.item-sheet') and call event.detail.waitUntil(promise) to await writes, including when the user presses ESC. Rejection keeps the item open. Losing read access forces immediate closure without waiting for writes. For separately maintained source checkouts, set GRAVEWRIGHT_SERVER_APP_PATHS to their package root directories ( : separated on Linux/macOS, ; on Windows). Relative paths resolve against the VTT checkout. These explicitly trusted paths survive virtual-environment synchronization; app dependencies still require installation. The Python packages remain outside the VTT repository. The checkout ships a default folder for these apps: extensions/django , set by GRAVEWRIGHT_DJANGO_MODULES_ROOT . It is appended to sys.path when it exists, so a package placed directly in it only needs its import path in GRAVEWRIGHT_SERVER_APPS ; explicit GRAVEWRIGHT_SERVER_APP_PATHS entries precede it. Browser module sources have a matching default folder, extensions/api ( GRAVEWRIGHT_API_MODULES_ROOT ), which is documentation and authoring space only — installed signed packages still live under MEDIA_ROOT/modules . A configured folder that does not exist prevents startup; deleting the shipped defaults without configuring them is supported. Git ignores the contents of both folders, so extensions stay out of this repository. Ethical module porting (ethical-module-porting.md) Compendiums supplied by a system package A browser system may declare up to 16 JSON collections in its manifest: json "content": {"compendiums": "compendiums/entities.json", "compendiums/gear.json" } Paths must be relative package paths ending in .json . Absolute paths, traversal, URLs and symlinks outside the approved package are rejected. Each collection is limited to 8 MiB, 64 packs and 20,000 entries in total. An entry is limited to 256 KiB; JSON nesting is limited to 24 levels. Collections contain declarative JSON, and each entry's data belongs to its provider. The core does not execute expressions or fetch external assets from those fields: json { "name": "Example equipment", "packs": { "id": "gear", "label": "Equipment", "type": "item_pack", "entries": { "id": "survey-kit", "name": "Survey kit", "type": "gear", "systemId": "author.example-system", "data": {"revision": "original", "description": "Plain text"} } } } Supported pack kinds are actor_pack , item_pack and spell_pack . Every entry must use the provider's own systemId and a type registered in its system.actorTypes or system.itemTypes . Pack IDs must be unique within the collection; entry IDs must be unique within their pack. IDs accept ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons and hyphens, up to 120 characters, and must start with a letter or digit. Names and labels are limited to 120 characters. Keep IDs and relative paths stable across updates so permissions and entry references remain stable. Installation validates the declarations and files. The native compendium UI exposes them only in campaigns using that system's exact active, pinned, approved and non-revoked package version. Every read checks installed bytes against the approved archive; changing a file does not authorize new content. Collections do not declare campaign IDs. The host binds access internally. Packs are private to the GM by default. Existing compendium read grants and role defaults control player visibility; importing documents remains a GM action. The host treats data as opaque JSON and retains the provider's fields; it does not interpret revisions or game rules. Update the VTT base to a version supporting content.compendiums before installing a package that uses this optional declaration. Declared collection JSON files are not served by generic package asset URLs. Read and import their entries through the table-scoped compendium API, which checks the active system and the user's current read grants. Use api.compendiums.state() to discover visible pack and entry IDs. api.compendiums.read({packId, id}) still returns one entry; api.compendiums.read({packId, ids: id1, id2 }) returns {entries: ... } containing the same documents in requested order. A batch accepts 1–100 unique IDs; do not combine id with ids . Invalid or duplicate IDs produce invalid_data . A missing entry fails the entire batch with not_found , without partial results. Native packs retain full source documents; packs created in a table retain their individual kind , data and version envelope. Every read rechecks table membership and current grants, plus the active version and integrity of installed collections. Reads create no mutation receipts and publish no compendiums.changed event. Reusing a request ID does not retain access after revocation. A read-only role may read under a valid grant and still cannot import documents. The root index contains only pack metadata and each entry's id , name , kind , type and version . It does not include document bodies or archives. type is the provider's registered document type, not a host rules category; spell_pack is a compatibility pack kind that routes to item documents without adding spell rules. Full documents are loaded through authorized individual or batch reads. Installed collections share the same bounded, verified content cache regardless of provider or document type; permissions, package selection and revocation are checked on each request and are never cached with content. Legacy actor imports without a type use the system's declared actor default, the same contract as actor creation, instead of a built-in actor type. Module modal windows Use api.ui.openModal(element, {nested = true, canClose = () = true}) for module windows. It mounts the shared Gravewright modal component synchronously and returns the same element, with close() , suspend() and resume() methods. Pass a section , div or form created in the host document. Native HTML dialog elements and elements from another document are rejected. The host adds table-modal-window , traps focus, makes the background inert, restores focus on close, and handles Escape. Modules provide their content, accessible name, translated labels and close button; a modal does not automatically gain a movable title bar. js mount({root, api, signal}) { const doc = root.ownerDocument; const panel = doc.createElement('section'); panel.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Details'); // Use your translated label. const close = doc.createElement('button'); close.type = 'button'; close.textContent = 'Close'; // Use your translated label. panel.append(close); const modal = api.ui.openModal(panel); close.addEventListener('click', () = modal.close(), {signal}); } nested: true keeps an existing modal underneath the new one; closing the child restores the parent. Set nested: false to request closing the previous modal. canClose is a synchronous guard for Escape; explicit close() calls remain under the module's control. close() emits gravewright:sheet-flush , so attach a listener to the returned element and call event.detail.waitUntil(promise) during the event to await pending writes. A rejected write keeps the modal open. suspend() temporarily hides the modal for interactions such as picking on the map; resume() restores it. The API is bound to the activation or surface lifetime. Disposal forces the modal closed, even when a save is pending, and releases its focus and background state. Normal close releases the lifetime cleanup immediately. Opening a modal after disposal throws stale_context ; opening an already mounted element throws conflict . This helper is available to start , customize , registration and surface callbacks. api.ui.register retains its existing registration-phase behavior.

title: Frontend architecture
summary: Jinja2, Datastar, native JavaScript, PixiJS, styles and asset preparation.
text: Documentation index (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/frontend.md) · API reference (api.md) The application renders Jinja2 HTML on the server, uses Datastar for reactive signals and fragment updates, and runs JavaScript controllers for interactive workspaces. The game board uses PixiJS and a separate source/build pipeline. There is no single application-wide SPA build step. Follow a page from its template base.html (../../gravewright/web/jinja2/gravewright_web/base.html) loads the shared stylesheet, vendored Datastar, and gravewright_modules/frontend-api.js , which creates window.gravewright . The /inside workspace and game table extend that shell. table/page.html (../../gravewright/table/jinja2/gravewright_table/page.html) composes feature templates and loads table, map, journal, actor, dice and module controllers. Useful areas to inspect: Location Purpose --- --- gravewright/web/jinja2/ Shared shell, Inside pages and reusable HTML gravewright/accounts/jinja2/ Authentication and initial account setup templates gravewright/web/static/gravewright_web/css/ Design tokens, base styles and component classes gravewright/web/static/gravewright_web/inside/ Inside account/campaign/admin controllers and styles gravewright/web/static/gravewright_web/windows.js Movable/resizable window behavior gravewright/table/static/gravewright_table/realtime.js Socket connection, subscriptions, authenticated fragments and event dispatch gravewright/modules/static/gravewright_modules/ Public browser API, signed-module runtime, transport and lifecycle gravewright/maps/frontend/ Editable board, wall, token, lighting, selection and tool sources gravewright/maps/static/gravewright_maps/workspace.js Native map workspace integration gravewright/pdf_system/frontend/ Editable PDF mapping/controller sources App-specific jinja2/ , static/ , and messages.json Domain UI, styling and text catalogs Templates carry IDs and data- attributes that native controllers and extension surfaces depend on. Changing one may affect the corresponding controller, Datastar signals, and module attachment. Check all three before renaming selectors or replacing an entire panel. modules/static/gravewright_modules/domain-api.js exposes the generated domain contract to pages and leased modules. file-api.js keeps file bytes in multipart requests and returns authenticated blobs; global-api.js owns account, campaign, administration and package adapters on the page lifetime. These adapters preserve caller cancellation and native permission checks. See the extended public API (api.md) for MapBuilder, blueprints, ownership, library files and system-owned operations. Manual PDF fields For the complete player/GM workflow, see the PDF System guide (pdf-system.md). This section identifies the implementation and its validation boundaries. In a Gravewright PDF System character sheet, the GM can open a PDF and choose Map fields . Select text, number, checkbox or multiline text, then drag a rectangle over its area on the page. Add field creates a rectangle with the keyboard. Select a rectangle to rename it, change its percentage bounds, drag it or resize its lower-right corner. Arrow keys move the selected rectangle one display pixel (Shift: ten); Delete removes it and Escape cancels a gesture. Finish mapping returns to filling the sheet. Changes save automatically. Mappings belong to that actor or independent token copy, PDF source and page. They stay aligned through zoom and spread changes and coexist with native PDF form widgets. Authorized players can fill the fields; only the GM can change their definitions. The overlay leaves the original PDF file unchanged, including when downloading it. Deleting a rectangle retains its stored value. Number and single-line text fields can also be chosen for token bars. pdf_system/frontend/manual-fields.js owns stable identities and normalized display-page geometry; frontend/controller.js combines manual definitions with native widgets. static/gravewright_pdf_system/manual-editor.js owns gestures, selection and disposal. pdf_system/manual_fields.py validates at most 256 definitions across sources, page bounds, names, types and values, and enforces GM-only layout changes through the normal sheet-save service. Omitted layouts are preserved for older clients. The generated controller follows the existing map asset build pipeline. The GM can double-click a native or manually mapped field, or focus it and press F2, to open Field actions in the existing application modal. Choose a token value, enter a roll formula and label, or use one of six presets: d20, highest or lowest of two d20s, 2d6, exploding d6 and 4dF. @value references that field's current numeric value; an empty value is zero and checkboxes use zero or one. Formulas without @value also work on text fields. Clear the formula to remove the roll action. Assigning or removing a token-bar binding preserves the field's current value. Saving validates the complete candidate before updating the displayed sheet; Cancel and Escape discard the draft. Saved roll actions appear as buttons above the PDF for authorized editors. Players can also double-click a configured field; Alt+Enter rolls a focused field. The GM's double-click continues to open configuration, where Roll saved action executes the saved formula without applying the draft. Rolls use the native dice notation (../../gravewright/dice/grammar/notation/GRAMMAR.md), publish to chat in the current scene context and retain normal request receipts and reconnect retries. Configuring an action consumes no randomness. pdf.fieldActions is optional and holds up to 256 source/field-bound roll definitions with a 512-character formula and a 48-character label. The server compiles formulas using the dice parser and compiler, preserving omitted actions and rejecting changes by non-GMs. frontend/field-actions.js builds isolated save candidates, preserves canonical bar values and expands the bounded numeric @value reference. static/gravewright_pdf_system/field-actions-editor.js owns the modal's draft and disposal. Reference field inserts @{field-key} into a roll or calculated formula. The picker shows readable names; manual keys remain stable when fields are renamed, and native PDF references retain their exact form-field name. Braces and backslashes in native names are escaped by the picker. Reference values are numeric and limited to the existing ±1,000,000 range. Calculated value formula accepts deterministic arithmetic, comparisons and the native numeric functions, with references to other fields. Clear it to return to ordinary editing. Calculated controls are read-only and update in dependency order. The server recomputes results on every sheet save, rejects circular references including aliases through token bars, and retains the previous canonical result when an input is temporarily nonnumeric or a calculation cannot execute. pdf.fieldBindings records validated original field addresses for references; bar overrides resolve against the current token mapping. Only the GM can change bindings or pdf.calculatedFields . The server's formulas.py and calculated_fields.py own validation and authoritative calculation; frontend/formulas.js mirrors the deterministic subset for immediate feedback. Archived field values and bindings remain available after removing a rectangle; diagnostics identify references whose visible field has disappeared. While mapping, Shift/Ctrl-click or drag a selection rectangle to select multiple fields on a page. The layout toolbar supports copying, pasting, duplication, six alignments, horizontal/vertical distribution and optional snapping to a five-point grid. Ctrl+C/V/D and Ctrl+Z/Shift+Z provide the same operations. The toolbar is inside Layout tools , initially collapsed in narrow sheet windows and expandable by keyboard or touch. Each gesture is one history step, limited to 50 steps in the active PDF. Undo restores definitions while retaining current character values; switching documents clears the history. Copies receive new UUIDs and remap formulas inside the selection. frontend/layout-editor.js owns geometry and layout-history.js owns definition snapshots and clipboard identities. Mapping library opens campaign templates for GMs. Save or replace the current mapping, apply a template to the current sheet or selected actors, and import or export versioned JSON. Templates contain rectangles, actions, calculations, bindings and optional document geometry, without PDFs, character values, names or media. Existing values are retained by field identity and canonical bars; templates do not merge unrelated fields by their visible labels. Independent token snapshots retain their own layouts unless explicitly applying a template to that open snapshot. Batch application validates all actor revisions before committing any changes. Stable manual IDs already used by another PDF in the same sheet cause a validation error rather than reassigning that PDF's fields. MappingTemplate and its initial migration belong to pdf_system . The /api/containers/<id /pdf-mappings routes enforce GM and campaign boundaries, revision checks and operation receipts. Limits are 128 templates per campaign, 100 actors per batch and 1 MB per JSON import, in addition to sheet limits. Campaign archives include the templates and validate their portable bundles on restore. Template changes require a new application to update a character. Filled PDF downloads a separate flattened copy of every PDF page with the current field values, including repeated native widgets across pages. It renders through the bundled PDF.js at 144 dpi and writes JPEG page images in a minimal PDF container, preserving Unicode text as rendered by the browser. The original remains available separately. The copy contains no editable widgets or executable PDF content. Export rejects text that cannot fit its rectangle, excessive page/image complexity or a result over 100 MB, and downloads only after every page succeeds. It supports at most 100 pages, 16 million pixels per page and 128 million pixels per operation. Closing or switching documents cancels the work. The container follows the image-XObject and byte-offset structure of ISO 32000-1 (https://opensource.adobe.com/dc-acrobat-sdk-docs/pdfstandards/PDF32000_2008.pdf). The PDF mapping diagnostics button checks missing fields or references, calculation errors, absent pages and differences from saved document size, rotation or fingerprint. pdf.sourceMetadata keeps the expected document descriptor when applying a template; opening a PDF does not silently replace it. Diagnostics use authored labels as text and provide navigation to fields that are still present. Export and diagnosis never modify the original PDF. node --test gravewright/pdf_system/frontend/ .test.js covers the field model; manage.py test gravewright.pdf_system.test_manual_fields covers persistence and authorization. The isolated browser scenario tests/e2e/pdf_manual_fields.py exercises drawing, filling, navigation, native widgets, token copies, roles and Translator in English, Portuguese and Spanish. manage.py test gravewright.pdf_system.test_field_actions and tests/e2e/pdf_field_actions.py cover roll configuration, bar-value preservation, chat delivery, cancelled/invalid drafts, permissions and responsive translated modals. manage.py test gravewright.pdf_system also covers templates, calculations, metadata and campaign archive round trips. tests/e2e/pdf_workbench.py exercises the combined workflow and parses/renders the generated PDF with PDF.js. Map Builder workspace GET /game/<campaign_id /map-builder renders maps/builder.html (../../gravewright/maps/jinja2/gravewright_maps/builder.html) through maps/builder.py . It checks current GM membership and validates the optional folder query against that campaign. The new-scene chooser performs normal same-tab navigation; the builder uses the base shell with its own static/gravewright_maps/builder/ controllers, without mounting table runtime, scene subscriptions or the table workspace. Native effects use the dedicated preview described below. The table's scene directory reads the optional builderProjectId from the GM projection of maps.services.state() . It is resolved in one campaign-scoped ID query from the project's current scene link; non-GM projections do not include it. Linked scenes keep the same compact row and map icon, colored with --danger , and add Edit with MapBuilder beside the normal edit action in the context menu. Shift+F10 or the context-menu key opens the menu from a focused scene. Menus render in the directory's document, including detached windows; the edit action opens the editor in the main game tab. The project endpoint rechecks GM membership and campaign ownership on load. native-effects.js is a builder adapter to the same light, particle and shader catalogs as the tabletop. Its small eager builder-catalog.js bundle supplies presets without starting WebGL; builder-native.js loads lazily for visible sources. The editable entries are frontend/native/builder-catalog.js and frontend/native/builder-preview.js . The latter reuses PixiBoardRenderer and SceneLayers on a transparent overlay synchronized to the SVG camera and wall geometry. Hidden/empty layers, page hiding and disposal release rendering and animation resources. Native effects remain separate from the generated raster. frontend/native/builder-editors.js hosts the same LightEditor and EffectEditor widgets used by the game against a detached builder draft. Its builder-editor-model.js adapter maps the builder's light radius names and resolves compact preset references for GLSL editing without expanding an unchanged source. Transactional widget footers are enabled only in this host; the game's existing autosave behavior remains available to its normal host. Draft validation and preview never call scene commands. Saving returns one candidate to workspace.js , which checks editability and commits one project history step. Cancel/close disposes preview timers, shader validation and any nested prompt, preserving the project and live scene. static/gravewright_maps/wall-editor.js and the wall_editor.html template share the wall configuration window with the table's wall controller. Its builder host writes optional native presentation, channel, elevation and discovery settings to the source wall/door. Door and lever Smart Object behavior windows remain separate from physical wall configuration. builder/torch-model.js binds a decoration to native light/effect source rows. Mechanism state and flame illumination are independent; preview projects the mechanism's quarter turn and gates enabled components without rewriting source coordinates. model.js expands composed selections once for transforms and duplication, while object-removal.js reconciles ownership and Blueprint light references atomically. Component editor buttons reuse builder-editors.js and retain the selected parent. On the table, lever-controls.js hosts both lever and torch interactions, and image-components.js projects linked render nodes through image/selection previews without recreating GPU resources. The domain's torches.py validates scene-local ownership, applies authoritative transforms and flame gating, and keeps native group operations within map transactions. Entry is read-only. The Studio's workspace.js composes the editor controllers, navigation and drawing gestures. Its directly served sibling modules own these boundaries: Module under static/gravewright_maps/builder/ Responsibility --- --- project-persistence.js Draft recovery/storage, HTTP/CSRF, receipt identities and the save queue workspace-library.js Campaign asset catalog, brush choices and material controls workspace-import.js Asset import/edit modals and their listener lifetime inspector-controller.js Shared selection fields, section modals and region/torch configuration object-menu.js Object context menu, keyboard navigation and model submenu interactive-presets.js Configurable generic object Blueprints and their catalog modal shader-control.js Typed shader property controls shared by Blueprint editing, simulation and logs layer-controller.js Layer controls, contents, selection and drag listeners productivity.js , productivity-model.js Grouping, atomic arrangement, campaign object bundles, area guides and object strokes player-test.js , player-test-model.js Detached player rehearsal, area crossings and rollback-only behavior requests canvas-renderer.js SVG artwork, selection overlays and disposable terrain/wall caches Controllers receive explicit state and callbacks rather than importing the workspace or sharing globals. Persistence tests import its public factory; they do not extract function text from workspace.js . A disposed save owner cannot write a late acknowledgement over a recovered draft. model.js owns cell-space geometry and undo history, and viewport.js owns the independent SVG camera. Camera listeners, pointer capture, requests and resize observation end on pagehide ; history restoration remounts the editor. builder_services.py owns campaign-scoped project revisions, retry receipts, validation, scene generation and updates. See Map Builder (map-builder.md) for the source schema, native geometry and raster boundaries. newDocument() creates one empty, generically named layer with a fresh UUID; the controller localizes its initial Layer 1 name. It creates no layers by object type. Schema-3 normalization preserves authored layers, including an empty layer list after removing the final empty layer. The server accepts that list only with no objects, and empty-map generation renders just the background. Version-1/2 upgrades retain their existing Base-layer conversion. All element kinds accept an authored name of up to 120 characters. Optional names stay omitted on unnamed legacy rows; regions and shaders retain their required names. The inspector supplies the existing Empty Object label for older unnamed controllers. element_names.py validates type, whitespace, length and NUL at the server boundary. Native edits, scene generation and linked updates preserve labels without replacing UUIDs or Blueprint targets. Static floor artwork remains baked; a dynamic surface carries its source name on the native image. The Selection inspector owns one name field per selected element, and layers, behavior catalogs and light/door choices prefer authored labels. The library's persistent tool strip exposes its additional controls through data-builder-dock-tool ; existing panel tool selectors remain distinct. Tool changes flush the focused property before returning focus to the canvas. The strip scrolls independently on narrow screens and keeps a stable layout when the native light/effect library replaces the asset cards. The header mode selector honors optional editingMode: "tiles" "paint" ; omission defaults to Tiles without changing the source. Tiles and terrain Painting share layers, native objects, camera and project history. Existing floor.paint color/opacity still renders independently through SVG and the raster, multiplying shape coverage, texture alpha and opacity. Selecting the new terrain brush does not reinterpret those earlier styles or convert existing geometry. Floors retain their layer and transform contracts. SVG and Pillow use different antialiasing at coincident contour/cut boundaries; pixel comparisons keep interiors exact and isolate that subpixel boundary band. floor-painter.js owns transient floor gestures and commits one complete edit. model.js supplies swept brush footprints, family-aware flood fill, material sampling and atomic floor subtraction. floor-geometry.js supplies continuous contours and excluded cuts when snapping is disabled, along with shape-aware hit testing and source/raster budgets. The server validates the same optional floor shape contract and rasterizes its union-minus-cuts mask with bounded antialiasing.
