Custom upload surfaces must keep the real file input reachable by keyboard, show its focus, and prevent window dragging from the upload target. Check empty, selected, disabled and error states at narrow viewport widths with synthetic data; operating-system file selection remains the native file picker. Native state and realtime Native UI code calls the shared domain API where implemented and still has dedicated HTTP/socket adapters for specialized flows such as uploads, board subscriptions and rendered fragments. The public browser API does not replace every native transport. The realtime controller connects the current table's authenticated WebSocket, tracks subscriptions and reconnect state, and dispatches gravewright: browser events. The server sends user-authorized projections and rendered HTML; private actor data, chat audiences and scene visibility are enforced before delivery. Insert user-provided text with textContent . Existing HTML fragment insertion is for HTML rendered by the trusted server templates, not arbitrary module or chat text. gravewright:api-event is the internal adapter event consumed by the domain API; api.changed notifications trigger fresh authorized reads. Public integrations should use api.events.on(...) as documented in API events (api.md domain-events), rather than copying the native socket command protocol. Subscriptions are not a durable change stream: reconnect and reread current state. Creating gravewright.forTable(...) alone does not open a socket. The native item and compendium directories sort copies of visible entries by their displayed names using the active locale; stored document order and IDs stay unchanged. Compendium packs, filters and previews use compact rows and content-sized default windows, with internal scrolling for long content. Manual window layouts retain the shared drag, resize, minimize and reset controls. GMs can create the first compendium from the empty directory; read access does not expose import or permission controls. System-owned item editors remain in their packages and use the existing host contracts. Repeated item projections preserve open action menus and focus; document or permission changes invalidate them. Sources and generated assets Most app-specific JavaScript files under static/ are directly served source. Some files there are committed build outputs. In particular, maps/scripts/build.cjs (../../gravewright/maps/scripts/build.cjs) bundles the following: Editable entry/source Generated destination --- --- maps/frontend/widgets/game-board/ui/board.js maps/static/gravewright_maps/vendor/board.js and named runtime/ modules maps/frontend/shared/rendering/render-profile.js maps/static/gravewright_maps/render-profile.js maps/frontend/native/tools.js maps/static/gravewright_maps/tools.js maps/frontend/native/builder-catalog.js , builder-preview.js maps/static/gravewright_maps/builder-catalog.js , builder-native.js maps/frontend/native/builder-editors.js maps/static/gravewright_maps/builder-editors.js maps/frontend/native/table-modules.js table/static/gravewright_table/media-workspace.js maps/frontend/features/walls/{ui,model}/walls.js maps/static/gravewright_maps/walls/ Scene-layer sources and lighting profiles maps/static/gravewright_maps/sources/ maps/frontend/calibration.js , directory.js Corresponding map static model/controller files maps/frontend/shared/lib/dom/tree-drag.js actors/static/gravewright_actors/tree-drag.js maps/frontend/features/tokens/ui/controller.js tokens/static/gravewright_tokens/controller.js pdf_system/frontend/controller.js pdf_system/static/gravewright_pdf_system/controller.js Paths in this table are relative to gravewright/ . Edit the source and rebuild these destinations. Do not make one-off fixes in minified board chunks or vendored libraries. Tools, the board, Builder catalogs, editors and preview retain their public entry URLs while importing named ES modules from gravewright_maps/runtime/ , following the source's feature paths. Shared modules have one browser identity; PixiJS and its unsafe-eval adapter are emitted once as vendor/pixi.js . Preview and editor imports stay lazy, and the visibility worker keeps its relative resource URL plus the existing public worker entry. The Runner manifest includes every emitted module and license notice. Ship the complete generated graph. This layout uses more small requests while avoiding repeated bundled copies; artifact sizes alone do not establish a browser performance improvement. From the repository root: sh npm ci --include=dev --prefix gravewright/maps/frontend npm run build --prefix gravewright/maps/frontend npm test --prefix gravewright/maps/frontend The build uses the locked PixiJS and esbuild dependencies in maps/frontend/package-lock.json (../../gravewright/maps/frontend/package-lock.json), targets ES2022, and keeps /static/ imports external. A shared render-profile module stays external so all features use the same runtime profile. The build also collects package license/notice files and writes vendor/packages.json ; retain those outputs when redistributing built assets. It explicitly rejects including Vue packages. Windows runner preparation The Gravewright Runner (windows-runner.md) reuses verified Node.js/npm inside data/runner, or downloads its managed copy into that installation when necessary. Its CMD batch file calls scripts/prepare_frontend.py (../../scripts/prepare_frontend.py) in --plan mode to check package versions, fingerprints and a real esbuild operation. A matching healthy dependency installation can be reused even on first launch. The batch file itself executes npm ci --include=dev --include=optional when dependencies need installation, and the existing npm run build for the first preparation or an invalidated build. It then calls the helper in --record mode to verify and save the completed output state. esbuild is required during preparation even though Python development dependencies are omitted from normal runner installation. The plan returns exit code 0 for current assets, 10 for npm installation plus build, or 11 for build only. The batch launcher handles these decisions explicitly. Both helper modes accept --node , --npm-cli and --state-dir ; the helper's default mode remains available to perform complete preparation in developer scripts and regression tests. The npm project remains gravewright/maps/frontend ; its ignored node_modules/ is installed there and generated static assets are written to the destinations above. These outputs are committed application assets, so a source change followed by runner preparation can produce a version-control diff. Review and include the appropriate generated outputs and notices when contributing frontend changes. Preparation state stays inside the extracted project under data/runner/frontend/<source-location-hash /state.json . Managed tools and npm/uv caches are also local to this installation. Dependency checks include the package files and selected Node/npm versions. Build checks include editable sources, the build script and hashes of generated outputs. The batch file requests an output manifest, including vendor notices, from build.cjs through its optional GRAVEWRIGHT_BUILD_MANIFEST process variable. A later launch skips a valid unchanged build; changed inputs or missing/modified outputs cause preparation again. A failed build stops launcher startup instead of serving an unverified frontend. collectstatic then copies the prepared public assets to the project-local data/staticfiles directory. The module domain-method registry has its own generation command: sh uv run --locked python scripts/generate_frontend_api.py This generates only modules/static/gravewright_modules/frontend-contract.js from contracts/frontend.json . The original SDK's generated.js and JSON schemas are separate artifacts; this script does not regenerate them. collectstatic gathers deployable assets but does not run either JavaScript build. Board layers and resource lifetimes The New scene chooser includes Empty map . Its form asks for the scene name, background color, width and height in pixels, whether to show the grid, and whether to activate it after creation. Creation uses the current folder. When activation is unchecked, the creator previews the new scene while players stay on the existing active scene. The server creates ordinary lossless map tiles within the configured image and tile-count limits, so existing rendering, permissions, tools and campaign archives continue to work. The GM scene directory shows player dots in each player's saved identification color and a GM badge on the scene currently being viewed. Dot tooltips identify players, including offline members whose destinations persist. The context menu's Activate for selected players opens a checkbox list for one or more players; Activate for players still activates for everyone and clears individual destinations. Changing identification color refreshes the dots without reloading. The GM badge also identifies a private preview; there is no additional Preparing label. Scene pointers show other participants as translucent colored dots with their names, using each sender's saved ping color. The user's own mouse keeps its native cursor. Remote motion is interpolated in scene coordinates and projected through the viewer's camera, preserving screen size through pan/zoom. Positions are transient, sampled at most ten times per second, and discarded when users leave, disconnect or change scene. A stationary pointer remains visible across delayed updates; silence alone is not a departure. Scene tool overlays publish positions just like the rendering surface, excluding interface controls. Switching browser windows or tabs pauses publication while preserving the last shared position. Only actual scene departures, disconnects and explicit hide packets remove it; losing window focus is not a departure. Preferences → Mouse pointers has independent controls for viewing participants' pointers and sharing one's own. Both default to enabled, persist per profile on the current device and synchronize across tabs. Hiding received pointers keeps their last positions available for immediate redisplay without rendering them. Disabling sharing immediately hides that user's pointer remotely and stops publication; it does not affect map pings or other participants' settings. The same house menu has a Keyboard shortcuts topic for the table's executable dock tools and windows, including campaign search. table/shortcuts.js derives the defaults from the rendered dock, records combinations in focused fields, updates accessible shortcuts/tooltips and dispatches the existing buttons. Mappings persist per profile/device under gravewright.shortcuts.<profile and synchronize across tabs. Each layer has its own tool scope; window bindings conflict across all layers. Existing default precedence is preserved. Users can unassign actions or restore all defaults. Escape cancels recording; text editing, composition, modal keyboard navigation and reserved browser/editing combinations retain their native behavior. Tool-specific gestures are not remapped here. These table additions use the installed Translator's English source-key contract: Jinja tr(...) , the native gwText(...) adapter and createTranslator().t(...) for browser-owned controls. Reviewed pt-BR/es host supplements cover new keys without changing installed signed language archives. Without an active language package, the host falls back to English and preserves the saved locale choice. Player names, scene names and authored measurement titles are marked translate="no" ; key combinations and action IDs also remain unchanged. The integration scenario tests/e2e/table_translator.py accepts an explicit GRAVEWRIGHT_TRANSLATOR_CATALOG_ROOT containing real en.json , pt-BR.json and es.json catalogs. It installs a disposable package and checks the new table controls, uploaded Smart Objects, circular areas, authored values and fallback. Only authorized viewers of the same scene receive positions. Streamers receive pointers without sending them, and the GM layer does not publish mouse movement. The table dock provides drawing through Mini Paint ( Draw , shortcut B ). Rectangles and ellipses belong to that editor; there is no separate Shapes tool or T shortcut. Existing shared area markers remain visible, and their stored data and public APIs remain compatible. Measure continues to provide local scene measurements. Enable Title to edit a measurement label directly on the map, above its dimensions. Each title follows its measurement through movement and zoom and stays visible when the tool closes. Titles share the same local lifetime as measurements; they are not broadcast or saved to the campaign. The maps/frontend/ tree separates entity models, feature models/UI, shared utilities, and the game-board widget. The board widget coordinates rendering, input, tile scheduling/cache/prefetch, native layers, vision polygons, lighting and shaders. Feature code contains walls, tokens, drawings, measurements, effects, and selection. Algorithm tests live beside the relevant models and are bundled by maps/scripts/test_models.cjs for Node's test runner. Use one consistent coordinate system across controllers and renderer calls: logical scene pixels, top-left origin, token centers as anchors. Camera pan/zoom converts scene positions into CSS viewport coordinates; device pixel ratio affects rendering resolution. Mixing these units causes selection, token and lighting misalignment. The extension overlay API exposes explicit conversion helpers instead of exposing the PixiJS renderer. Async work belongs to a page, board, module activation, or individual mount. Lifetime (../../gravewright/modules/static/gravewright_modules/lifetime.js) cancels API calls and disposes subscriptions; map source code has its own shared lifecycle helpers. Add/remove listeners and observers with their owner. Release rendering resources and pending work during board teardown or scene changes. A listener or cached API handle that outlives its owner can update the next scene with old data. Updates to the current scene preserve camera pan/zoom, token art and mounted layers, including revisions caused by teleport automation. Only a scene change resets the camera. Raster revisions refresh existing tile keys by URL and keep the previous decoded tiles visible until replacements are ready; superseded requests cannot paint an older revision. A failed replacement retains its current art while the bounded retry runs. Region occupancy and geometry refresh their own overlay, keeping unrelated floor, light and shader resources mounted. Token names, fallback initials and condition badges rasterize at a density matched to the camera zoom and renderer resolution. Power-of-two density bands, capped at eight, keep enlarged text sharp without regenerating textures during panning or within the same zoom band. External labels use centered sans-serif text with a thin outline and extra line spacing for conditions below the name. The browser scenario tests/e2e/token_text_resolution.py checks zoom, normal/dense displays, label updates and renderer disposal. Configure token lets the GM choose each bar's color and audience: everyone, owner and GM, or GM only. The server omits restricted bars from each recipient's token state. Existing sheet display flags remain the defaults until overridden. These settings belong to the scene token, survive duplication and do not change the system sheet schema. Bars keep their 5px gap above/below the token; the name and condition badges leave room for them. No numerical bar labels are added. The name can appear always, only on selection, only on hover, or on selection/hover (the compatibility default). A per-token switch controls the combat turn indicator: a static green outline for the current turn and a muted dashed outline for the next. tests/e2e/token_appearance.py checks native saves, recipient filtering, colors, turn indicators and the editor at desktop/mobile widths. Token acknowledgements and realtime snapshots can carry native teleports: {id, version} metadata, filtered against the recipient's visible tokens and their exact revisions. The token workspace remembers each accepted teleport revision across normal reads. It bypasses movement interpolation and recreates only that token's Pixi object at its destination; repeated delivery keeps the same replacement. Logical identity, selection and sheet data remain unchanged, and older asynchronous art loads cannot restore an earlier object. Successful token commands apply the authorized token snapshot in their acknowledgement. They do not issue another token GET or request scene layers; committed scene changes arrive through the existing realtime subscription. Failures and version conflicts still reload authoritative state. A movement with no displacement and no traversed path does not save or enter the busy state. Paths that leave and return to the same position remain real operations so region entry/exit automation is preserved. The token workspace saves silently, including when a confirmation takes longer. Pending commands keep the interaction guard for concurrent edits. Errors and route instructions remain immediate; there is no saving notice or notice timer. Unchanged status text is not rewritten on every paint. Local token previews reuse the static scene key and image reconciliation while their immutable scene inputs remain the same. They do not walk all native image transforms or reconstruct the component-origin index on every frame. A new image snapshot still reconciles its transforms and artwork; changed walls, effects, scene identity and role still invalidate their owning resources. Movement notifications refresh scene layers and tokens without rebuilding the unchanged actor directory or combat panel. Actor/combat edits and other token commands retain the relevant notifications. Paired layer/token notifications deliver spatial audio once through the token refresh; independent layer edits still refresh audio. Live authorization and extension change hooks remain in place. Same-scene teleport advances token revisions, not scene metadata or raster revisions. Its layer/token notifications carry region and appearance changes without requesting a new scene manifest or changing existing tile URLs. Repeated portals therefore retain the decoded floors and raster textures already loaded. Native image updates SceneImageArt reconciles ordinary image textures independently of the static scene key. A source change keeps the sprite and its previous art until the new texture is decoded; late results cannot overwrite newer state or a closed scene. Current art survives same-scene light/geometry rebuilds. Composed surfaces and grouped floors use a separate cache with the same lifecycle. Unchanged composites rebind synchronously during effect rebuilds; material replacement retains current art until decoding completes. Changed masks, geometry, group membership or visibility revoke obsolete coverage immediately. Composition closes all input bitmaps, including failed and cancelled loads, and publishes no partial floor. Each art cache retains at most eight idle textures and 16 MiB of idle decoded RGBA data, evicting the least recently used entries. Scene/role changes and disposal abort pending loads and release textures/bitmaps. Only art in the authorized projection is requested; inactive appearances are not prefetched. Token-art references wait for a pending unload of the same URL before loading again. Pixi's loader can otherwise return its old cached texture while unloading is about to destroy it. Independent URLs remain concurrent. Dispose applications with explicit removeView: true, releaseGlobalResources: false options: boolean true also releases process-wide pools still used by other boards and previews. Scene-owned textures and renderer resources still end with their owner. GM-private images and Empty Object markers remain visible at 55% opacity in all workspaces, with selection and interaction restricted to GM. Private drawings multiply their authored opacity by the same factor. Server projections still exclude private elements from player/streamer clients. Realtime delivery sends committed maps.layers and tokens.state before their dependent audio/combat refreshes. Every delivery retains its own authorization check. Token-triggered changes may share the same scene revision; never discard snapshots solely because that revision is equal. Lighting and vision work SceneLayers calculates light occlusion once for each static scene key and reuses those polygons for masks, the light atlas and the GM darkness veil. createVisibilityContext shares wall indices and keeps at most eight filtered subsets for finite ranges or elevation. Preserve the original ray arithmetic and wall membership: changing a BVH can change rounding at coincident endpoints. Torch and pulse frames update additive Pixi sprites over immutable falloff textures. Shaders receive a GPU render texture; only particles that respond to light request CPU samples, capped at eight samples per second. Profiles keep their existing animation rates. A scene owns the texture pool and releases it after shader bindings, the atlas and sprite layers. Vision changes coalesce once per animation frame. Scenes with at least 128 wall segments use the same-origin module worker emitted as vendor/visibility-worker.js ; smaller scenes and unavailable workers use the same geometry synchronously. The worker keeps one active job and the latest pending snapshot, transferring coordinate buffers. Native observers carry a sourceId so movement can retain the last completed view while the next calculation runs. Selection, range, elevation, cone and preview changes revoke that view immediately; wall and scene changes terminate the old worker. Never reuse visibility across those boundaries or quantize the configured vision range or token positions. Pending movement retains the existing veil texture until a result arrives; unrestricted GM vision reuses its static veil without repainting on token moves. Compare full frames and completed worker jobs when profiling. Queuing work is not completion, and headless software WebGL results do not establish hardware GPU performance. Rebuild both board and worker entries together with the normal asset build. Extending the interface The host's SurfaceRegistry (../../gravewright/modules/static/gravewright_modules/surface-registry.js) accepts gravewright.ui.register(domain, declaration) and returns an unregister function. It supports registered table surfaces plus app.shell and inside.content . A mount receives {root, context, api, signal, onDispose} . It gets a fresh lifetime and a dedicated root; failed mounts are cleaned up, and replaced native elements have their previous visibility restored. This global registry permits one replacement per domain. Installed signed packages use ModuleRuntime instead. Its registrations are synchronous during module activation, its calls carry module identity/lease/revision, and competing replacements are chosen using table preferences. Use the module's register callback for installed packages; global UI registration is for host-page integrations and has different ownership/selection rules. Full examples and supported names are in modules (modules.md). Frontend verification Run the checks affected by the source you changed: sh node --test tests/modules/ .test.mjs tests/effects/ .test.mjs npm test --prefix gravewright/maps/frontend uv run --locked python tests/e2e/frontend_api.py For rendering or interaction changes, use relevant scenarios under tests/e2e/ , including mixed_selection.py , token_routes.py , light_rendering.py , effect_geometry.py , effect_pixels.py , map_prefetch.py and realtime.py . The browser harness and dependencies are explained in testing (testing.md). Test player and GM sessions where behavior is permission-dependent, and check disposal/reconnect when adding subscriptions. Keep labels and message catalogs aligned with the application's supported languages.

title: Testing
summary: Django, node:test, Playwright and native validation with disposable data.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/testing.md) Run commands from the source root after uv sync --locked . The repository uses Django/unittest for Python, Node's built-in runner for JavaScript and standalone Playwright scripts for browser flows. There is no root npm test or configured pytest runner. Known Windows limitations - Windows limits paths to 260 characters. Map Builder scenarios install a fixture module under their output directory; a long --output path, such as one nested in the user's temporary folder, makes that installation fail with "Invalid module archive". Use the default output under data/ or another short path. - tests/e2e/escape_windows.py does not start its own server. It needs ownership_server.py on 127.0.0.1:30002 and data/permissions-review-seed.json from that fixture. Controlled local environment Tests load the project's .env unless a process variable overrides it. For local HTTP browser tests, use a shell with these settings rather than inheriting a production HTTPS origin or external Redis: bash export DJANGO_DEBUG=true export DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS='127.0.0.1,localhost, ::1 ,testserver' export GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN='' export DJANGO_SECURE_COOKIES=false export GRAVEWRIGHT_REDIS_URL='' export TRUSTED_PROXIES='' export GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_URL='' export GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_KEYS_FILE='' export GRAVEWRIGHT_RELEASES_REPOSITORY='' These are shell-local settings, not changes to .env . Browser fixtures normally override the database and media with temporary directories. Tests may override individual settings as part of a scenario. Python bash uv run --locked python manage.py check uv run --locked python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run uv run --locked python manage.py test config gravewright --noinput The runner uses the explicit file-backed data/test-gravewright.sqlite3 database to exercise SQLite locking. --noinput authorizes replacing that test database if it already exists. Do not point it at valuable data or run parallel suites against the same path. Changing GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE does not change this explicit test database name. Media-writing tests generally create temporary storage; use a disposable GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT for an extra boundary when running the full suite. Focused examples: bash uv run --locked python manage.py test config gravewright.accounts gravewright.realtime --noinput uv run --locked python manage.py test gravewright.table.tests.test_frontend_api gravewright.modules --noinput uv run --locked python manage.py test gravewright.dice --noinput Release checks for marketplace Django apps and managed updates also include: bash uv run --locked python tests/e2e/django_marketplace.py uv run --locked python tests/e2e/automatic_updates.py --runner These use isolated data and exercise dependency preparation, Django routes, migration failure recovery, preservation across core upgrades and .old rollback. JavaScript Use a current Node.js release with native ES modules and node:test ; these commands were checked with Node 24. No root package installation is needed for these tests. bash node --test tests/modules/ .test.mjs tests/effects/ .test.mjs For all colocated JavaScript tests as well, this Python launcher avoids shell-specific recursive globs: bash uv run --locked python - <<'PY' from pathlib import Path import subprocess files = sorted(str(p) for base in ('gravewright', 'tests') for p in Path(base).rglob(' ') if p.name.endswith(('.test.js', '.test.mjs'))) subprocess.run( 'node', '--test', files , check=True) PY Coverage includes module lifetimes and contracts, shader parsing, board input, tile scheduling, visibility, walls, selection, token routes and PDF field mapping. Pure geometry/model tests do not replace checking the actual GPU-rendered board. Module tests cover multipart card-image uploads from lifecycle contexts, activation leases, native permissions and cancelled operations. The Django gravewright.modules.test_card_assets suite also verifies image validation, asset reuse, table isolation and failed-upload cleanup. Browser scenarios uv run --locked python tests/e2e/door_rotation_anchor.py checks door pivot selection, rotation, Undo, opening/closing artwork, the shared wall editor and saved settings in English, Portuguese and Spanish at desktop and mobile widths. It uses an isolated campaign and accepts --output and --browser-executable . The campaign management scenario (../../tests/e2e/campaign_management.py) uses disposable campaign data to exercise native PDF sheets, diary and quest editors, co-GM access, denied requests and GM revocation. It checks that management opens no game WebSocket or table presence, comparing before/after snapshots of broadcast, private scene navigation and presence. It also checks English, Portuguese and Spanish at mobile widths, then opens the real table to verify shared documents, player filtering and audio playback in two clients. This describes the scenario's coverage, not the result of a particular run. bash uv run --locked python tests/e2e/campaign_management.py --output data/cm-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " Replace <existingChromium with an existing Chromium executable. Choose a new or empty output directory for each run; fixtures, logs, state comparisons and screenshots stay in that installation-local directory. The campaign preparation scenario (../../tests/e2e/campaign_preparation.py) uses the same disposable fixture to exercise the dashboard, the reference picker without a table connection, the session planner, the timeline and calendar, quest columns with prerequisites, connections, the player preview and restoring a journal from the trash, and checks phone-width layouts. Run it with the same --output and --browser-executable options as the scenario above. tests/e2e/campaign_preparation_regressions.py checks session draft preservation, editing during an in-flight save, asynchronous reference-picker errors and retry, stale comparisons during concurrent GM edits, private revision permissions and atomic rejection of a historical revision restore whose physical file is missing. It also checks the exact native error in English and its Portuguese/Spanish translations at 320px. Use a separate fresh output directory: uv run --locked python tests/e2e/campaign_preparation_regressions.py --output data/prep-regressions --browser-executable "<existingChromium " . gravewright.administration.test_preparation_archives covers preparation and history round trips, retained files, each GM's snapshot dashboard, old-archive compatibility, typed reference remapping, chronology and rejection of malformed metadata, conflicting asset owners and quest cycles. The progress-clock scenario (../../tests/e2e/clocks.py) uses isolated campaign fixtures to check shared clocks in management and the real table, realtime updates, player and streamer permissions, private and scene-scoped filtering, concurrent revisions, persistence and pinned display. It also checks English, Portuguese and Spanish at 320px and preserves management's broadcast, navigation and presence boundaries. Run it with uv run --locked python tests/e2e/clocks.py --output data/clocks-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " , using a fresh output directory. This describes coverage rather than a particular run's result. tests/e2e/map_builder_clocks.py checks native clock nodes, typed Amount wires, execution continuations, save/reload, and nonmutating server rehearsal with clock/receipt/media snapshots. It exercises player-triggered GM bindings, private-clock filtering, realtime pinned HUD changes and live node editing for advance, reduce, set and reset, plus English, Portuguese and Spanish at desktop and 320px. Use a fresh directory, for example uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_clocks.py --output data/mbclocks-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " . tests/e2e/clues.py covers one-step and progressive discoveries through the native campaign manager, table and MapBuilder editor. It checks undiscovered-record and GM-note filtering in player JSON, events and DOM; reveal/hide, permissions, revisions, receipt retries, persistence, scene scope, pinned displays and a nonmutating server rehearsal. Native clue nodes exercise typed numeric inputs, execution continuations and live advance/reduce/set/reset/reveal/hide actions. English, Portuguese and Spanish are checked with long authored content at 320px and desktop widths. Run with a fresh installation-local output directory: uv run --locked python tests/e2e/clues.py --output data/clues-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " . tests/e2e/progress_hud.py (../../tests/e2e/progress_hud.py) checks transparent clock/clue cards and empty segments, minimal pinned displays, direct left/right progress controls, permissions and independent local positioning with multiple real clients. Double-clicking a name opens the native editor for GMs and a read-only description for players/streamers. Long and empty descriptions and revoked access during pending reads exercise modal lifetime and privacy. It compares requests, socket frames and persisted campaign state to verify moving an indicator does not publish a campaign change, then checks saved positions after reload and English/Portuguese/Spanish layouts at 320px. Use a fresh output: uv run --locked python tests/e2e/progress_hud.py --output data/progress-hud-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " . This describes the scenario's coverage, not the outcome of a particular run. Journal reference validation and portable identity remapping use the owning domain suites and the shared resource registry: bash uv run --locked python manage.py test gravewright.journals gravewright.table.tests.test_journal_resource_api gravewright.administration.test_journal_resource_archives --noinput node --test tests/modules/journal-resource-links.test.mjs tests/modules/mindmaps-ui.test.mjs uv run --locked python tests/e2e/journal_resource_links.py --output data/journal-links-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " The browser scenario inserts typed references with @ in the native journal editor, reopens saved links, exercises table and management access, checks hidden-target preservation and permission changes during pending reads, and reviews translated desktop/320px layouts with synthetic resources. Use fresh local output and independent fixture databases. These commands describe coverage, not a completed release validation. It also checks cancellation, email boundaries, slash blocks, replacement of the captured trigger range and translated empty-editor hints. The journal chapter scenario (../../tests/e2e/journal_chapters.py) exercises empty chapters, nested hierarchies, moving pages, renaming and reparenting, deletion without page loss, older category groups and retained resource links. It checks native campaign management and table clients, player filtering and owner saves that preserve omitted private structure, then inspects English, Portuguese and Spanish at desktop and 320px, including eight nested levels. Use a fresh isolated output: uv run --locked python tests/e2e/journal_chapters.py --output data/journal-chapters-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " . This describes scenario coverage, not the result of a particular run. Mind-map graph, access, redacted-link, resource projection, archive and Blueprint checks use the owning suites: bash uv run --locked python manage.py test gravewright.table.tests.test_mindmaps gravewright.table.tests.test_resource_links gravewright.table.tests.test_mindmap_review gravewright.administration.test_mindmap_archives gravewright.maps.tests.test_blueprint_mindmaps --noinput node --test tests/modules/mindmap-model.test.mjs tests/modules/mindmaps-ui.test.mjs uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_mindmaps.py --output data/mindmaps-builder-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " The isolated Builder scenario authors both mind-map nodes, saves/reopens their bindings, checks rehearsal rollback and committed completion, and verifies that open requests reach only authorized recipients. Responsive translated editors use synthetic topics. These commands describe coverage rather than a release validation result; keep each run's fixtures and output separate. tests/e2e/mindmaps.py (../../tests/e2e/mindmaps.py) exercises the native manager and tabletop with a GM, selected player editor, ordinary reader and streamer. It covers graph authoring, real pointer/keyboard input, local undo/redo, saving, concurrent revisions and preserved drafts. Live link revocation must redact identities without losing unrelated edits, including newly linked unsaved resources. Native close/confirmation modals retain focus and drafts on cancel. English, Portuguese and Spanish layouts are checked at 320px with authored text preserved. Run in a new installation-local output directory: uv run --locked python tests/e2e/mindmaps.py --output data/mindmaps-check --browser-executable "<existingChromium " . It also checks that loading drops removed event graphs without removing elements or assets. The fixture isolates campaign, database, media, port and output with synthetic artwork. Server tests in gravewright.maps.tests.test_blueprint_state_sprite exercise explicit state and image actions, snapshot-based conditions and retry receipts. The current server event contract is covered by test_blueprint_events , test_blueprint_base_events and test_blueprint_references . Their fixtures use starting events and explicit state/condition nodes; cross-element execution uses named signals. Coverage includes discarded retired graphs, active-graph UUID and type validation, lock permissions, bounded chains, full rollback and retry receipts. test_blueprint_testing also verifies that a GM can rehearse a paused scene without changing its stored pause flag: normal actions, destruction and unexpected failures leave gameplay paused and produce no committed effects. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_object_areas.py checks object, torch and Empty Object area-event ports, local simulation, rolled-back rehearsal, authorized player token crossings and private occupancy. It inspects rotated bounds and full pass-through movements, with desktop and localized narrow layouts. Server suites test_object_areas and test_object_area_integration cover per-token events, explicit actions, pause, blocked moves, geometry edits, scene updates, imports, occupancy counts, listener limits and atomic rollback. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_target_connections.py checks wiring an Empty Object's area action to other objects through Target , dragging in either direction at different zoom levels, compatible producer selection, keyboard and cancellation, autosave, server rehearsal and committed token entry. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_area_live_sync.py checks an Empty Object explicitly interacting with a lever that owns state, image and light actions. A player drags a token in, out and back in; pushed states, interaction controls, rendered image pixels and light state update on both live GM and player boards without reloading. The fixture also distinguishes project autosave from applying a new exit graph with Update scene . test_blueprint_interact_action covers native and authored targets, typed groups, torch components, lock rules, bounded chains, rollback, retries, rehearsal and delayed token context. The finite Smart Object combination matrix is checked at three layers: - tests/fixtures/map_builder_connections.json defines 28 value producers and 38 consumer variants, including nodes without a Target input. Both gravewright.maps.tests.test_blueprint_connection_matrix and builder/blueprint-connection-matrix.test.mjs check all 1,064 pairs against the same expected types. They also require every registered value port to appear in the fixture. Rejected connections preserve the graph; accepted connections survive full validation and reject a second incoming value wire. - gravewright.maps.tests.test_blueprint_action_matrix checks 362 action, target-kind and reference/group cases, including all writable states, native versus authored interaction, lights, sounds, missing/foreign references and mixed groups. It asserts effects and separate applied, missing and unsupported target identities. test_blueprint_event_matrix checks 387 owner/event/state, control, permission, pause, audience, timer/delay and two-token presence cases. Events only start flows; state changes do not implicitly run another object's interaction graph. - uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_combination_matrix.py exercises 131 real browser cases: typed references/groups in both wiring directions, forward/reverse node creation, Boolean/number/text adapters, logic composition, event capabilities, unavailable resources, cancellation, atomic undo, autosave, reload and same-scene update. A server rehearsal identifies an existing unsupported target by name. It uses synthetic assets and the shared isolated campaign, database, media, port, output and browser fixture. These matrices cover the enumerated contracts, not every possible authored graph. Run the existing behavior suites above as well for longer execution chains and live GM/player synchronization. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_sprite_targets.py checks the full node catalog on doors, levers, torches, Empty Objects and regions. It authors an Empty Object's area entry/exit directly into Change sprite with an ordinary image connected to Target , without a target interaction graph. Real player token movement checks the received image and rendered pixels in both GM and player browsers, plus autosave/reload, reference remapping, same-scene updates, native move/resize and restoration. Manual native geometry retains the update conflict guard. It uses the shared disposable fixture and synthetic artwork. gravewright.maps.tests.test_blueprint_sprite_targets covers typed references and groups, every owner kind and visual mode, private base-image restoration, native edits, resource deletion, archive remapping/validation, rollback and receipt retries. builder/blueprint-sprite-targets.test.mjs checks the shared catalog and image-resource contracts; the connection matrix includes sprite's typed Target input. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_gm_layers.py verifies that Empty Objects are editable only on GM, public images can move to GM and return through their context menus, and hidden controllers still trigger area actions from real player token drags. It checks ordinary images, levers, torches and live sprite overrides on both boards, private payloads, generation, source updates and reload. gravewright.maps.tests.test_empty_gm_layer checks native routing, legacy read privacy, player command rejection, linked update compatibility and unchanged manual-geometry conflict protection. Image-layer and interaction model tests check workspace selection, mixed selections and stale keyboard controls. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_element_names.py checks all eight element name fields, automatic saving, reopening, Undo/Redo, duplication and reference labels. It creates Empty Objects and regions directly from the library tool strip, checks keyboard access and localized desktop/390/320 px layouts, and generates/updates the linked scene without replacing identities or target UUIDs. gravewright.maps.tests.test_builder_element_names covers validation, Unicode, unnamed legacy rows, native edits, dynamic surfaces and atomic failed writes. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_event_latency.py measures real token-area entry/exit and direct interaction against a scene with 52 synthetic images in GM/player clients. It records mouse release or interaction through the first matching rendered WebGL pixel, socket acknowledgements/projections and image fetch/decode/upload counts. Screenshot polling is outside the timed interval. Compare runs on the same host and fixture; timings are observations, not pass/fail thresholds. The scenario also checks faint GM-only Empty markers, art and drawings across tabs, GM-only editing and player payload privacy. Use the usual fresh --output and --browser-executable options. Image-art model tests cover reuse, bounded eviction, failures, stale results and disposal; gravewright.realtime.tests.test_scene_update_priority covers real socket delivery before blocked audio, post-commit ordering and live authorization. gravewright.maps.tests.test_blueprint_performance measures real domain commands with synthetic data. It checks bounded inventory queries, projected token paths, state/image/light effects, fresh asset metadata and ownership on the next command, cleanup after errors and one history notification after commit. To record SQL counts and timings, set GRAVEWRIGHT_EVENT_BENCHMARK_OUTPUT to an explicit JSON file under an installation-local test directory and run that suite with the disposable test database/media configuration above. Normal tests run one sample; benchmark mode runs five eight-object chains and three sixteen-area entries. Each sample uses a new receipt UUID and rolls back afterward; effect assertions run outside the timed interval. The interval includes authorization, receipts, SQL and synchronous serialization, excluding the outer transaction's disk flush, network delivery and browser rendering. On the measured synthetic fixture, SQL counts changed from 101 to 42 for the chain and from 286 to 174 for area entry. Timings depend on the host and are not pass/fail thresholds. uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_blueprints.py checks the door's Smart object modal, draft cancellation, connections, local simulation, undo, saved projects and localized mobile layouts. It also opens GM and player clients to verify native state, active artwork, light and audio synchronization, retries, locked-door permissions, the GM Automation window, scene updates and image cleanup. It uses the same isolated output/browser options. Python validation and compatibility checks are in test_blueprints , test_blueprint_data_nodes , test_automation_runs , test_blueprint_references , test_builder_blueprints and test_blueprint_compatibility under gravewright.maps.tests ; editor graph tests run with node --test gravewright/maps/static/gravewright_maps/builder/blueprint-model.test.mjs . uv run --locked python tests/e2e/map_builder_levers.py checks enabling lever behavior, its two-state editor and object images, references and simulation, saved/reopened projects, localized desktop/mobile layouts, generation and an actual player double-click unlocking a door. It checks active-image projection and the private Automation log using isolated state and synthetic assets. gravewright.maps.tests.test_levers covers native interaction, retries, bounded chains and rollback, roles, updates, image deletion and campaign archives. tests/e2e/map_builder_blueprint_assets.py focuses on state-only image type guards, saved volume precision and native copying without a base door image. tests/e2e/map_builder_instance_nodes.py checks two real door-instance nodes, their labeled verb ports, separate state appearance, native state and draft isolation, unchanged legacy saves, explicit conversion after editing, and localized keyboard/mobile layouts. It uses the same isolated output and browser options. tests/e2e/map_builder_drag_connections.py exercises real mouse and touch cable dragging, the node chooser at the drop point, direct input connections, multiple branches, typed value wires, cancellation and cycle rejection. It checks saved/reloaded connections, placement with zoom and panning, and localized mobile layouts. It uses the same isolated output and browser options. Some scenarios accept --original /path/to/reference for optional pixel comparisons against another checkout's dist/frontend . That checkout is not needed for ordinary smoke tests. reference_tokens.cjs is an auxiliary comparison tool, not part of the root Node unit command. tests/e2e/https.py (../../tests/e2e/https.py) runs the installed Daphne with direct TLS and behind a temporary TLS proxy. It checks browser account setup, Secure __Host- cookies, HSTS, CSRF rejection, authenticated WSS join/chat and page reload. Raw TLS handshakes check rejection of missing, foreign, HTTP and wrong-port WebSocket origins. The scenario generates temporary certificates and uses isolated database/media paths, production security settings, a test-only static handler and an in-memory channel layer. It needs the locked Python dependencies and Playwright Chromium above; no external Redis or Nginx is required. It leaves the system certificate store and application data untouched and writes diagnostics to test-results/https/ . This tests the application transport contract; verify your deployed Nginx configuration and certificate separately using the deployment guide (deployment.md). tests/e2e/realtime_processes.py specifically starts a temporary redis:7-alpine Docker container and two ASGI processes. It requires Docker access and network/image availability; it cleans up its own container. It is separate from the default Django/Node suites. Windows runner validation tests/e2e/runner.py (../../tests/e2e/runner.py) starts the actual Python runner with temporary personal data and no Redis. It checks first-time setup, collected static assets, HTTP security, authenticated messages between two WebSocket sessions, occupied-port rejection and restart persistence of the configuration, session, campaign, chat and media. It checks that the project .env is preserved across restarts and existing development data remain unchanged. The scenario needs the development dependencies and Playwright Chromium above; ordinary runner startup does not. config/test_frontend_preparation.py (../../config/test_frontend_preparation.py) covers dependency reuse/installation, source and output changes, missing packages or a broken esbuild executable, failed-build retries, corrupt state and concurrent preparation. It also checks the batch --plan / --record handoff, incomplete dependencies and invalid manifests without running npm installation/build in those helper modes. These controlled subprocess tests belong to the normal Django suite and do not replace an actual npm build. Run the focused suite with uv run --locked python manage.py test config.test_frontend_preparation --noinput . The Windows workflow (../../.github/workflows/windows-runner.yml) uses CMD to run tests/windows/runner.py (../../tests/windows/runner.py). On any operating system, its source check verifies that obsolete launcher scripts and references are absent: sh python tests/windows/runner.py --source-check On Windows, run the complete native scenario from the source root: bat python tests\windows\runner.py The scenario creates a temporary checkout with spaces, punctuation and Unicode in its path and runs the actual BAT without a data-directory override. Managed uv, Python, Node/npm, caches and temporary files stay under the project's data/runner/ ; state and logs stay under data/ . A fake legacy AppData profile contains another installation's active pointer, and snapshots verify it remains unchanged. Repeated offline installation also ignores compatible external PATH tools. The test reads the icon shortcut through Windows COM, checks that an invalid port fails without pausing, and verifies creation and reuse of .env , preservation of .venv , Python/npm locks, saved configuration and user/machine/parent-process PATH . Generated frontend outputs are prepared only in the disposable checkout. The same scenario runs the frontend preparation unit tests and the real Python server scenario in Chromium. --skip-browser omits installation of the browser-test dependencies and the browser scenario while keeping the batch checks. Diagnostics are saved under test-results/windows-runner/ . The temporary source, environment and campaign data are cleaned up when the scenario finishes. Use "Install Windows.bat" --check --no-pause --data-dir "<temporary-data-directory " for a manual batch preparation check that exits without serving requests. This still installs missing dependencies, builds assets when needed and applies migrations. Workflow presence does not mean its jobs have already passed for a release; --source-check alone does not validate native batch execution. Before publishing a Windows build, run that workflow and check a normal double-click launch, automatic browser opening, Ctrl+C and closing the console on a Windows computer. The runner guide (windows-runner.md) describes diagnostic mode with an isolated data directory. Tests run on Linux or another operating system verify the Python runtime there, not native Windows CMD or shortcut behavior. When reporting results, name the commands, versions and failures. A browser scenario that could not launch is not a passing test.

title: Configuration
summary: Installation-local configuration, execution profiles and environment settings.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/configuration.md) Loading and validation The source of truth is config/environment.py (../../config/environment.py), config/engine.py (../../config/engine.py), config/settings.py (../../config/settings.py) and .env.example (../../.env.example). Settings load once at process startup. Exported variables take precedence over .env ; interpolation is disabled, so ${VALUE} remains literal. Relative paths resolve against the source root; ~ expands to the service user's home. Booleans accept 1/true/yes/y/on and 0/false/no/n/off , case-insensitively. Invalid spellings fail startup. Engine numeric limits must be positive. Join-code minimum ≤ default ≤ maximum, and viewport area cannot exceed width × height. GRAVEWRIGHT_PORT must be 1–65535. Public origins normalize the scheme and hostname to lowercase, preserving explicit ports and IPv6 brackets; HTTPS://VTT.EXAMPLE.COM therefore enables the same HTTPS settings as https://vtt.example.com . They reject paths, trailing slashes, credentials, empty ports, control characters, query strings and fragments, including empty ? or delimiters. These validations do not imply that every setting has the same numeric parser or upper bound. The native Runner for Windows (windows-runner.md), Linux (linux-runner.md) and macOS (macos-runner.md) reads defaults from .env.example , then .env in the project root, with local security settings enforced by its dedicated profile. If the project .env is missing, it generates a complete configuration from .env.example with a new private secret. It never imports configuration from user-data directories. The reference below describes the standard server settings; feature settings also apply to the Runner, while its bind address, debug, cookies, host/origin, proxy trust and single-process Channels choices are fixed for local execution. Set the Runner's port in the project .env . Environment reference Values below match the sample/default configuration. An empty cell shown as “empty” means no configured value. Byte values use binary units in explanations. Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- GRAVEWRIGHT_HOST 127.0.0.1 Launcher bind address; main.py only GRAVEWRIGHT_PORT 3000 Launcher port, 1–65535; main.py only DJANGO_DEBUG true Django debug mode; false requires private secret and Redis in standard server settings DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS 127.0.0.1,localhost, ::1 Comma-separated hosts, without scheme or port GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN empty Public HTTP(S) origin; pins the WebSocket origin/Host including port, adds host and CSRF trusted origin, enables Secure cookies for HTTPS GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE data/gravewright.sqlite3 SQLite filename; relative to source root; :memory: is supported GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT data/media Private upload/module storage, relative to source root GRAVEWRIGHT_CONTENT_ROOT data/vtt/compendiums Disk content collections in standard server settings; the Runner uses its state directory's compendiums/ GRAVEWRIGHT_MODULES_ROOT GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT/modules Private folder where module ZIP archives and extracted packages are installed; may be absolute or source-root-relative GRAVEWRIGHT_API_MODULES_ROOT extensions/api Default folder for browser module sources, relative to source root; installed signed packages still live under the media root GRAVEWRIGHT_DJANGO_MODULES_ROOT extensions/django Default folder for trusted Django apps, relative to source root; appended to sys.path when it exists GRAVEWRIGHT_SERVER_APPS empty Comma-separated import paths of trusted Django apps added to INSTALLED_APPS GRAVEWRIGHT_SERVER_APP_PATHS empty Extra package roots for those apps ( : on Linux/macOS, ; on Windows); they precede the default Django folder GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTH_MAX_ATTEMPTS 30 Authentication attempts per client-IP window GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTH_WINDOW_SECONDS 300 Authentication window in seconds GRAVEWRIGHT_REDIS_URL empty Channels Redis URL; standard server settings allow empty/in-memory delivery only in debug APP_NAME Gravewright Fallback product name; persisted host preferences can override DEFAULT_LOCALE en Fallback locale; additional languages require an installed, enabled language package PRIVACY_ENABLED false Initial privacy publication setting; the saved Privacy checkbox takes precedence CAMPAIGN_JOIN_CODE_ENABLED true Enable campaign join-code workflow CAMPAIGN_CLONE_ENABLED true Enable campaign cloning CAMPAIGN_SNAPSHOTS_ENABLED true Enable campaign snapshots CAMPAIGN_SNAPSHOT_RETENTION 20 Maximum retained snapshots per campaign; pruned during snapshot creation ADMINISTRATIVE_AUDIT_ENABLED true Enable administrative audit records ADMINISTRATIVE_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS 180 Audit retention in days; pruning occurs when audit code runs TARGETED_HANDOUTS_ENABLED true Enable targeted journal/handout sharing CAMPAIGN_EXPORT_ENABLED true Enable portable campaign exports JOIN_CODE_DEFAULT_EXPIRES_HOURS 168 Default join-code lifetime in hours JOIN_CODE_MIN_EXPIRES_HOURS 1 Minimum requested join-code lifetime in hours JOIN_CODE_MAX_EXPIRES_HOURS 720 Maximum requested join-code lifetime in hours JOIN_CODE_MAX_USES_LIMIT 1000 Upper limit for a join code's allowed uses JOIN_CODE_REDEEM_MAX_ATTEMPTS 10 Maximum code redemption attempts per window JOIN_CODE_REDEEM_WINDOW_SECONDS 600 Code redemption attempt window in seconds TRUSTED_PROXIES empty Comma-separated proxy IPs/CIDRs trusted for forwarded client IPs and ASGI HTTP/WebSocket schemes; empty ignores forwarding headers DATABASE_POOL_TIMEOUT 30 SQLite lock wait in seconds; this is not a connection pool size DATABASE_ECHO false Configure django.db.backends debug logging; actual SQL capture also follows Django's debug cursor behavior WS_MAX_MESSAGE_MB 0.0625 Application limit per WebSocket message in MB (1 MB = 1024 1024 bytes) WS_COMMANDS_PER_SECOND 20 WebSocket command rate per connection WS_BURST_COMMANDS 40 WebSocket command burst capacity APP_DEBUG false Application/table renderer diagnostics; independent of DJANGO_DEBUG COMMAND_PALETTE_ENABLED true Enable the table command palette LOBBY_READY_CHECK_ENABLED true Enable lobby readiness controls DYNAMIC_LIGHTING_ENABLED true Enable dynamic-lighting feature GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTOMATION_WORKER_ENABLED true Run the ASGI background worker for persistent Blueprint Delay continuations; false leaves pending waits stored without executing them SCENE_VIEWPORT_MAX_WIDTH_CHUNKS 16 Maximum streamed viewport width in chunks SCENE_VIEWPORT_MAX_HEIGHT_CHUNKS 16 Maximum streamed viewport height in chunks SCENE_VIEWPORT_MAX_AREA_CHUNKS 256 Maximum streamed viewport area in chunks FOG_MAX_OPS_PER_COMMAND 64 Maximum fog operations per command FOG_MAX_POLYGON_POINTS 128 Maximum points per fog polygon FOG_MAX_COORDINATE_ABS 100000 Maximum absolute fog coordinate FOG_REQUIRE_EXPECTED_VERSION true Require expected scene-state version for fog changes TOKEN_CREATE_MANY_MAX 50 Maximum tokens per batch creation command BOARD_MARKERS_MAX_PER_SCENE 500 Maximum markers per scene BOARD_MEASUREMENTS_MAX_PER_USER 50 Maximum persisted board measurements per user JOURNAL_IMAGE_MAX_MB 10 Journal image attachment limit in MB (1 MB = 1024 1024 bytes) JOURNAL_PDF_MAX_MB 25 Journal PDF attachment limit in MB (1 MB = 1024 1024 bytes) PDF_SYSTEM_UPLOAD_MAX_MB 10 PDF character sheet upload limit in MB (1 MB = 1024 1024 bytes) GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_MAX_PIXELS 64000000 Decoded map pixel limit GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_PILLOW_MAX_PIXELS 64000000 Additional decoded-pixel ceiling when using the Pillow tiler GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER auto Map tiler: auto , vips or pillow MAP_UPLOAD_MAX_MB 51200 Map upload limit in MB (50 GiB); other limits still apply MAP_IMAGE_MAX_WIDTH 500000 Maximum source map width in pixels MAP_IMAGE_MAX_HEIGHT 500000 Maximum source map height in pixels MAP_MAX_TILE_COUNT 4096 Maximum generated map tiles GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_URL empty HTTPS URL of the module catalog JSON GRAVEWRIGHT_MARKETPLACE_KEYS_FILE empty Local Ed25519 trust-key JSON path; relative to source root GRAVEWRIGHT_RELEASES_REPOSITORY Gravewright/gravewright owner/repo used for compatible Django release discovery; empty leaves it unconfigured The native installer configures the official Marketplace automatically when no catalog is configured. Existing custom catalogs are preserved. Two optional commented settings are also recognized: Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- DJANGO_SECRET_KEY Development-only insecure fallback Set a persistent random private value outside debug mode; do not use the fallback in production DJANGO_SECURE_COOKIES false Enable secure cookies; a configured HTTPS public origin always enables them. This flag does not configure TLS or the WebSocket origin GRAVEWRIGHT_CONTAINER is read by release discovery to label the install format when set to 1 , true or yes ; it does not configure a container runtime or provide automatic updates. DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE selects the Python settings module; entry points default to config.settings . Blueprint Delay worker The ASGI host starts the Delay worker automatically. Daphne uses its reactor startup/shutdown hooks, including normal Runner execution; other ASGI hosts must deliver lifespan startup/shutdown events. Importing Django or running a management command does not start a scheduler. The worker checks due database rows every 250 ms, processing at most 20 per pass; actual execution can be later under load or after downtime. It does not require connected browsers, HTTP polling, Redis jobs or a separately launched process. Pending waits live in the configured SQLite database and survive a server restart. GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTOMATION_WORKER_ENABLED=false disables processing for that process without discarding the queue. Scene-level Pause automation instead holds only that scene's waits until resume. The updater's existing managed maintenance flag holds the queue through health verification until the update is committed or rolled back. Apply the normal migrations before starting the host; the worker reports database failures in server logs and retries, rather than treating them as successful executions. See Persistent Delay (map-builder.md persistent-delay) for cancellation and copying. Map tiling and large images GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_MAX_PIXELS is the exact map pixel limit. At startup, Pillow's header guard is raised to at least that configured value so it does not impose an unrelated lower limit. Exceeding either pixel guard reports a pixel-limit error. The independent byte, dimension and tile-count limits still apply. Both pixel settings must be positive; restart the server after changing them. GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER=auto uses libvips when available and otherwise uses Pillow. pillow always selects Pillow; vips requires libvips and fails startup when it is unavailable. The default dependencies and native installers do not select the optional vips extra. For a source environment, install it with: bash uv sync --locked --extra vips For a native Runner, install into the Python environment named by its generated launcher; the checkout's .venv may be a different environment. Keep --extra vips on subsequent dependency syncs. A plain exact uv sync , a native reinstall or preparation for a managed core update selects the default dependencies and can remove or omit the extra. Check availability again after those operations; setting GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER=vips does not install dependencies. Pillow decodes the entire map. Its additional GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_PILLOW_MAX_PIXELS ceiling defaults to 64 million pixels, even if the overall map limit is higher. A larger image requires libvips or an explicit increase to that ceiling after assessing available memory. This pixel ceiling bounds accepted image size, not resident memory: decoding, orientation, resampling and codecs also allocate memory. Libvips streams ordinary maps in strips, but formats, codecs and EXIF rotations can require additional memory and temporary disk space. Only one map pyramid is generated at a time per server process, including decoding. Separate workers can still process maps concurrently. Both engines produce lossless WebP tiles with the same 512-pixel layout and partial edge tiles; reduced levels can differ because the resampling filters differ. Native tiling stages the source image and generated tiles under installation-root data/runner/tmp/ . An explicit GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT changes the tool root, and a Django FILE_UPLOAD_TEMP_DIR override takes precedence for tiling scratch space; relative paths resolve against the installation root. The directory must be writable and have room for the source, staged tiles and any codec spill files while final tiles are saved to media storage. Storage or native generation failures remain server errors, and already saved tiles are removed if the upload fails. See deployment (deployment.md) for synchronous upload timeouts and capacity planning. Settings without environment switches The following are configured in Python, not loaded automatically from similarly named .env entries: Setting Current behavior --- --- DATABASES.default.TEST.NAME data/test-gravewright.sqlite3 , regardless of GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE GRAVEWRIGHT_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS / GRAVEWRIGHT_PRESENCE_TTL 5-second heartbeat / 20-second presence TTL DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE 8 MiB for Django request-data handling; not a universal uploaded-file byte cap SESSION_COOKIE_AGE 12 hours; session data is stored in the database TIME_ZONE America/Sao_Paulo , with timezone-aware datetimes STATIC_ROOT Source-root staticfiles/ ; the Runner uses its state directory's staticfiles/ MAILERS.default Console email backend Authentication bodies are separately limited to 16 KiB in middleware. Archive imports/exports have limits in gravewright/administration/archives.py . Map uploads have independent byte, decoded-image and generated-tile bounds. Check the owning code before assuming one limit governs every path. Persisted host preferences gravewright.administration.preferences stores app identity, update channels and privacy content in the HostSettings singleton. APP_NAME and DEFAULT_LOCALE provide fallbacks, not forced overrides of every saved value. English is built in; the available locale list comes from installed, globally enabled, compatible language packages. The native installer installs and activates the official Translator when pt-BR is selected. Setting DEFAULT_LOCALE=pt-BR alone in a manual source installation does not install it. Existing user language choices take precedence over host defaults. Privacy publication is enabled when either the environment flag or the stored privacy flag is true. Snapshot/audit retention is enforced by the relevant operation paths, not a background scheduler supplied by this project. User preferences and campaign settings are separate from these host settings. For HTTPS, set the exact browser-facing public origin, including any non-default port. Other entries in DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS do not become additional permitted WebSocket origins when a public origin is configured. Without it, WebSocket validation derives the origin from the ASGI scheme and Host; an absent scheme defaults to HTTP. The ASGI proxy adapter (../../config/proxy.py) accepts exactly one X-Forwarded-Proto header with value http or https only from the immediate socket peer in TRUSTED_PROXIES . It ignores duplicate, comma-separated, malformed or untrusted values. Keep Daphne's --proxy-headers disabled so the original peer remains available for this check. The same trust list controls client-IP forwarding (../../gravewright/accounts/client_ip.py). See deployment (deployment.md) for a TLS proxy example, Redis and storage requirements. Installation-local Runner storage Default state remains inside the extracted project: data/ for logs, locks, collected assets and content collections; data/runner/ for managed tools, environments, caches and temporary files; data/updates/ for update transactions and recovery. The installer, Runner and main.py configure their child-process storage before launching tools. No default selects configuration or an active release from AppData, HOME, XDG or macOS Library directories. Runner --data-dir selects its state directory, including compendiums/ and staticfiles/ ; it does not relocate database or uploaded media. Set their explicit environment paths in project .env . An explicit GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT selects managed tool/cache storage. Relative overrides resolve from the installation root. A non-writable directory is an error rather than a request to fall back to a shared user directory. For manual shell commands, configure local tool storage (upgrading.md local-tool-storage) before invoking uv or npm.

title: Deployment
summary: Hosting, security, reverse proxies, backups and operational recovery.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/deployment.md) This guide covers server deployments. For local play, use the separate Gravewright Runner for Windows (windows-runner.md), Linux (linux-runner.md) or macOS (macos-runner.md), which manages installation-local storage and a single-process local profile. Before upgrading to 0.3.2 , follow the upgrade and recovery guide (upgrading.md). HTTPS and WebSockets Gravewright supports HTTPS pages and secure WebSockets (WSS). Set GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN to the browser-facing origin, such as https://vtt.example.com . SameOriginWebSocketMiddleware (../../gravewright/realtime/security.py) uses that configured origin to validate the browser's Origin and the request's Host , including the effective port. This also works with Daphne 4.2.3 , whose WebSocket scope omits scheme . Behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy, TrustedProxySchemeMiddleware (../../config/proxy.py) restores the HTTP/HTTPS or WS/WSS scheme before the ASGI router handles the request. It accepts exactly one X-Forwarded-Proto: http or https header only when the socket peer belongs to TRUSTED_PROXIES . Untrusted, duplicate, comma-separated or malformed values leave the original scheme unchanged. This lets Django correctly recognize HTTPS for CSRF checks and HSTS responses. The public origin is an allowlist, not a TLS listener or permission grant. Table WebSockets still require an allowed host, one valid matching browser origin, a valid session and campaign authorization. With no configured public origin, WebSocket checks use the ASGI ws / wss scheme; an omitted scheme defaults to local HTTP. Direct TLS with Daphne therefore requires the public HTTPS origin. DJANGO_SECURE_COOKIES=true alone does not supply it. Runtime configuration Run from a versioned source checkout as an account that can write the configured database and private storage. Use a persistent, private DJANGO_SECRET_KEY , DJANGO_DEBUG=false , an explicit allowed-host list, the intended public origin and a Redis URL. A public origin must be an HTTP(S) origin with no path or trailing slash. HTTPS enables secure session/CSRF cookies and HSTS in settings. Before invoking uv, configure installation-local tool storage (upgrading.md local-tool-storage) in the same shell. Generate a secret locally and put it in protected configuration, preserving it across restarts: bash uv run --locked python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(64))' Do not paste the generated value into an issue, commit or shared log. See configuration (configuration.md) for limits, paths and environment precedence. bash uv sync --locked --no-dev uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py migrate --noinput uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py collectstatic --noinput uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py check --deploy uv run --locked --no-dev daphne -b 127.0.0.1 -p 3000 config.asgi:application These commands assume production values have already been set and storage directories exist. check --deploy can report settings requiring an operator decision; verify the public endpoint as described below as well. The last command binds plain HTTP to loopback behind the TLS proxy. Normal main.py execution starts the managed supervisor and Daphne; main.py --dev invokes Django's development runserver . Direct Daphne execution above leaves process supervision and upgrades to the operator. config.wsgi cannot serve WebSockets. Nginx reverse proxy For Nginx and Daphne on the same host, configure these values in protected application configuration, together with your private DJANGO_SECRET_KEY : dotenv DJANGO_DEBUG=false DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=vtt.example.com GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://vtt.example.com TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1/32 GRAVEWRIGHT_REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0 Use the loopback Daphne command above without --proxy-headers . That option rewrites the socket peer before Gravewright checks it and conflicts with application-managed proxy trust. TRUSTED_PROXIES controls both forwarded client-IP resolution and the ASGI scheme adapter. Trust only the proxy addresses that can connect to Daphne; keep its upstream port private. In a container topology, replace loopback with the actual immediate proxy address or a narrowly scoped trusted network. The following Nginx example belongs inside its http context. Replace the domain, existing certificate/key files and absolute checkout path before enabling it. The 100 MiB request-body limit is an example operational limit; size it for your uploads and server capacity. The TLS directives and WebSocket upgrade handling follow the Nginx HTTPS guide (https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/configuring_https_servers.html) and WebSocket proxy guide (https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/websocket.html). nginx map $http_upgrade $gravewright_connection_upgrade { default upgrade; '' close; } server { listen 80; server_name vtt.example.com; return 308 https://vtt.example.com$request_uri; } server { listen 443 ssl; server_name vtt.example.com; ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/vtt.example.com/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/vtt.example.com/privkey.pem; ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; client_max_body_size 100m; location /static/ { alias /srv/gravewright/staticfiles/; } location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Host $http_host; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection $gravewright_connection_upgrade; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header Forwarded ""; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host ""; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port ""; proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s; } } Host $http_host preserves the browser-facing port; Nginx passes Origin through unchanged. The proxy overwrites the trusted forwarding values rather than appending client-supplied data. See Nginx proxy header configuration (https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html proxy_set_header). For a public port other than 443, include it in GRAVEWRIGHT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN , the TLS listener and redirect target. DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS contains hostnames without ports. Nginx handles the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect; this checkout does not enable Django's global SSL redirect. Install a valid certificate and arrange renewal, validate the configuration with nginx -t , then reload Nginx through your service manager. After configuration changes, verify login, Secure session/CSRF cookies, HSTS on an application response and an authenticated table connection with status 101 over WSS. Check two browser sessions and rejection of a foreign WebSocket origin. The automated direct-TLS and proxy regression is documented in testing (testing.md). Static files and private storage Serve /static/ from the staticfiles/ directory produced by collectstatic . Runtime app assets, including frontend modules served by custom views, still need their corresponding application routes. With debug disabled, Django does not automatically serve collected files through the development static handler. Keep MEDIA_ROOT private: uploaded maps, PDFs, journal files, audio, cards and installed module packages are served by guarded routes. A public /media/ alias would bypass these checks. Back up private storage together with the database, including attachments retained by deleted journal history. Optional disk compendium collections in the configured GRAVEWRIGHT_CONTENT_ROOT need backup too: standard settings default to data/vtt/compendiums/ , while the Runner uses data/compendiums/ . Configure upstream upload limits and timeouts explicitly for your deployment. The default map byte limit is 50 GiB, while decoded-pixel, dimension and tile limits apply separately; a high accepted byte limit does not imply that the server can process such a file within available memory. Large map uploads Map generation remains synchronous within the upload request. It runs outside the event loop, but a large map or time spent waiting for another map can exceed a reverse proxy's response timeout. Size proxy_read_timeout for observed upload processing times; the example's 300s is not a guarantee for every image. A proxy timeout can disconnect the uploader while the server continues processing, so check the scene list before retrying. For larger maps, install the optional libvips dependencies into the environment that runs the server and raise GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_MAX_PIXELS only as needed. In the source deployment commands above, use uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra vips ; retain the extra on later syncs. The native installers and managed update preparation select default dependencies without this extra. GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_TILER=vips makes missing native support a startup error; auto falls back to Pillow, whose separate GRAVEWRIGHT_MAP_PILLOW_MAX_PIXELS ceiling defaults to 64 million pixels. See configuration (configuration.md map-tiling-and-large-images) before increasing either ceiling. Generation is serialized per process; multiple ASGI workers can still add their memory and disk use. Libvips streams ordinary maps, while rotations and some codecs require additional resources. Reserve writable installation-local data/runner/tmp/ space for the encoded source, the complete staged tile set and native spill files, in addition to final media storage. Explicit Runner-root or Django upload-temp overrides retain their documented precedence. Measure representative formats, transparency and orientations on the intended server before raising limits; this change does not add background jobs or a global memory quota. Persistent Blueprint waits The ASGI application starts a database-backed Delay worker automatically when Daphne's reactor starts.
