This includes the normal Runner launch; no separate worker command or browser connection is needed. Other ASGI hosts must enable lifespan startup/shutdown. WSGI does not supply this lifecycle. Standard Django management commands do not start the worker. The existing managed updater maintenance flag holds the queue during server health verification until the update is committed or rolled back. Apply migrations before startup. Pending continuations live in the same private database as the scene, survive process restarts and become eligible when their deadline passes. A scene's paused automation keeps them pending until resumed. The worker checks at 250 ms intervals in batches of 20; timing is subject to load and availability. Shutdown waits for the current transaction to finish. If a process ends during a transaction, its uncommitted continuation remains pending for a later claim. Check server logs for database failures and the GM's Automation → Waiting view for pending work. Every ASGI process may run its own worker; database transactions serialize claims and effects, preventing duplicate application across competing workers. GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTOMATION_WORKER_ENABLED=false disables that process's worker without deleting waits. Campaign exports, snapshots and clones omit pending continuations; a full database backup includes them. A restored database can therefore resume overdue work on startup. Use the disabled-worker setting while inspecting a recovery copy before intentionally enabling its automation. See configuration (configuration.md blueprint-delay-worker) and Persistent Delay (map-builder.md persistent-delay). Multiple processes All workers need the same database, media files, secret, module trust configuration and Redis channel layer. Standard server settings require GRAVEWRIGHT_REDIS_URL with debug disabled, even for one process. The dedicated local runner is a separate profile and cannot be used for this deployment. In-memory Channels cannot exchange events between workers. SQLite is the configured database engine and uses IMMEDIATE transactions. Redis provides event delivery, not a replacement database or durable record of gameplay. Multiple ASGI processes still share SQLite's write contention; the source does not supply a PostgreSQL configuration or claim horizontally distributed storage support. Size deployments based on observed workloads. Use a service manager to supervise ASGI and Redis, retain logs, and shut down gracefully. Test two browser sessions, player/GM visibility, uploads, WebSocket reconnection and worker restarts after any hosting change. Backups and restoration Campaign exports are portable content packages; snapshots are campaign recovery points. In 0.3.2 , complete exports, clones and snapshots include clocks, clues, session preparation, timeline events, dashboard metadata and journal history/trash with retained attachments. Portable imports remap references and do not create campaign members or restore source-user permissions. Snapshots restore dashboards only for current GMs. Older archives without preparation metadata preserve the target's existing preparation/history data. See campaign management (campaign-management.md) for selection and dashboard rules and archives.py (../../gravewright/administration/archives.py) for the content graph. Neither format is a full instance backup: user accounts, host settings, installed module state, command receipts and pending Blueprint waits are outside portable content packages. A full database/media backup includes them. Trashed attachments still consume private storage until released by history cleanup; do not prune those files manually. For a consistent full backup: 1. Stop application writes, including every ASGI process and any maintenance process. 2. Copy the configured SQLite database and associated journal/WAL files if present, all private media, optional content collections, and required configuration/trust-key files. A SQLite backup operation is also suitable for the database, but it must be coordinated with the media snapshot. 3. Keep the matching source version, lock file and licenses with the backup record. Protect secrets separately and restrict access to the backup. 4. Restore into a separate directory first, with the same configuration paths adjusted for that environment. Verify login, a campaign, representative uploads and installed modules before switching traffic. Do not copy only db.sqlite3 in the source root or restore older code over a newer migrated database. Test a rollback using a matching database/media backup rather than assuming migrations can be reversed. Updates and optional services Core update discovery uses GRAVEWRIGHT_RELEASES_REPOSITORY , defaulting to Gravewright/gravewright ; an empty value disables it. Compatible Django release artifacts require SHA-256 metadata. Managed installations started with the Runner or main.py can install updates from Administration, including file replacement, migrations, restart and recovery. Direct ASGI deployments require operator-managed upgrades. Marketplace configuration uses an HTTPS catalog and a local file of trusted Ed25519 public keys. An empty URL leaves online discovery unconfigured. Review module authors and code before installation because modules execute on the application's origin. See modules (modules.md). Mail currently uses Django's console backend. Privacy text and publication settings are operator-managed content; enabling a flag does not supply a completed privacy policy or an operational email service. Dependency, Redis-server, browser and container-image licenses must also be considered for the actual distributed deployment; see third-party notices (../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). In-app updates on Windows, Linux and macOS Normal main.py and Gravewright Runner launches now enable the supervisor by default. Windows users keep starting Gravewright Runner.bat ; Linux/macOS source installations use uv run --locked python main.py . Only developers need --dev for autoreload. No special update mode is required. Use Administration → Updates → Install update on all three platforms. The interface controls download, SHA-256 validation, isolated locked dependencies, backup, migrations, restart and failure recovery. The progress modal shows the confirmed stage and elapsed time. Download percentages use received bytes; other stages use an activity indicator. Keep the Runner open during installation. Active table connections briefly disconnect during the swap; connection checks become less frequent while the server is unavailable, and pause when the page is hidden or offline. The page reloads after the server confirms that the target version is running. Releases require a higher version, the supervisor files, and a Gravewright-VERSION-django.zip asset with a GitHub SHA-256 digest. The default repository is Gravewright/gravewright ; an explicitly empty value disables discovery. The legacy initial 0.1.0-alpha.0 release predates the supervisor; that old installation must first receive the updated launcher to support in-app installation. The published 0.1.1 package also uses the earlier supervisor. After updating it to 0.1.2 from Administration, stop the old launcher, extract the new ZIP over the original source folder and run its installer with the same personal data directory. This one-time launcher replacement enables Django activation and the new file replacement workflow. Preserve the personal data and updates directory. Updates replace application files in the original project folder, including the installer, scripts and assets, remove obsolete code, and regenerate the platform Runner. Local .env , Python environments, caches and persistent data/extension directories are preserved. New dependencies are prepared in isolation before the replacement. Keep a .old copy for rollback is checked by default. After success, the updater's retained/ directory holds the previous code and matching data snapshots under .gravewright-rollback . The folder is named after the installation directory, for example data/updates/retained/gravewright.old for a Runner installation extracted as gravewright ; collisions add a unique identifier. Normal main.py uses data/updates/<installation-hash /retained/ instead. Use the actual path recorded by your installation, rather than constructing it from the target release version. Unchecking removes the temporary recovery copy after success. Temporary recovery is always retained during installation: migration, file replacement or startup failures restore code, launchers and data. Interrupted transactions recover at next launch. To restore a retained copy, stop the runner and use the installation's Python (shown in the generated BAT): bat "PATH_TO_PYTHON\python.exe" -X utf8 scripts\rollback_update.py "data\updates\retained\gravewright.old" Restoration also returns the database and media to the backup's point in time, discarding later changes. Keep updater state and environments together with the .old copy: it references the previous Python. Dirty Git checkouts remain protected. Never run another server against the same database during an update or restoration. Runner updates live in the extracted project's data/updates/ directory. main.py also keeps its managed state under the project's data/updates/ on Windows, Linux and macOS. No default updater state is shared through AppData, HOME or XDG directories. Preserve data/ and reserve disk space for environments and retained backups. The Automatic updates workflow runs native Windows/Linux/macOS tests. Run uv run python tests/e2e/automatic_updates.py and the same command with --runner for isolated HTTPS upgrades and deliberate migration/startup failures.

title: Windows installer and Runner
summary: Native Windows preparation, portable tools, startup and recovery.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/windows-runner.md) Install, configure, then run 1. Extract the complete project ZIP into a writable local folder. Use Windows 10 version 1803 or newer, or Windows 11, on x64/AMD64, with curl.exe , tar.exe , certutil.exe and a modern WebGL browser. ARM and 32-bit Windows are not supported by this installer. 2. Double-click Install Windows.bat . It detects compatible tools, downloads missing tools, installs locked dependencies and builds the frontend when needed. Internet is required for missing downloads. 3. Answer the configuration questions. Enter keeps the displayed value; Ctrl+C cancels without saving the answers. The installer then prepares the database and generates Gravewright Runner.bat beside itself, plus an optional icon shortcut. 4. Open Gravewright Runner.bat or its shortcut to start the application. It uses the prepared Python environment and saved settings, without downloading tools, installing dependencies, rebuilding the frontend or asking configuration questions. The default address is http://127.0.0.1:3000 . 5. Create the first owner account in the browser. Keep the runner console open; press Ctrl+C to stop the server. Closing the browser does not stop it. The installer finishes without starting the server. Run it again whenever you want to change settings, repair missing dependencies or prepare a new project version. It reuses compatible tools and unchanged frontend assets. The runner is generated for this Windows installation; do not distribute it to another computer. After moving or replacing the project, run the installer in the new folder to regenerate the runner and shortcut. Tools and preparation Tool Installation-local managed tool --- --- uv Verified uv 0.12.13 Python Managed CPython 3.14, Windows x64, standard GIL build Node.js/npm Verified Node.js 24.19.0 with npm No administrator privileges, permanent PATH changes, Docker or Redis server are required. The installer reuses verified tools in this installation and does not depend on tools in another OS profile. Python dependencies use an isolated environment and uv sync --locked --no-dev . Frontend preparation runs npm ci --include=dev --include=optional when required, then npm run build ; input/output hashes allow unchanged assets to be reused. Installation updates generated assets and ignored node_modules in the source folder. Configuration and personal data The project .env includes every setting and section from .env.example . Missing settings are filled automatically, preserving saved values, the private secret and custom options. The installer asks for table name, language ( en or pt-BR ), local port, modules folder, join codes, campaign snapshots, campaign exports and whether to allow tunnels. The tunnel option is a single yes/no choice; no URL is requested. It saves the answers together, preserving the secret and unrelated settings. On subsequent installations the saved answers are the defaults. Relative database, media and modules paths start at the project root. Selecting pt-BR automatically installs and globally activates the official signed Translator (https://github.com/Gravewright/translator). A missing or unverifiable translation is an installation error; an installed, verified package is reused offline. The official signing keys are added without removing existing trusted keys. Before preparing the Translator, the installer configures the official Gravewright Marketplace automatically when no catalog is configured, including installations that previously declined it. It verifies the official public keys and saves the catalog settings without an extra question. Existing custom catalogs are preserved; custom key files are kept intact, with any required official keys added to a managed copy. A complete, verified official configuration is reused offline on later installations. Unattended --check does not configure the Marketplace. The database and media use GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE and GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT from the project .env , defaulting to data/gravewright.sqlite3 and data/media in the project. Runner state, collected assets, managed tools and caches also stay inside the extracted project folder : Path Purpose --- --- data/compendiums/ Local content data/staticfiles/ Collected public assets data/logs/runner.log Startup/runtime diagnostics data/runner.lock Prevents concurrent use of the same data data/marketplace/<source-location-hash /trusted-keys.json Managed official and retained publisher public keys, when needed data/runner/ Downloaded tools, caches and environments per source location data/runner/prepare.lock Prevents simultaneous dependency preparation data/runner/frontend/<source-location-hash /state.json Frontend preparation state The installer creates and reads .env in the project root, next to Install Windows.bat . If it does not exist, a complete configuration is generated from .env.example with a new private secret. Configuration files in user-data directories are never imported. Python environments are managed separately. Defaults come from .env.example , then the project .env ; local network/security bounds are enforced by the runner. The secret is generated automatically. Stop the server before changing settings or backing up the project .env and the entire personal data directory. Preserve the secret, database and media together. Back up before installing a new version, since migrations can make older source versions incompatible. Local execution boundary The runner serves HTTP only on 127.0.0.1 , with one server process and in-memory Channels. Django debug stays disabled; origin, host, session, CSRF and campaign permissions remain active. Private uploads use guarded application routes. Set GRAVEWRIGHT_ALLOW_TUNNELS=true to accept any tunnel hostname through a local agent, with no URL registration or provider restriction. HTTP and HTTPS origins follow each request Host; WebSockets and CSRF still require a matching origin. The server keeps listening on 127.0.0.1:<port and trusts scheme headers only from local agents. Changing tunnel URLs requires no configuration change. Set the flag to false to restrict access to the local host. The Runner does not install or start tunnel software. For direct LAN or internet hosting, use deployment (deployment.md). Diagnostics and validation For unattended installation with defaults, without configuration questions or server startup: bat "Install Windows.bat" --check --no-pause --data-dir "data\check" This installs dependencies, prepares assets/database and generates a runner pointing at the selected state directory. It is not read-only. A later normal installation asks the questions. --data-dir changes Runner state, logs and collected assets; the database and uploads still follow project .env . For isolated checks, use a disposable project copy with separate database/media configuration as well. --port overrides only the installation check, not the saved port. The generated runner accepts --no-browser , --no-pause , --data-dir , --port and --check . Runner --check checks the application/database without tool installation or frontend preparation; it can apply migrations and collect static assets. --port applies only to that run. To configure saved values, open the installer. For download failures, inspect the console and connectivity to GitHub, nodejs.org and package sources. Do not bypass checksum failures. If an older launcher reports No download found for cpython-3.14+gil-windows-x86_64-none , use the complete updated project. If files or the prepared Python are missing, run the installer again. If the port is occupied, stop the other server or change the saved port. For application failures, inspect data/logs/runner.log and redact private information before sharing it. The installer owns tool/dependency preparation. create_runner.py (../../scripts/windows/create_runner.py) generates the startup BAT from its template (../../scripts/windows/runner.bat); create_shortcut.py (../../scripts/windows/create_shortcut.py) creates the optional icon shortcut. gravewright_runner.py (../../scripts/gravewright_runner.py) owns personal settings, locking and server lifecycle. See testing (testing.md): the native Windows harness covers installation, reconfiguration, private Python downloads, offline reuse and the generated runner. Browser validation is separate when --skip-browser is used. Updates and rollback The 0.3.2 release uses Gravewright-0.3.2-django.zip and its matching checksum. It adds database migrations for clocks, clues, campaign preparation and journal history. Follow upgrading (upgrading.md) before installing it. A manual upgrade requires the complete archive and another run of Install Windows.bat , preserving .env , data/ and explicit storage overrides. Same-version reissues require manual installation because discovery compares version numbers. Updates replace the project files in place, including the installer, and regenerate the runner with the new Python environment. In Administration → Updates, Keep a .old copy for rollback controls whether the old code and matching data snapshot are retained after success. Temporary recovery remains available during installation. See deployment (deployment.md) for restoration instructions. The runner executes an immutable launcher copy under data/.runner-launchers , allowing the project BAT to be safely replaced during an update. Preserve that folder together with personal data and backups.

title: Linux installer and Runner
summary: Native Linux preparation, portable tools, dependencies and platform limits.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/linux-runner.md) · macOS (macos-runner.md) · Windows (windows-runner.md) Install, configure, then run The 0.3.2 release includes these launchers in its complete Gravewright-0.3.2-django.zip archive, generated by build_release.py (../../scripts/build_release.py). For an existing installation, read upgrading (upgrading.md) before replacing files or migrating the database. 1. Use a complete source checkout or newly generated ZIP containing Install Linux.sh . Put it in a writable local folder; keep all project files together. Use Linux x64 or ARM64 and a modern WebGL browser. 2. Open a terminal in that folder and run: bash bash "./Install Linux.sh" 3. The installer detects the distribution, reuses verified local tools, downloads missing tools inside the extracted folder, installs locked Python/npm dependencies and prepares the frontend. Answer the configuration questions. Enter keeps the displayed value; Ctrl+C cancels without saving the answers. 4. The installer prepares the database and generates Gravewright Runner.sh beside itself, then exits without starting the server. Start it with: bash bash "./Gravewright Runner.sh" 5. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 and create the first owner account. Keep the terminal open while playing; Ctrl+C stops the application. Closing the browser does not stop the server. A file manager that supports “Run in Terminal” can open the executable shell files directly. Run the installer again to change saved settings, repair missing dependencies or prepare updated/moved project files. The generated Runner uses the prepared environment and never installs tools, runs npm or asks installation questions. Paths with spaces and Unicode are supported; quote filenames in terminal commands. Distribution and tool requirements The Bash installer reads /etc/os-release , matching both ID and ID_LIKE . It recognizes these package-manager families when basic download/extraction prerequisites are missing: Family Examples Package manager --- --- --- Debian Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives apt-get Fedora / RHEL Fedora, RHEL, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux dnf or yum SUSE openSUSE and derivatives zypper Arch Arch Linux, Manjaro and derivatives pacman Alpine Alpine Linux apk Recognizing a family is not a claim that every release has been tested. The official private Node.js binaries need glibc 2.28+ and Linux kernel 4.18+ on x64/ARM64, as documented in Node.js 24's platform requirements (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.19.0/BUILDING.md platform-list). On Alpine/musl, place native Node.js 22/24 and npm 10+ in data/runner/node/native first (bin/node and lib/node_modules/npm); the installer does not substitute a glibc Node binary. Unsupported architectures or incompatible tools produce a diagnostic instead of a global tool installation. Basic requirements are Bash 3.2+ , HTTPS-capable curl , CA certificates, tar /gzip and SHA-256 verification ( sha256sum or shasum ). Minimal Alpine installations may need Bash installed before the entrypoint can run. Missing distribution prerequisites can require the package manager and sudo ; run Gravewright itself as your regular user. An unrecognized ID / ID_LIKE stops the installer before prerequisite preparation, even if tools are present. Report those identifiers so the family can be supported, or use the manual terminal workflow (getting-started.md). Tool Installation-local managed tool --- --- uv Verified uv 0.12.13 Python Managed standard-GIL CPython 3.14 for the native platform Node.js/npm Verified Node.js 24.19.0/npm; Alpine requires a native distribution inside the local tools folder Internet is required for missing tools and packages. Verified tools are reused from this installation; tools in another OS profile are not selected. Private tools, Python environments and caches stay in the Runner directory. The installer does not change shell profiles or the permanent PATH, and does not require Docker, Homebrew or Redis. Python preparation uses uv sync --locked --no-dev ; frontend preparation uses npm ci --include=dev --include=optional and npm run build when hashes indicate work is needed. It preserves a developer .venv and source lock files. Existing frontend outputs are reused when inputs and outputs are unchanged. Configuration and storage Configuration is saved in the project's .env , next to the installer. Missing options are filled from .env.example ; existing secrets, unrelated settings and saved answers are preserved. The installer asks for table name, language, local port, module folder, join codes, snapshots, campaign exports and tunnel access. Relative database/media/module paths start at the project root. Selecting pt-BR installs and activates the signed official Translator; a verified installed package can be reused offline. The official Marketplace is configured automatically when no catalog is configured. Existing custom catalogs are preserved, and verified official settings are reused offline. Unattended --check does not configure it. Location Purpose --- --- Project .env Configuration and persistent private secret Project data/gravewright.sqlite3 Default database ( GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE ) Project data/media/ Default private uploads and module packages ( GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT ) data/runner/ Private tools, caches and prepared environments data/ Default Runner state, logs and collected public assets Runner state logs/runner.log Startup/runtime diagnostics Runner state runner.lock , .runner-launchers/ , updates/ Instance lock, immutable launcher copies and update recovery --data-dir chooses Runner state , not the database or uploads. Change .env to relocate those. GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT can select an absolute private-tool directory before running the installer; it is useful for isolated checks and does not change HOME. Prepared environments and frontend state are separated by source location, so moving a project requires rerunning the installer. Local execution and updates The Runner listens only on 127.0.0.1 , with one server process and in-memory Channels. Debug remains off and host/origin, CSRF, sessions and campaign permissions remain active. --no-browser prints the address without opening a browser. For LAN/public HTTPS hosting, use deployment (deployment.md); the local launcher does not configure a public server. The tunnel option permits a separately managed local tunnel agent; the Runner does not install tunnel software. Stop the Runner before reconfiguring or backing up. Preserve the configured database, private media and project .env together, plus Runner state for update recovery. Migrations can prevent older code from opening a newer database. Supported managed updates replace project files and regenerate the platform launcher; .runner-launchers keeps the executing launcher separate from replacement files. For manual updates, extract/checkout the complete new project and rerun its installer before starting. See deployment and rollback (deployment.md). Upgrade or reinstall 0.3.2 Version 0.3.2 retains the Alpha development stage and the numeric release channel convention. Use the complete ZIP and its matching SHA-256 file . A compatible managed installation can find it through Administration using its configured release repository. A host already on 0.3.2 will not be offered an automatic update to that same version; reinstall such a package manually. Stop the Runner and back up .env , the configured database/media/module paths and Runner state. Replace application files from the complete archive in the existing project folder, preserving configuration and data. Run bash "./Install Linux.sh" again to prepare locked dependencies and apply migrations, then use its regenerated Runner. Do not replace the installation with only the shell entrypoint: its supporting scripts are part of the update. If you move the project, preserve storage paths and rerun installation in the new location. See the 0.3.2 notes (../releases/0.3.2.md) for the new migrations. POSIX SIGHUP is handled as an orderly stop, like terminal shutdown; it does not bypass supervisor cleanup. Interrupted update transactions are recovered on the next start. Preserve data/.runner-launchers/ and data/updates/ with Runner state, or their equivalents under an explicit state override. The historical 0.2.1 refresh notes (../releases/0.2.1.md) remain specific to that old reissue. Checks and troubleshooting Unattended preparation, without configuration questions or server startup: bash bash "./Install Linux.sh" --check --no-pause --data-dir "data/check" bash "./Gravewright Runner.sh" --check --no-browser --data-dir "data/check" These checks write files : installation prepares tools/dependencies/frontend, .env , database and Runner; Runner --check can run migrations and collect static assets. They are not read-only. Use a disposable source copy and explicit directories for experiments. Installer flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER , --no-browser , --no-pause and --help . Runner flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER and --no-browser ; a port override applies only to that run. After one successful installation, unchanged tools/packages/assets can be reused with UV_OFFLINE=1 and npm_config_offline=true . This is not a promise that a fresh installation or changed dependencies work offline. See uv's offline setting (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/environment/ uv_offline). Symptom Action --- --- File manager displays the script as text Open a terminal and use the quoted bash command Missing curl, CA certificates, tar or hash utility Install the prerequisites reported for your detected distribution; retry as the regular user Node cannot start / missing GLIBC Check the platform requirements; Alpine/musl needs native Node/npm under data/runner/node/native Download/checksum failure Check GitHub, nodejs.org and package-source connectivity; rerun with the complete project and retain checksum verification Moved project / prepared Python missing Run Install Linux.sh again in the new location Port in use Stop the other process or use --port 3001 ; use the installer to change the saved default Another Runner uses the same state Stop that Runner; the OS lock is released on exit. A persistent lock file is normal Startup fails Read the selected state directory's logs/runner.log ; redact private details before sharing POSIX smoke tests (../../tests/posix/smoke.py) exercise a disposable source copy, private tools, paths with spaces/Unicode, unattended preparation, offline reuse, real HTTP readiness and graceful shutdown. The POSIX Runner workflow (../../.github/workflows/posix-runner.yml) runs the native checks on Linux and macOS; mocked distribution tests separately cover detection branches. Platform CI does not imply every recognized distribution was tested. All paths in the storage table are relative to the extracted project. data/runner/tmp/ holds bootstrap temporary files. Explicit relative state/tool overrides resolve from this project, never from the caller's working directory.

title: macOS installer and Runner
summary: Native macOS preparation, portable tools, startup and platform support.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/macos-runner.md) · Linux (linux-runner.md) · Windows (windows-runner.md) Install, configure, then run Use macOS 13.5 or newer , on Intel x64 or Apple Silicon ARM64, with a modern WebGL browser. The managed Node.js version follows Node.js 24's macOS requirements (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.19.0/BUILDING.md platform-list). The 0.3.2 release includes these launchers in its complete Gravewright-0.3.2-django.zip archive, generated by build_release.py (../../scripts/build_release.py). Intel Macs require Apple's Command Line Tools (or a selected Xcode installation with its compiler and SDK) for the dependency source build described below. Homebrew is not required. 1. Extract the complete new archive or use a checkout containing Install macOS.command , in a writable local folder. Keep all project files together. 2. Open Install macOS.command in Finder. It opens Terminal and prepares the installation. You can also open Terminal in the project directory and run: bash bash "./Install macOS.command" 3. The installer detects the native architecture, reuses verified local tools, downloads missing tools inside the extracted folder, installs locked dependencies and prepares the frontend. Answer the configuration questions. Enter keeps the displayed value; Ctrl+C cancels without saving the answers. 4. It prepares the database and creates Gravewright Runner.command beside itself, then exits without starting the server. Open that generated file in Finder, or run: bash bash "./Gravewright Runner.command" 5. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 and create the first owner account. Keep the Terminal window open; Ctrl+C stops the application. Closing the browser does not stop it. The generated Runner uses the prepared Python and saved settings without installation questions, dependency downloads or npm builds. Rerun the installer to change saved settings, repair dependencies or prepare new/moved project files. Paths with spaces and Unicode are supported; quote filenames. A .command launcher is a Terminal script, not a signed .app bundle. Permissions and tools macOS's Bash 3.2 is supported; installing a newer shell or Homebrew is not required. The bootstrap uses curl , system CA trust, tar /gzip and shasum -a 256 or another supported SHA-256 utility. Run it as your regular user; missing Python, uv and Node.js are prepared privately, without sudo , global package installation or permanent PATH/shell-profile changes. Tool Installation-local managed tool --- --- uv Verified uv 0.12.13 Python Managed standard-GIL CPython 3.14 for the native platform Node.js/npm Verified Node.js 24.19.0/npm The installer selects darwin-x64 or darwin-arm64 according to the running architecture; compatible tools must match. Internet is required for missing downloads. Verified tools are reused from this installation. Python preparation uses uv sync --locked --no-dev in a private environment; frontend preparation uses npm ci --include=dev --include=optional and npm run build when needed. Unchanged frontend inputs/outputs are reused. The developer .venv and source lock files are preserved. Docker and Redis are not needed for this local profile. Intel dependency compilation Cryptography removed official macOS x86_64 support and Intel wheels in version 49; see its changelog (https://cryptography.io/en/50.0.1/changelog/ v49-0-0). Gravewright builds the locked cryptography 50.x release locally on Intel. This is a Gravewright-maintained source-build path covered by our platform CI, not restored upstream Intel support. The locked cryptography version is unchanged. The build needs Apple's xcrun -selected SDK, Clang, Make and Perl. If they are missing, the interactive installer starts Apple's system dialog with: bash xcode-select --install Finish the Apple installation, then rerun Install macOS.command . Gravewright does not wait for the system dialog to finish. Installer --check does not open it: it exits with an instruction to install the missing tools and retry. A full, correctly selected Xcode installation can also provide them. The cryptography source-build guide (https://cryptography.io/en/50.0.1/installation/ building-cryptography-on-macos) describes the compiler/library requirements. With those Apple prerequisites available, Gravewright downloads SHA-256-pinned Rust components, builds a static private OpenSSL and compiles cryptography against them. It uses Rust 1.99.0 (https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/10/01/Rust-1.99.0/) ( rustc , Cargo and the standard library) without rustup, and OpenSSL 3.5.9 LTS (https://openssl-library.org/source/), without Homebrew. The first Intel installation can take several minutes longer; verified prepared tools, OpenSSL and build caches are reused. Offline reuse requires a completed earlier preparation, including the compiled dependency and its cached inputs. On both Mac architectures, the installer sets AUTOBAHN_USE_NVX=0 for dependency preparation, using Autobahn's Python fallback instead of its optional native NVX extension. This avoids requiring that optional compiler build on Apple Silicon, including macOS 13.5/14. It does not remove Intel's cryptography compiler/SDK requirement. Normal Runner startup performs no compilation. If Finder reports a permission error after extraction, use Terminal in the project folder: bash chmod u+x "Install macOS.command" The generated Runner is executable. If macOS blocks a downloaded script, use Apple's per-item Privacy & Security → Open Anyway flow only for a download you trust; see Apple's instructions (https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445). Do not remove security settings globally. Running bash is also useful when diagnosing a script's ordinary execute-permission problem. Configuration and storage The installer creates/completes the project's .env from .env.example , preserving saved values, its private secret and custom settings. It asks for table name, language, port, modules folder, join codes, snapshots, campaign exports and tunnel access. Relative database/media/module paths are resolved from the project root. Selecting pt-BR installs and activates the verified official Translator; a verified installed package can be reused offline. The official Marketplace is configured automatically when no catalog is configured. Existing custom catalogs are preserved, and verified official settings are reused offline. Unattended --check does not configure it. Location Purpose --- --- Project .env Configuration and persistent private secret Project data/gravewright.sqlite3 Default database ( GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE ) Project data/media/ Default private uploads and module packages ( GRAVEWRIGHT_MEDIA_ROOT ) data/runner/ Private tools, caches and environments per source location Runner tools rust/1.99.0-x86_64-apple-darwin/ Verified private Intel Rust compiler/Cargo/standard library Runner tools openssl/3.5.9-darwin-x64/ Private static OpenSSL for the Intel dependency build Runner tools cargo/ Private Cargo cache; no use of a personal ~/.cargo installation data/ Default Runner state, logs and collected assets Runner state logs/runner.log Startup/runtime diagnostics Runner state runner.lock , .runner-launchers/ , updates/ Instance lock, immutable launcher copies and update recovery --data-dir relocates Runner state , not the database or uploads; configure those in .env . Set GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT to an explicit absolute or project-relative path before installation to use a different private-tool directory, for example in an isolated test. It does not change HOME or import configuration from another installation. Moving the project requires installation again because its prepared environment and frontend state are associated with its source location. Local execution, updates and backups The Runner binds HTTP only to 127.0.0.1 , with one server process and in-memory Channels. Debug remains off, while host/origin, CSRF, session and campaign checks stay active. --no-browser prints the address without opening the default browser. The installer can allow a separately managed local tunnel agent, but does not install tunnel software. For direct LAN access or public HTTPS, follow deployment (deployment.md). Stop the Runner before changing settings or backing up. Preserve the configured database, private media and project .env together; also retain Runner state for update recovery. Migrations can make older application versions incompatible. Supported managed updates replace project files and regenerate the macOS launcher; immutable copies in .runner-launchers keep the running launcher independent of those replacements. For manual updates or a moved project, run the new folder's installer before starting. See deployment and rollback (deployment.md). Upgrade or reinstall 0.3.2 Version 0.3.2 retains the Alpha development stage and the numeric release channel convention. Use the complete ZIP and its matching SHA-256 file. A compatible managed installation can find it through Administration using its configured release repository. Hosts already on 0.3.2 do not receive an automatic same-version update; reinstall such a package manually. Stop the Runner and back up project .env , configured database/media/module paths and Runner state. Replace the application files with the complete package in the existing installation folder, preserving configuration and data. Open Install macOS.command again to prepare locked dependencies and apply migrations, then use the regenerated Runner. The entrypoint and supporting scripts must be replaced together. If moving the project, preserve storage paths and prepare the new location with the installer. See upgrading (upgrading.md) and the 0.3.2 notes (../releases/0.3.2.md) for the new migrations. SIGHUP follows the orderly Runner shutdown path, including supervisor cleanup. An interrupted update transaction is recovered on the next start; preserve data/.runner-launchers/ and data/updates/ , or their equivalents under an explicit state override. The historical 0.2.1 refresh notes (../releases/0.2.1.md) remain specific to that old reissue. The native CI matrix includes Intel and Apple Silicon; consult its workflow results for actual platform validation. Unattended checks and troubleshooting bash bash "./Install macOS.command" --check --no-pause --data-dir "data/check" bash "./Gravewright Runner.command" --check --no-browser --data-dir "data/check" Installer --check prepares tools/dependencies/frontend, writes configuration, migrates the database and generates the Runner without questions or server startup. Runner --check validates the prepared application and can migrate/collect static assets. Neither is read-only. Use a disposable project copy and explicit directories for experiments. Installer flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER , --no-browser , --no-pause and --help . Runner flags are --check , --data-dir PATH , --port NUMBER and --no-browser . --port applies only to that run. After a successful installation, unchanged tools/packages/assets can be reused with UV_OFFLINE=1 and npm_config_offline=true ; fresh or changed dependencies still need downloads. See uv's offline setting (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/environment/ uv_offline). Symptom Action --- --- Finder cannot execute the file Check execute permission, or use the quoted bash command in Terminal macOS blocks the download Follow Apple's per-item approval flow for trusted downloads Download or checksum failure Check connectivity to GitHub, nodejs.org and package sources; preserve integrity checks Wrong architecture / incompatible OS Use the native compatible tools and macOS 13.5+; do not mix Intel/ARM tool installations Intel compiler/SDK prerequisite is missing Complete xcode-select --install , then rerun the installer; unattended --check does not launch Apple's dialog First Intel installation takes longer Rust/OpenSSL and cryptography preparation includes compilation; inspect progress and retain the private cache for reuse Prepared Python is missing or project moved Run Install macOS.command again in the new location Port is occupied Stop the other process or use --port 3001 ; rerun the installer to change the saved port Another Runner uses the same state Stop it; OS locking releases on exit. A remaining lock file is normal Application fails to start Inspect the selected state's logs/runner.log and redact private details before sharing The POSIX smoke test (../../tests/posix/smoke.py) installs into a disposable source/tool/state fixture without changing HOME or personal configuration. It covers quoted/Unicode paths, offline reuse, real HTTP readiness and graceful shutdown. The native CI workflow (../../.github/workflows/posix-runner.yml) runs Linux and Intel/Apple Silicon macOS jobs; browser behavior is covered separately by the project's browser tests. All paths in the storage table are relative to the extracted project. data/runner/tmp/ holds bootstrap temporary files. Explicit relative state/tool overrides resolve from this project, never from the caller's working directory.

title: Map Builder reference
summary: Builder workflows, Smart Objects, automation, supported limits and developer contracts.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/map-builder.md) · Universal VTT (universal-vtt.md) · Frontend (frontend.md) Map Builder is the campaign GM's workspace for editable map projects. Draw a map from materials or import a finished image, add native walls, doors, objects, lights and effects, then generate or update a scene. The project remains editable separately from the scene used at the table. This guide describes the Map Builder implementation in the documented 0.3.3 source revision. See the release notes (../releases/0.3.3.md). The Smart Objects design direction (smart-objects-direction.md) distinguishes implemented capabilities from proposals. Find the right workflow Your starting point Where to go --- --- Build a new room Build the first room ( build-the-first-room) Choose between grid tiles, soft painting and a map image Choose a starting method ( choose-a-starting-method) Organize images, families and collections Build larger maps ( build-larger-maps) Organize or select project objects Selection and project layers ( selection-and-project-layers) Recover a failed or conflicting save Automatic saving ( automatic-saving), then Troubleshooting ( troubleshooting) Apply edits to the same game scene Update a generated scene ( update-a-generated-scene) Add a switch, torch, region or timed behavior Smart Object reference ( smart-object-reference) Import/export a Universal VTT file Universal VTT interchange (universal-vtt.md) Integrate with source documents or HTTP operations Developer reference ( developer-reference) GM access and entry points Open the campaign's Scenes directory and choose New scene → Map Builder . The selected scene folder is retained for the project and its first generated scene. Only a current campaign GM can open or manage Builder projects; players and streamers cannot edit them. Opening the editor does not switch the players' broadcast. To resume, use Panels → Projects , or right-click a scene linked to a project and choose Edit with MapBuilder . The linked scene has the red map icon in the GM's directory. Edit with MapBuilder also works on ordinary image and Universal VTT scenes: the first opening creates a linked editable project. Edit an existing scene Right-click any scene as GM and choose Edit with MapBuilder . The existing base raster becomes a project background; representable walls, doors and lights become editable objects. Opening creates no duplicate scene and changes neither the broadcast nor the GM's scene selection. Subsequent openings reuse the same project. Use Update scene to apply edits to that scene. With a scene open, GMs can also choose Edit Scene in the top bar beside Game, GM and Effects. It edits the scene currently viewed by that GM, including a private selection. The button is hidden when no scene is open. Exact image dimensions, fractional grid sizes and offsets are retained. Imported collision walls have Show wall artwork disabled so generation does not paint new lines over the finished image. They appear as dashed editing guides and are omitted from Preview. The door has the equivalent artwork option. Artwork already baked into the source image cannot be removed by moving a wall or opening a door. Tokens, fog, drawings, image overlays, audio and complex native objects stay in the scene. Objects outside Builder limits or with unsupported properties stay native; import warnings remain available in Review . They are preserved by updates but are not included in the Builder preview. A missing or unreadable base raster prevents conversion without leaving a partial project. For fractional native grids, disable snapping when positioning between Builder workspace cells. Project, preview and game scene Action Result Effect on the game scene --- --- --- Edit, Undo/Redo, automatic saving or Ctrl+S Save the editable project Requires Generate scene or Update scene to apply to the table Preview Inspect artwork with every project layer shown No scene write; editing pauses Simulate in a Smart Object editor Trace one local graph No gameplay effects Test behavior Rehearse through the server and report predicted changes The rehearsal is rolled back Generate scene Create the project's first native, GM-only scene Opens it for the GM; the previous player broadcast remains Update scene Apply project changes to the linked scene Clients viewing that scene receive the committed update Activate for players in the scene context menu Make the scene player-visible and broadcast it Connected players switch to it Builder tools Open Builder tools in the header. Select objects with Shift-click or a selection rectangle before using selection actions. - Group selection in a layer creates a named layer and moves the selection into it. Use Project layers to hide, lock, select or move the group. - Align and distribute aligns edges or centers and distributes three or more objects with equal gaps. Rotation applies to the selection as a group. Invalid bounds, locked layers and overlapping doors leave the document unchanged. - My objects saves up to 100 selected objects, including linked components, artwork, activation radii and Smart Object graphs. Models belong to the campaign and can be placed in another project in that campaign. Choose Place, then click the map; Escape cancels. Copies receive new IDs and remap internal references. Keep references self-contained or bound to campaign resources. The library holds 128 models; deleting a model preserves instances already placed on maps. - Show all object activation areas displays named, colored circular guides without selecting objects. It respects layer visibility and isolation and is omitted from Preview and generated scenes. Region rectangles are included too. - Object brush stamps an imported object or image family along a drag. Choose Objects in the normal library, select artwork and enable Paint multiple objects. Configure spacing and size/rotation variation. Each stroke is one Undo step; project limits still apply. - Test as player opens a detached map with a test pawn. Click or use arrows to walk, adjust vision radius and Interact with nearby objects. It shares the table's collision and visibility geometry, including open doors. Area crossings rehearse enter/exit events through the server's rollback-only behavior engine. Choose a campaign actor for token-dependent actions. Reset discards the rehearsal. Closing preserves the draft and live scene. Timers do not advance and messages, audio and camera changes are not delivered to players. This is a generic map rehearsal, not a simulation of system-specific rules. Build the first room 1. As the campaign GM, choose New scene → Map Builder . The selected scene folder carries into the project. Entering does not change the current scene or the players' broadcast. 2. Enter the map name directly in the header. Open Panels → Settings → Map settings to choose dimensions, cell size and background. Return to Layers to rename Layer 1 or add another named layer. 3. Start with the default solid floor, plain wall and native door, or choose Import in the bottom Library for your own artwork. In the import modal, choose image files and their type: Floor , Wall , Door or Object . Optionally assign them to an existing asset family or create a new one. Select an image or family in the library to use its brush. 4. Open Panels → Tools . With Floor , choose freehand brush, rectangle, circle or polygon and paint the floor. Draw walls and doors by dragging between their start and end points. A door is an independent segment and needs no existing wall. Drawing it over a collinear wall replaces that span. 5. Use Select to move objects and open Panels → Selection to edit their properties. Press E to erase objects. Walls and doors move and delete independently. Undo/redo restores edits, including removed objects. Space-drag moves the view; the wheel changes zoom, and 0 fits the map. 6. Changes save automatically; the header shows their status. Panels → Projects lists saved projects so you can reopen them. New project waits for pending changes before starting a blank project. 7. Choose Generate scene . The builder saves the source, renders the image, runs the native tile pipeline and creates a new GM-only scene in that folder. The GM opens that scene; players remain on their existing broadcast. In the scene's context menu, Activate for players makes it player-visible and broadcasts it in one operation, including to players already connected. In the game's Scenes directory, a scene linked to a saved builder project keeps the same map icon, colored red. Right-click it and choose Edit with MapBuilder , alongside the normal Edit action, to reopen that project directly. Entering the editor does not change the players' scene. After editing, the primary header action becomes Update scene and applies changes to that same scene, keeping its identity and project link. Imported images and scenes without a linked source keep their normal controls. Project links are visible only to the GM. Workspace controls The canvas fills the space below the header, with a horizontal Library along the bottom. Panels → Tools contains drawing tools, the active material, brush options, the active layer and grid snapping. Between the editable map name and history, the header provides Select , Paint , brush size and Erase . Undo , Redo , save status, Preview and scene generation follow them. View controls and map dimensions in cells sit below the canvas. Select (V) supports Shift-click and dragging a selection box for multiple objects. Paint (F) returns to the floor's freehand brush in paint operation, using its current material and selecting Floor in the library. Its size stays synchronized with Tools : in Tiles, 1–20 cells with grid snapping or 0.05–20 without it; Painting always uses 0.05–20 cells. / also adjusts the size. The size field is available for the freehand floor brush, including its area eraser. Erase (E) deletes a whole clicked object; use Erase floor in Tools to erase only part of a floor. Editing controls pause in Preview or while an operation requiring exclusive access is running. Background automatic saving keeps editing available. With the floor brush active, hold Shift + left mouse button and drag horizontally to resize it without painting. Drag right to increase the size or left to decrease it; the anchored footprint and size update as you drag. Release to keep the size or press Escape to restore it. This works in Tiles and Painting, including area erasure; it changes only the brush preference, without editing the map or adding an undo step. The header's name field applies and saves valid names after a short typing pause. Enter or Escape returns focus to the canvas; Undo reverts an accepted name change. The name stays synchronized with Settings . Header history buttons use Ctrl+Z to undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo. Library and tool strip The library toolbar provides search, Import , type categories and direct Select , Erase , Pan , Empty Object and Region tools. Floor, wall, door, object and light brushes stay in the same strip; Effects keeps the Particles/Shaders selector. These shortcuts close the auxiliary panel and return focus to the map. On smaller screens the strip has its own horizontal scrolling, including keyboard focus, without shifting when categories change. Search, filters, categories and the collapse arrow keep their positions when switching to native lights or effects; the hidden import action retains its slot. Empty filtered results show a message. Checkboxes use the same compact native control across settings, layers and object properties, with label and Space-key activation. Its arrow collapses the asset cards while leaving the toolbar accessible. On entry, Floor is highlighted and the gallery shows only images classified as Floor in this project. Clicking Floor , Wall , Door or Object filters the gallery and activates that drawing tool. Choosing a native light or effect preset activates its placement tool. The material selector in Tools follows the active brush and includes its default appearance. Selection and project layers Panels , at the upper right of the map, opens an auxiliary panel with Tools , Layers , Selection , Settings , Projects and Review tabs. The panel can be closed without hiding the library. Selecting or painting does not open the panel automatically. Object properties are available in Selection and through the object's right-click menu. Select an object and press Shift+F10 or the keyboard's context-menu key for the same menu. On touch screens, use Object options at the top of its selection properties. The menu opens separate Properties , Appearance and Behavior modals, plus Torch components , Presence filters , the native editor or Edit nodes when supported by the selected element. Property changes save as fields are applied; Undo reverses them. Duplicate , Rotate and Delete are also available in the menu. For an Object or Empty Object, choose Ready-made models and a model from the list. The 14 models include a chest, book, altar, bell, warning trap, pressure plate, dice challenge, quest giver, quest completion, entrance sign, timed switch and door controls. The same models appear under Behavior and in the node editor's Object catalog . Search the catalog and configure its door, journal, recipients or dice as needed. Check Add a sound when activated to choose a campaign sound and volume, or Use an active image to choose another Object image. Unchecked options add no sound or image override. The inactive state keeps the original image; Empty Objects remain image-free. Apply installs the editable nodes as one undo step; closing the catalog leaves the object unchanged. Replacing existing authored nodes requires confirmation. Select one element and edit Element name (or Object name/Region name ) to name it independently of its image file. Floors, walls, doors, decorations, lights, particles, shaders and regions support names of up to 120 characters. Press Enter or leave the field to apply and save automatically; Escape discards the field's pending edit. Layers, behavior targets, light/door choices and the scene network display authored names. Clearing an optional name restores the normal label; Empty Objects, regions and shaders keep a required name. Undo/Redo and duplication preserve names. Renaming keeps the element's identity and node connections; Update scene applies it to the existing scene. Double-click a door on the map to open its Smart object behavior editor in a modal. Review shows a project summary and scene generation action. The panel heading keeps the current map name visible. Its six labeled tabs remain available in two rows, including on narrow screens, while each tab keeps its own scroll position. Use the arrow keys to move between tabs, Home/End to reach the first/last tab, and Escape outside a text field to close the panel. Closing restores focus to the control that opened it and preserves the selection; clicking the current tab keeps it open. Tools places the current material, active layer and brush settings before the compact tool palette. Painting's hardness and intensity appear together; expanded help contains the brush instructions and shortcuts. Selection provides a Select on map action when nothing is selected. Projects keeps long project names readable, and Review groups the map and object counts before the scene actions. Opening and navigating panels does not edit the map. Selection places editable properties before the material thumbnails used to change the selected object's appearance. Layers organizes named project layers: create, rename, reorder, hide or lock them, and choose the active layer for new objects. Move selected objects between layers in Selection or with Move here on the destination layer. The list shows the top layer first, with counts and active/hidden/locked states. Paint on in Tools changes the active layer. Select selects editable objects in a layer; Solo temporarily isolates it, including its native lights and effects. Show all ends isolation and reveals all layers; Unlock all removes their locks. Layer operations Drag a layer's reorder handle or use its arrows to change its position. Expand Layer contents to select an individual object. Duplicate layer copies an unlocked layer and offsets all its contents exactly one cell right and one cell down. The copy appears immediately above the original, visible and unlocked, with new object IDs and remapped references between copied Smart Objects. The operation is refused without changes if the copy would leave the map, overlap doors or exceed project limits. Duplication is one undo step. Merge down moves a visible, unlocked layer into its adjacent visible, unlocked lower layer. Paint order, object identities and Smart Object references are preserved. A merge is one undo step. A layer containing terrain erasers cannot be merged over a lower layer with floors, because that would change which floors those erasers affect. Delete an empty, unlocked layer after moving or removing its objects, including the final layer. Create a visible, unlocked layer before drawing again. Layer names, order, visibility and locks are saved with the project. Objects on hidden or locked layers cannot be edited. Hiding a layer changes the editor view; generation includes every project layer. Preview Preview keeps the map in place and hides the grid, selection, brush guides and map outline. Drawing and property editing pause, while pan, zoom, save and scene generation remain available. Preview temporarily shows all layers, including those hidden in the editor. Back to editing restores their previous visibility and resumes editing. Choose a starting method Method Use it for What remains editable --- --- --- Tiles Grid rooms, repeated materials, precise shapes or unsnapped hard edges Concrete floor images/shapes, walls and other project objects Painting Soft terrain transitions and gradual material blending Brush strokes and their masks, with the same project objects and layers Import ready-made map A finished PNG/JPEG/WebP/TIFF to trace or decorate One background image plus the objects you place over it Import Universal VTT A .uvtt , .dd2vtt or .df2vtt containing grid/wall/door/light data A new linked scene and Builder project, with an image background and editable compatible objects Tiles and Painting are modes of the same project; switching modes preserves existing work. A ready-made background can be used with either mode. For file format support, warnings and interchange limits, follow the Universal VTT guide (universal-vtt.md). Tiles and Painting The header's mode selector switches between Tiles and Painting in the same project. New projects start in Tiles. Changing modes preserves existing floors, walls, doors, native objects, layers and camera; the mode change is one undo step and is saved with the project. Tiles uses materials, image tiles and asset families. Grid snapping replaces covered cells; disabling snapping retains continuous placement and shapes. Brushes, rectangles, circles, polygons, fill, area erasure and sampling share the same project, layers and undo history. Walls, doors, objects, native lights/effects, preview and scene generation remain available in this workspace. New projects start with one empty, renameable Layer 1 . It can mix floors, walls, doors, objects and native effects; no layers are assigned to object types. Open Panels → Layers to rename it or add your own named layers. Importing assets, saving and generating an empty map with only its background remain available. Existing projects retain their authored layers. Terrain Painting Choose Painting in the header and select a floor image or family from the library. Drag on the map to blend that material with the existing floor using a continuous circular brush. Terrain painting uses fractional positions regardless of the Tiles snapping setting; grid visibility remains your display choice. Returning to Tiles restores its snapping controls without converting existing strokes. The header size field and Panels → Tools share the brush diameter, from 0.05 to 20 cells. Edge hardness (%) controls the solid center and the softness of the outer edge. Brush intensity (%) controls how strongly each brush dab adds material. Holding the pointer down while stationary continues building up the material; passing over an area again blends it further. Textures retain their map-space scale and orientation while different materials mix. In Tools , choose Operation → Erase floor for a soft area eraser using the same size, hardness and intensity. It clears earlier floors on the active layer, revealing lower layers or the background; other layers, walls, doors and native objects are preserved. New paint added afterward is unaffected by that earlier eraser. The header's Erase (E) still deletes an entire object. Each completed terrain gesture is one undo step. Escape cancels the active stroke, including accumulated paint while holding still. Locked or hidden layers cannot be painted. Preview pauses editing; save/reopen, generation and linked scene updates preserve the soft masks and mixed textures. Import a finished map Choose Library → Import → Import ready-made map , or use the same action in Panels → Settings or Projects . Upload one PNG, JPEG, WebP or TIFF image (up to 25 MB), or choose an image already in this campaign. Set its width and height in cells and cell size. An empty project suggests a bounded grid from the image dimensions; check these values against the map's authored grid. The image fills the map once beneath all layers. Add walls, doors, objects, lights and behaviors over it. It is independent of brush categories and is never tiled as a floor texture. Replacing it keeps existing objects in place; dimensions that would put objects outside the map are rejected. Remove map image in Settings removes the background without deleting its campaign image. Import, replacement and removal use Undo/Redo and automatic saving, and appear in generated or updated scenes. Build larger maps Library, families and collections Search the library by image name and choose a type category to filter it. Asset classifications and optional names, collections and families belong to the project; they do not rename campaign images used elsewhere. Import opens the application's import modal. Choose one or more images, set their type to Floor , Wall , Door or Object , and optionally choose or create an asset family. You can also choose or enter a collection. The chosen type, family and collection apply to all files in that upload. Lights do not use image assets and are outside this import workflow. Each type category shows only that project's images of the selected type. Campaign images without a project type remain available under Unclassified images in Panels → Tools → Material . Select one there to assign the active tool's type; its card then appears in the matching category. This classification does not change the campaign image or its use in another project. Use the library's Collection filter to show one collection or All collections . Open Library settings below the asset cards to edit the selected image's project name, collection and type. Scroll within the dock to reach these controls; the dock keeps its configured height. Collections are optional names of up to 80 characters, with surrounding spaces removed. A family card appears when at least one member belongs to the selected collection; choosing the family still paints with all its members. An asset family groups variations of the same material or object, such as three dungeon floor tiles. Family names belong to this project, are trimmed, must contain 1–80 characters, and are matched exactly. All images in a family must have the same type. Select a family card in the library or choose the family under the material selector's family group to paint with all its members. Individual images remain selectable when you want a specific variation. Double-click an existing image card to open the asset editing modal and change its name, type, family or collection. An image already used on the map cannot change type; upload a separate copy to use it with another brush. Adding or removing a family member affects future painting; it does not replace images already painted. Remove asset in this modal asks for confirmation in the application's modal, then deletes the image from the whole campaign. This also cleans up dependent saved projects and native scenes, preserving floor, wall and door geometry. Other unsaved changes in the current project are retained. Undo cannot restore the deleted file. Tiles brushes, erasing and sampling In Tiles , the floor tool has five drawing options: - Brush: drag with a square or round brush. With snapping enabled, it paints cells; the round stamp is centered on the pointer's cell and the square stamp starts there. With snapping disabled, both brushes follow the pointer continuously, centered on it, with fractional sizes from 0.05 cells. Strokes connect pointer positions without gaps. A hover guide shows the actual area. Use the size buttons or / to decrease/increase the brush size. - Rectangle: drag between opposite corners to fill a rectangular area. - Circle: press at the center and drag to set the radius. - Polygon: click at least three vertices, then press Enter or double-click to finish. Finish and Cancel offer the same actions in Tools . Press Escape to cancel the unfinished shape. - Bucket fill (G): replace connected cells with the same material and rotation on the active layer. Variants of one floor family count as the same material; empty space forms its own region. Connections use the four neighboring cells. With snapping disabled, this tool becomes Fill shape : it changes the clicked floor's material while retaining its exact outline and erased holes. Snap to the grid controls floor geometry as well as pointer positions. With it disabled, rectangles use fractional corners, circles have smooth round outlines, polygons retain their drawn vertices and brush strokes follow free paths. These shapes remain free geometry when saving, reopening or generating the scene. Grid visibility is an independent display setting. Choose Operation → Erase floor to remove only the covered floor area using the brush or a shape. Other layers and object types remain intact. Erasing a large floor preserves its uncovered pieces. With snapping disabled, the eraser follows the same free geometry as the brush and shapes. When cutting legacy rectangles by grid cells, an operation that would leave a fragment below their 0.05-cell minimum is rejected without changing it. Sample (I) or Alt-click a floor on the active layer to reuse its concrete image and texture rotation. Sampling returns to the paint brush. In Tools , Erase (E) deletes a whole clicked object, while Pan (H) moves the view. Snapped floor painting fills grid cells. For new or different material, a family chooses one member at random for each cell and saves that concrete image reference in a 1 × 1 floor tile. Free painting chooses one concrete image for the complete stroke or shape. The choices remain stable through the gesture preview, undo/redo, reopening and scene generation. Families for walls, doors and objects choose an image for each new placement. Each complete stroke or shape is one undo step. In Tiles, painting the same floor again leaves the covered area unchanged, without adding objects or an undo step. Existing eligible family variants keep their images. With snapping enabled, each matching cell is skipped independently. Without snapping, a stroke or shape is ignored when its complete area already has the same material, including coverage shared by several floors. Holes and another material painted above that floor still need painting. A different floor replaces the covered area on the active layer, removing the old material underneath. A free stroke crossing matching and different materials replaces its complete footprint. Geometry outside that footprint and floors on other layers remain intact. Opening an existing project does not rewrite its floors. The project still has a combined limit of 2,000 objects. If a stroke or shape would exceed that limit, the whole operation is rejected without changing the map. Native lights, effects and editing windows Panels → Tools controls floor stamp size, wall/door thickness, floor texture orientation and object dimensions/rotation for the active tool. Its material selector also chooses a family, a library image or the default appearance. Snap to the grid toggles snapping. Object in Tools places an image inside its configured bounding box while preserving the image's aspect ratio. Lights in the library offers the VTT's Steady , Torch and Pulse presets. Choose one and click the map to place a native light. Selection exposes bright/dim radii, color, intensity, animation, cone angle, rotation, elevation and enabled state. Light placement requires the host's dynamic lighting feature. Lights do not use image assets. Effects offers the VTT's native particle profiles and shader presets. Choose a preset and click the map, then use Selection to adjust its native properties: particle type, density and scale, or shader radius, opacity, intensity, speed and blend mode, plus position, rotation, color, enabled state and light interaction. Effects are project objects with layers, selection, movement, duplication, rotation, deletion and undo/redo. Their centers stay inside the map; their visible extent can reach beyond that center, like a light's radius. The game's editing windows are available inside the builder. Double-click a wall, light, particle emitter or shader, or use its edit action in Selection . The light and effect windows are the same components used at the table: shaders include the full GLSL editor, preset library and AI prompt helper; particles and lights expose their own native controls. The prompt helper copies instructions and accepts pasted code; it does not contact an AI service. Walls and doors use the game's Configure wall/door window for presentation, movement, vision, light and sound blocking, elevation limits and secret-door discovery. For a door, use Selection to open that window; double-clicking still opens its separate Smart object behavior editor. Physical barrier settings and behavior graphs belong to the same object and can be edited independently. Each window edits a private project draft and previews its supported changes locally. Save applies the complete edit as one undo step. Cancel , close and Escape discard it. Opening or changing a window never edits the selected game scene or the players' scene. Save/reopen and generation preserve these settings; applying them to a linked scene requires Update scene . In Effects , the library selector shows Particles or Shaders , filters the search and arms that tool with its last preset without placing an object or adding an undo step. Returning to an image category restores the previous collection filter. The canvas and Preview use the tabletop's native animated renderer for these lights and effects, including walls and door openings. The overlay follows the builder camera and layer visibility; Preview temporarily shows all project layers. Hidden or empty effect layers release their renderer. These elements remain dynamic native objects when generating or updating the scene, outside the raster background. They can be edited afterward with the VTT's normal tools. With grid snapping enabled, ordinary wall gestures follow horizontal or vertical cell boundaries and use whole-cell intersections. Nearby existing endpoints and edges take priority and may be fractional; extending from an existing fractional endpoint preserves that anchor. Turn snapping off to draw diagonal walls or use fractional coordinates. Moving a selection containing walls uses whole-cell offsets while snapping is enabled. Opening a saved project does not realign existing walls or doors. Near map edges, a group containing walls stops at the last permitted whole-cell offset instead of using a fractional remainder. All objects keep their relative positions. With Select , Shift-click adds or removes individual objects, and dragging an empty area selects objects intersecting the rectangle. Select all includes editable objects on visible, unlocked layers. Duplicate and Rotate apply to the whole selection; quarter turns rotate floors and their texture orientation along with walls, doors, objects and lights. A group move uses a single clamped offset to preserve relative positions. An invalid transform changes nothing, including when it would overlap another door. Each operation is one undo step. Wall joins and editable nodes Select one wall with Select to show its endpoint circles and plus handles. Dragging an endpoint moves every wall sharing that point in the same editable layer, including walls with different materials or thicknesses. Doors keep their own geometry. A locked or hidden layer cannot be edited through these handles. The middle + divides the wall into two segments. Drag it to create and move the new corner in one gesture. The + beside either endpoint extends the wall: drag it, or click it and then click the map to confirm the new endpoint. Nearby editable endpoints and edges attract the endpoint; connecting to an edge creates a shared T node. This proximity snapping also works with grid snapping off. Escape cancels a drag or armed extension. Each completed node move, split or extension is one undo step. Focus a handle with the keyboard: Enter or Space activates a plus, and arrow keys move an endpoint by one cell with grid snapping on, or 0.1 cell with it off; Shift uses a whole cell. Enter confirms an armed extension at the current pointer position. Invalid or out-of-bounds edits leave the source unchanged. Extension prompts and recovery messages appear at the lower left of the canvas, aligned with the zoom controls. On narrow screens, messages sit above the view controls and wrap without covering their buttons. Connected corners and T junctions use joined wall artwork in the canvas, Preview and generated image. Contiguous collinear segments with the same layer, image and thickness share a texture origin and direction, preserving the pattern when a segment is reversed. Isolated walls retain their authored direction. Door openings remain clear. These visual joins do not add collision walls or rewrite saved endpoints when opening a project. Door rotation Select one door and choose Rotation anchor point in its properties or game editor: Start of door , Center of door or End of door . The marker on the selected door shows its pivot. Rotate keeps that point fixed; existing doors default to the center. With an explicit anchor, opening rotates the image 90° around that point and closing restores it. Default (center) retains the original behavior of hiding the image when open. Explicit Blueprint hidden appearances remain hidden. Multiple objects rotate around their selection's center. The choice follows Undo/Redo, automatic saving, duplication and generated scene updates, and also controls rotation of a single door with the game's Select tool. Empty Objects Choose Library → Objects → Empty Object , or Panels → Tools → Empty Object , then click or drag to place an image-free object. In Selection, edit its name, size, rotation and layer. Selection, moving, duplication and multiple selection work like other objects. Double-click it to edit the same Smart Object nodes, states, signals and actions as an ordinary object. Events only start the sequence; logic nodes make decisions. Use it as a controller for lights, sounds and other elements without placing an image. In the game, it is placed directly on the GM layer.
