Concurrent changes to the same calibration field conflict; native raster size changes conflict because they require a fresh background, rather than silently stretching the saved source image. Doors and decorations optionally store strict Boolean interactionEnabled ; absence retains the enabled default without rewriting older documents. Optional editingMode: "tiles" "paint" selects the workspace; an omitted value defaults to Tiles without rewriting an older source. Terrain strokes optionally store floor.brush: {operation, points, radius, hardness} . Each point contains normalized u, v, alpha coordinates inside the floor box, radius contains normalized horizontal/vertical radii, hardness ranges from 0 to 1, and operation is paint or erase . Paint uses source-over coverage; erase removes coverage from earlier floors on the same layer. The same brush representation is used by the canvas and server rasterization. Existing floor paint: {color, opacity} remains readable independently of the terrain brush. Color is six-digit hex or null for a texture/default material; solid color requires assetId: null . Opacity ranges from 0 to 1 and multiplies texture alpha and shape coverage. Reading and rendering retain stored geometry/styles; rows without paint retain their existing output. Free floors optionally store shape: {contours, cuts} . Each entry is a polygon ring of normalized u, v points inside the floor's bounding box; coverage is the union of contours minus the union of cuts, with even-odd fill inside each ring. Shape-free rows retain the existing rectangular format. Moving/resizing uses that box, and quarter turns rotate the normalized geometry with the floor. Asset classifications may have a project-local name , collection and optional family . The family string adds metadata to version 3 without changing the schema version; projects without it retain their existing behavior. Membership derives from entries in assets with the same type and family name. Painted objects retain their concrete assetId ; reading or rendering a project does not choose another family member. Coordinates and thicknesses use grid cells; generated native coordinates use pixels. Every logical object has a UUID. Doors store their own endpoints ( x1 , y1 , x2 , y2 ), thickness, optional image and initial state, just as walls have their own geometry. An optional door blueprint extends schema version 3 without changing its version. The current blueprint format is version 2 , with an element kind , fixed state-value definitions and optional graphs . Doors, levers and torches accept interact and destroy ; regions accept presence:enter , presence:exit and destroy . Named receivers use signal:<name . Event nodes carry only their exact event ID and layout, and expose one execution output, next ; they have no state filter or comparison parameter. Loading older containers promotes their format and discards change , enter:<state , exit:<state and interact:<state graphs, without converting their actions or removing scene elements and asset files. States store default appearance and optional assetId . Nodes store their ID, type, layout position and typed parameters; execution edges require kind: "execution" and from , to , output . Ordered fan-out is supported. Typed value edges use kind: "data" and target input , with one source per input. Pure value nodes accept no execution edges. A native door may also carry a live sprite set by Change sprite. It is play state like door_state : audiences receive only the resulting appearance. A state action does not emit another event or automatically clear that sprite. The instance node projects the real object without storing a second current state. A reference's saved output ID remains door ; its value type is now element , preserving existing connections while accepting compatible live element references. A decoration may carry lever: {"state": "off"} (or "on" ) and an optional version 2 , kind: "lever" blueprint with those two states. Change sprite nodes can use any imported campaign image, including materials. State appearances use assets classified as decoration . Generated native images keep their box and base-image metadata in private lever data; participant projections include only lever.state and the active image. Scene updates keep live state and detect conflicts in manual changes to the generated image. Ordinary images controlled by Change sprite use a private spriteBase: {assetId, layer, width, height} restoration record, with pixel box dimensions and a live sprite appearance. Participant projections omit both. Native edits preserve or adopt the bounded box; campaign archives remap its asset ID and validate the active image, fit and ownership before committing an import. Generated decorations whose fitted scale exceeds the ordinary image editor's range use the same restoration record, retaining their authored pixel box through generation, native edits, scene updates and campaign copies. Source light targets use authored IDs and are remapped to native scene IDs during generation. Doors without this field retain their existing behavior. Asset classification belongs to the project rather than changing the campaign image for all other uses. Versions 1 and 2 remain readable. The editor upgrades them to one Base layer without rounding endpoints; version 1 wall-linked doors are converted without moving or discarding them. Merely reading an old project does not change its stored document or revision. By default, the raster contains the background, repeated floor textures and wall strips. Artwork explicitly marked dynamic uses the separate native composition described above. Wall artwork uses the bounding box of pixels with alpha at least 8 , discarding transparent padding without altering the uploaded image. The cropped image's horizontal direction follows the wall from start to end. Its aspect ratio sets the repeat length at the configured wall thickness, so horizontal, vertical and diagonal walls show the same proportions. Repeats keep their position along the original wall across door openings. The editor and generated image use this same placement. Floors and then wall strips follow project layer order within each paint pass; layer reordering does not interleave those object types. Decorations become native map-layer images; lights, particles and shaders remain native editable objects with their animation and lighting behavior. Neither is baked into the raster, so the native VTT can render and edit them. Collinear wall intervals occupied by doors are omitted from both the raster and ordinary native walls, even when a door spans several wall segments. Each door creates its own native segment, with its normal movement, vision, light and sound behavior. Its optional image is rendered separately. Without a blueprint appearance override, it appears while closed or locked and disappears when open. Deleting that image preserves the native door's geometry. This default behavior requires no object behavior graph. Deleting a campaign image removes its classifications and material references from saved projects, preserving their geometry with the default appearance. Other members of its asset family and their existing placements are preserved. Project revisions advance so open editors must refresh before saving again. This known asset cleanup also updates ownership history, so the linked scene can still be updated without restoring deleted artwork. Deleted state images revert to native appearance in source and native blueprints, as do Change sprite nodes that used them; a live sprite using the image is cleared. Set appearance actions using a deleted material are removed and their execution continuations reconnected; connected data references never become execution wires. Deleting a campaign sound removes its sound nodes and reconnects their continuations in both the current source and the generated snapshot, including dynamic-surface recipes, so campaign copies remain importable after deletion. Deleting a native light removes the affected live action references; deleting a generated light still causes the normal scene-update conflict. builder_render.py rasterizes the validated document; builder_services.py uses the existing tiling.generate_pyramid pipeline and persists scene metadata, tiles, walls and the GM's private selection in one transaction. Rendering occurs before the write transaction; permissions, source revision and asset ownership are checked again before publication. Storage written for a failed operation is removed. Realtime invalidation happens after commit. Runtime resources and scene refresh Event execution reuses read-only asset, sound, light and blueprint inventories within one command, then discards them. Mutable states and ownership are checked again on later commands. A token's accepted path is projected once for an area pass, preserving listener order and teleport cancellation. Multiple area events retain all their history entries while publishing one history invalidation after commit. Rollback, permission checks and retry receipts remain authoritative. Committed scene changes reach the board before dependent audio/combat refreshes. Changing an ordinary image replaces its texture in place, retaining the previous art until the replacement is ready. Unchanged art is reused, including across light/geometry rebuilds within the same scene. The scene owns a bounded cache of recently used textures and releases it on scene/role changes and disposal. It loads only art in the viewer's current authorized scene projection. HTTP operations and limits All endpoints below are under /api/containers/<campaign_id /map-builder : Method and suffix Purpose --- --- GET Project summaries, campaign image/sound metadata and current limits GET /projects/<project_id Read the editable source and revision POST /projects/<project_id Create or save a project POST /projects/<project_id /generate Generate a scene from the saved revision POST /projects/<project_id /update Update the linked scene from the saved revision POST /projects/<project_id /sync Import compatible changes from owned native objects into the source project GET /templates List this campaign's GM-owned behavior templates GET /templates/<template_id Read a typed template definition and revision POST /templates/<template_id Create/update a snapshot template DELETE /templates/<template_id Delete a template with its expected revision GET /testing-catalog GM-only campaign actor choices for rehearsal POST /test Rehearse an unsaved document without saving or generating it The GM scene-network endpoints are /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/network ( GET ) and /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/network/<element_id ( POST ). A save carries request_id , expected_version , expected_project_version (or null for standalone native elements) and blueprint . They use the existing command receipts and publish no private graphs to players or streamers. GM rehearsal uses POST /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/test/<element_id with request_id , expected_version , event , and optional tokenId and native blueprint draft. Builder rehearsal instead accepts request_id , document , source elementId , event and optional campaign actorId . Both return private traces, predicted changes, scheduling summaries and warnings, then roll back. Live controls use POST /api/maps/<scene_id /automation/control/<element_id with request_id , expected_version , action and value (omit value for interact ). Actions are state , interact , flame , visibility , appearance , interaction and region . A null appearance restores a managed surface's base artwork or an intelligent element's state appearance. Material choices must be ordinary campaign assets; generated masks are not reusable materials. Writes carry a UUID request_id and integer expected_version ; new projects expect version 0 . Save also carries folder_id and document . Retrying the same logical request returns its receipt. Reusing that UUID for a different payload is rejected. A revision conflict requires rereading the current project; clients must not silently overwrite another saved revision. Update also carries expected_scene_version . Synchronization carries the same two expected revisions and returns {project, scene, synchronized} without changing the native scene. Its generation manifest records generated object IDs, authored source identities, kinds, data and a private sourceDocument baseline; only those owned resources can be replaced or removed. An update rechecks permissions, revisions, ownership and generated data after rendering, inside the publication transaction. Notifications occur after commit, and superseded tile files are removed only after successful publication. Limits include a 1 MB source document, 32 project layers, 2,000 combined floor/wall/door/decoration/light/particle/shader/region objects, 5,000 generated native objects, 256 classified images, dimensions of 1–200 cells and cell sizes of 16–256 px. The output is also limited to 16,777,216 pixels or the configured server limit, whichever is smaller; the dimension limits cannot all be used simultaneously. Painted surface complexity is bounded separately. Uploads reuse the campaign image endpoint and its 25 MB / 40 million decoded pixel limits. Free-floor geometry allows up to 128 contour/cut rings per floor, 256 vertices per ring, 4,096 points per floor and 16,384 points per document. Additional pixel-area and edge/scan-line budgets bound mask rendering; exceeding a limit rejects the whole gesture or server operation. Blueprints allow up to 32 nodes and 64 connections per event graph, with at most 128 nodes across a door's graphs. Each graph requires one matching event node; cycles, references to missing graph nodes and duplicate connections are rejected. State transitions and executed actions are also bounded on the server. Delivery plan Use the Smart Objects design direction (smart-objects-direction.md) for proposed adapters, visual node organization, animation and cross-scene/group transport. The supported behaviors and their limits are documented in this guide; future plans do not change saved project, permission or system-package contracts.

title: Universal VTT import and export
summary: Import/export workflows, coordinates, limits and authorization.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/universal-vtt.md) · Map Builder (map-builder.md) Use Universal VTT to bring a finished map, its grid, walls, doors and lights into Gravewright, or to download an interchange copy of a native scene. Only a campaign GM can import or export. Imported scenes start visible only to the GM and do not replace the scene currently broadcast to players. Choose the import path The Builder offers two different import actions: What you have Action Result --- --- --- A .uvtt , .dd2vtt or .df2vtt file containing an image and map data Import Universal VTT in Builder A new linked native scene and editable Builder project with compatible walls, doors and lights The same file, when only a game scene is needed New scene → Import Universal VTT A native scene; use Edit with MapBuilder later to create its source A PNG, JPEG, WebP or TIFF image Import ready-made map A background in the current Builder project; add walls, objects, lights and behaviors over it For an image, choose Library → Import → Import ready-made map , or the same action in Settings or Saved projects . Upload an image (up to 25 MB) or choose an existing campaign image, set the width and height in cells and the cell size, then choose Use map image . The image fills the map beneath its layers. Project changes save automatically; Generate scene or Update scene applies them to the game. See Import a finished map (map-builder.md import-a-finished-map) for replacement, removal and Undo/Redo. A Universal VTT import cannot reconstruct the source map's brush strokes, individual assets or Builder layers from its flattened background. Importing from Builder saves the current draft first, creates a separate linked project and loads it in the editor. Compatible collision geometry and lights remain editable; the flattened background remains one image. Both paths keep the new scene GM-only. Import a Universal VTT scene 1. In Scenes , choose New scene → Import Universal VTT . To import into a scene folder, start the new-scene action from that folder. The same importer is available under Saved projects → Import Universal VTT in the Builder. 2. Select the Universal VTT file and check Scene name . Selecting a file fills an empty name from its filename; you can change it. Names must contain 1–120 characters. The dialog has no grid or lighting controls: those values come from the file. 3. Choose Import scene and wait for the result. The import dialog cannot close while this request is running. 4. Read the warnings, then choose Close . Warnings describe the scene already created; there is no approval or preview step before creation. 5. Inspect the scene in Scenes . Check grid alignment, wall openings, door states and lighting with the native scene tools before activating it for players. The destination folder comes from the action that opened the importer; there is no folder picker inside the dialog. The folder must belong to this campaign. The background is stored as scene tiles, while walls, doors and lights remain editable native objects. Import from the scene directory creates no Builder project; import from Builder creates and loads one. Neither path overwrites an existing scene or Builder draft. Update scene applies Builder edits to the same linked scene. Import warnings report objects that must remain native. Read the import warnings Warnings indicate an imported approximation, rather than a failed import: Warning concerns What to check --- --- Portals imported as doors Every portal becomes a door. Check intended windows, movement and sight behavior, and whether each opening should start open or closed. Ambient color Colored ambient light becomes an approximation using scene darkness. Baked lighting Lights start disabled because the file says the image already contains lighting. Check before enabling them to avoid lighting the artwork twice. Light range or intensity Ranges above 200 cells and intensities above 1 are clamped to those maxima. Zero-range lights These start disabled. Set an appropriate native radius before enabling them. Per-light shadows Per-light shadow settings have no direct equivalent. Degenerate wall segments Extremely short segments were ignored; inspect the surrounding wall. Recover from an import error If validation fails, read the message, correct the name or source file and choose Import scene again. Invalid files, unsupported images or excessive geometry do not leave a partially created scene. If the file contains lights and the installation reports Dynamic lighting is disabled , the operator must enable that feature or provide a file without lights. If the connection fails, the server may already have completed the import. Keep the same dialog open, leave the file and name unchanged and choose Import scene again: the dialog reuses the operation's request UUID and the server returns the original result instead of creating another scene. There is no separate Retry button or automatic retry. Changing either field or reopening the dialog starts a new operation. After closing the dialog or reloading the page following an uncertain result, check Scenes before importing again, to avoid creating a second scene. Export the current scene If you are working in the Builder, first finish Generate scene or Update scene . Automatic saving stores the project; exporting reads the native scene already applied to the game, including its subsequent native edits. A saved project or an unpublished draft is not the export source. 1. Right-click the scene in Scenes and choose Export Universal VTT . 2. Choose Prepare export and wait for preparation to finish. 3. Review the warnings, then choose Download Universal VTT to save a .uvtt file. The prepared download is a snapshot. If the scene changes after preparation, close and reopen the exporter to prepare a new copy. You can close the export dialog while preparation is pending. Export does not modify the scene, project, receipts or stored artwork. What the download keeps Content Exported representation --- --- Map background and visible scene images One embedded PNG; individual image objects and materials become pixels Dynamic floors and walls Flattened with their current material, mask, opacity, rotation and layer erasure Door artwork Current appearance, including the open quarter-turn around an explicit start, center or end anchor Grid and origin Cell size and coordinate alignment; fractional pixel cell sizes are rounded and the raster resampled, with a warning Walls and doors Wall segments and portals reflecting current open/closed state Enabled native lights Position, color, intensity and range; cones, animation, elevation and unlimited ranges are approximated GM-only image artwork is omitted. Locks, secret-door presentation, height ranges and separate movement, vision, light and sound barrier channels are not preserved. A secret door's geometry can still be present: check the file before sharing it with players. Blueprints, variables, timers, presence regions, tokens, cards, markers, journal permissions, particles, shaders, fog, drawings and audio are not transferred. Disabled lights are omitted. The file does not restore a Builder project or campaign state, and another application's interpretation may differ. Keep the original project and use the installation's backup process for recovery. If preparation fails, read the error before trying again. Missing or unreadable background tiles and exceeded composition limits prevent a complete export; the dialog does not offer a partial download. Format and coordinate contract The accepted container is JSON with numeric format: 0.2 or format: 0.3 ; the three supported filename extensions use this contract. Export uses 0.2 . These are interchange versions, independent of the Gravewright application version. Import requires an embedded, single-frame PNG or WebP image encoded as raw base64, not a data URL, file path or remote URL. Image metadata is removed; EXIF orientation is not applied to map coordinates. Input field Interpretation --- --- resolution.map_size Positive width ( x ) and height ( y ) in cells resolution.pixels_per_grid Integral numeric pixels per cell ( 70 and 70.0 are equivalent) resolution.map_origin Origin offset in cells; fractional values retain grid alignment line_of_sight , objects_line_of_sight Polylines split into consecutive native wall segments portals .bounds Two endpoints defining the native door; collinear walls are cut around its opening portals .closed Required boolean: true means closed, false means open lights Cell-based position and range, intensity, color and shadow setting environment Baked-lighting flag and ambient color Image dimensions must equal the rounded products of map_size and pixels_per_grid . For example, a 20 × 15-cell map at 70 pixels per cell needs a 1400 × 1050-pixel image. Object positions become (point - map_origin) × pixels_per_grid . Portal bounds determine door geometry; portal position , rotation and freestanding do not add separate native placement or behavior. Portal cutting uses a separate bounded geometry adapter and tolerates producer rounding up to 0.05 pixels when matching a collinear wall. It retains the original door coordinates; walls beyond that tolerance are unaffected. Optional software and creator labels are bounded metadata; they never become paths or executable data. Colors accept six-digit RRGGBB or eight-digit AARRGGBB , optionally prefixed with . Light alpha multiplies the clamped intensity. For example, color 80ff0000 and intensity 1 produce a red light with intensity approximately 0.502 . Imported range becomes the dim radius, with a zero bright radius. Limits and authorization These limits apply in addition to installation configuration: Resource Limit --- --- JSON upload/download 64 MiB Embedded compressed image 48 MiB Raster area 16,777,216 pixels, or the lower configured map/Pillow limit Native objects, including wall segments after portal cuts 5,000 Line-of-sight vertices 20,000 Wall/portal intersection checks 2,000,000 Floor composition groups during export 32 Cumulative export composition work 134,217,728 pixels Pixels per grid cell Integer from 1 to 10,000 Input light range / intensity Finite, nonnegative, at most 1,000,000; clamped to native 200 cells / 1 Configured upload bytes, image dimensions and tile-count limits may be lower. Duplicate JSON keys, invalid numbers or base64, unsupported or animated images, inconsistent dimensions and excessive geometry are rejected. Uploaded filenames never become server paths. Artwork used during export must belong to the campaign; generated masks must also belong to that exact scene. Players and streamers cannot import or export. Import rechecks GM membership and folder ownership before committing, records a request receipt and removes newly stored tiles if the operation fails. The same request UUID with the same file, name and folder replays the original result; a changed payload with that UUID is rejected as a conflict. Import through the public interface never activates the new scene for players. HTTP contract and implementation checks - POST /api/containers/{campaign}/universal-vtt/import : multipart file , name , request_id , optional folderId and optional string builderEditable: "true" "false" (default false); returns {scene, warnings, builderEditable} and project when editable. The mode is included in the receipt fingerprint; scene/project/file creation rolls back together. - GET /api/maps/{scene}/universal-vtt : returns {filename, document, warnings} . document is the downloadable UVTT JSON. The service is universal_vtt.py (../../gravewright/maps/universal_vtt.py), with GM-only HTTP views (../../gravewright/maps/universal_vtt_views.py) and the import/export dialog (../../gravewright/maps/static/gravewright_maps/universal-vtt.js). Focused tests (../../gravewright/maps/tests/test_universal_vtt.py) cover geometry, grid/ARGB conversion, current artwork, receipts, rollback, isolation and limits. The browser scenario (../../tests/e2e/map_builder_universal_vtt.py) covers the public modals, a lost-response retry, downloads, round trips and role boundaries. Use the isolated environments described in Testing (testing.md). The shared scene adapter (../../gravewright/maps/builder_import.py) is also used by Edit with MapBuilder . Its integration tests (../../gravewright/maps/tests/test_builder_import.py) cover scene identity, native edits, cloning and rollback; validation tests (../../gravewright/maps/tests/test_builder_import_validation.py) cover exact bounds, image scale, native-only properties and bounded query work.

title: Application workflow reference
summary: Complete project guide to campaign preparation and tabletop tools.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/user-guide.md) Accounts and campaigns Create the first VTT owner at /setup , then sign in at /login . Other users register at /register . The owner manages the host and creates campaigns from /inside . A campaign is also called a container in HTTP routes and a table in browser/realtime interfaces. The native ruleset is Gravewright PDF System , with character actors. Invite players using a campaign join code; the campaign GM configures expiration and maximum uses and can revoke codes. Successful first-time joins increment the usage count automatically. Membership gives a player access to a campaign, while document and scene permissions determine what they can actually see or change. A streamer link provides a restricted read-only view and is not a player account. In Systems and Modules , Install lists the newest compatible, non-revoked version of each package. Search, categories and pagination operate on that selection. VTT update alerts The installation owner has a bell next to their name in the library header. A gold marker appears when a newer verified VTT release is available. Open it to compare installed and available versions; View update opens Administration directly on the Updates tab. Installation still requires the owner's explicit action there. Discovery runs without blocking the library. The visible page refreshes the indicator every five minutes, reusing the host's 24-hour release cache. Check for updates in Administration performs an explicit fresh check and updates the bell immediately. Player accounts do not receive host administration alerts. The Updates tab highlights the full installed release name and loads its bundled notes immediately, including offline. It has no release-channel selector. When a newer version is available, its name and notes appear with the installation controls. Notes support readable headings, lists, code and safe links; Portuguese notes are selected when available for a Portuguese interface. Prepare the table Before entering play, choose Manage campaign on the campaign card. Its GM workspace (campaign-management.md) edits the same campaign records without starting the table connection or joining presence. Prepare the dashboard, session plans, timeline/calendar, quest columns and prerequisites, connections, player previews and journal history/trash there. Scenes, character sheets, files and other native tools remain available from that workspace. 1. Create a campaign and open its table. 2. Create/import a map scene and configure its grid and initial view. Activate for players makes that scene player-visible and broadcasts it. Opening a scene privately does not share it. 3. Create actors, attach PDF sheets when needed, and place their tokens in the scene. Actor data and placed token state are related but distinct; a token represents an actor on a particular map. 4. Prepare journals, handouts and resources, granting access intentionally. Check with a separate player session before sharing. 5. Invite players, use the lobby/readiness controls where enabled, and broadcast the intended scene. Board tools include selection, movement, drawing, measurement, walls, fog, lighting, map pings and effects. Permissions and the active tool determine available actions. The GM can prepare hidden material without broadcasting it. Rendering depends on browser WebGL capability and the scene's complexity. Enter Map Builder As the campaign GM, open New scene . Choose the workflow that matches your source: Source and goal Action Result --- --- --- An image you want to use directly as a scene Upload map A native scene with its configured grid and visibility A map you want to build or keep editing as a project Map Builder An editable project; generating a scene is a separate action A finished image you want to add walls, objects or behaviors over Map Builder → Library → Import → Import ready-made map A project background with editable elements above it A .uvtt , .dd2vtt or .df2vtt file New scene → Import Universal VTT , or the Builder's import action A GM-only native scene; the Builder path also creates a linked editable project Importing an image does not detect walls or reconstruct its original layers. The scene-directory importer creates only a native scene. The Builder importer also creates a linked project. Use Edit Scene in the table's top bar to open or adopt the selected existing scene; compatible native geometry remains editable over its background. The importer/exporter guide (universal-vtt.md) explains supported fields and warnings. For a first Builder project: 1. Choose New scene → Map Builder and name the project in the header. Entering the Builder preserves the players' current scene. 2. Use Panels → Settings for map dimensions and cell size. The header chooses Tiles or Painting ; Panels → Tools holds the active brush options. 3. Import your own images through Library → Import , or choose a ready-made map background. Set the grid dimensions to match the image. 4. Paint floors and add walls, doors, objects, lights or effects. Panels → Layers controls the active layer, visibility, locks and contents. Select an element and use Panels → Selection for its properties. 5. Wait for the header to report that the project is saved. Edits save automatically; the status button and Ctrl+S synchronize immediately. Reopen saved work through Panels → Projects . 6. Use Preview to inspect the map. Use Test behavior for an available Smart Object graph; rehearsal reports predictions without committing gameplay effects. See the Map Builder guide (map-builder.md) for supported objects. 7. Choose Generate scene to create a private native scene. After linking, the header action becomes Update scene to apply later project edits to that same scene. A revision conflict stops the update for explicit recovery. 8. In Scenes , use Activate for players when the scene is ready to share. These actions have different effects: Action What it changes --- --- Automatic saving / Ctrl+S The editable project Generate scene / Update scene Native scene artwork and generated resources Activate for players Scene visibility and the players' broadcast If saving fails, keep the tab open and use the recovery controls. Reload saved project adopts the server version; Save a copy preserves the local document under a new project identity. A browser draft is recovery storage, not a backup. The Map Builder guide (map-builder.md) covers drawing modes, asset removal, layer operations, Smart Objects, shortcuts, limits and troubleshooting. During a game Open Mind maps , Clues and Clocks from their icons in the lower dock. Hover or focus an icon to read its tooltip. The campaign manager keeps these tools in its sidebar. Area Purpose --- --- Actors and tokens Character data, PDF field mapping, placed tokens, movement and visual state PDF System (pdf-system.md) Manual fields on noneditable PDFs, field actions, formulas, mapping templates and filled-PDF export Clocks (clocks.md) and clues (clues.md) Campaign/scene progress and discoveries, shared with the manager and MapBuilder mechanisms Mind maps (mindmaps.md) Movable topic graphs, notes, completion and typed campaign links; selected player editors collaborate on the table while the GM manages access Chat and dice Shared messages, supported private/GM projections, rolls and presets Journals (journals.md) Diaries, quests, quest boards, weighted roll tables, image/PDF attachments and campaign resource references Audio Uploaded tracks, playlists, synchronized playback and positional sound controls Cards Deck assets, drawing, hands and table card state Combat Encounter turns, initiative and effects Compendiums Reusable content packs, access controls and imports Modules Optional browser extensions and replacement/overlay surfaces Use the dice notation reference (../../gravewright/dice/grammar/notation/GRAMMAR.md) for supported expressions. Journal rich text is stored as structured documents; access to GM sections and handouts is filtered by the server. An export or screenshot may have a different audience from the live table, so select what you share deliberately. Diaries support empty chapters and nested subchapters. Each page can belong to one chapter or none; removing a chapter keeps its pages and subchapters. Use the page index to organize the tree in the table or campaign manager. In editable journal text, type / to insert blocks or @ to open the campaign reference picker. Opening a reference checks the target's current permissions; sharing the journal does not share a private target. See the journal guide (journals.md) for page destinations, unavailable references and player editing. Browser audio may require a user interaction before playback. If the table stops updating, check connection status and reconnect; refreshing a page reloads authorized state. Module activation changes may require clients to load the new module set before issuing extension calls. Preserve content Campaign export/import, cloning and snapshots are available according to host feature settings and permissions. Full campaign archives include preparation, clocks, clues, mind maps, PDF mapping templates and journal history/trash with their retained files. Portable exports remove user-specific permissions and omit chat; snapshots also preserve access/chat for restoration. Resource-only compendium exports omit preparation and history. These files are not full instance backups. Before restoring a snapshot or replacing campaign contents, use the recovery procedures in deployment (deployment.md). Maps, music, PDFs and other uploads retain their own licenses and ownership. The project license does not authorize redistribution of game books or media you do not own. Modules may use different licenses; see licensing (../../LICENSING.md). Current limits - Host catalogs include English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish. English is the default when no preference is saved. Changing the interface language does not translate authored names, text or assets; installed systems provide their own translations. - The native PDF ruleset does not provide item types; the generic item backend should not be read as a complete native item editor/catalog. - The provided extension loader runs JavaScript in the main page. Install code you trust; signatures do not provide isolation. - Online marketplace discovery requires a catalog and trusted publisher keys. Managed hosts install core updates from Administration after the owner requests them. Django packages in Modules activate for the entire server and restart it automatically; browser modules remain table-specific. For development or integrations, continue with the API (api.md) and module (modules.md) guides.

title: Campaign management
summary: Native GM preparation, seven planning tools, archives and history outside the table.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (Brasil) (../pt-BR/campaign-management.md) · User guide (user-guide.md) Use Manage campaign on a campaign card or its cover preview to prepare campaign content before entering the tabletop. The link opens /campaigns/<campaign-uuid /manage for the selected campaign. Access follows the current campaign membership. Every campaign GM can use it, including a co-GM whose account has the participant role. A host owner who is only a player in that campaign receives no management access. Players, streamers and nonmembers cannot use this GM workspace. Changing or revoking membership takes effect on subsequent authorized requests. Content tools The management area uses the campaign's existing documents and native editors. There is no second campaign copy to merge back into the table. Area What to prepare --- --- Journals and quests Diaries, pages, quests, quest boards and roll tables in the native journal editors, with their normal attachments and access rules Clocks (clocks.md) Progress clocks for the campaign or selected scene, with visibility, player controls and pinning shared with the table Clues (clues.md) Staged discoveries shared with the table; content is delivered to players only after completion and public visibility Mind maps (mindmaps.md) Topic graphs with notes, branches and links to native resources; the GM configures readers and selected player editors, who use the same graphs on the table Characters and PDF sheets (pdf-system.md) Campaign actors and system sheets; in the PDF System, PDF selection, manual fields, saved rolls, calculations and reusable mappings Items Item documents and forms supplied by the campaign's installed system Scenes and MapBuilder Campaign scenes, editable map projects and compatible existing scenes; generating or updating a scene remains an explicit operation File library Campaign images, PDFs and audio through the native upload, folder and file tools Audio Tracks, playlists and the campaign's supported audio configuration Cards Native decks, card artwork and permitted deck operations Compendiums Authorized campaign and installed content, using the existing catalog and document tools Members and permissions Invitations, current participants and the native document, folder and page access editors In Participants , Invite players creates an invitation valid for 24 hours with a maximum of 10 uses. The native modal displays the read-only code; Copy code copies it to the clipboard when selected. Remove participant opens a native confirmation modal identifying the person before submitting the removal. The campaign service rechecks the caller's GM membership and refuses removal of another GM or the caller's own membership. Journals and quests use the same document models and editors as the game. The management area does not introduce a separate note format or quest system. GM-only diary pages and private documents retain their existing audience rules. Opening a document or assigning it to a quest does not grant players permission to read its private contents. Character sheets opened from the actor directory edit the campaign actor. Independent token snapshots retain their own state and native synchronization rules. PDF layout changes remain GM operations; character values still follow the sheet's permissions. Item types and game rules belong to the installed system, so a system without item types does not gain an item catalog here. See the MapBuilder guide (map-builder.md) for adoption, linked sources and scene updates, and Universal VTT (universal-vtt.md) for import limits and warnings. Preparation tools These tools are for campaign GMs only. Session plans, timeline events, private notes and dashboard choices are stored with the campaign, and players never receive them. Each GM has their own dashboard. Other GMs see changes to shared records the next time the page refreshes, which happens automatically every 15 seconds. Area What it does --- --- Overview dashboard Pinned documents, the next planned session, pending work, sheet diagnostics and upcoming events. Customize dashboard shows, hides and reorders these panels for you Quests Columns for each quest status. Drag a card to another column, or use Move quest to from the keyboard. Cards show assigned characters, objective progress (objectives can be checked off on the card) and prerequisites. A quest that is active before its prerequisites are completed shows a warning Session planner An ordered sequence of scenes, encounters, quests, journals, characters, items, audio and notes, plus a checklist and private notes. Finish session records a summary and pending work; remaining steps and checklist entries are suggested as pending work. That pending work then appears on the dashboard Timeline Events with an in-world date as free text, an optional calendar date, an "upcoming" flag and links to campaign documents. Events are listed in the order you set. The calendar view shows events and planned sessions that have a calendar date Connections What a character, item, journal or scene links to, and where it is used: references in journal text, quest assignments and prerequisites, quest boards, scene pins, tokens, session plans and timeline links View as player Choose a player to see the journals, pages, characters, items and scenes the server sends that player. Journals open in a read-only preview of the player's version, with GM-only blocks removed History and trash Earlier versions of each journal, compared line by line with the current version. A GM can restore any of them. Deleted journals go to the trash, and restoring one brings back its identifier, pages, access, quest board links and files without restoring the rest of the campaign Type @ in editable journal text to open the reference picker in the manager. It searches campaign resources through the authorized HTTP API without joining the table. Each target retains its own access controls. In the manager, a scene reference selects that scene for preparation; on the table it opens the scene directory. Quest prerequisites are stored with the quest and are visible only to GMs. They cannot form a cycle. Editors that do not send prerequisites keep the stored ones. A version is recorded before each change to a journal. Saves by the same person within five minutes are combined into one version, and each journal keeps its 50 most recent versions. Restoring a version records the replaced content as a new version, so a restore can itself be undone. A version cannot be restored if it uses files that were later removed from the document. The trash keeps up to 200 deleted journals. Files belonging to a trashed journal are deleted only when that journal is deleted permanently. Map pins removed together with a journal are not recreated when it is restored. Sheet diagnostics come from the campaign system through the optional preparation.diagnostics system operation. The PDF System reports sheets with no PDF selected and saved calculations that cannot be evaluated; page geometry is still checked when a sheet is opened. Systems that do not provide this operation do not show the panel. Campaign exports, copies and snapshots include session plans, timeline events, dashboards and journal history, including files retained by the trash. Select Preparation when copying to include session plans, events and dashboard choices; history follows Journals . Copies include physical files. Portable imports assign one dashboard to the importing GM (their matching dashboard, or the first source dashboard, with the source owner's dashboard preferred), without adding campaign members or user permissions. Snapshots restore each current GM's own dashboard. Older archives that did not store preparation keep existing preparation and history when restored into a campaign. Select Mind maps separately to copy collaborative graphs. Typed links point to copied resources; omitted targets become unavailable without binding to the source campaign. Portable copies clear selected editor grants, while snapshots preserve them in the same campaign. Scene-scoped maps follow the scene selection. See Mind maps (mindmaps.md) for collaboration and resource permissions. Restoring a revision revalidates document visibility, prerequisite quests and files before saving. Its expected version is the one displayed in the comparison; if another GM edits the document, open a fresh comparison before restoring. Missing files leave the trash entry intact and report an error. Session drafts survive selecting the current session, and inputs are disabled while saving. Preparation allows 200 session plans and 1,000 timeline events per campaign. Each session holds up to 64 steps and 64 checklist entries, with up to 32 pending entries recorded when finishing. Each GM can pin 24 documents; each event can link to 24 documents. Calendar dates use YYYY-MM-DD ; an in-world date is authored text and the core does not interpret a game's calendar. Full campaign archives contain private preparation, GM notes and journal history. Share them only with their intended recipients. A portable import removes user-specific grants; it does not sanitize authored secrets into player handouts. Resource-only compendium exports omit preparation and history. Keep physical files when archiving trash attachments; exporting such an archive without its files is rejected. Preparing content and entering play Opening management does not start the tabletop canvas, Pixi renderer, game WebSocket connection or table presence. You can organize content without joining the live scene. Enter table remains a separate action. Saves change the shared campaign records. Explicit commands such as playback, broadcasting a scene or drawing cards retain their native effects and permissions; use them when you intend to change that campaign state. Merely opening management does not execute those commands. Keep the normal save and conflict workflow. Each new logical mutation uses a new request UUID; a retry of the same operation reuses its UUID. Revisions detect concurrent editing. If a document changed elsewhere, reload current state and review the edit rather than replacing its expected revision silently. Native editors keep their pending-save, closing and disposal behavior. Authorization and integration The server rechecks campaign membership, GM access and resource ownership. Hidden buttons are not the authorization boundary. A management URL or a known asset ID does not authorize access to another campaign. Content delivered to players and streamers remains filtered by the corresponding native services. The Inside page adds can_manage to its presentation rows using current memberships; the public campaign JSON format is unchanged. Management tools reuse the public browser API and native domain services instead of writing documents directly or creating separate stores. See the API reference (api.md) for revisions, receipts, file transfers and system-owned capabilities.

title: Journals and resource links
summary: Independent chapters, page access, campaign references and portable journal content.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/journals.md) Open Journals on the table or in the campaign manager (campaign-management.md). The manager edits the campaign's existing documents without joining the table. Diaries, pages, quests, quest boards and roll tables retain their native editors, attachments and access controls. On narrow screens, use Collapse pages to leave more room for the document. Show pages restores the page index. Rename a page from its heading While editing a page you own, click its name in the document header, or focus the name and press Enter or Space . Type a name of up to 120 characters. Enter or leaving the field confirms and saves it; Escape cancels. An empty name keeps the previous title. Renaming preserves the page's contents and links. Read-only pages and reading mode do not offer this control. Chapters and subchapters Chapters organize a diary independently of its pages. A chapter can be empty, contain several pages and contain subchapters. Each page belongs to at most one chapter; pages can also remain outside every chapter. Choose New chapter to create an empty chapter. Its form lets you name it and choose a parent chapter. A chapter's actions also provide New subchapter , Edit chapter , sibling ordering and Delete chapter . Editing a chapter can change its name or parent without changing its identity or the pages it contains. The parent selector excludes relationships that would make the hierarchy circular. Use a page's Move to chapter action to choose its chapter or No chapter . Deleting a chapter keeps its pages outside any chapter and moves its immediate subchapters to the deleted chapter's parent. Deleting a page remains a separate operation. Existing category groups become chapters when an older diary is opened; their pages and links remain in place. The hierarchy follows the diary's existing access controls. Players see chapters needed by their authorized pages, their ancestors and genuinely empty branches. A branch containing only hidden pages is omitted. Saving an editable public page preserves the private pages and chapter structure that the player cannot see. Reading and streamer access do not provide chapter editing controls. A diary supports up to 128 chapters, eight chapter levels and 64 pages. You cannot remove a chapter that is still required by protected pages; existing page permissions continue to apply when reorganizing the diary. Insert a campaign reference 1. Open a journal or page that you can edit and place the cursor in its rich text. 2. Type @ at the start of a paragraph or after a space. Search by name and use Resource type to narrow the campaign catalog. 3. Select a resource and choose Add link . The reference is inserted at the cursor and saved with the journal's other changes. 4. Open the reference. Characters, items, journals, individual pages, scenes and mind maps open in their native sheet, document or editor after checking access. Other resource types show a current preview with native controls where available. The empty editor shows Type / to insert blocks or @ to insert references . / continues to open the block menu. Confirming a reference replaces the typed @ ; cancelling the picker leaves it as ordinary text. An @ inside an email address does not open the picker. The catalog covers the campaign resources available to your account, including characters, items, journals and individual pages, scenes and their resources, clocks, clues, mind maps, files, audio, cards, compendiums and preparation tools. Some resources exist only when their feature or system package is available. Quests and other journal types appear with the journal resources. Selecting an individual page keeps its page destination. References point to existing resources. They do not copy a sheet or grant access to its contents. Authored journal text and resource names keep their original language. Existing journal hyperlinks and links to individual pages continue to work alongside the campaign reference picker. Access and unavailable resources A shared journal can contain a reference to a resource that only the GM can read. Each recipient receives the reference according to the target's own permissions. An unavailable target displays Unavailable resource ; its private name and identity are omitted from the recipient's projection. Changing a resource's visibility or deleting it can make an existing reference unavailable. Opening a reference checks access again. Saving an otherwise editable journal preserves existing unavailable references, so a player can update their notes without removing the GM's hidden connections. This does not allow the player to insert a guessed private target or change its permissions. Journal ownership still controls who can edit its rich text. Reading a journal does not grant editing rights, and streamer access remains read-only. GM notes, private pages and hidden content keep their existing audience restrictions. Save and recovery Journal changes use the existing save and conflict handling. Keep the window open when a save fails, review the displayed error and resolve a version conflict before replacing the saved document. Refreshing the page reloads authorized server state. Campaign archives and snapshots retain references along with the journal's structured text. Included targets are remapped to the copied campaign's resources, including individual page destinations. Referenced resources must also be included when transferring content to another campaign; omitted targets remain unavailable instead of binding to an unrelated resource. Use deployment and recovery (deployment.md) for backups of the installation.

title: Progress clocks
summary: Shared segmented goals, permissions, pinned indicators and MapBuilder controls.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (Brasil) (../pt-BR/clocks.md) · Campaign management (campaign-management.md) Progress clocks track tasks, threats, countdowns and other campaign goals with filled segments. They belong to the campaign and work with every game system. The table and the GM's campaign manager edit the same saved records. Create and configure On the table, open Clocks from its icon in the lower dock. Before entering play, open Manage campaign and select Clocks . A campaign GM can create a clock, choose its name and color, and set its current progress. Clock description stores optional authored text up to 4,000 characters. Only a GM edits it; readers of a public clock can read its description. Choose a preset with 4, 6, 8, 10 or 12 segments, or Custom for an integer between 2 and 24. Progress stays between zero and the number of segments. A campaign can contain up to 128 clocks. Choose the clock's scope: Scope Where it appears --- --- Campaign In that campaign across scenes Current scene Only when viewing the associated scene Selecting a scene context in the campaign manager prepares that scene's clocks. It preserves the table's broadcast, each participant's private scene selection and table presence. Entering the tabletop remains a separate action. Deleting a scene also removes clocks associated with that scene. Audience and controls Setting or role Behavior --- --- GM only The server sends the clock only to campaign GMs Players Participants viewing its scope can see the clock Players can advance this clock Players can advance or reduce progress on that public clock GM Can configure, advance, reset and delete clocks Streamer Can view permitted clocks with read-only controls Pinned Displays the permitted clock in the table's pinned-clock area Player editing changes progress. Configuration, visibility, scene scope, resetting and deletion remain GM operations. Hiding a control is a presentation choice; the server checks the participant's current membership and permission on every request. Private clocks and clocks belonging to another viewed scene are filtered before delivery. When you can edit a clock, left-click its face to advance one segment or right-click to reduce one. These controls work in the full clock list, campaign manager and pinned table display. Focus the face and use Right/Up to advance or Left/Down to reduce. The full clock window and campaign manager also provide + and − buttons; pinned clocks show only the name and clock face. Progress stays within its segment bounds, and a pending change finishes before another face action is accepted. The server checks the same saved revision and permissions used by the other progress controls. Use Reset to return to zero or the GM editor to revise the configuration. Closing the clock window leaves saved clocks intact. Reloading restores saved progress. Pinned clocks use the same authorized records as the full list. Double-click the clock's name, or focus it and press Enter or Space. For a GM, this opens the native clock editor, including its description. Players and streamers see a simple read-only description modal. Opening rechecks current access; a private clock's description is never delivered to those readers. Authored text keeps its wording and is displayed as text, including line breaks. Arrange pinned clocks Clock cards and unfilled segments have transparent backgrounds. On the table, each pinned clock can be moved independently: drag its title to the desired position. You can also focus the title and move it with the arrow keys, one pixel at a time, or ten pixels while holding Shift. Escape cancels an active drag. Positions stay within the visible browser area when its size changes. Positions are saved locally for each account, campaign and indicator in that browser. Reloading restores them; another person's layout stays unchanged. Wide and narrow screens keep separate positions, restoring each layout when you resize back. Moving a clock sends no position command or broadcast and changes no campaign, scene or progress data. Even a read-only participant can arrange the clocks they are allowed to see. Pinning/visibility remain shared GM configuration, and progress changes still follow the permissions above. Synchronization and integration The tabletop receives committed clock changes through its existing realtime connection. Campaign management uses HTTP, refreshing on focus and through its normal periodic refresh. Refresh campaign retrieves current state immediately. Concurrent edits use the saved version. If a clock changes while an operation is pending, refresh its current state and review the action. Each logical write uses a new request UUID; retrying that exact operation reuses its UUID so it is applied once. Browser integrations use the clocks domain of the public API (api.md): state , create , update , advance , reset and delete . Changes to an existing clock provide its id and integer version ; advancing also provides delta . Create and update accept the native fields name , description , segments , value , color , visibility , playersCanEdit , pinned and scopeSceneId . Visibility is gm or players ; scopeSceneId: null selects campaign scope. The request's sceneId supplies the current viewing context. Returned clocks expose their saved scope as clock.sceneId . Integrations retain the same campaign, scene and role checks as the native UI. description defaults to "" and accepts only a string of at most 4,000 characters. Omitting it during an update preserves the existing text. The clock faces are native SVG artwork. No external VTT module or game-system package is required. MapBuilder mechanisms The Smart Object Control clock node connects a mechanism's event to an advance, reduce, set or reset operation. It accepts a configured amount or a connected numeric input. Changes use the same saved clock and update permitted table windows and pinned displays after commit. A GM-authored node authorizes its specific clock operation when a participant interacts with that mechanism. This includes private clocks and clocks whose direct player editing is disabled. It does not grant general clock access or expose private names and values. The runtime requires an active campaign GM. Clock scope still restricts which scene may execute the binding. See Control progress clocks in MapBuilder (map-builder.md control-progress-clocks) for connections, amount limits and safe simulation/rehearsal workflows. Backups and upgrading Campaign exports, snapshots, restores and clones preserve clock configuration, progress and campaign or scene scope. Clone options can omit all clocks with clocks: false . Omitting scenes with scenes: false also omits scene-scoped clocks while preserving campaign clocks when clocks are included. This feature adds the gravewright_table migration 0003_progress_clock ; descriptions add 0006_clock_description . Older campaign archives without that field import with an empty description. Copies and snapshots preserve its exact authored text, including text that happens to contain resource UUIDs. Apply pending migrations before restarting an existing installation: bash uv run --locked python manage.py migrate

title: Staged clues
summary: GM-authored discoveries, completed revelation and protected notes.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (Brasil) (../pt-BR/clues.md) · Progress clocks (clocks.md) Clues track discoveries with the same campaign and scene scopes as progress clocks. A GM can prepare a finding in advance, record private notes and reveal the finding immediately or after several steps. The table and campaign manager use the same saved clues, independently of the campaign's game system. Prepare a clue Open Clues from its icon in the table's lower dock, or select Clues in Manage campaign . A campaign GM can create and edit clues with these fields: Field Meaning --- --- Name Authored title, up to 120 characters Content Finding shown after discovery, up to 4,000 characters GM notes Private preparation notes, up to 4,000 characters Segments Required progress, an integer from 1 to 24; defaults to 4 Progress Current value between zero and the number of segments Color Clue display color Visibility Reveal when discovered, or GM only Scope The whole campaign or the selected scene Pinned Show the permitted clue in the table's pinned area Use one segment for a finding that should appear in a single step. Use several segments for an investigation that requires multiple discoveries. A campaign can contain up to 128 clues. GM notes are separate from Content: they remain private even after the finding is revealed. Authored names, content and notes keep their original wording when the interface language changes. Selecting a scene in campaign management prepares that scene without changing the table's broadcast, private navigation or presence. A scene-scoped clue is available only in its scene. Deleting the scene removes its scoped clues. Discovery and visibility Players and streamers receive a clue only when both conditions hold: its progress is complete and its visibility is Reveal when discovered . Before then, the server omits the record, including its name, content, identifier and unfinished progress. It does not send a placeholder or a count of undiscovered clues. GM notes are omitted from every player and streamer projection. Only campaign GMs can configure clues or change their progress directly. Players and streamers can open permitted findings as read-only content. Pinning a clue follows the same discovery and visibility checks as the full list. A GM can left-click the clue's progress bar to advance one step or right-click to reduce one. Focus the bar and use Right/Up to advance or Left/Down to reduce; the full list and manager also provide + and − controls. This works in the campaign manager, the full table list and the pinned display, with the same segment bounds, revision and pending-operation checks. Players and streamers cannot change clue progress through these gestures. GM operation Result --- --- Advance or reduce Change progress within its segment bounds Reveal Complete progress and make the finding visible to players Hide Make the finding GM only while preserving progress Reset Return progress to zero while preserving visibility Delete Remove the clue Reducing a completed clue below its required progress removes it from player views until it is complete again. Hiding a clue removes its current presentation; participants may already remember content they previously discovered. Closing a window does not delete saved clues. Reloading restores their saved configuration and progress. Double-click a clue's name, or focus it and press Enter or Space. A GM opens the native clue editor. Players and streamers open a simple read-only modal showing the discovered clue's Content as its description. It never includes GM notes. Current discovery and visibility checks still apply when opening or refreshing the modal. No additional description field is stored for clues. Arrange pinned clues Clue cards and unfilled steps have transparent backgrounds. Pinned clues show only their name and progress bar; use the name to open the editor or description. Each pinned clue on the table moves independently when you drag its title. Focus the title and use the arrow keys to move one pixel, or Shift plus an arrow to move ten. Escape cancels an active drag. Resizing the browser keeps indicators within its visible area. Each account's positions are saved for that campaign and indicator in the current browser and restored after reload. Wide and narrow screens keep separate positions, restoring each layout when you resize back. Moving an indicator sends no position command or broadcast, changes no campaign/scene/progress data and leaves other participants' layouts unchanged. Players and streamers can arrange their permitted discoveries locally while their clue content and progress remain read-only. Pinning and visibility remain shared GM settings; undiscovered clues are still omitted by the server. MapBuilder mechanisms Use Control clue in a Smart Object's Blueprint to connect a map interaction to advance, reduce, set, reset, reveal or hide. A numeric Amount connection overrides the configured amount for advance, reduce and set. Reset, reveal and hide ignore Amount. A GM-authored binding authorizes that specific operation when a participant interacts with the mechanism. It grants no general clue controls and exposes no undiscovered content or GM notes. Execution requires an active campaign GM and retains the clue's campaign and scene restrictions. Simulate describes the planned action without changing saved clues. Test behavior uses the server engine, previews before and after values and rolls back clues and receipts with the rehearsal. Committed play updates the same saved clues and their permitted table displays. See Control clues in MapBuilder (map-builder.md control-clues) for connections, amount limits and the difference between generating and updating a scene. Synchronization, backups and upgrading The tabletop receives committed changes over its existing realtime connection. Campaign management refreshes its HTTP projection without entering the table or creating presence. Concurrent edits require the current integer revision; after a conflict, review the refreshed clue before submitting another operation. Retries of the same operation reuse its request UUID so progress is applied once. Campaign exports, snapshots, restores and clones preserve clue configuration, content, GM notes, progress and scope. Clone options can omit clues with clues: false . Omitting scenes with scenes: false also omits scene-scoped clues while preserving included campaign clues. Included Blueprint bindings are remapped to the copied clues; omitted targets remain unavailable instead of controlling the original campaign's clue. This feature adds the gravewright_table migration 0004_progress_clue . Apply pending migrations before restarting an existing installation: bash uv run --locked python manage.py migrate Extension authors can use the clues domain of the public API (api.md). The API applies the same discovery, privacy, scope and role checks as the native UI.

title: Mind maps
summary: Collaborative topic graphs, authorized player editors and 37 typed resource links.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/mindmaps.md) · Campaign management (campaign-management.md) Open Mind maps from its icon in the table's lower dock or in the campaign manager. Both interfaces use the same saved campaign graphs. The visual reference is MindMeister (https://www.mindmeister.com/pt): a central topic, branches, movable topics and connections. This implementation runs inside Gravewright and needs no external account or service. Create and organize The GM creates a named map, chooses campaign or scene scope, and configures visibility and editors. New maps are private to the GM. Choose a map to open its editor; add root, child or sibling topics and select a topic to edit its label, notes, color, completion and collapsed branches. Reparenting rejects cycles. Additional labeled connections can relate topics outside their parent branch. Drag topics to position them. Drag empty canvas to pan, use the zoom controls or wheel, and choose Fit map to frame the graph. Undo and redo operate on the local draft. Save mind map writes the graph with its expected version. Closing a modified graph asks whether to discard its draft using the native modal. A conflict preserves the local draft and offers an explicit reload of the saved graph; it never silently overwrites another editor's version. The directory is shared between interfaces, while navigation and zoom are local to the open editor. The campaign manager remains a GM workspace; authorized players use the tabletop editor. Resource links Link campaign resource searches authorized native campaign resources. Links store typed identities, not copied documents or an access grant. The catalog supports these 37 types: Domain Link targets --- --- Characters Actors, their accessible assets including PDF sources, character folders Items Items and folders Journals Diaries, quests, quest boards, roll tables, readable pages, attachments, folders and board entries Scenes Scenes, folders, native scene objects, raster tiles, drawings, tokens and encounters Library Map images and file folders Progress Clocks and discovered clues, subject to their native visibility Audio Tracks and playlists Cards Decks, individual cards, deck definitions and card artwork Compendiums Campaign/installed packs and entries, plus native entry attachments Preparation Session plans and timeline events Authoring MapBuilder projects, behavior templates and PDF mapping templates Other Visible chat messages and other mind maps Native scene objects include walls/doors, lights, images and controllers, particles, shaders, markers, journal pins, spatial sounds and zones. Each follows its own native projection: GM layers, secret barriers, private pages, unrevealed clues and cards unavailable to the viewer do not become discoverable links. Internal package files without a native campaign entity are not separate link targets. Chat search follows the native recent-history window; an existing link can still resolve an older message if the viewer retains access. Opening a link rechecks its current permission. Missing and denied targets use the same neutral unavailable state; hidden target IDs, names and URLs are absent from player payloads. Editing another topic preserves such a link through an opaque placeholder. Removing the link removes it from the graph. Authored topic text belongs to the whole map's audience: write private notes in a private map. Collaboration and permissions Only campaign GMs create/delete maps, change their scene scope, configure visibility and grant editors. Visible to players permits reading; selected player editors can also read and modify a private map. All GMs can edit. An authorized player can rename a map and edit its graph, but cannot change its access list. Streamers are always read-only. Scene scope additionally requires native access to that scene, even for a selected editor. Table clients receive committed invalidations and re-read their own projection. Campaign management refreshes through its existing HTTP lifecycle. Permission changes are checked again on reads, saves and receipt retries. A revoked editor cannot continue writing or use an old receipt to retrieve private data. MapBuilder Smart Objects offer two nodes: Node Behavior --- --- Open mind map ( openMindMap ) Opens an authorized map, optionally focused on a topic, for the triggering user, players or selected users Control mind-map topic ( mindMapNode ) Completes, resets or toggles the configured topic's completion Bindings must belong to the campaign and use campaign scope or the current scene. A GM-authored control delegates only that specific effect through the native service and requires an active campaign GM; it grants no general player editing rights. Opening never bypasses recipient permissions. Deleted targets remain repairable bindings. Simulation describes the effect; server rehearsal rolls back data, receipts and notifications. Delayed execution rechecks targets. Storage, limits and APIs A campaign supports 64 maps. Each graph supports 500 topics, 1,000 additional connections, 16 resource links per topic, 2,048 links overall and 1 MiB of JSON. Labels and connection text are limited to 240 characters, notes to 8,000, and coordinates to ±100,000. IDs are UUIDs; references also support native numeric and composite identities through their registered type. Campaign copies/exports select Mind maps separately. Omitting scenes also omits scene-scoped maps. Typed links remap to copied resources, while excluded targets become inert and authored text/local topic IDs stay exact. Portable archives clear source editor grants; snapshots restore grants in the same campaign. A campaign archive does not replace an installation backup. Python exposes api.mindmaps.state , read , resources , resolve and command . The browser exposes the same reads plus create , update , node , delete , list , get and mindmaps.changed . See the API reference (api.md) for payloads, operation UUIDs and required versions. Apply migration 0005_mind_maps (../../gravewright/table/migrations/0005_mind_maps.py) before starting this code against an existing installation.

title: PDF System
summary: Manual PDF fields, token bars, roll actions, calculations, mapping libraries and export.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (Brasil) (../pt-BR/pdf-system.md) · Campaign management (campaign-management.md) · API reference (api.md system-owned-operations-and-the-pdf-system) The bundled PDF System uses an uploaded PDF or a bundled template as a character sheet. Native PDF form fields and manually drawn fields share character values, token bars and saved roll actions. The same actor sheets are available in the table and in Manage campaign → Characters . Map a PDF without editable fields 1. Open the actor sheet as a campaign GM and select its PDF. 2. Choose Map fields , then text, number, checkbox or multiline text. 3. Draw a rectangle over the desired page area. Add field also creates a rectangle without dragging. 4. Name the field and adjust its bounds. Drag to move it or use its lower-right handle to resize. Arrow keys move it one displayed pixel; Shift moves ten. 5. Choose Finish mapping to fill the fields. Changes save through the normal sheet workflow. Rectangles use page-relative coordinates and stay aligned during zoom and page navigation. The GM configures the layout; participants with sheet editing rights fill its values. Existing PDF widgets remain usable. Removing a rectangle keeps its stored value. The original PDF is unchanged. Use Shift/Ctrl-click or a selection rectangle for multiple fields. Layout tools offers copy/paste, duplication, alignment, distribution and optional five-point snapping. Ctrl+C/V/D and Ctrl+Z/Shift+Z provide clipboard and history shortcuts. History keeps 50 layout steps for the active PDF and preserves current character values when undoing. Switching documents clears that layout history. Field actions, token bars and formulas As GM, double-click a native or manual field, or focus it and press F2, to open Field actions . Select a token value, configure a roll label and formula, or choose a preset. The six presets are d20, highest or lowest of two d20s, 2d6, exploding d6 and 4dF. Number and single-line text fields can supply token bars. Changing a binding preserves its current value. Formula Meaning --- --- 1d20 + @value Roll with this field's current numeric value 2d6 Roll without reading the field's value 1d20 + @{field-key} Read the numeric value of another mapped field Use Reference field to insert an existing field's exact key. Manual keys remain stable when a field is renamed. Native names containing braces or backslashes are escaped by the picker. Empty values are zero; checkboxes are zero or one. Other nonnumeric inputs prevent the roll. See the dice notation (../../gravewright/dice/grammar/notation/GRAMMAR.md) for supported roll expressions. Saving an action validates it without rolling dice. Authorized editors execute saved actions with the buttons above the PDF or Alt+Enter on a focused field. Players can also double-click configured fields. A GM's double-click opens configuration; Roll saved action runs the previously saved action. Results use native dice/chat visibility, scene context and retry receipts. Calculated value formula uses deterministic arithmetic, comparisons and numeric functions with @{field-key} references. Calculated fields are read-only. The server recomputes them in dependency order on sheet saves and rejects cycles, including cycles through token-bar aliases. If a calculation temporarily fails, the previous canonical result remains available and diagnostics explain the issue. Clear the formula to return the field to ordinary editing. Reuse mappings Mapping library lets campaign GMs save or replace a mapping template, apply it to the current sheet or selected actors, and import/export versioned JSON. Mappings contain rectangles, roll actions, calculations, field/bar bindings and optional document metadata. They contain no PDF bytes, character values or media. Apply a template to the same PDF layout. Values are retained by field identity and canonical bars, rather than merged by visible labels. Batch application validates every target revision before committing any changes. A template update does not automatically change sheets that used its older definition.
