Actor sheets and independent token snapshots have separate state. Applying a template to the actor does not rewrite its independent snapshots; an open snapshot must be targeted explicitly. Mapping JSON does not authorize distributing the source PDF or its contents. Campaign archives preserve the mapping library. Diagnose and export PDF mapping diagnostics reports missing fields/references, calculation problems, absent pages and differences from saved page dimensions, rotation or document fingerprint. It can navigate to fields that are still present. The campaign preparation dashboard also reports missing PDFs and saved calculation problems; actual page geometry is checked when opening the sheet. Filled PDF renders every page and its current values into a separate, flattened PDF at 144 dpi. It includes manual fields and repeated native widgets, and contains no editable form widgets or executable PDF content. The original download remains available separately. Export fails rather than truncating overflowing text or returning an incomplete document. Closing the sheet or switching its PDF cancels the work. Limits and integration Resource Limit --- --- Manual fields / roll actions / calculated fields 256 of each per sheet, across PDF sources Field bindings 1,024 per sheet Roll formula / label 512 / 48 characters Mapping templates 128 per campaign Mapping JSON import / batch application 1 MB / 100 actors Filled PDF 100 pages, 16 million pixels per page, 128 million pixels per operation, 100 MB output All writes recheck membership, sheet permissions, source identity and revisions. After a conflict, review fresh state before saving; use the same operation UUID only to retry the same operation. Layout changes and templates require a GM. Streamers remain read-only. Text in the host's controls passes through Translator; authored names, formulas and document content retain their wording. Browser integrations discover the campaign system with await api.system.state() and call its pdf. operations through api.system.call() . Python integrations use the public api.pdf_system facade or the api.systems dispatcher. See the API guide (api.md) for payloads, token contexts, revisions, templates and diagnostics. PDF inspection, flattened rendering and layout history run in the browser; server diagnostics inspect stored mappings and an optional observed descriptor without parsing PDF bytes. Implementation and verification entry points are in Frontend architecture (frontend.md manual-pdf-fields) and Testing (testing.md).

title: Upgrade and recovery
summary: Three migrations for 0.3.3, compatible backups, manual replacement and recovery.
text: Documentation (../README.md) · Português (../pt-BR/upgrading.md) This guide covers the Gravewright 0.3.3 — Alpha release. Its source artifact is Gravewright-0.3.3-django.zip , with the matching Gravewright-0.3.3-django.zip.sha256 . See the release notes (../releases/0.3.3.md) for features and deployment (deployment.md) for public-server configuration. Before upgrading 1. Record the running version and configured paths. Stop all table and campaign manager writes, then stop the Runner and every ASGI/maintenance process using the installation. A browser closed by itself does not stop the server. 2. Back up .env , the configured database and private media together. Include external module/content directories, local extensions/ , trust keys and Runner/update recovery state. By default, .env and extensions/ are at the installation root; the database, media and runtime/recovery state are under data/ . Protect this backup: it contains accounts, GM secrets, private sheets and retained deleted attachments. 3. Retain the matching application source and lock files with the backup. Test recovery in a separate directory with separate database/media settings before using an important campaign as the first upgrade check. 4. Use the complete release archive and its matching SHA-256 value. Never reuse the checksum of a different ZIP or replace only an installer entrypoint. Do not redirect defaults to a shared OS profile to repair an installation. A non-writable installation must report the failing path. Explicit operator storage overrides remain supported, and must be backed up as well. Upgrade paths After completing the stopped-instance backup, restart the current Runner for a compatible managed installation, then use Administration → Updates → Install update . Keep Keep a .old copy for rollback enabled when recovery is wanted. Leave that Runner open while the supervisor downloads, verifies, prepares dependencies, snapshots data, migrates, replaces files and restarts. Reconnecting browsers reload after the target version is confirmed. Do not run a second server against that database during this process. For a manual upgrade, stop the installation, preserve the configuration and data listed above, replace application files with the complete release, then run the platform installer and use its regenerated Runner: Platform Prepare the upgrade Start --- --- --- Windows Install Windows.bat Gravewright Runner.bat Linux bash "./Install Linux.sh" bash "./Gravewright Runner.sh" macOS bash "./Install macOS.command" bash "./Gravewright Runner.command" The installers preserve project .env and prepare locked Python/frontend dependencies. They apply migrations before startup. Rerun installation after moving the source because launchers and environments refer to its location. Do not copy a generated Runner from another machine or installation. Source deployments started directly with Daphne require an operator-managed upgrade. Configure local tool storage below, prepare the frontend as described in frontend (frontend.md), and run from the installation root with the intended configuration: bash uv sync --locked --no-dev uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py migrate --plan uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py migrate --noinput uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py collectstatic --noinput uv run --locked --no-dev python manage.py check Retain --extra vips on dependency synchronization if that installation uses the optional libvips tiler. After these commands, restart the service using its existing deployment profile. check --deploy and public HTTPS/WSS verification also apply to public deployments. Numbering and same-version packages The release identifier is 0.3.3 , following 0.3.2 . The updater compares version numbers, so a compatible installation on 0.3.2 can discover 0.3.3 through its configured release repository. The project remains in Alpha and the host SDK contract is unchanged; optional APIs still need capability checks. Historical release notes retain their original identifiers. An installation reporting the earlier incorrectly numbered 3.0.1 considers 0.3.3 a lower version and will not receive it through automatic discovery. Back up its matching source, database and media, then use the manual installation procedure with the complete 0.3.3 archive and matching checksum. This corrects the release numbering; do not try to downgrade the database by swapping older code over it. If recovery is needed, restore matching source, database and media together. A host already reporting 0.3.3 will not receive a reissued 0.3.3 through version discovery. Use the manual upgrade procedure with the replacement ZIP and its own checksum. Do not downgrade a database by swapping older source over it; recovery requires matching source, database and media. Database migrations in 0.3.3 Compared with 0.3.2, this release adds three migrations: Migration Stored capability --- --- maps/0014_sceneassignment.py (../../gravewright/maps/migrations/0014_sceneassignment.py) Individual player scene assignments maps/0015_builderobjectpreset.py (../../gravewright/maps/migrations/0015_builderobjectpreset.py) Campaign-owned reusable Builder object presets tokens/0002_token_appearance.py (../../gravewright/tokens/migrations/0002_token_appearance.py) Token name, turn-indicator and bar presentation settings Older installations also need earlier pending migrations. The preceding 0.3.2 release added these seven migrations relative to 0.3.1: Migration Stored capability --- --- table/0003_progress_clock.py (../../gravewright/table/migrations/0003_progress_clock.py) Progress clocks and retry receipts table/0004_progress_clue.py (../../gravewright/table/migrations/0004_progress_clue.py) Staged clues and their separate retry receipts table/0005_mind_maps.py (../../gravewright/table/migrations/0005_mind_maps.py) Mind-map graphs, visibility, selected editors and separate retry receipts table/0006_clock_description.py (../../gravewright/table/migrations/0006_clock_description.py) Authored clock descriptions, empty on existing clocks campaigns/0005_preparation.py (../../gravewright/campaigns/migrations/0005_preparation.py) Personal GM dashboards, session plans, timeline events and preparation receipts journals/0004_revision.py (../../gravewright/journals/migrations/0004_revision.py) Journal revisions, trash and retained attachment metadata pdf_system/0001_initial.py (../../gravewright/pdf_system/migrations/0001_initial.py) Reusable PDF mapping templates, their bundles and revisions Run the normal migration command rather than applying only these files: Django orders their dependencies and also includes missing earlier migrations. The new tables do not fabricate history for changes made before the feature existed. Keep the pre-upgrade backup; do not assume older application code can open the migrated database safely. Campaign archives and instance backups Recovery material What it preserves --- --- Complete campaign export or clone Selected campaign content, clocks/clues, mind maps, preparation, timeline, portable dashboard metadata and journal history/trash; typed references are remapped Campaign snapshot Campaign recovery data, including the new preparation/history content; dashboard restoration applies to current GM memberships Coordinated full instance backup Database, private files, accounts, permissions, host/module state and pending automation, together with configuration and matching application source The preparation selection controls session plans, timeline events and dashboard metadata. The journals selection controls journal history/trash. Portable imports do not recreate source users or campaign memberships; individual access grants are sanitized. A full snapshot can preserve permissions, while it cannot turn an absent user into a current member. Portable import assigns suitable dashboard metadata to the importing GM; merge preserves an existing dashboard. Trashed documents can retain physical attachments. Complete campaign exports, clones and snapshots include these files; an export that excludes files is rejected when they are needed to preserve the trash. Do not manually delete retained files from media storage. Restoration validates file availability, resource ownership, revisions and quest prerequisites before committing. Archives from older versions remain importable. If they lack preparation metadata, restoring them preserves existing preparation/history instead of deleting data that the archive never contained. Campaign packages still omit pending Blueprint continuations and command receipts; a full database backup includes them. See campaign management (campaign-management.md) for detailed selection rules. Verification and recovery After startup, check that Administration reports 0.3.3 . Sign in as a GM and a player using a synthetic or copied campaign. Verify the campaign manager and table, a mapped PDF, map upload/Universal VTT import, a clock, and a clue whose content remains hidden until completion. Check private journal visibility, session save/reopen, history/trash restoration and a representative backup round trip. Verify a mind map (mindmaps.md) with a selected player editor: unreadable links stay unavailable, ordinary graph edits preserve those links, and a copied graph targets copied campaign resources. Use the testing guide (testing.md) for isolated automated scenarios. Also check individual scene assignments, the saved blank-map grid, cursor preferences, token bar audiences and a reusable Builder object. Rehearse a Smart Object shader action before applying it to a live scene. If managed installation fails, retain updater transactions, backups and logs; the supervisor attempts recovery and handles interrupted transactions on the next launch. Preserve .env , data/ , tool environments and immutable launcher copies together. Avoid deleting recovery directories to suppress a failure. A retained .old folder contains the previous source and matching data under .gravewright-rollback . Its name comes from the installation directory, with a unique suffix for collisions. Runner defaults place it under data/updates/retained/ ; normal main.py places it under data/updates/<installation-hash /retained/ . With every server stopped, invoke rollback_update.py (../../scripts/rollback_update.py) using the installation's Python and the actual retained path, as shown in deployment (deployment.md). This returns data to the backup time and discards subsequent changes. When inspecting a restored full database, use GRAVEWRIGHT_AUTOMATION_WORKER_ENABLED=false before startup if overdue Blueprint waits must remain paused during inspection. Re-enable only when the recovery copy is intended to execute its automation. A campaign-only archive does not restore that pending queue. Local tool storage Native installers, generated Runners and main.py configure tool caches and temporary storage inside data/runner/ automatically. Manual uv/npm commands need the same environment before they run. From the writable installation root, use a fresh shell and keep these variables scoped to that shell. On Linux/macOS Bash: bash export GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT="$PWD/data/runner" mkdir -p "$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/tmp" export UV_CACHE_DIR="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/cache" export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/python" export UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/python-bin" export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_BIN=0 UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_REGISTRY=0 UV_PYTHON_NO_REGISTRY=1 export npm_config_cache="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/npm-cache" export CARGO_HOME="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/cargo" export RUSTUP_HOME="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/rustup" export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/xdg-cache" export XDG_DATA_HOME="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/xdg-data" export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/xdg-config" export TEMP="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/tmp" TMP="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/tmp" TMPDIR="$GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT/tmp" On Windows PowerShell: powershell $env:GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT = Join-Path (Get-Location).Path 'data/runner' $gravewrightTools = $env:GRAVEWRIGHT_RUNNER_ROOT New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $gravewrightTools 'tmp') Out-Null $gravewrightPaths = @{ UV_CACHE_DIR = 'cache'; UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR = 'python'; UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR = 'python-bin' npm_config_cache = 'npm-cache'; CARGO_HOME = 'cargo'; RUSTUP_HOME = 'rustup' XDG_CACHE_HOME = 'xdg-cache'; XDG_DATA_HOME = 'xdg-data'; XDG_CONFIG_HOME = 'xdg-config' TEMP = 'tmp'; TMP = 'tmp'; TMPDIR = 'tmp'; LOCALAPPDATA = 'profile/local'; APPDATA = 'profile/roaming' } foreach ($entry in $gravewrightPaths.GetEnumerator()) { $gravewrightPath = Join-Path $gravewrightTools $entry.Value New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $gravewrightPath Out-Null Environment ::SetEnvironmentVariable($entry.Key, $gravewrightPath, 'Process') } $env:UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_BIN = '0' $env:UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_REGISTRY = '0' $env:UV_PYTHON_NO_REGISTRY = '1' These commands do not change HOME or permanent OS configuration. An operator's explicit tool-root override can replace data/runner/ ; use an absolute path or resolve it against this installation, never another installation's active state. For two independent installations, prepare each inside its own shell and root.

title: Ethical module porting
summary: Licenses, content rights and mapping an integration to the owning domains.
text: Porting a module starts with identifying which parts you are authorized to adapt. Its features can then be mapped to Gravewright's domains. The code license, content license and permissions to use trademarks must be examined separately. 1. How to read a module's license Examine the exact version you intend to port. Look for files such as LICENSE , COPYING , NOTICE , the README, file headers and the terms accompanying images, fonts, audio and content collections. The manifest's license field is an indication; by itself, it does not resolve exceptions or materials with their own licensing terms. For each part, answer: Question What to check --- --- Who can authorize its use? The rights holder for that code or content. The module maintainer may not control the rights to images or game material. What does the license cover? The entire package, code only, specific files or an expressly identified selection. May I modify it? Permission to adapt, translate and create derivative versions. May I distribute the adaptation? Modifying something for personal use and providing copies to others are different situations. May I charge for it? Commercial permission and any restrictions on the context of use. Being free of charge does not waive the other conditions. What must I preserve or provide? Credits, license text, notices, identification of changes and source code, as required by the applicable terms. Are there additional limits? License version, exceptions, excluded materials and authorizations restricted to particular uses or environments. Record the source, version and terms you find. If there is a contradiction or authorization is missing for a part, leave that part out of the port until you clarify it with the rights holder. A public repository or a free download is not equivalent to a license to adapt and redistribute. In the absence of a license, do not assume those permissions. Reference on the absence of a license (https://choosealicense.com/no-permission/). 2. License types and what to look for This table guides your reading; the actual conditions are those of the text and version applicable to the material. Type Consequence for the port --- --- Permissive, such as MIT and BSD Generally allow adaptation and redistribution, including commercially, while preserving the required notices. Check the variant; similar names can have different conditions. Apache-2.0 Allows adaptation and distribution subject to conditions such as preserving the license, identifying modified files and reproducing relevant NOTICE notices, where present. Includes patent provisions and does not grant general authorization to use trademarks. Strong copyleft, such as GPL Allows porting, including commercially. When distributing a covered derivative work, requires compliance with copyleft and making the corresponding source code available under the license's conditions. Check the version, exceptions and compatibility of the combined parts. AGPL In addition to copyleft, contains a specific obligation to offer corresponding source code to users interacting remotely with a modified version, under the license's conditions. File-level copyleft, such as MPL-2.0 Covered files and their modifications retain MPL obligations when distributed. Independent files may have another license; moving covered code into a new file does not remove its obligations. Proprietary or custom license Read the express permissions. Buying or receiving access to a module does not, by itself, establish authorization to distribute a port. Dual licensing Check whether you can choose one of the licenses or whether different parts require cumulative compliance with multiple conditions. No identified license Request authorization to reuse the material; do not treat silence as permission. References: license comparison (https://choosealicense.com/appendix/), Apache-2.0 (https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), GPL-3.0 (https://choosealicense.com/licenses/gpl-3.0/), AGPL-3.0 (https://choosealicense.com/licenses/agpl-3.0/) and MPL-2.0 explanation (https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/MPL/2.0/FAQ/). Content licenses Text, illustrations and other resources may have terms different from those of the code. For Creative Commons licenses, examine the elements present: Element What it means for the analysis --- --- BY — attribution Provide the required credits, identify the license and indicate changes where applicable. SA — share alike When sharing an adaptation, use the same license or a license accepted as compatible. NC — noncommercial Commercial use falls outside the authorization. The analysis considers purpose and context; the file being free of charge is not enough. ND — no derivatives Does not authorize sharing adapted material. A simple format change is not automatically an adaptation, but translating or transforming the content requires a separate analysis. The elements combine: a license with BY, NC and ND requires observing all three. Also check the version. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) and CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/). 3. What can and cannot be ported Make the decision component by component, rather than relying only on the module's name or main license. Situation Decision --- --- Code under a license authorizing adaptation and distribution It can be ported while meeting its conditions and those of the dependencies used. Open-source code accompanied by images with reserved rights Authorization for the code does not automatically cover the images. Exclude them or obtain separate authorization. Content expressly released for adaptation and redistribution It can be included within the authorized scope, with the required notices and conditions. Authorization only for personal use or a specific environment Do not extend that authorization to distribution in Gravewright. Request permission covering the intended use. A book, adventure, map or collection purchased by the user The purchase does not establish authorization to incorporate that material into a distributed module. Check the granted rights separately. Material without a license or with uncertain ownership Do not include it until the necessary authorization is clarified. Resources you created They can be used insofar as you hold the necessary rights; check any contributions and incorporated materials. For example, a module may contain permissively licensed code, an artist's icons and descriptions licensed by a publisher. Porting the code may be authorized while porting the icons and descriptions depends on other permissions. The main license does not turn the entire package into material freely available for reuse. 4. Intellectual property considerations Separate functionality from expression. Describing that a function calculates a roll helps map its behavior. Copying its implementation, text or presentation involves materials that need examination. Rewriting code does not automatically release incorporated content or resolve every intellectual property issue. Do not use conversion as a justification. Translating descriptions, extracting text from a document or converting a collection into another format does not create authorization to redistribute it. Check the terms of the source content. Treat trademarks and visual identity separately. Do not assume a software license allows you to reuse logos or present the port as official. Preserve credits without suggesting a nonexistent partnership, approval or endorsement. Apache-2.0 itself distinguishes the code license from trademark rights. Section 6 of Apache-2.0 (https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). Credit does not replace permission. Identifying the author is required by various licenses, but does not authorize a use that their terms do not allow. Keep specific authorizations and respect exactly the material and conditions they cover. Gravewright's license does not change the source license. The permission for independent modules allows them to use other licenses, including proprietary ones, within its scope. It does not grant rights to third-party code or resources, or remove obligations concerning copied or adapted core code. See the licensing policy (../../LICENSING.md) and the normative text of the independent-module permission (../../LICENSE-EXCEPTION). 5. How to map features to domains After identifying what is authorized, describe each feature in terms of what it does and the data it uses. Then find the responsible domain in Gravewright. The source module's names and internal organization do not need to be reproduced. Feature Gravewright domain How to interpret the mapping --- --- --- Characters, creatures and sheet data actors The character is a native actor. The sheet's specific presentation corresponds to the actor.sheet surface. Character representation on the map, position, vision and conditions tokens Distinguish actor data from the data of its representation in a scene. The corresponding sheet surface is token.sheet . Inventory, equipment, powers, ancestries, hindrances and addable abilities items + actors Model components as items; the sheet retains the character-owned association or copy data, according to the rule. Drag and drop connects the item library to the sheet. Editing an item's specific data items Use the native item as the document and item.sheet as the presentation surface. Maps and scene objects maps Relate resources to maps and scene operations available in the contract. Notes, documents, adventures and shared information journals Map the document and its access, including GM-only content. Participants, initiative, rounds and turns combat The domain controls combat state; the specific rule determines how to calculate values. Decks, drawing, discarding and shuffling cards Separate deck operations from the rules that interpret the drawn card. Tracks, playlists and positional sounds audio Map playback behavior; authorization to distribute audio remains independent. Reusable document libraries compendiums Map the collection and its documents, including the rights and permissions of each piece of content. Domains handle data and operations. Surfaces such as actor.sheet and item.sheet handle presentation. A custom sheet does not imply creating another character directory; custom item types do not imply creating another global inventory. Use the corresponding native structure. For each feature, record: Field Example --- --- Behavior Add equipment to a character and account for its modifier. Material involved Calculation logic, equipment data, description and icon. Identified rights License and authorization for each part, including exclusions. Domains items for equipment; actors for character data. Presentation item.sheet for editing; actor.sheet for displaying equipment on the sheet. Port boundary Implement the authorized behavior and exclude any description or icon without permission. A feature may involve several domains. A card that changes initiative combines cards and combat ; a power applied to a creature may involve items , actors and tokens . If the contract has no corresponding operation, record the gap rather than assuming every behavior of the source is already supported. Available domains and operations are listed in the API documentation (api.md); surfaces are described in the module documentation (modules.md). This mapping must preserve native access permissions and distinguish shared data from data belonging to each character or scene.

title: Contributing
summary: Contribution conventions, licensing, review and validation requirements.
text: English (CONTRIBUTING.md) · Português (Brasil) (CONTRIBUTING.pt-BR.md) Contributions can improve code, tests, accessibility, documentation, translations or examples. Begin with local setup (docs/en/getting-started.md) and the architecture (docs/en/architecture.md). Working on a change 1. For a substantial feature or API change, explain the problem and proposed behavior in an issue so maintainers and module authors can discuss compatibility. Small fixes can go directly to a pull request. 2. Work on a branch in your own checkout. Keep the change focused and preserve unrelated work. 3. Follow the domain's existing service, permission, transaction and event patterns. Development (docs/en/development.md) explains where changes belong. 4. Run the checks relevant to the change from testing (docs/en/testing.md). For permission or persistence changes, exercise both authorized and unauthorized users and retry/version-conflict behavior. 5. Update English documentation and its Portuguese counterpart whenever behavior or setup changes. Keep code identifiers and commands identical between translations. 6. Describe the problem, resulting behavior, validation and any known limits in the pull request. Include screenshots when visual behavior changes; use synthetic campaign data. Portable storage contract All default VTT storage stays in the extracted project folder: data/ for data, logs and Runner/update state; data/runner/ for managed tools and their caches. Do not introduce AppData, HOME or XDG defaults or shared installation metadata. Follow AGENTS.md (AGENTS.md) and retain regression tests for independent copies. Code and documentation Use English for new comments, docstrings, API documentation and identifiers. Explain responsibilities, trust boundaries, side effects and non-obvious constraints. Avoid comments that merely repeat a statement. Public functions should describe their inputs, results, permission assumptions and important exceptions where these are not apparent from the signature. Keep database schema changes in migrations. Never edit an already published migration to change its meaning. Do not edit generated frontend-contract.js directly; update the source contract and run the generator. Preserve upstream copyright headers, license files and notices when touching vendored assets. Do not commit .env , database files, uploaded documents, installed modules, private keys, browser session state or test-results/ . Use fake accounts and assets you are authorized to distribute in test fixtures. There is currently no repository-wide formatter/linter configuration. The automatic updates workflow (.github/workflows/automatic-updates.yml) checks upgrade recovery on Windows, Linux and macOS, plus browser and module behavior. Follow nearby style, run checks appropriate to the change and report the commands you actually ran; do not claim CI passed when it did not run. Licensing contributions By intentionally submitting an original contribution for inclusion in Gravewright core, you offer it under GPL-3.0-only with the Gravewright Independent Module Permission . You retain your copyright. Confirm you have the rights to submit it, and identify separately licensed material explicitly. See LICENSING.md (LICENSING.md) and LICENSE-EXCEPTION (LICENSE-EXCEPTION). Independently developed third-party modules may use any license under that permission, whether or not they use the supplied APIs. Submitting a change to the core is different from distributing an independent module. When adding a dependency, document its source, version, license and notices in both third-party notice files and preserve the required license texts. Communication Be respectful, describe observable behavior and give actionable feedback. Bug reports should include project version, operating system, Python/browser versions, minimal steps, expected and actual results, and redacted logs. Use the repository's issue tracker for ordinary bugs and SECURITY.md (SECURITY.md) for vulnerabilities.

title: Licensing
summary: Project licensing, independent module permission and third-party obligations.
text: English (LICENSING.md) · Português (Brasil) (LICENSING.pt-BR.md) Project grant Unless a file or a preserved third-party notice states otherwise, Gravewright's first-party source code, accompanying documentation and original assets are licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 only , with the additional permission in LICENSE-EXCEPTION (LICENSE-EXCEPTION). You may redistribute and modify that material under GPL version 3 as published by the Free Software Foundation. No option to use a later version is granted. The project is distributed without any warranty, including the implied warranties of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose, to the extent permitted by law. See LICENSE (LICENSE) for the complete terms. The GPL text is kept unmodified. The example “or any later version” notice in its appendix is not the project's license grant; the grant above specifies version 3 only. Independent modules The project explicitly permits independently written modules under any license, including proprietary licenses, using or not using its APIs . This is an additional permission under GPLv3 section 7; LICENSE-EXCEPTION (LICENSE-EXCEPTION) is the operative text. The Portuguese version is informative. Situation Project policy --- --- Original module using the browser SDK, Python interfaces, HTTP or WebSockets Any module license, subject to the additional permission and its own dependencies Original module using internal interfaces or another integration mechanism Same permission; no promise of API stability or technical support Modifications to Gravewright core distributed to others GPL-3.0-only continues to apply to the core, including applicable source obligations Core implementation copied into a module The copied/adapted material remains covered by its license; the module label is not an exception Maps, books, music, PDFs, campaign data or other uploaded content No ownership transfer or automatic GPL licensing; the content owner's terms apply Bundled third-party code or assets Preserve and comply with their own licenses and notices A paid module can be open source or proprietary. The permission covers both. It does not grant a module author rights to other people's assets or cancel a dependency's copyleft obligations. Only material for which the relevant copyright holders have granted the permission benefits from it. Contributions and notices By intentionally submitting original contributions for inclusion in the core, you offer them under GPL-3.0-only with the same additional module permission. Contributors retain their copyright. Clearly identify reused material and its license when submitting it; do not replace existing upstream notices with a project notice. See CONTRIBUTING.md (CONTRIBUTING.md). For a new first-party source file, an optional short header is: text Licensed under GNU GPL version 3 only, with the Gravewright Independent Module Permission. See LICENSE, LICENSE-EXCEPTION and LICENSING.md in the source root. Do not add this header to vendored files. The custom SPDX license reference in pyproject.toml names the complete GPL-3.0-only plus module-permission terms; its text is in LICENSES/LicenseRef-Gravewright-GPL-3.0-only-with-module-permission.txt (LICENSES/LicenseRef-Gravewright-GPL-3.0-only-with-module-permission.txt). It is a project-defined reference, not an SPDX-listed exception or an assertion that this custom permission has separate OSI approval. The underlying GPL license identifier is GPL-3.0-only . Distribution Distributions should carry LICENSE , LICENSE-EXCEPTION , this policy and applicable THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and upstream license files. Check the actual contents of a release, including bundled wheels, JavaScript, fonts and native libraries; the source notice inventory does not automatically describe every possible deployment image. The permission follows the mechanism described in GPLv3 section 7 (https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html section7). The GNU project's plugin discussion (https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html GPLPlugins) explains why a module policy needs to address how programs interact rather than rely on the word “plugin.” The project-defined permission above implements the intended broader integration policy.

title: How to use AI to create an RPG system
summary: Build sheets, item templates and automation as one installable package for the host version you actually use.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Create a small original system with a character sheet, an NPC sheet and an empty gear template. Begin with a vertical slice: create a character, edit one numeric field, save it and reopen it. Context to give the assistant - docs/en/modules.md: manifest, system descriptors, sheet lifecycle, combat providers and package installation. - docs/en/api.md and gravewright/modules/contracts/schemas/manifest.json: supported interfaces and accepted manifest fields. - The target release of the VTT and an explicit list of original or licensed material you may distribute. Step by step 1. Specify actor/item types, editable fields, validation and the target host release before asking for code. 2. Ask the assistant to inspect the existing public contracts and produce the smallest working package. 3. Review sheet loading, asynchronous saving, cancellation and conflict handling before adding rules. 4. Add combat automation and translation catalogs inside that same system package only when the first sheet works. 5. Build a ZIP with its manifest at the archive root; follow the documented signing/install process on a disposable host. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Implement an original system named Example Expedition. Deliver one installable system package containing character and NPC sheets, an empty gear item template, assets, translations and any automation. Do not create a separately installed Server Rules companion. Start with name, a numeric stamina field and an inventory list. Define server-accepted data shapes using the target release contracts, rather than guessing manifest keys. Use the supplied scoped module API, the documented sheet-save lifecycle and native modals. Handle cancellation, permission denial and version conflicts by refreshing state. Keep game rules inside the package. Do not add system-name conditionals to the host, depend on a newer host version or bundle rulebook text/catalogs. Show the exact package tree, manifest, code, license and installation steps; identify any requirement that the target public API cannot support. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Create a character, change stamina, close while saving and reopen; confirm the saved value. - Open with GM, authorized player and read-only access; verify that denied writes are rejected by the server. - Make conflicting edits in two sessions; refresh and resolve the conflict without silently replacing the expected revision. - Install and remove the package in a disposable host; check cleanup and English fallback. Ready when A character can complete the create → edit → save → reopen flow on the requested host, and everything the system needs ships in one package. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to create a browser module
summary: Add a useful interface feature using the scoped browser API, permissions and the module lifecycle.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Create a small actor-directory addition that counts only the actors readable by the signed-in user. This is a concrete first module with a visible result and no game-specific rules. Context to give the assistant - The minimal Actor counter package in docs/en/modules.md. - The browser domain API, events and cancellation behavior in docs/en/api.md. - The target release contract, especially frontend.json and the manifest schema. Step by step 1. Choose an existing documented extension surface, such as actor.directory. 2. Give the assistant the actual minimal package example and ask it to explain every lifecycle hook it uses. 3. Start with a read-only feature; subscribe through the scoped API rather than polling the whole page. 4. Verify repeated mount/unmount and activation changes before packaging. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Create example.actor-counter as a browser module on the requested host release. Use the documented actor.directory surface and the supplied api.actors.list() / api.events.on("actors.changed", ...) interfaces after verifying their signatures. Show a visible count of readable actors. Use start/register/stop and the host lifecycle as documented. Avoid global window handles when a scoped context is supplied. Respect signal.aborted and dispose resources. Scope CSS to the module root, keep text at least 12px, use existing design tokens and translation hooks, and use DOM textContent for untrusted labels. Produce manifest.json, main.js, styles.css and a license file with exact signing/install instructions. There is no assumed npm SDK or unsigned upload endpoint. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Add/remove a readable actor and check that the count follows committed state. - Verify a player does not count hidden actors. - Open/close repeatedly and deactivate the module during a pending request; check for duplicate listeners and stale updates. - Run the focused module/browser checks documented by the project in isolated data. Ready when The feature updates from authorized state, survives repeated mounting and stops cleanly when its context is disposed. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI for a Python integration
summary: Use the public Python facade from trusted server code while preserving campaign authorization and transactions.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Build a read-only campaign report from authorized actor/journal data. Run it in an isolated development installation with a caller who really belongs to the campaign. Context to give the assistant - The Python interface section in docs/en/api.md and the exports under api/. - docs/en/architecture.md: membership, Context, service boundaries and post-commit events. - The target host version and the real signatures/tests of the public functions needed by the report. - For a 0.3.2 target, the journal/mind-map guides describe the shared 37-type resource catalog, live permission projections and opaque unavailable references. Step by step 1. Separate a trusted server integration from a browser module; the browser does not receive arbitrary Python execution. 2. Choose the caller and campaign explicitly; constructing Context does not grant permission. 3. Ask for a read-only implementation first, using the facade and current projections. 4. If a later change writes data, review its request identity, expected revision and notifications separately. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Implement a read-only campaign report in trusted Python code for this target release. Initialize Django using the documented environment. Inspect the exports and signatures in api/ and use api.Context for the explicit campaign/user. Do not guess a REST endpoint or API-key scheme. Read only the resources the caller may access; do not bypass the API with direct ORM queries, private host imports or database writes. Return a short synthetic example and structured error handling for missing membership, permission denial and missing resources. Keep configuration, temporary output and caches in the installation or explicitly selected disposable test directory. Do not read real credentials into logs or reports. If the requested report needs campaign links on 0.3.2, inspect api.journals.resources/resolve or api.mindmaps.resources/resolve and use current authorized results. Never recover hidden IDs or labels from opaque placeholders, and never treat a link as an access grant. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Compare a GM report with an authorized player report and confirm hidden resources are filtered before output. - Attempt a different campaign and a revoked membership; confirm access fails. - Check that generating the report does not change database content or send chat/dice messages. - Revoke target access after linking it and confirm the next report omits its private identity/title; keep local journal page/chapter IDs separate from host resource IDs during portable transfers. Ready when The report uses supported public functions, exposes only the caller’s authorized data and has no write side effects. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to plan a Smart Object
summary: Turn an interaction idea into a verified Map Builder node plan, then simulate and playtest it.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Design a door that lights a nearby lamp, shows a short message and changes to an Opened state when interacted with. Keep the first example local to one object. Context to give the assistant - docs/en/map-builder.md: supported nodes, connections, targets, simulation and playtest. - The current validator and tests for Map Builder blueprints in the target release. - A plain-language list of the map’s states, objects and the authorized effect of each interaction. - On VTT 0.3.3 or newer, the Control shader reference and the separate Test as player rehearsal. - On host 0.3.2, Control clock, Control clue, Open mind map and Control mind-map topic bind native campaign resources; confirm their supported actions in the exact target reference. Step by step 1. Describe the starting state, event, actions, audience and desired final state. 2. Ask the assistant for a node-by-node plan before requesting serialized data. 3. Create the nodes in the real editor, select targets with its controls and simulate the path. 4. Playtest the scene, reset/commit intentionally, and only then generate/update the GM scene. Activate for players separately. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Plan a Map Builder Smart Object for a synthetic Lantern Gate on the requested release. On interaction, enable a nearby native light, show an original short message to the intended audience and change the door state to Opened. Inspect current documentation/validators before naming node types, ports or fields. Verify the generic interact/destroy and presence:enter/presence:exit events against this release; do not reuse deprecated state-specific event names. Give the exact editor actions, targets and expected simulation path. Explain state guards if repeated interactions should be prevented. If the target implements VTT 0.3.3 Control shader, offer an optional action that sets one existing same-map shader opacity to 0.35, using a fixed Number or compatible variable. Verify its native limits and torch visibility/flame gating. Omit the shader action on a host that does not implement it. Do not invent a downloadable blueprint JSON format or call private scene commands from the browser. Only produce importable JSON if the target release explicitly documents and validates that format. Explain how to test both permitted and denied interaction and distinguish project editing, generated scene, playtest state and player activation. If the requested mechanism tracks progress or reveals a graph on 0.3.2, select an existing authorized clock/clue/map with the native target picker. Delegate only a configured GM-authored effect, retain scene scope, and do not grant general editing or expose unfinished clues. On older hosts, report an unsupported capability instead of requiring an unrequested upgrade. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Run Simulate and confirm the selected event follows the intended connections. - Start Playtest, interact, observe the light/message/state, and reset; check the chosen persistence behavior. - If using the shader option, use Test behavior to inspect its predicted changes without saving them. On 0.3.3, use Test as player for movement and activation areas; timers do not advance and this does not replace a real player permission check. - Check GM/player interaction rules, missing targets and repeated actions. - Generate/update the scene privately; activate it only after verifying the intended result. - Rehearse the configured effect without persisting changes, test a permitted real player, then revoke access or remove the target and confirm hidden clues/private graphs do not become readable. Ready when The real node graph produces the intended interaction in playtest and its publication/persistence behavior is understood. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to investigate a bug
summary: Give the assistant a reproducible case, trace it to the owning domain and verify the cause before changing code.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Investigate one observable failure, such as a token moving back after a rejected edit. Distinguish a server conflict, a permission denial and a rendering problem rather than treating them as the same symptom. Context to give the assistant - Installed host/package versions, browser/OS and a minimal reproduction with synthetic data. - Expected versus observed behavior and redacted error.code, network status and timestamps. - docs/en/code-map.md, architecture.md and the owning domain’s service and tests. Step by step 1. Reproduce in an isolated installation and record the smallest sequence that fails. 2. Ask for hypotheses and evidence to distinguish them before requesting a patch. 3. Trace the entry point through transport, service validation, persistence and presentation. 4. Change the owning layer and verify the original case plus the relevant permission/conflict boundary. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Investigate this bug: minimal steps, expected result, observed result . Target release: version . Read AGENTS.md, inspect git status and preserve pending work. Use the code map to locate the owning domain. Reproduce using synthetic data and separate request IDs/revisions, transport results and rendered state. Inspect error.code instead of translated text. Show the evidence for the cause before implementing the smallest fix. Keep rules/authorization in services and notifications after commit. Do not force success by refreshing an expected revision silently, suppressing errors, removing assertions or bypassing permissions. Run focused validation and report commands, outputs and any remaining uncertainty. Do not publish logs, credentials or campaign data. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Confirm the original reproduction now behaves as expected. - Test the denied/expired/stale case relevant to the cause, rather than only the successful GM path. - Review the diff for unrelated changes, data writes and weakened assertions. Ready when The failure has a demonstrated cause, a focused correction and evidence that the original case and its relevant boundaries work. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to write useful tests
summary: Turn a behavior change into focused Django, node:test or Playwright coverage with disposable data.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Protect an actual boundary, such as rejecting another campaign’s resource or avoiding duplicate effects on retry. Select the smallest test layer that can observe that behavior. Context to give the assistant - docs/en/testing.md: actual commands, explicit test database and browser fixture isolation. - The changed service/controller and neighboring tests, plus a clear expected outcome. - The project’s current tools: Django/unittest, node:test and standalone Playwright scripts. Step by step 1. Write the intended behavior and an example failure before generating assertions. 2. Ask the assistant to choose service, pure JavaScript or real-browser coverage with a reason. 3. Allocate independent database, media, module state, ports and outputs. 4. Run the focused test; broaden only when a new failure or unresolved concern warrants it. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Add meaningful regression coverage for behavior in owning domain . Read docs/en/testing.md and the existing neighboring fixtures. Use Django/unittest, node:test or the documented Playwright harness; do not invent a root npm test or pytest runner. Isolate data, media, packages, ports and outputs without editing the real .env. Changing GRAVEWRIGHT_DATABASE alone does not relocate the explicitly configured Django test database. Cover the real boundary: authorized/denied caller, retry with the same operation UUID, conflict refresh, or visible rendering outcome . Give each new logical operation a fresh UUID. Avoid tests that merely repeat implementation constants or documentation. Preserve assertions and report why the test would fail without the fix. Run the narrowest relevant command and report actual results. Treat source-only checks as insufficient when the change requires native/browser execution. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Review fixture isolation before running any command that can replace a test database. - Check that assertions observe behavior at the actual boundary. - Record the focused command and result; preserve logs in disposable local output. Ready when A focused test can detect the original regression, uses isolated state and passes with the intended implementation. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to translate an extension
summary: Prepare English, Portuguese and Spanish catalogs through the official translation mechanism.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Translate the interface of your own package while preserving identifiers, authored campaign content and exact legal notices. Context to give the assistant - The package’s existing keys/catalogs and its i18n registration and lookup calls. - docs/en/modules.md: private catalogs, context.i18n and document-type labelKey. - A glossary of game terms you are authorized to translate and screenshots of long/empty states. Step by step 1. Inventory interface strings without changing identifiers or player-authored text. 2. Keep English as the fallback and preserve explicit language choices. 3. Ask for matching key sets in en, pt-BR and es using the official package mechanism. 4. Inspect long text, placeholders, pluralization, missing keys and narrow layouts in the real interface. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Translate the interface strings of package using its supported i18n mechanism. Inspect the existing catalogs and context.i18n registration/lookups. Keep catalogs inside the owning package and preserve English fallback and explicit user language choice. Produce en, pt-BR and es with identical keys. Preserve interpolation variables, identifiers, command names and document data. Do not translate user-authored names or exact license notices. Use the glossary original terms . Mark ambiguity for review instead of inventing rules or copying proprietary book passages. Register translated type labels through documented labelKey behavior where applicable. Do not change core language globally as a shortcut. Validate missing keys, long text, empty states, focus and layout at narrow widths, with interface text at least 12px. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Compare key sets and placeholder names across all three catalogs. - Switch languages in the actual package; check fallback without translating campaign content. - Inspect the longest labels and empty/error states on a small viewport. Ready when The package uses its official catalogs with matching keys, readable layouts and preserved authored/legal content. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: How to use AI to contribute to the core
summary: Prepare a focused change in the correct layer, with compatible contracts, aligned documentation and reviewable validation.
text: Replace bracketed values before sending the prompt. Give the assistant the relevant public files from the exact target release; use synthetic examples and keep credentials, private campaigns and proprietary material out of its context. What you will build Implement one well-defined generic capability or correction. Use a concrete before/after example and keep system-specific requirements in their package. Context to give the assistant - AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/en/development.md and the architecture/code map. - The owning service, frontend controller and existing tests relevant to the requested behavior. - The target public release and any compatibility or migration constraints. Step by step 1. Describe the user-visible problem and decide whether it belongs to core or a system package. 2. Inspect current work and use a separate checkout when needed to protect it. 3. Ask for a small implementation following existing service, modal, translation and design conventions. 4. Review contracts, generated files, migrations, licensing and aligned English/Portuguese docs before preparing a contribution. Copy and adapt this prompt text Repository: local checkout or public repository Target host release: installed/requested version; preserve it Task scope and authorization: what may be changed/published Implement this focused generic change: before/after example . Target release: version . Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, inspect git status and the owning implementation/tests, and preserve existing work. Keep domain validation, authorization and persistence in services. Keep the Django/Jinja2/Datastar/native JavaScript/PixiJS stack and the existing modal system. Preserve installation-local storage, campaign isolation, request receipts/revisions and notifications after commit. Do not add game-system conditionals to the core. If a browser contract changes, edit gravewright/modules/contracts/frontend.json and regenerate with scripts/generate_frontend_api.py; review source and generated counterpart together. Use meaningful focused tests, visually check layout changes with synthetic data, align English/Portuguese docs and preserve third-party notices. Provide the resulting diff, validation commands/results and actual limitations. Prepare a reviewable contribution; publish or merge only within the authorization given for this task. Inspect the actual files and supported APIs before proposing code. Do not invent commands, fields, endpoints or package capabilities. Use disposable test data and installation-local tools/caches. Explain any unsupported requirement and validate the result with the project’s real tools. Deliver concrete files or editor steps, the checks performed and any unresolved limits. How to validate - Run the relevant Django/node/browser checks described by the repository for the changed behavior. - Inspect the diff for private data, unrelated changes, generated-only edits and changed published migrations. - Verify translations and actual visual behavior when UI changes; use native execution for Runner/installer/updater work. Ready when The change belongs in the right layer, preserves compatibility and data, and has a focused diff with truthful validation evidence. Continue with the module reference (docs:modules), public API (docs:api) and testing guide (docs:testing).

title: Sua primeira sessão
summary: Da instalação a uma cena compartilhada com personagens, anotações e dados.
text: Escolha seu papel Gravewright é uma mesa virtual hospedada por você e acessada pelo navegador. Uma pessoa opera a instalação; os mestres de cada campanha preparam a aventura; jogadores entram nas campanhas. Essas responsabilidades têm permissões diferentes. A versão 0.3.3 é uma prévia alpha: ensaie recursos novos antes de depender deles durante a partida. Se alguém já hospeda sua mesa, peça o endereço e o código de convite. Não é necessário instalar outro servidor para participar. Prepare sua primeira partida 1. O responsável segue Instalação (wiki:installation), inicia o Runner gerado e abre o endereço informado. Numa instalação nova, cria o primeiro proprietário em /setup . 2. O proprietário cria uma campanha na biblioteca. Escolha o sistema PDF nativo ou um sistema instalado compatível com as fichas pretendidas. 3. Abra a mesa. Crie ou envie uma cena, configure a grade e prepare-a em particular. 4. Crie atores, anexe ou configure suas fichas, conceda acesso aos jogadores e coloque seus tokens. 5. Adicione um diário ou material. Confira o que cada jogador pode ler. 6. Convide um jogador com um código da campanha. Use outra sessão como jogador para conferir o resultado. 7. Escolha Ativar para jogadores na cena preparada. Envie uma mensagem e experimente 1d20 + 3 na interface de dados. Confira o resultado As duas sessões devem mostrar a cena transmitida pretendida. O jogador deve controlar seu personagem e ver somente os materiais compartilhados. Abrir uma cena privada como mestre não a transmite. Salvar um projeto do Map Builder não gera nem transmite uma cena. Se algo estiver faltando Confira vínculo com a campanha, permissões dos documentos e cena transmitida antes de reenviar conteúdo. Se o tabuleiro estiver vazio, confira suporte a WebGL e erros de rede no navegador. Reconectar ou atualizar recarrega o estado autorizado para aquela conta. Faça backup antes de importações ou atualizações importantes.

title: Instalar e iniciar o Gravewright
summary: Prepare uma instalação portátil no Windows, Linux ou macOS e entenda o Runner.
text: Antes de começar Baixe o ZIP completo da release oficial e extraia-o para uma pasta gravável. Preserve sua estrutura. O instalador prepara dependências e configuração; o Runner gerado inicia uma instalação já preparada. Ferramentas e pacotes ausentes precisam de internet no primeiro download. Plataforma Instalador Iniciar após instalar --- --- --- Windows x64 Install Windows.bat Gravewright Runner.bat Linux x64 / ARM64 bash "./Install Linux.sh" Gravewright Runner.sh macOS Intel / Apple Silicon Install macOS.command Gravewright Runner.command O Windows exige Windows 10 versão 1803 ou superior, ou Windows 11. O macOS exige 13.5 ou superior. Os downloads Linux gerenciados atendem distribuições glibc. Macs Intel também precisam das Command Line Tools e do SDK Apple; a primeira compilação de cryptography pode demorar mais. Instale e inicie 1. Execute o instalador da plataforma na instalação extraída e responda às perguntas de configuração. 2. Inicie o Runner gerado. Mantenha seu terminal aberto durante a partida. 3. Abra o endereço informado; o endereço local habitual é http://127.0.0.1:3000 . 4. Crie o proprietário em /setup e entre na biblioteca de campanhas. 5. Pressione Ctrl+C no terminal do Runner para encerrar o servidor. Encontre seus arquivos Os padrões ficam dentro desta instalação: configuração e segredos em .env , banco em data/gravewright.sqlite3 , uploads e pacotes em data/media/ , logs em data/logs/ , ferramentas e caches em data/runner/ . Inclua esse conjunto no backup. Duas instalações extraídas mantêm estados independentes. Recupere uma falha de inicialização Se o Runner informar ferramentas preparadas ausentes, execute novamente o instalador na pasta completa. Faça isso também depois de mover ou atualizar a instalação. No Linux/macOS, use bash com o nome do script entre aspas se a abertura por clique falhar. Uma falha de permissão exige tornar gravável a pasta indicada; não mova somente o banco como solução. O Runner gerado atende o computador local em loopback. Jogadores remotos precisam de hospedagem pública configurada intencionalmente com HTTPS e WebSockets; consulte a referência de implantação para devs. Um endereço local funcionando não torna a mesa acessível pela internet.

title: Campanhas, convites e jogadores
summary: Crie uma campanha, convide pessoas e diferencie contas de jogador de links de transmissão.
text: Crie a campanha O proprietário da instalação cria campanhas na biblioteca em /inside . Escolha nome, capa e sistema adequados às fichas. Abra a campanha para preparar a mesa. Cada campanha possui seus membros e recursos; entrar em uma não concede acesso às outras. O Gravewright PDF System integrado oferece uma base genérica para fichas. Outros sistemas de RPG são instalados separadamente. Confira a compatibilidade antes de organizar sua campanha em torno de um pacote opcional. Escolha ou troque a capa 1. Abra a criação ou edição da campanha na biblioteca. Preencha os campos e escolha a origem da capa: do computador ou por URL. Imagens locais aceitam PNG, JPEG ou WebP, até 5 MB. 2. Para uma imagem local, arraste-a até a área de upload ou foque o controle de arquivo e o acione pelo teclado. Escolher um arquivo continua abrindo o seletor do sistema operacional. Para uma URL, use o campo de endereço. 3. Confira a prévia antes de salvar. Remover imagem limpa tanto uma imagem recém-selecionada quanto a capa já salva. Clicar novamente na origem ativa preserva a imagem; trocar de origem limpa a seleção para você escolher a substituta. 4. Salve e confira o cartão da campanha. Se houver erro de validação, corrija o campo indicado e envie novamente. Os modais de campanha e os demais formulários do host compartilham campos, uploads, foco e estados de erro no tema da aplicação. Em telas estreitas, role dentro do modal até as ações. A criação de atores e pastas também usa modais da aplicação: Cancelar fecha sem criar o recurso, e os controles aguardam durante o salvamento. Mantenha o formulário aberto até receber sucesso ou uma mensagem de erro útil. Convide um jogador 1. Peça ao jogador que se cadastre em /register , ou entre por /login se já possuir conta. 2. Como mestre da campanha, crie um código de acesso e escolha validade e máximo de usos. 3. Envie o endereço da hospedagem e o código pelo canal privado que vocês utilizam. 4. Peça que ele entre na campanha; confira seu vínculo e atribua acesso ao ator e aos documentos apropriados. 5. Revogue o código quando ele não for mais necessário. A entrada bem-sucedida de um novo membro incrementa o contador de usos. Se falhar, confira expiração, revogação, usos restantes e campanha associada. Ter conta no servidor não torna a pessoa membro de todas as campanhas. Prepare a sessão Escolha Gerenciar campanha no cartão da campanha para preparar documentos, fichas e planejamento nativos sem entrar na mesa. O gestor de campanha (wiki:campaign-management) atende aos mestres da campanha, inclusive co-GMs; não transmite uma cena nem cria presença na mesa. Use pastas e nomes claros para cenas, atores e diários. Prepare cenas privadas sem transmiti-las; ative a cena pretendida quando o grupo estiver pronto. Se os controles de lobby/prontidão estiverem habilitados, use-os para coordenar o início. Use o acesso de espectador intencionalmente Um link de transmissão oferece acesso restrito de leitura. Não substitui uma conta de jogador e não permite editar a campanha nem projetos do Map Builder. Confira o que o espectador vê antes de transmitir; preparação privada do mestre e permissões de documentos continuam exigindo configuração. Se faltar um ator ou diário, confira o acesso ao recurso depois de confirmar o vínculo. Se faltar um mapa, confira visibilidade da cena e transmissão atual. Veja um ensaio prático em Permissões (wiki:permissions).

title: Gerenciar a campanha antes de jogar
summary: Prepare os mesmos registros fora da mesa, com sete ferramentas de planejamento e recuperação do mestre.
text: Abra a área do mestre Escolha Gerenciar campanha no cartão ou na prévia da capa. Qualquer mestre atual da campanha pode entrar, inclusive um co-GM com conta de participante. Ser proprietário da instalação não concede esse acesso a uma campanha na qual a conta é apenas jogador. Jogadores e streamers utilizam suas ferramentas autorizadas na mesa. Gestor e mesa compartilham diários, missões, atores, fichas, itens, cenas, biblioteca, áudio, cartas, compêndios, relógios (wiki:clocks), pistas (wiki:clues) e mapas mentais (wiki:mindmaps). Preparar por aqui não cria presença na mesa nem altera a transmissão. Gerar/atualizar cenas e executar ações ao vivo continuam sendo operações explícitas. Use as sete ferramentas de preparação Ferramenta Uso prático --- --- Painel pessoal Fixar documentos e organizar painéis de próxima sessão, pendências, diagnósticos e eventos Planejador de sessões Ordenar cenas, encontros, missões, personagens, áudio e notas; manter checklist e concluir com resumo e pendências Cronologia e calendário Registrar datas livres do mundo, datas de calendário opcionais, eventos futuros e documentos vinculados Colunas de missões Alterar status, conferir pré-requisitos/personagens atribuídos e concluir objetivos visíveis Conexões Examinar vínculos e usos de personagens, itens, diários e cenas, incluindo referências tipadas dos diários Ver como jogador Inspecionar os documentos filtrados pelo servidor para o jogador escolhido, em prévia somente leitura Histórico e lixeira Comparar revisões, restaurar uma versão ou recuperar um diário excluído e seus arquivos retidos Cada mestre possui um painel pessoal; sessões e cronologia são preparação compartilhada entre mestres. Esses registros não são entregues a jogadores. O gestor atualiza o estado autorizado automaticamente. Um conflito exige revisar a versão atual; mantenha o rascunho aberto em vez de substituir silenciosamente a revisão de outro mestre. Prepare e confira 1. Selecione o contexto de cena sem alterar a transmissão da mesa. 2. Edite fichas e diários nativos, prepare o progresso e vincule os documentos da sessão. 3. Use Ver como jogador para conferir o público e teste interações numa sessão separada de jogador. 4. Salve antes de sair do editor selecionado. Compare uma revisão no histórico antes de restaurá-la. 5. Entre na mesa e ative a cena quando o grupo estiver pronto. Cópias e exportações incluem a preparação e o histórico selecionados; snapshots preservam recuperação da campanha. Destinos omitidos não se vinculam a recursos não relacionados, e arquivos retidos ausentes impedem restauração incompleta. Um ZIP de campanha não substitui backup consistente da instalação. Veja a referência do gestor (docs:campaign-management) e backup e atualização (wiki:backups-updates).

title: Relógios de progresso e objetivos fixados
summary: Compartilhe objetivos por segmentos entre mesa e gestor, com público e permissões de progresso explícitos.
text: Configure um relógio Abra Relógios no dock inferior da mesa ou Gerenciar campanha → Relógios . O mestre define nome, descrição opcional, cor e 2–24 segmentos. O escopo de campanha acompanha suas cenas; o escopo de cena aparece apenas na cena associada. As duas interfaces editam os mesmos registros. Escolha Somente mestre ou Jogadores . Um relógio público pode permitir que jogadores avancem ou reduzam o progresso; isso não concede configuração, reinício ou exclusão. Streamers permanecem somente leitura. Relógios fixados mostram apenas nome e mostrador na mesa. Registros privados e fora do contexto são filtrados antes da entrega. Avance e consulte Quando autorizado, clique com o botão esquerdo no mostrador para avançar um segmento ou com o direito para recuar. Foque o mostrador e use Direita/Cima ou Esquerda/Baixo para as mesmas ações. O progresso respeita os limites e é compartilhado; aguarde a ação pendente antes de repetir. O editor completo também possui botões de progresso. Dê dois cliques no nome ou foque-o e pressione Enter/Espaço. O mestre abre o editor nativo. Jogadores e streamers abrem uma descrição somente leitura após nova conferência de acesso. A descrição do relógio aceita até 4.000 caracteres autorais, preservando seu idioma. Organize seus indicadores locais Arraste cada relógio fixado pelo título. As setas movem o título focado um pixel; Shift move dez e Escape cancela o arrasto. Cartões e segmentos vazios possuem fundo transparente. A posição fica somente naquele navegador, por conta, campanha e indicador; telas largas e estreitas mantêm layouts separados. Um leitor pode organizar os indicadores permitidos. Mover não envia comando ou transmissão de posição nem altera o progresso compartilhado. Use Controlar relógio no MapBuilder para vincular um Objeto Inteligente a uma ação específica configurada pelo mestre. O nó respeita o escopo e não concede edição geral. O ensaio reverte os efeitos. Veja relógios (docs:clocks) para limites, APIs e retentativas e pistas (wiki:clues) para descobertas por etapas.

title: Revelar pistas pela descoberta
summary: Prepare uma descoberta em particular e revele apenas quando o progresso estiver concluído e o público permitir.
text: Prepare a descoberta Abra Pistas no dock inferior da mesa ou em Gerenciar campanha . Como mestre, preencha nome, Conteúdo para jogadores, Notas do mestre privadas, cor e 1–24 segmentos. Use um segmento para uma descoberta única ou vários numa investigação. Escolha escopo de campanha ou cena e se deseja fixar a pista. Jogadores e streamers só recebem o registro quando o progresso está completo e a visibilidade permite Revelar quando descoberta . Antes disso não recebem nome, identificador, progresso incompleto nem contagem de pistas desconhecidas. As notas continuam privadas após revelar. Mesa e gestor compartilham a mesma pista, independentemente do sistema de RPG. Avance, revele e oculte Somente mestres alteram progresso diretamente: botão esquerdo na barra avança uma etapa, direito recua; as setas também funcionam. Revelar completa a descoberta e permite visibilidade aos jogadores; Ocultar torna a pista exclusiva do mestre sem limpar o progresso; Reiniciar zera o progresso sem mudar o público. Recuar uma pista completa a oculta até concluir novamente. Jogadores podem lembrar o texto que já leram. Pistas fixadas mostram apenas nome e barra. Dê dois cliques no nome ou pressione Enter/Espaço: o mestre abre o editor nativo, enquanto jogadores e streamers leem o Conteúdo descoberto numa descrição simples. O acesso é conferido novamente; notas do mestre nunca se tornam a descrição. Mova e conecte o indicador Arraste o título para organizar a pista localmente; setas movem um pixel e Shift move dez. As posições são por conta/campanha/navegador e guardam layouts separados para telas largas/estreitas. Transparência e arrasto seguem os relógios (wiki:clocks); mover não transmite nem altera progresso compartilhado. O nó Controlar pista do MapBuilder delega uma ação configurada de avanço, recuo, valor, reinício, revelação ou ocultação com autorização nativa. Não concede editor geral de pistas aos jogadores. Veja a referência de pistas (docs:clues) e Objetos Inteligentes (wiki:smart-objects).

title: Mapas mentais colaborativos
